{怎么|zěn me}{卖|mài}？ ("how is it sold?") is the market way to ask a price. Prices with {块|kuài}{五|wǔ} are
the "and a half" of HSK 1: {两|liǎng}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ} is 2.50, and lesson 09 has the rest of the money words.

## Reading: a birthday cake

> {今天|jīn tiān}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}。{下午|xià wǔ}，{邻居|lín jū}{王|Wáng}{阿姨|ā yí}{送来|sòng lái}{一|yí}{个|gè}{大|dà}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}，{上面|shàng miàn}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{新鲜|xīn xiān}{的|de}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}。{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}，{但是|dàn shì}{这么|zhè me}{大|dà}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}，{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{吃不完|chī bu wán}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{大卫|Dà wèi}{和|hé}{安娜|Ān nà}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{电话|diàn huà}。{晚上|wǎn shang}{他们|tā men}{来|lái}{了|le}，{大卫|Dà wèi}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{西瓜|xī guā}，{安娜|Ān nà}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{冰激凌|bīng jī líng}。{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{很|hěn}{甜|tián}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{说|shuō}{好吃|hǎo chī}。{我们|wǒ men}{吃|chī}{了|le}{一半|yí bàn}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}，{冰激凌|bīng jī líng}{都|dōu}{吃完|chī wán}{了|le}，{西瓜|xī guā}{太|tài}{大|dà}，{只|zhǐ}{吃|chī}{了|le}{一|yì}{点儿|diǎnr}。{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{多|duō}，{大卫|Dà wèi}{说|shuō}：“{我|wǒ}{饿|è}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{点|diǎn}{外卖|wài mài}{吧|ba}！”{安娜|Ān nà}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}：“{你|nǐ}{还|hái}{吃得下|chī de xià}{吗|ma}？”{大卫|Dà wèi}{说|shuō}：“{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{是|shì}{甜|tián}{的|de}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{饺子|jiǎo zi}！”

{={只|zhǐ}=} (only) is lesson 26's word: {只|zhǐ}{吃|chī}{了|le}{一|yì}{点儿|diǎnr}, "only ate a little".

1. Who brought the cake?
2. Why did the writer phone two friends?
3. What did they finish completely?
4. What did David want at about nine o'clock, and why did Anna laugh?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. The neighbour, Mrs Wang ({邻居|lín jū}{王|Wáng}{阿姨|ā yí}).
2. The cake was too big to finish alone ({我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{吃不完|chī bu wán}).
3. The ice cream ({冰激凌|bīng jī líng}{都|dōu}{吃完|chī wán}{了|le}). Half the cake and a little of the watermelon were left.
4. He was hungry and wanted a takeaway, dumplings; Anna wondered if he could still eat anything
   ({你|nǐ}{还|hái}{吃得下|chī de xià}{吗|ma}？).

"Today is my birthday. In the afternoon my neighbour Mrs Wang brought round a big cake with lots of
fresh fruit on top. I was very happy, but I couldn't finish a cake that size on my own, so I
phoned David and Anna. They came in the evening: David bought a watermelon and Anna bought ice
cream. The cake was very sweet and everyone said it was delicious. We ate half the cake and
finished all the ice cream; the watermelon was too big, and we only ate a little of it. A bit
after nine, David said, 'I'm hungry, let's order a takeaway!' Anna laughed: 'You can still eat
something?' David said, 'Cake is sweet. I want dumplings!'"
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{我|wǒ}{饿|è}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{点|diǎn}{外卖|wài mài}{吧|ba}。
= I'm hungry. Let's order a takeaway.
{我|wǒ}{吃饱|chī bǎo}{了|le}，{谢谢|xiè xie}！
= I'm full, thank you!
{太|tài}{多|duō}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{吃不完|chī bu wán}。
= That's too much: I can't finish it.
{我|wǒ}{吃不下|chī bu xià}{了|le}。
= I can't eat any more.
{你|nǐ}{尝尝|cháng chang}，{很|hěn}{甜|tián}！
= Have a taste. It's very sweet!
{苹果|píng guǒ}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}{一|yì}{斤|jīn}？
= How much is a jin of apples?
{你|nǐ}{听得懂|tīng de dǒng}{吗|ma}？
= Can you understand?
```

## Pronunciation

- {饿|è}: just a falling *e*, the vowel of {的|de} with a full fourth tone. No consonant before it.
- {渴|kě} sounds exactly like {可|kě} (in {可以|kě yǐ}); {课|kè} (class) falls.
- {饱|bǎo} dips; {包|bāo} (in {包子|bāo zi}) is level. {饱|bǎo} in {吃饱|chī bǎo} keeps its third tone.
- {斤|jīn} is level; {近|jìn} (near) and {进|jìn} (enter) fall.
- {甜|tián} rises; {天|tiān} is level.
- {冰激凌|bīng jī líng}: two level tones, then a rising one. {香蕉|xiāng jiāo} and {西瓜|xī guā} are both level + level.
- Potential complements: the middle syllable is light, *kàn bu jiàn*, *tīng de dǒng*; keep the tones of
  the verb and of the result.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{能|néng}{吃完|chī wán}~~ for "I can't finish it": the result that can't be reached is a potential
  complement, {我|wǒ}{吃不完|chī bu wán}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{得|de}{不|bù}{完|wán}~~: in the negative, {不|bù} replaces {得|de}: {吃不完|chī bu wán}. ({吃|chī}{得|de}{不|bù}{多|duō} with both is a degree
  complement: "doesn't eat much".)
- ~~{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{吃不完|chī bu wán}~~: {把|bǎ} doesn't take a potential complement. Say {蛋糕|dàn gāo}{我|wǒ}{吃不完|chī bu wán}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{饿|è}~~ / ~~{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{渴|kě}~~: adjectives take no {是|shì}. {我|wǒ}{饿|è}{了|le}, {我|wǒ}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{渴|kě}.
- {两|liǎng}{斤|jīn}{的|de}{香蕉|xiāng jiāo} is not wrong but sounds like a description; for buying, number + {斤|jīn} + noun:
  {两|liǎng}{斤|jīn}{香蕉|xiāng jiāo}.
- Writing {渴|kě} with {口|kǒu} (that's {喝|hē}, drink) or {喝|hē} with the water radical 氵: thirst has water, drinking has a mouth.

## Key points

- {饿|è} hungry, {饱|bǎo} full ({吃饱|chī bǎo}{了|le}), {渴|kě} thirsty: adjectives, no {是|shì}; {了|le} for "I've got hungry".
- Potential complement: verb + {得|de} / {不|bù} + result or direction: {吃得完|chī de wán} / {吃不完|chī bu wán},
  {看不见|kàn bu jiàn}, {买不到|mǎi bu dào}, {搬不进去|bān bu jìn qù}. Questions: …{吗|ma}？ or {吃得完|chī de wán}{吃不完|chī bu wán}？
- {吃不下|chī bu xià}, {放不下|fàng bu xià}, {坐不下|zuò bu xià}: no more room.
- Degree {吃|chī}{得|de}{很|hěn}{多|duō} (how) vs potential {吃得完|chī de wán} (can): negatives {吃|chī}{得|de}{不|bù}{多|duō} vs {吃不完|chī bu wán}.
- {尝尝|cháng chang} / {尝|cháng}{一下|yí xià}: have a taste. {甜|tián} sweet, {新鲜|xīn xiān} fresh.
- {斤|jīn} = 500 g: {多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}{一|yì}{斤|jīn}？ {两|liǎng}{斤|jīn}{香蕉|xiāng jiāo}.
- {点|diǎn}{外卖|wài mài} / {叫|jiào}{外卖|wài mài}: order a takeaway.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Being a guest and treating friends: 个个, 天天
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 06 was snacks at home. This one goes out: to a restaurant with friends, and to a friend's
home as a guest. Who pays, who serves whom and what you say at the table matter as much as the
food. You'll learn:

- {请客|qǐng kè} (to treat someone), {做客|zuò kè} (to be a guest) and {客人|kè rén} (a guest);
- measure-word reduplication: {个个|gè gè}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī} (every one is delicious), {天天|tiān tiān} (every day), and
  {一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yí}{个|gè}{地|de} (one by one);
- {差不多|chà bu duō} (almost; about the same) and {好多|hǎo duō} (lots of);
- {加|jiā} (to add) and the words of the table: {菜单|cài dān}, {筷子|kuài zi}, {勺子|sháo zi};
- drinks: {酒|jiǔ}, {啤酒|pí jiǔ}, {饮料|yǐn liào}, {矿泉水|kuàng quán shuǐ};
- {公斤|gōng jīn} (kilogram) beside last lesson's {斤|jīn}.

## {请客|qǐng kè}, {做客|zuò kè}, {客人|kè rén}

The {客|kè} of {不客气|bú kè qi} is a guest. Three words are built on it:

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {请客|qǐng kè} | to treat (someone to a meal), to pay for everyone | {今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{请客|qǐng kè}！ It's my treat today! |
| {做客|zuò kè} | to be a guest (at someone's home) | {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{朋友|péng you}{家|jiā}{做客|zuò kè}。 I'm visiting a friend's home. |
| {客人|kè rén} | guest; customer | {客人|kè rén}{来|lái}{了|le}！ The guests are here! |

{请客|qǐng kè} is a verb with its own object, so the person you treat goes in a {请|qǐng} sentence of its own
(HSK 2's pivotal sentence): {我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{吃饭|chī fàn} (I'll treat you to a meal), not ~~{我|wǒ}{请客|qǐng kè}{你|nǐ}~~.

{我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你们|nǐ men}{喝|hē}{咖啡|kā fēi}。 — I'll buy you all a coffee.

{上|shàng}{次|cì}{你|nǐ}{请客|qǐng kè}，{这|zhè}{次|cì}{我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}。 — You paid last time; this time it's on me.

In China friends often take turns to pay for the whole table rather than splitting the bill, and
it's common to see two people insisting on paying. Splitting the bill exists too, especially
among young people, and has a name: AA{制|zhì} ({制|zhì}: system).

{做客|zuò kè} is what you do at someone's home: {去|qù}…{家|jiā}{做客|zuò kè}. The host says {欢迎|huān yíng} (welcome,
lesson 23) and the guest is treated with care: the host pours the tea, puts food in the guest's
bowl, and keeps saying {多|duō}{吃|chī}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}！ (Eat more!).

{客人|kè rén} is a guest at home and also a customer in a shop or restaurant: {今天|jīn tiān}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{客人|kè rén}{很|hěn}{多|duō}.

## Measure-word reduplication: every single one

Double a measure word and it means "every one, each and every": a **measure-word
reduplication**. HSK 2 doubled verbs ({看看|kàn kan}, and last lesson {尝尝|cháng chang}) and adjectives ({高高|gāo gāo}{的|de}); now the
measure word:

| Doubled | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {个个|gè gè} | every one | {这里|zhè lǐ}{的|de}{菜|cài}{个个|gè gè}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}。 Every dish here is delicious. |
| {件件|jiàn jiàn} | every item | {她|tā}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{件件|jiàn jiàn}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。 Every one of her clothes is pretty. |
| {本本|běn běn} | every book | {这些|zhè xiē}{书|shū}{本本|běn běn}{都|dōu}{有意思|yǒu yì si}。 Every one of these books is interesting. |
| {天天|tiān tiān} | every day | {他|tā}{天天|tiān tiān}{喝|hē}{咖啡|kā fēi}。 He drinks coffee every day. |
| {人人|rén rén} | everyone | {人人|rén rén}{都|dōu}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{她|tā}。 Everyone likes her. |
| {家家|jiā jiā} | every family | {过年|guò nián}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{北方|běi fāng}{家家|jiā jiā}{都|dōu}{吃|chī}{饺子|jiǎo zi}。 At New Year every family in the North eats dumplings. |

{天|tiān}, {人|rén} and {家|jiā} are nouns, but they double like measure words ({天|tiān} even counts like one: you say {三|sān}{天|tiān},
not ~~{三|sān}{个|gè}{天|tiān}~~). Most other nouns don't: not ~~{菜菜|cài cài}~~ or ~~{书书|shū shū}~~.

The rules:

- The doubled word comes **before the verb**, as the subject or the topic, and it's usually
  followed by {都|dōu}: {个个|gè gè}{都|dōu}{好吃|hǎo chī}.
- It's **never the object**: not ~~{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{个个|gè gè}~~. Say {个个|gè gè}{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{喜欢|xǐ huan} or {我|wǒ}{个个|gè gè}{都|dōu}{喜欢|xǐ huan} (I like every one), or with
  {每|měi}: {每|měi}{个|gè}{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{喜欢|xǐ huan}.
- {每|měi} + measure ({每|měi}{个|gè}{菜|cài}, HSK 2) says the same plainly; the doubled form is warmer and
  stresses that there's no exception.

### One by one: {一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yí}{个|gè}{地|de}

With {一|yī} in front, the doubled phrase says *how* something is done, step by step. It goes before
the verb, often with {地|de} (HSK 2's adverbial {地|de}):

{菜|cài}{一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yí}{个|gè}{地|de}{上来|shàng lái}{了|le}。 — The dishes came out one by one.

{孩子|hái zi}{一|yì}{口|kǒu}{一|yì}{口|kǒu}{地|de}{吃|chī}{冰激凌|bīng jī líng}。 — The child is eating the ice cream mouthful by mouthful.

{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yí}{个|gè}{地|de}{进来|jìn lái}。 — Come in one at a time, please.

{上|shàng} is "to serve" (food comes *up* to the table): {上菜|shàng cài} (serve the dishes), {菜|cài}{上来|shàng lái}{了|le}.

## {差不多|chà bu duō} and {好多|hǎo duō}

{差不多|chà bu duō} is "not much different": about the same, or almost. Its {不|bu} is light.

{我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{哥哥|gē ge}{差不多|chà bu duō}{高|gāo}。 — My brother and I are about the same height.

{差不多|chà bu duō}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}。 — It's almost ten. Let's go.

{菜|cài}{差不多|chà bu duō}{了|le}，{不用|bú yòng}{再|zài}{点|diǎn}{了|le}。 — That's about enough food; no need to order more.

{这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{差不多|chà bu duō}。 — These two restaurants are about the same.

Before an adjective it's "about as…" ({差不多|chà bu duō}{高|gāo}), before a number or time "almost"
({差不多|chà bu duō}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}), and at the end of a sentence "about right, nearly there" ({差不多|chà bu duō}{了|le}). Next lesson
has {差|chà} on its own (poor quality; short of).

{好多|hǎo duō} is spoken "lots of, a great many": {好|hǎo} here is "very", as in {好|hǎo}{大|dà}{的|de}{西瓜|xī guā}
(what a big watermelon).

{今天|jīn tiān}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{里|lǐ}{好多|hǎo duō}{人|rén}！ — There are so many people in the restaurant today!

{我们|wǒ men}{点|diǎn}{了|le}{好多|hǎo duō}{菜|cài}。 — We ordered loads of dishes.

{好多|hǎo duō} works like {很|hěn}{多|duō} before a noun, usually with no {的|de}. Don't mix it up with {好|hǎo}{多|duō}{了|le}, "much
better": {我|wǒ}{的|de}{感冒|gǎn mào}{好|hǎo}{多|duō}{了|le} (my cold is much better), an adjective + {多|duō}{了|le} comparison
(lesson 04).

## {加|jiā}: to add

{加|jiā} is "to add, to put in more":

{咖啡|kā fēi}{要|yào}{加|jiā}{糖|táng}{吗|ma}？ — Do you take sugar in your coffee?

{不|bù}{加|jiā}{糖|táng}，{加|jiā}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{牛奶|niú nǎi}。 — No sugar, a little milk.

{我们|wǒ men}{再|zài}{加|jiā}{一|yí}{个|gè}{菜|cài}{吧|ba}。 — Let's order one more dish.

{加|jiā} is also "plus": {一|yī}{加|jiā}{一|yī} is one plus one. Waiters ask {要|yào}{加|jiā}{冰|bīng}{吗|ma}？ (Do you
want ice? {冰|bīng}: ice, lesson 10).

## At the table

| Word | Meaning | Measure |
|---|---|---|
| {菜单|cài dān} | menu | {一|yí}{个|gè} / {一|yì}{张|zhāng}{菜单|cài dān} |
| {筷子|kuài zi} | chopsticks | {一|yì}{双|shuāng}{筷子|kuài zi}, a pair (lesson 08) |
| {勺子|sháo zi} | spoon | {一|yì}{把|bǎ}{勺子|sháo zi} (lesson 03's {把|bǎ} as a measure) |
| {碗|wǎn} | bowl | {一|yí}{个|gè}{碗|wǎn}; {一|yì}{碗|wǎn}{米饭|mǐ fàn}, a bowl of rice |
| {盘子|pán zi} | plate | {一|yí}{个|gè}{盘子|pán zi} |

{服务员|fú wù yuán}，{请|qǐng}{给|gěi}{我们|wǒ men}{菜单|cài dān}。 — Excuse me (waiter), could we have the menu?

{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{会|huì}{用|yòng}{筷子|kuài zi}，{有|yǒu}{勺子|sháo zi}{吗|ma}？ — I can't use chopsticks. Do you have a spoon?

{服务员|fú wù yuán} (waiter, server; staff) is {服务|fú wù} (service, lesson 19) + {员|yuán}; it's also what you call
out to get their attention. {用|yòng} (to use) is lesson 09's word, and {张|zhāng} its measure for flat things.

### Table manners

Customs vary by region and family, and a foreign guest is forgiven almost anything, but a few
are widely kept:

- Don't stand your chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice: it looks like the incense sticks at a
  funeral. Lay them across the bowl or on the rest.
- The host or the person next to you may put food in your bowl ({夹菜|jiā cài}, to pick up food for
  someone). It's a kindness; eat a little, or leave some to show you're full.
- At a toast, people say {干杯|gān bēi} ("dry the glass": cheers). When you clink glasses with an
  older person or a host, holding your glass a little lower is a polite touch.
- Many people don't drink alcohol, and saying {我|wǒ}{开车|kāi chē}，{不能|bù néng}{喝|hē}{酒|jiǔ} (I'm driving, I can't drink) is
  always accepted. Drinking and driving is against the law in China.

## Drinks

| Word | Meaning | Note |
|---|---|---|
| {酒|jiǔ} | alcohol, alcoholic drink | wine, spirits, beer: anything with alcohol |
| {啤酒|pí jiǔ} | beer | {啤|pí} is there for the sound of "beer" |
| {饮料|yǐn liào} | drink, soft drink | the menu word for everything to drink |
| {矿泉水|kuàng quán shuǐ} | mineral water | {矿|kuàng} mineral + {泉|quán} spring + {水|shuǐ} water |

{喝|hē}{酒|jiǔ} is "drink alcohol", so {他|tā}{不|bù}{喝|hē}{酒|jiǔ} means he doesn't drink. Count drinks with containers:
{一|yì}{瓶|píng}{啤酒|pí jiǔ} (a bottle of beer: lesson 03's {瓶子|píng zi}), {一|yì}{杯|bēi}{饮料|yǐn liào} (a glass of something to drink:
HSK 1's {杯子|bēi zi}).

{你们|nǐ men}{要|yào}{什么|shén me}{饮料|yǐn liào}？ — What would you like to drink?

{两|liǎng}{瓶|píng}{啤酒|pí jiǔ}，{一|yì}{瓶|píng}{矿泉水|kuàng quán shuǐ}。 — Two beers and a bottle of mineral water.

## {公斤|gōng jīn} and {斤|jīn}

{公斤|gōng jīn} is the kilogram; {公|gōng} marks the metric unit. One {公斤|gōng jīn} is two {斤|jīn}:

| | grams | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {半|bàn}{斤|jīn} | 250 | {半|bàn}{斤|jīn}{饺子|jiǎo zi} |
| {一|yì}{斤|jīn} | 500 | {一|yì}{斤|jīn}{苹果|píng guǒ} |
| {一|yì}{公斤|gōng jīn} | 1,000 | {一|yì}{公斤|gōng jīn}{米|mǐ} (a kilo of rice) |

{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{公斤|gōng jīn}{苹果|píng guǒ}，{就|jiù}{是|shì}{四|sì}{斤|jīn}。 — I bought two kilos of apples, that's four jin.

{你|nǐ}{多|duō}{重|zhòng}？ (How much do you weigh? {重|zhòng}: heavy, lesson 28) is answered in {公斤|gōng jīn} or in {斤|jīn}:
{六十|liù shí}{公斤|gōng jīn} is {一百二十|yì bǎi èr shí}{斤|jīn}, and people often give their weight in {斤|jīn}.

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 啤 | beer | pí | 口 | 11 | {啤酒|pí jiǔ} |
| 饮 (traditional 飲) | drink | yǐn | 饣 | 7 | {饮料|yǐn liào} |
| 料 | material; stuff | liào | 斗 | 10 | {饮料|yǐn liào} |
| 矿 (traditional 礦) | mine; mineral | kuàng | 石 | 8 | {矿泉水|kuàng quán shuǐ} |
| 泉 | spring (of water) | quán | 水 | 9 | {矿泉水|kuàng quán shuǐ} |
| 差 | lack; poor; differ | chà (and others) | 工 | 9 | {差不多|chà bu duō}, {差|chà} (lesson 08) |
| 加 | add | jiā | 力 | 5 | {加|jiā} |
| 单 (traditional 單) | single; list | dān | 丷 | 8 | {菜单|cài dān} |
| 筷 | chopstick | kuài | ⺮ | 13 | {筷子|kuài zi} |
| 勺 | spoon, ladle | sháo | 勹 | 3 | {勺子|sháo zi} |

- **啤** is 口 + 卑 (*bēi*, for the sound). It was made for the loanword {啤酒|pí jiǔ}. Many characters
  made to write foreign sounds have 口 on the left: {咖啡|kā fēi} (HSK 2) is another pair.
- **饮** is food 饣 + 欠, the open mouth you know from {欢|huān} and {歌|gē}. {饮|yǐn} is the written word for "drink"
  ({喝|hē} is the spoken one): you'll see it in {饮料|yǐn liào} and on signs.
- **料** is rice 米 + 斗, a ladle for measuring grain: what you measure out, "material, stuff". Its
  radical is 斗.
- **矿**: stone 石 (lesson 03's new radical) + 广 for the sound (*guǎng*, which has drifted to *kuàng*).
  Traditional 礦 has 廣 instead of 广.
- **泉**: water 水 under a shape now written 白. The whole character began as a drawing of water
  flowing out of a spring.
- **差**: the top looks like 羊 (sheep), with 工 at the bottom; that's its shape, not its story. It has
  other readings in later words (*chā*, *chāi*); here it's *chà*.
- **加**: strength 力 + mouth 口. "Adding force to your words" is a memory aid only.
- **单**: a dot and a short left-falling stroke on top, a box with a cross, then a long horizontal and a vertical through the middle.
  Make Me a Hanzi files it under 丷 (those two short strokes); some dictionaries list it under 八, and
  traditional 單 is filed under 口.
- **筷**: bamboo ⺮ + {快|kuài} (fast) for the sound. A well-known story says boat people avoided the
  old word for chopsticks, *zhù*, which sounded like "stop", and called them "fast" instead.
- **勺** is a drawing of a ladle with something in it: the outline 勹 and the dot inside.

### Stroke order

- **勺**: the left-falling stroke, then the horizontal that turns down into a hook, then the dot
  inside. Three strokes.
- **加**: 力 first (the turning stroke with a hook, then the left-falling stroke through it), then 口.
- **差**: the dot and left-falling stroke on top, the three horizontals, then the long left-falling
  stroke, and 工 last.
- **单**: the dot and the short left-falling stroke first, then the box (vertical, turning stroke, the two horizontals inside and
  below), then the long horizontal, and the vertical through everything last.
- **饮**: 饣 (three strokes), then 欠: the left-falling stroke, the horizontal with a hook, then
  the left-falling and right-falling strokes.

```trace
啤饮料矿泉差加单筷勺
```

Write it: {饮|yǐn}, {差|chà}, {加|jiā}, {单|dān} and {勺|sháo} are characters to know by hand. Write each one three times
on paper or on the pad, from memory, then check its strokes against the pad.
=}

## Dialogue: it's my treat

{王芳|Wáng Fāng} (王芳) has invited {大卫|Dà wèi} (大卫) to dinner, and a {服务员|fú wù yuán} (服务员,
waiter) brings the menu.

```dialogue
# It's my treat
王芳: {今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{请客|qǐng kè}，{你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{什么|shén me}？
= It's my treat today. What would you like?
大卫: {这里|zhè lǐ}{的|de}{菜|cài}{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{吃|chī}{过|guo}，{你|nǐ}{点|diǎn}{吧|ba}。
= I haven't had any of the dishes here. You order.
服务员: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{菜单|cài dān}。{你们|nǐ men}{喝|hē}{什么|shén me}{饮料|yǐn liào}？
= Here's the menu. What would you like to drink?
王芳: {一|yì}{瓶|píng}{啤酒|pí jiǔ}。{大卫|Dà wèi}，{你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？
= A bottle of beer. David, how about you?
大卫: {我|wǒ}{开车|kāi chē}，{不能|bù néng}{喝|hē}{酒|jiǔ}。{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{矿泉水|kuàng quán shuǐ}。
= I'm driving, so I can't drink. I'll have mineral water.
王芳: {我们|wǒ men}{点|diǎn}{三|sān}{个|gè}{菜|cài}，{再|zài}{加|jiā}{一|yí}{个|gè}{汤|tāng}，{差不多|chà bu duō}{了|le}。
= Let's order three dishes and a soup as well. That should be about right.
大卫: {这些|zhè xiē}{菜|cài}{个个|gè gè}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}！{你|nǐ}{天天|tiān tiān}{来|lái}{这儿|zhèr}{吃饭|chī fàn}{吗|ma}？
= Every one of these dishes is delicious! Do you eat here every day?
王芳: {不|bú}{是|shì}{天天|tiān tiān}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{来|lái}{一|yí}{次|cì}。{你|nǐ}{会|huì}{用|yòng}{筷子|kuài zi}{吗|ma}？
= Not every day, once a week. Can you use chopsticks?
大卫: {会|huì}，{但是|dàn shì}{吃|chī}{汤|tāng}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{饺子|jiǎo zi}，{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{一|yì}{把|bǎ}{勺子|sháo zi}。
= Yes, but for the dumplings in the soup I'd like a spoon.
王芳: {服务员|fú wù yuán}，{请|qǐng}{给|gěi}{我们|wǒ men}{一|yì}{把|bǎ}{勺子|sháo zi}。{还有|hái yǒu}，{买单|mǎi dān}！
= Excuse me, could we have a spoon? And the bill, please!
大卫: {下|xià}{次|cì}{我|wǒ}{请客|qǐng kè}！
= Next time it's my treat!
```

{汤|tāng} is soup (outside the HSK 3 list). {买单|mǎi dān} ("buy the list") is the everyday way to ask for
the bill; {结账|jié zhàng} is another. {这里|zhè lǐ}{的|de}{菜|cài}{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{吃|chī}{过|guo} uses HSK 2's experiential {过|guo} with the
object as the topic.

## Reading: a guest at a friend's home

> {上|shàng}{个|gè}{星期六|xīng qī liù}，{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{同学|tóng xué}{小|xiǎo}{张|Zhāng}{家|jiā}{做客|zuò kè}。{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{公斤|gōng jīn}{苹果|píng guǒ}，{小|xiǎo}{张|Zhāng}{的|de}{妈妈|mā ma}{说|shuō}：“{你|nǐ}{是|shì}{客人|kè rén}，{别|bié}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}！”{她|tā}{做|zuò}{了|le}{好多|hǎo duō}{菜|cài}，{菜|cài}{一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yí}{个|gè}{地|de}{上来|shàng lái}，{个个|gè gè}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}。{小|xiǎo}{张|Zhāng}{的|de}{爸爸|bà ba}{一直|yì zhí}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{夹菜|jiā cài}，{还|hái}{说|shuō}：“{多|duō}{吃|chī}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}！”{我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{了|le}{三|sān}{碗|wǎn}{米饭|mǐ fàn}，{最后|zuì hòu}{真|zhēn}{的|de}{吃不下|chī bu xià}{了|le}，{就|jiù}{说|shuō}：“{我|wǒ}{吃饱|chī bǎo}{了|le}，{谢谢|xiè xie}{叔叔|shū shu}{阿姨|ā yí}！”{我们|wǒ men}{喝|hē}{了|le}{饮料|yǐn liào}，{没有|méi yǒu}{喝|hē}{酒|jiǔ}，{因为|yīn wèi}{小|xiǎo}{张|Zhāng}{的|de}{爸爸|bà ba}{第二|dì èr}{天|tiān}{要|yào}{开车|kāi chē}。{差不多|chà bu duō}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{我|wǒ}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{了|le}。{小|xiǎo}{张|Zhāng}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{他们|tā men}{家|jiā}{最|zuì}{能|néng}{吃|chī}{的|de}{客人|kè rén}！

{一直|yì zhí} (all the time, kept on: lesson 21) and {最后|zuì hòu} (in the end: lesson 25) are later words.
{最|zuì}{能|néng}{吃|chī}{的|de}{客人|kè rén} is "the guest who can eat the most": {能|néng}{吃|chī}, "can eat (a lot)", is a compliment
to a good eater.

1. What did the writer bring, and what did Xiao Zhang's mother say about it?
2. How were the dishes served, and what were they like?
3. Why didn't anyone drink alcohol?
4. What did Xiao Zhang say at the end?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Two kilos of apples ({两|liǎng}{公斤|gōng jīn}{苹果|píng guǒ}); she said a guest shouldn't buy things ({你|nǐ}{是|shì}{客人|kè rén}，{别|bié}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}).
   Hosts often say this: it's politeness, and bringing a small gift is still the custom.
2. One by one ({一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yí}{个|gè}{地|de}{上来|shàng lái}), and every one was delicious ({个个|gè gè}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}).
3. Xiao Zhang's father had to drive the next day.
4. That the writer was the guest who ate the most of any they'd had.

"Last Saturday I visited my classmate Xiao Zhang at home. I bought two kilos of apples, and Xiao
Zhang's mother said, 'You're our guest, you shouldn't buy anything!' She made lots of dishes;
they came out one by one, and every one was delicious. Xiao Zhang's father kept putting food in
my bowl and saying, 'Eat some more!' I ate three bowls of rice, and in the end I really couldn't
eat any more, so I said, 'I'm full, thank you!' We had soft drinks, not alcohol, because Xiao
Zhang's father had to drive the next day. At about ten I went home. Xiao Zhang said I was the
best eater they'd ever had as a guest!"
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{请客|qǐng kè}！
= It's my treat today!
{服务员|fú wù yuán}，{请|qǐng}{给|gěi}{我们|wǒ men}{菜单|cài dān}。
= Excuse me, could we have the menu?
{我|wǒ}{开车|kāi chē}，{不能|bù néng}{喝|hē}{酒|jiǔ}。
= I'm driving: I can't drink.
{这些|zhè xiē}{菜|cài}{个个|gè gè}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}。
= Every one of these dishes is delicious.
{咖啡|kā fēi}{里|lǐ}{不|bù}{加|jiā}{糖|táng}，{谢谢|xiè xie}。
= No sugar in my coffee, thank you.
{差不多|chà bu duō}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}。
= It's almost ten. Let's go.
{下|xià}{次|cì}{我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{吃饭|chī fàn}。
= Next time I'll treat you to a meal.
```

## Pronunciation

- {酒|jiǔ}: *j* + *iu* (short for *iou*), a dipping tone. It sounds like {九|jiǔ} (nine); {就|jiù} falls.
- {啤酒|pí jiǔ}: a rising tone, then a dipping one. {矿泉水|kuàng quán shuǐ}: 4 + 2 + 3.
- {差不多|chà bu duō}: a strong fall on {差|chà}, a light *bu*, then level *duō*.
- {勺子|sháo zi}: *sh* with the tongue curled back, and a rising tone; {少|shǎo} (few) dips.
- {筷子|kuài zi} and {块|kuài}: the same syllable, both falling.
- {个个|gè gè}, {天天|tiān tiān}, {人人|rén rén}: both syllables keep their tones (not light, as the second syllable of a
  doubled verb is: {尝尝|cháng chang}).

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{请客|qǐng kè}{你|nǐ}~~: {请客|qǐng kè} already has its object. Say {我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{吃饭|chī fàn} or {今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{请客|qǐng kè}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{个个|gè gè}~~: a doubled measure word can't be the object. {个个|gè gè}{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{喜欢|xǐ huan}.
- {个个|gè gè}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī} isn't wrong, but {都|dōu} is almost always there: {个个|gè gè}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}.
- ~~{菜菜|cài cài}{都|dōu}{好吃|hǎo chī}~~: ordinary nouns don't double. Double the measure word: {个个|gè gè}.
- {好多|hǎo duō}{的|de}{人|rén} is heard, but the usual form puts {好多|hǎo duō} straight before the noun: {好多|hǎo duō}{人|rén}.
- Writing {筷|kuài} with grass 艹 on top: chopsticks were bamboo, ⺮.

## Key points

- {请客|qǐng kè} (treat: {今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{请客|qǐng kè}), {请|qǐng} + person + {吃饭|chī fàn}; {做客|zuò kè} (be a guest: {去|qù}…{家|jiā}{做客|zuò kè}); {客人|kè rén} (guest, customer).
- Doubled measure words = every one, before the verb with {都|dōu}: {个个|gè gè}, {件件|jiàn jiàn}, {天天|tiān tiān}, {人人|rén rén}, {家家|jiā jiā}.
- {一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yí}{个|gè}{地|de} + verb: one by one.
- {差不多|chà bu duō}: about the same ({差不多|chà bu duō}{高|gāo}), almost ({差不多|chà bu duō}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{了|le}). {好多|hǎo duō} + noun: lots of.
- {加|jiā}: add ({加|jiā}{糖|táng}, {加|jiā}{一|yí}{个|gè}{菜|cài}). {菜单|cài dān}, {筷子|kuài zi} ({一|yì}{双|shuāng}), {勺子|sháo zi} ({一|yì}{把|bǎ}).
- {酒|jiǔ}, {啤酒|pí jiǔ}, {饮料|yǐn liào}, {矿泉水|kuàng quán shuǐ}; {一|yì}{瓶|píng}, {一|yì}{杯|bēi}.
- {一|yì}{公斤|gōng jīn} = {两|liǎng}{斤|jīn} = 1,000 g.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Buying clothes: 又…又, 或者
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 1 gave you {衣服|yī fu} and {穿|chuān}, and HSK 2 {裤子|kù zi} and the colours. This lesson takes you
into a clothes shop: you'll name what you want, ask for your size, try it on, change it and say
whether you're happy with it. You'll learn:

- clothes: {大衣|dà yī}, {上衣|shàng yī}, {衬衫|chèn shān}, {裙子|qún zi}, {短裤|duǎn kù}, {雨衣|yǔ yī}, {鞋|xié}, and the measure
  words that go with them ({件|jiàn}, {条|tiáo}, {双|shuāng});
- fitting: {合适|hé shì}, {大小|dà xiǎo}, {试|shì} (try on), {换|huàn} (change);
- choosing: {选|xuǎn} and {选择|xuǎn zé}, {种|zhǒng} (kind: {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}), {满意|mǎn yì} (satisfied);
- {又|yòu}…{又|yòu}…: both… and… ({又|yòu}{便宜|pián yi}{又|yòu}{好看|hǎo kàn});
- {或者|huò zhě} (or) in statements, beside HSK 2's {还是|hái shi} in questions;
- {差|chà}: poor (quality), and short of;
- two more colours: {黄色|huáng sè} and {蓝|lán}.

## Clothes and their measure words

| Word | Meaning | Measure |
|---|---|---|
| {大衣|dà yī} | overcoat, winter coat | {件|jiàn} |
| {上衣|shàng yī} | top, jacket (what you wear above the waist) | {件|jiàn} |
| {衬衫|chèn shān} | shirt, blouse | {件|jiàn} |
| {雨衣|yǔ yī} | raincoat | {件|jiàn} |
| {裙子|qún zi} | skirt; dress | {条|tiáo} |
| {短裤|duǎn kù} | shorts | {条|tiáo} |
| {裤子|kù zi} | trousers (HSK 2) | {条|tiáo} |
| {鞋|xié} | shoe, shoes | {双|shuāng} (a pair); {一|yì}{只|zhī} (one shoe) |

Clothes you put on over your body, {衣服|yī fu} of all kinds, take {件|jiàn}. Long things that hang from
the waist take {条|tiáo}, the measure of long, narrow things (a fish, a road). Things in pairs take
**{双|shuāng}**:

{一|yì}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié} — a pair of shoes

{一|yì}{双|shuāng}{筷子|kuài zi} — a pair of chopsticks

{两|liǎng}{双|shuāng}{袜子|wà zi} — two pairs of socks ({袜子|wà zi}: socks)

{双|shuāng} also means "both, double", as in {双|shuāng}{手|shǒu} (both hands). One shoe on its own is {一|yì}{只|zhī}{鞋|xié}.

Several of the words are built from parts you know: {大衣|dà yī} is a "big garment", {上衣|shàng yī} an
"upper garment", {雨衣|yǔ yī} a "rain garment", and {短裤|duǎn kù} "short trousers", with lesson 04's {短|duǎn}.
{裙子|qún zi} covers both skirts and dresses; a dress can be called {连衣裙|lián yī qún}, "joined-garment
skirt".

{上衣|shàng yī} is any top, as opposed to what you wear on your legs; on a shop label it often means a
jacket. You put clothes on with {穿|chuān} and take them off with {脱|tuō} (to take off):

{外面|wài miàn}{冷|lěng}，{你|nǐ}{穿|chuān}{上|shàng}{大衣|dà yī}{吧|ba}。 — It's cold out: put your coat on.

{进|jìn}{门|mén}{请|qǐng}{换|huàn}{鞋|xié}。 — Please change your shoes when you come in.

Taking off outdoor shoes at the door and putting on slippers is usual in Chinese homes; the host
will offer you a pair.

## Size and fit: {大小|dà xiǎo}, {合适|hé shì}, {试|shì}

{大小|dà xiǎo} ("big-small") is a noun: size. {合适|hé shì} is "suitable, fitting, right":

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衬衫|chèn shān}{大小|dà xiǎo}{合适|hé shì}{吗|ma}？ — Is this shirt the right size?

{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{大|dà}，{不|bú}{太|tài}{合适|hé shì}。 — It's a bit big. It doesn't really fit.

{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{裙子|qún zi}{你|nǐ}{穿|chuān}{很|hěn}{合适|hé shì}。 — This skirt really suits you.

{合适|hé shì} works for more than clothes: {明天|míng tiān}{去|qù}{合适|hé shì}{吗|ma}？ (Is tomorrow a good time to go?),
{这|zhè}{个|gè}{工作|gōng zuò}{对|duì}{你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{合适|hé shì} (this job is right for you).

Clothes are sized {大号|dà hào} (large), {中号|zhōng hào} (medium) and {小号|xiǎo hào} (small), or with letters
(S, M, L, XL). Shoes are sized by number, as in Europe: {你|nǐ}{穿|chuān}{多|duō}{大|dà}{的|de}{鞋|xié}？ — {我|wǒ}{穿|chuān}{四十|sì shí}{号|hào}{的|de}。
(What size shoes do you take? 40.)

**{试|shì}** is "to try": to try on, to try out. Like {尝|cháng}, it's often doubled or followed by {一下|yí xià}:

{我|wǒ}{可以|kě yǐ}{试试|shì shi}{吗|ma}？ — Can I try it on?

{你|nǐ}{试|shì}{一下|yí xià}{这|zhè}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié}。 — Try these shoes on.

{试衣间|shì yī jiān} ("try-clothes room") is the fitting room. {试|shì} is also "to try (doing something)":
{你|nǐ}{试试|shì shi}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ} (try speaking Chinese).

## {换|huàn}: change it

{换|huàn} is "to change, exchange": one thing out, another in.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{太|tài}{大|dà}{了|le}，{能|néng}{换|huàn}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{小|xiǎo}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{的|de}{吗|ma}？ — This one's too big. Could I change it for a smaller one?

{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{换|huàn}{一|yí}{个|gè}{颜色|yán sè}。 — I'd like a different colour.

{他|tā}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{换|huàn}{了|le}{衣服|yī fu}。 — He went home and changed his clothes.

{小|xiǎo}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{的|de} is "a smaller one": adjective + {一点儿|yì diǎnr} for "a bit more…", then {的|de} for "one". In the
same way: {大|dà}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{的|de} (a bigger one), {便宜|pián yi}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{的|de} (a cheaper one).

## Choosing: {选|xuǎn}, {选择|xuǎn zé}, {种|zhǒng}

{选|xuǎn} and {选择|xuǎn zé} both mean "to choose". {选|xuǎn} is the short, everyday verb; {选择|xuǎn zé} is a little
more formal, and it's also a noun, "a choice":

{你|nǐ}{选|xuǎn}{哪|nǎ}{件|jiàn}？ — Which one are you going for?

{这里|zhè lǐ}{的|de}{鞋|xié}{太|tài}{多|duō}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{怎么|zěn me}{选择|xuǎn zé}。 — There are so many shoes here: I don't know how to choose.

{颜色|yán sè}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{选择|xuǎn zé}。 — There's lots of choice of colours.

**{种|zhǒng}** is the measure word for kinds and types. It goes with {这|zhè}, {那|nà}, {哪|nǎ} and numbers like any
measure word:

{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{衬衫|chèn shān}{很|hěn}{舒服|shū fu}。 — This kind of shirt is very comfortable.

{你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{哪|nǎ}{种|zhǒng}{颜色|yán sè}？ — Which colour do you like?

{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{大衣|dà yī}{有|yǒu}{三|sān}{种|zhǒng}{颜色|yán sè}。 — This kind of coat comes in three colours.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{大衣|dà yī} is one particular coat; {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{大衣|dà yī} is this kind of coat, this style.

**{满意|mǎn yì}** is "satisfied, pleased": {对|duì} + thing + {很|hěn}{满意|mǎn yì}.

{我|wǒ}{对|duì}{这|zhè}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié}{很|hěn}{满意|mǎn yì}。 — I'm very pleased with these shoes.

{你|nǐ}{满意|mǎn yì}{吗|ma}？ — Are you happy with it?

## {又|yòu}…{又|yòu}…: both… and…

{又|yòu} A {又|yòu} B joins two qualities that go together: both A and B. A and B are usually two adjectives
(or two verbs), and they point the same way, two good things or two bad things:

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{大衣|dà yī}{又|yòu}{便宜|pián yi}{又|yòu}{好看|hǎo kàn}。 — This coat is both cheap and good-looking.

{这|zhè}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié}{又|yòu}{贵|guì}{又|yòu}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}。 — These shoes are expensive and uncomfortable.

{西瓜|xī guā}{又|yòu}{大|dà}{又|yòu}{甜|tián}。 — The watermelon is big and sweet.

{孩子|hái zi}{们|men}{又|yòu}{唱|chàng}{又|yòu}{跳|tiào}。 — The children are singing and dancing.

- The two {又|yòu} come right before the adjectives, after the subject. Don't put {很|hěn} after {又|yòu}: the
  pattern already gives the weight ({又|yòu}{便宜|pián yi}{又|yòu}{好看|hǎo kàn}, not ~~{又|yòu}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}{又|yòu}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}~~).
- A good and a bad quality don't go together with {又|yòu}…{又|yòu}: for "cheap but ugly" use {但是|dàn shì}:
  {很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}，{但是|dàn shì}{不|bù}{好看|hǎo kàn}.

{又|yòu} on its own (again, in the past) and its character are lesson 26's; for now learn the pair as a
pattern. {跳|tiào} (to jump) is lesson 21's word; you know it from HSK 2's {跳舞|tiào wǔ}.

## {或者|huò zhě}: or, in a statement

{或者|huò zhě} is "or" when you're *saying* something, not asking: either one will do, or it's one of
two possibilities.

{你|nǐ}{可以|kě yǐ}{穿|chuān}{蓝色|lán sè}{的|de}{或者|huò zhě}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}。 — You could wear the blue one or the black one.

{星期六|xīng qī liù}{或者|huò zhě}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{买|mǎi}{鞋|xié}。 — We'll go and buy shoes on Saturday or Sunday.

In a question that asks someone to choose, Chinese uses {还是|hái shi} (HSK 2), not {或者|huò zhě}:

{你|nǐ}{要|yào}{蓝色|lán sè}{的|de}{还是|hái shi}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}？ — Do you want the blue one or the black one?

| | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {还是|hái shi} | a question: which one? | {你|nǐ}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}{还是|hái shi}{咖啡|kā fēi}？ |
| {或者|huò zhě} | a statement: either | {茶|chá}{或者|huò zhě}{咖啡|kā fēi}{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}。 Tea or coffee, either is fine. |

{或者|huò zhě} and its characters are taught in lesson 26, with its short form {或|huò}.

## {差|chà}: not good enough, and short of

Lesson 07's {差不多|chà bu duō} has {差|chà}, "to differ, to fall short". On its own it's an adjective, "poor,
bad (in quality)":

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}，{但是|dàn shì}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{差|chà}。 — This garment is cheap, but it's not very good.

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{还|hái}{很|hěn}{差|chà}。 — My Chinese is still poor.

As a verb it means "to be short of", with the amount after it:

{还|hái}{差|chà}{五|wǔ}{块|kuài}{钱|qián}。 — I'm still five kuai short.

{差|chà}{五|wǔ}{分|fēn}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}。 — Five to eight. (Eight, short of five minutes.)

The time pattern is {差|chà} + minutes + hour: {差|chà}{十|shí}{分|fēn}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn} is 8:50.

## Colours: {黄色|huáng sè} and {蓝|lán}

You know {颜色|yán sè} and the HSK 2 colours {红色|hóng sè}, {白色|bái sè}, {黑色|hēi sè} and {绿色|lǜ sè}. Add yellow and blue:

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {黄色|huáng sè} | yellow | {黄色|huáng sè}{的|de}{雨衣|yǔ yī} |
| {蓝|lán} / {蓝色|lán sè} | blue | {蓝|lán}{衬衫|chèn shān}, {蓝色|lán sè}{的|de}{裙子|qún zi}, {蓝天|lán tiān} (blue sky) |

Colours work as nouns with {色|sè} ({我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{蓝色|lán sè}) and as adjectives without it ({蓝|lán}{衬衫|chèn shān}, a blue shirt;
{天|tiān}{很|hěn}{蓝|lán}, the sky is very blue). Before a noun, the form with {色|sè} usually takes {的|de}: {蓝色|lán sè}{的|de}{裙子|qún zi}.

{黄|huáng} is also a common surname, {黄|Huáng}, and it's in {黄河|Huáng hé}, the Yellow River.

The rest are built from meanings or shapes:

- **双** is two hands 又 side by side: a pair. Traditional 雙 is two birds 隹 above a hand 又, "a
  pair of birds in the hand".
- **合** is a lid on a pot or a mouth 口: closing, fitting together. In {合适|hé shì} it's "fit".
- **适** is movement 辶 + 舌 in the simplified form (traditional 適 has 啇 instead, which gave the sound).
  The 舌 is a shape here, not "tongue".
- **鞋** is leather 革 + 圭 (*guī*, once the sound). 革 is the radical of shoes and saddles.
- **择**: hand 扌 + a simplified right side; traditional 擇 has 睪.
- **黄** is its own radical. It's in {黄色|huáng sè} and the surname {黄|Huáng}.

### Stroke order

- **双**: the left 又 first, its second stroke shortened to a dot-like stroke; then the right 又, with
  the long right-falling stroke last.
- **黄**: the top like 廿 (a horizontal, two short verticals), the long horizontal, then 由 (the box with
  its vertical), and the two short strokes at the bottom, left-falling then dot.
- **鞋**: 革 on the left (廿, then the box, the bottom horizontal written as a rising stroke, and the
  long vertical through it last), then 圭: two 土, one above the other.
- **适, 选**: the inside first (舌, 先), then 辶 last: dot, the bent stroke, the long sweep.
- **种**: 禾 first, its right-falling stroke shortened to a dot, then {中|zhōng}.

## Pronunciation

- {鞋|xié}: *x* with the tongue flat behind the lower teeth, a rising tone. {写|xiě} (write) dips and {谢|xiè}
  falls: the same syllable with three tones.
- {衬衫|chèn shān}: two retroflex syllables, *ch* and *sh*, tongue curled back; {衬|chèn} falls, {衫|shān} is level.
- {双|shuāng}: *sh* + *uang*, level. {选|xuǎn} and {换|huàn} both end in *-uan*, but {选|xuǎn} is *x* + *üan* (written
  -uan after *x*): lips rounded for ü.
- {种|zhǒng} dips; {中|zhōng} (middle) is level.
- {裙子|qún zi}: *q* + *ün* (written -un after *q*), rising, lips rounded.
- {试|shì} sounds like {是|shì}, {事|shì} and {市|shì}: only the context tells them apart.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{裙子|qún zi}~~: skirts, shorts and trousers take {条|tiáo}. Tops and coats take {件|jiàn}, shoes {双|shuāng}.
- ~~{你|nǐ}{要|yào}{蓝色|lán sè}{的|de}{或者|huò zhě}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}？~~ as a choice question: in questions use {还是|hái shi}. {或者|huò zhě} is for
  statements.
- ~~{又|yòu}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}{又|yòu}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}~~: no {很|hěn} after {又|yòu}. And ~~{又|yòu}{便宜|pián yi}{又|yòu}{难看|nán kàn}~~ ({难看|nán kàn}: ugly, lesson 22) mixes a
  good and a bad quality: use {但是|dàn shì}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{满意|mǎn yì}{这|zhè}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié}~~ sounds odd without {很|hěn}: say {我|wǒ}{对|duì}{这|zhè}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié}{很|hěn}{满意|mǎn yì} (or {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{满意|mǎn yì}{这|zhè}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié}, also natural).
- {这|zhè}{件|jiàn} vs {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{大衣|dà yī} is this coat, {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{大衣|dà yī} this kind of coat.
- {=Writing {选|xuǎn} with {先|xiān} outside 辶=}: the inside goes first, then 辶 underneath and round it.

## Key points

- {件|jiàn}: {大衣|dà yī}, {上衣|shàng yī}, {衬衫|chèn shān}, {雨衣|yǔ yī}. {条|tiáo}: {裙子|qún zi}, {短裤|duǎn kù}, {裤子|kù zi}. {双|shuāng}: {鞋|xié}, {筷子|kuài zi} (a pair).
- {大小|dà xiǎo}{合适|hé shì}{吗|ma}？ {试试|shì shi} / {试|shì}{一下|yí xià} (try on). {换|huàn}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{大|dà}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{的|de} (change for a bigger one).
- {选|xuǎn} / {选择|xuǎn zé}: choose ({选择|xuǎn zé} is also "a choice"). {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}: this kind. {对|duì}…{很|hěn}{满意|mǎn yì}: pleased with.
- {又|yòu} A {又|yòu} B: both A and B (two good or two bad qualities; no {很|hěn}).
- {或者|huò zhě}: or, in statements; {还是|hái shi}: or, in questions.
- {差|chà}: poor ({很|hěn}{差|chà}); short of ({还|hái}{差|chà}{五|wǔ}{块|kuài}); {差|chà}{五|wǔ}{分|fēn}{八|bā}{点|diǎn} (five to eight).
- {黄色|huáng sè} yellow, {蓝|lán} / {蓝色|lán sè} blue.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Money, cards and the bank: 块 and 元, 毛 and 角
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

You've paid in {块|kuài} since HSK 1. This lesson completes Chinese money: the smaller unit {毛|máo} (spoken)
and {角|jiǎo} (written), prices like ¥12.50, and totals with {一共|yí gòng}. Then it goes to the bank and
the phone: getting a bank card, paying by card or by phone, checking, receiving and charging.
You'll learn:

- {块|kuài} / {毛|máo} in speech, {元|yuán} / {角|jiǎo} in writing: ¥12.50 is {十二|shí èr}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ} or {十二|shí èr}{元|yuán}{五|wǔ}{角|jiǎo};
- {卡|kǎ}, {银行|yín háng}, {银行卡|yín háng kǎ}, {信用卡|xìn yòng kǎ}, {号码|hào mǎ}, and the measure word {张|zhāng};
- everyday verbs: {办|bàn} (handle; get done), {查|chá} (check), {带|dài} (bring), {收|shōu} / {收到|shōu dào} (receive),
  {用|yòng} (use), {起|qǐ} (rise; from… on);
- {办法|bàn fǎ} (a way), {有用|yǒu yòng} (useful);
- {电|diàn} (electricity), {开机|kāi jī} / {关机|guān jī}: when your phone dies;
- decimals, fractions and percentages: {三|sān}{点|diǎn}{五|wǔ}, {三分之一|sān fēn zhī yī}, {百分之五十|bǎi fēn zhī wǔ shí}.

## Money: {块|kuài} and {毛|máo}, {元|yuán} and {角|jiǎo}

The Chinese yuan (renminbi, "the people's currency") has a unit and a tenth of a unit, each with a
spoken and a written name:

| Value | Spoken | Written (price tags, banknotes, receipts) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 yuan | {块|kuài} | {元|yuán} |
| 0.1 yuan | {毛|máo} | {角|jiǎo} |
| 0.01 yuan | {分|fēn} | {分|fēn} |

| Price | Said | Written in words |
|---|---|---|
| ¥5 | {五|wǔ}{块|kuài}({钱|qián}) | {五|wǔ}{元|yuán} |
| ¥0.50 | {五|wǔ}{毛|máo}({钱|qián}) | {五|wǔ}{角|jiǎo} |
| ¥12.50 | {十二|shí èr}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ}({毛|máo}) | {十二|shí èr}{元|yuán}{五|wǔ}{角|jiǎo} |
| ¥2.20 | {两|liǎng}{块|kuài}{二|èr} | {二|èr}{元|yuán}{二|èr}{角|jiǎo} |
| ¥0.20 | {两|liǎng}{毛|máo} | {二|èr}{角|jiǎo} |
| ¥10.05 | {十|shí}{块|kuài}{零|líng}{五|wǔ}{分|fēn} | {十|shí}{元|yuán}{零|líng}{五|wǔ}{分|fēn} |

- The last unit is usually dropped in speech: {十二|shí èr}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ} is ¥12.50, just as {两|liǎng}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ} was in lesson 06.
- {两|liǎng} for 2 before {块|kuài} and {毛|máo} ({两|liǎng}{块|kuài}, {两|liǎng}{毛|máo}), but {二|èr} when it's the last digit after a unit ({两|liǎng}{块|kuài}{二|èr}). In formal writing, {二|èr}{元|yuán}, {二|èr}{角|jiǎo} are usual
  ({两|liǎng}{元|yuán} is common in print too), though prices are mostly written in figures.
- A gap is filled with {零|líng}: ¥10.05 is {十|shí}{块|kuài}{零|líng}{五|wǔ}{分|fēn}. {分|fēn} is rarely needed now; most prices end in whole
  {毛|máo}.
- {毛|máo} is also hair (on the body, and an animal's fur); {角|jiǎo} is also a horn and a corner. Hair on your head
  is lesson 04's {头发|tóu fa}.

{一共|yí gòng} (altogether) goes before the verb or the amount:

{一共|yí gòng}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？ — How much is it altogether?

{一共|yí gòng}{三十七|sān shí qī}{块|kuài}{八|bā}。 — Thirty-seven eighty altogether.

{我们|wǒ men}{班|bān}{一共|yí gòng}{有|yǒu}{二十|èr shí}{个|gè}{学生|xué sheng}。 — There are twenty students in our class altogether.

## Cards and the bank

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {卡|kǎ} | card |
| {银行|yín háng} | bank |
| {银行卡|yín háng kǎ} | bank card, debit card |
| {信用卡|xìn yòng kǎ} | credit card |
| {号码|hào mǎ} | number (of a phone, a room, a card) |

{信用|xìn yòng} is "trust, credit": {信|xìn} (to believe; a letter) + {用|yòng} (use). Cards, tickets, tables, beds and sheets
of paper are flat, and their measure word is {张|zhāng}:

{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{银行卡|yín háng kǎ}, {两|liǎng}{张|zhāng}{票|piào}, {一|yì}{张|zhāng}{桌子|zhuō zi}, {一|yì}{张|zhāng}{床|chuáng} — a bank card, two tickets, a table, a bed

{张|zhāng} is also one of the most common surnames: {张|Zhāng}{老师|lǎo shī}.

{号码|hào mǎ} is the number that identifies something: {电话|diàn huà}{号码|hào mǎ} (phone number), {房间|fáng jiān}{号码|hào mǎ} (room
number), {卡|kǎ}{的|de}{号码|hào mǎ} (the card number). The digits are read one by one, and 1 is read *yāo*
in them, as you learned in HSK 1:

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{电话|diàn huà}{号码|hào mǎ}{是|shì} 126 0157 6688。 — My phone number is 126 0157 6688 (*yāo èr liù, líng yāo wǔ qī, liù liù bā bā*: a made-up number).

## {办|bàn}, {办法|bàn fǎ}: getting things done

{办|bàn} is "to handle, to deal with, to get (something official) done". It's the verb for paperwork:

{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{办|bàn}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{银行卡|yín háng kǎ}。 — I'd like to get a bank card (open an account).

{今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{事|shì}{要|yào}{办|bàn}。 — I've got a lot of things to sort out today.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{很|hěn}{难|nán}{办|bàn}。 — This is hard to deal with. ({难|nán}: hard, lesson 18)

{办法|bàn fǎ} is "a way (to solve something), a means". {有|yǒu}{办法|bàn fǎ} is "to know what to do", and {没|méi}{办法|bàn fǎ} is
the very common "there's nothing for it, it can't be helped":

{你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{办法|bàn fǎ}？ — What can you do about it? / Any ideas?

{没|méi}{办法|bàn fǎ}，{今天|jīn tiān}{银行|yín háng}{不|bù}{开门|kāi mén}。 — It can't be helped: the bank isn't open today.

## {带|dài}, {查|chá}, {收|shōu}, {用|yòng}

**{带|dài}** is "to bring, to take (with you), to have on you":

{你|nǐ}{带|dài}{护照|hù zhào}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ — Have you brought your passport? ({护照|hù zhào}: passport, lesson 14)

{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{带|dài}{钱|qián}，{能|néng}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{吗|ma}？ — I haven't got any money on me. Can I use my phone?

**{查|chá}** is "to check, to look up":

{我|wǒ}{查|chá}{一下|yí xià}{这|zhè}{张|zhāng}{卡|kǎ}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}。 — I'll check how much money is left on this card.

{你|nǐ}{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{查|chá}{一下|yí xià}{银行|yín háng}{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}{开门|kāi mén}。 — Look up online what time the bank opens.

**{收|shōu}** is "to receive, to accept, to collect", the action; **{收到|shōu dào}** is "to have received", the result
(HSK 2's result complement {到|dào}):

{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{店|diàn}{不|bù}{收|shōu}{信用卡|xìn yòng kǎ}。 — This shop doesn't take credit cards.

{我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{发|fā}{了|le}{短信|duǎn xìn}，{你|nǐ}{收到|shōu dào}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ — I've sent you a text. Did you get it?

{收到|shōu dào}{了|le}，{谢谢|xiè xie}！ — Got it, thanks!

({发|fā}, to send, is lesson 20's word; {短信|duǎn xìn} is a text message.)

**{用|yòng}** is "to use". Like {坐|zuò} in {坐|zuò}{车|chē}{去|qù}, it comes before the main verb to say *with what*:

{我|wǒ}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{付|fù}{钱|qián}。 — I pay with my phone. ({付|fù}: to pay)

{他|tā}{用|yòng}{筷子|kuài zi}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 — He eats with chopsticks.

{用|yòng}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{怎么|zěn me}{说|shuō}？ — How do you say it in Chinese?

{有用|yǒu yòng} is "useful" and {没|méi}{用|yòng} "useless, no use": {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{很|hěn}{有用|yǒu yòng}, {哭|kū}{也|yě}{没|méi}{用|yòng} (crying won't
help; {哭|kū}: cry, lesson 24). Lesson 05's {不用|bú yòng} is "no need to".

## Paying by phone

Most everyday payments in Chinese cities are made with a phone: you scan a shop's QR code, or the
shop scans yours. Bank cards and cash are used too, and visitors can link a foreign card to the
payment apps. The words you'll hear:

| Phrase | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {手机|shǒu jī}{支付|zhī fù} | mobile payment |
| {扫码|sǎo mǎ} | scan the (QR) code: lesson 03's {扫|sǎo} + {码|mǎ} |
| {二维码|èr wéi mǎ} | QR code ("two-dimensional code") |
| {付|fù}{钱|qián} | to pay |
| {现金|xiàn jīn} | cash |
| {刷卡|shuā kǎ} | to pay by card ("swipe the card": lesson 03's {刷|shuā}) |

{可以|kě yǐ}{扫码|sǎo mǎ}{吗|ma}？ — Can I pay by scanning?

{我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{现金|xiàn jīn}，{可以|kě yǐ}{刷卡|shuā kǎ}{吗|ma}？ — I haven't got cash. Can I pay by card?

## {电|diàn}, {开机|kāi jī}, {关机|guān jī}: when the phone dies

{电|diàn} is electricity, the {电|diàn} of {电话|diàn huà}, {电脑|diàn nǎo} and {电视|diàn shì}. And with no battery, there's no paying by phone:

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{没|méi}{电|diàn}{了|le}。 — My phone's battery is dead.

{他|tā}{关机|guān jī}{了|le}，{打|dǎ}{不|bu}{通|tōng}。 — His phone is switched off: I can't get through. ({通|tōng}: get through)

{上课|shàng kè}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{请|qǐng}{关机|guān jī}。 — Please switch your phones off in class.

{开机|kāi jī} and {关机|guān jī} are "switch on" and "switch off" for phones and computers. {充电|chōng diàn} is "to
charge (a battery)". {打不通|dǎ bu tōng} is lesson 06's potential complement: the call can't get through.

## {起|qǐ}: to rise, and "from… on"

{起|qǐ} is in {起床|qǐ chuáng} (get up) and HSK 2's {起来|qǐ lái} (stand up). On its own it's "to rise, to get up",
and after {从|cóng} + time it means "starting from":

{我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{起|qǐ}。 — I get up at six every day.

{从|cóng}{下|xià}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{起|qǐ}，{这|zhè}{张|zhāng}{卡|kǎ}{不|bù}{能|néng}{用|yòng}{了|le}。 — From next month on, this card can't be used.

{从|cóng}…{起|qǐ} is typical of notices: banks and shops use it to say when something changes.

## Decimals, fractions and percentages

**Decimals** use {点|diǎn} (point), and the digits after it are read one by one. {一|yī} stays first tone in
numbers:

| Number | Said |
|---|---|
| 3.5 | {三|sān}{点|diǎn}{五|wǔ} |
| 0.8 | {零|líng}{点|diǎn}{八|bā} |
| 12.75 | {十二|shí èr}{点|diǎn}{七|qī}{五|wǔ} |
| 1.75 m (a height) | {一米七五|yì mǐ qī wǔ} (lesson 04) or {一|yī}{点|diǎn}{七|qī}{五|wǔ}{米|mǐ} |

**Fractions** are said bottom first: "of three parts, one". The pattern is number + {分之|fēn zhī} + number:

| Fraction | Said |
|---|---|
| 1/3 | {三分之一|sān fēn zhī yī} |
| 3/4 | {四分之三|sì fēn zhī sān} |
| 1/2 | {二分之一|èr fēn zhī yī} (in maths), usually {一半|yí bàn} |

**Percentages** are fractions of a hundred: {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī} + number.

{百分之五十|bǎi fēn zhī wǔ shí} — 50%; {百分之百|bǎi fēn zhī bǎi} — 100%, completely

{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{店|diàn}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{都|dōu}{打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé}。 — Everything in this shop is 20% off.

Shops give discounts as {折|zhé}, "tenths of the price you pay": {打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé} is paying 80%, so 20% off;
{打|dǎ}{五|wǔ}{折|zhé} is half price. You may remember it from HSK 2's shopping lesson.

**Writing numbers.** In print, prices, amounts, measurements and most dates are written in figures:
¥12.50, 3.5{公斤|gōng jīn}, 1.75{米|mǐ}, 50%. Words with a number inside, such as {一共|yí gòng}, {一起|yì qǐ} and {一半|yí bàn},
are always written in characters.

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 卡 | card | kǎ | 卜 | 5 | {卡|kǎ}, {银行卡|yín háng kǎ}, {信用卡|xìn yòng kǎ} |
| 信 | trust; letter | xìn | 亻 | 9 | {信用卡|xìn yòng kǎ}, {信|xìn} (lesson 20), {相信|xiāng xìn} (lesson 24) |
| 银 (traditional 銀) | silver | yín | 钅 | 11 | {银行|yín háng}, {银行卡|yín háng kǎ} |
| 行 | row; firm; walk | háng, xíng | 行 | 6 | {银行|yín háng}; {自行车|zì xíng chē} (lesson 13) |
| 码 (traditional 碼) | code; number | mǎ | 石 | 8 | {号码|hào mǎ} |
| 收 | receive; collect | shōu | 攵 | 6 | {收|shōu}, {收到|shōu dào} |
| 办 (traditional 辦) | handle, do | bàn | 力 | 4 | {办|bàn}, {办法|bàn fǎ} |
| 法 | method; law | fǎ | 氵 | 8 | {办法|bàn fǎ}, {方法|fāng fǎ} (lesson 17) |
| 带 (traditional 帶) | belt; bring | dài | 巾 | 9 | {带|dài} |
| 张 (traditional 張) | (flat things); stretch | zhāng | 弓 | 7 | {张|zhāng} |
| 角 | horn; corner; jiao | jiǎo | 角 | 7 | {角|jiǎo} |
| 毛 | hair, fur; mao | máo | 毛 | 4 | {毛|máo} |
| 共 | together; share | gòng | 八 | 6 | {一共|yí gòng} |

{行|xíng} has two readings: *háng* in {银行|yín háng} (a firm, a line of business) and *xíng* in {自行车|zì xíng chē} and {行|xíng}
("OK", lesson 28).

### Sound part: {马|mǎ}

{码|mǎ} is stone 石 + {马|mǎ} (horse) for the sound, an exact match. You know the same sound part in {吗|ma}
and {妈|mā}, with 口 and 女 for the meaning; {骂|mà} (to scold) is another. Four tones, one horse.

### Meaning stories

- **卡** is 上 above 下: something stuck between up and down. That's the meaning of its other reading,
  *qiǎ* (to get stuck). *kǎ*, "card", is usually explained as a borrowing of the English sound.
- **信** is a person 亻 + words 言: a person standing by their word. Trust, and then a letter.
- **银** is metal 钅 + 艮 (*gèn*, once the sound; it has drifted). 钅 is HSK 1's metal radical, also
  in {钱|qián} and {钟|zhōng}.
- **行** began as a drawing of a crossroads: going, walking, and a row (of shops).
- **办** is strength 力 with a dot on each side. Traditional 辦 has 力 between two 辛.
- **法**: water 氵 + 去. The traditional explanation is that law should be as level as water. It's
  also "method", as in {办法|bàn fǎ}.
- **带** began as a drawing of a belt with things hanging from it, which is why 巾 (cloth) is at the
  bottom. From "belt" came "to carry with you".
- **张** is bow 弓 + {长|cháng}: drawing a bow, stretching. 长 also helps with the sound (*zhǎng*, lesson 28).
- **角** is a drawing of a horn, and **毛** a drawing of a tuft of hair.
- **共** has 廾, two hands, at the bottom: holding something up together.

### Stroke order

- **办**: 力 first (the horizontal turning into a hook, then the left-falling stroke through it), then
  the dot on the left and the dot on the right.
- **毛**: the left-falling stroke on top, two horizontals, then the long vertical that bends right and
  ends with a hook.
- **收**: the left part (a short vertical with a rising stroke, then the long vertical), then 攵:
  left-falling, horizontal, left-falling, right-falling.
- **带**: the top (a horizontal and three short verticals), then the cover (a dot-like vertical and the
  horizontal with a hook), then 巾 (vertical, the turning stroke with a hook, the long vertical).
- **共**: the horizontal, the two verticals, the long horizontal, then the two short strokes at the bottom,
  left then right: a short left-falling stroke and a dot.

```trace
卡信银行码收办
```

```trace
法带张角毛共
```

Write it: all but {银|yín} and {码|mǎ} are characters to know by hand: {卡|kǎ}, {信|xìn}, {行|xíng}, {收|shōu}, {办|bàn}, {法|fǎ}, {带|dài}, {张|zhāng}, {角|jiǎo},
{毛|máo} and {共|gòng}. Write each one three times on paper or on the pad, from memory, then check its strokes
against the pad.

### Handwriting review

These HSK 1 and 2 characters are among the 100 to know by hand, and money, numbers and time use
them all the time. Cover the right-hand column, write each one from memory, then check it on the
pad.

| Character | Pinyin | Meaning | In this module |

## Dialogue: at the bank

{安娜|Ān nà} (安娜) goes to a bank to get a bank card. She talks to a member of staff, a
{工作人员|gōng zuò rén yuán} (工作人员: "work person").

```dialogue
# At the bank
工作人员: {您|nín}{好|hǎo}，{您|nín}{要|yào}{办|bàn}{什么|shén me}？
= Hello. What can I do for you?
安娜: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{办|bàn}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{银行卡|yín háng kǎ}。
= I'd like to get a bank card.
工作人员: {好|hǎo}{的|de}。{您|nín}{带|dài}{护照|hù zhào}{了|le}{吗|ma}？
= Certainly. Have you brought your passport?
安娜: {带|dài}{了|le}，{给|gěi}{您|nín}。
= Yes, here you are.
工作人员: {请|qǐng}{写|xiě}{一下|yí xià}{您|nín}{的|de}{电话|diàn huà}{号码|hào mǎ}。{银行|yín háng}{会|huì}{给|gěi}{您|nín}{发|fā}{短信|duǎn xìn}。
= Please write down your phone number. The bank will send you a text.
安娜: {我|wǒ}{收到|shōu dào}{了|le}！{短信|duǎn xìn}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{号码|hào mǎ}。
= I've got it! There's a number in it.
工作人员: {对|duì}，{请|qǐng}{说|shuō}{一下|yí xià}。……{好|hǎo}{了|le}，{这|zhè}{是|shì}{您|nín}{的|de}{卡|kǎ}。{从|cóng}{今天|jīn tiān}{起|qǐ}{就|jiù}{可以|kě yǐ}{用|yòng}{了|le}。
= Right, please read it out. … Done. Here's your card. You can use it from today.
安娜: {太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}。{这|zhè}{张|zhāng}{卡|kǎ}{能|néng}{在|zài}{手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}{用|yòng}{吗|ma}？
= Great. Can I use this card on my phone?
工作人员: {能|néng}。{您|nín}{在|zài}{手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}{也|yě}{能|néng}{查|chá}{到|dào}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}。{请|qǐng}{带|dài}{好|hǎo}{您|nín}{的|de}{卡|kǎ}，{别|bié}{丢|diū}{了|le}。
= Yes. You can also check on your phone how much is left. Please keep your card safe, don't lose it.
安娜: {谢谢|xiè xie}！{手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}{能|néng}{查|chá}，{真|zhēn}{有用|yǒu yòng}！
= Thank you! Being able to check on my phone is really useful!
```

{银行|yín háng}{会|huì}{给|gěi}{您|nín}{发|fā}{短信|duǎn xìn} uses {会|huì} for "will": something that's going to happen. {带|dài}{好|hǎo} is "take
along carefully" ({好|hǎo} as a result complement). {手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}{能|néng}{查|chá}，{真|zhēn}{有用|yǒu yòng}: "(that you) can check on the phone: really useful", the
first half standing as the topic.

## Reading: no battery, no money

> {上|shàng}{个|gè}{星期六|xīng qī liù}，{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{朋友|péng you}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}。{我们|wǒ men}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}、{牛奶|niú nǎi}{和|hé}{两|liǎng}{瓶|píng}{饮料|yǐn liào}，{一共|yí gòng}{一百二十八|yì bǎi èr shí bā}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ}。{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{付|fù}{钱|qián}，{但是|dàn shì}{手机|shǒu jī}{没|méi}{电|diàn}{了|le}，{关机|guān jī}{了|le}！{朋友|péng you}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{也|yě}{只|zhǐ}{有|yǒu}{百分之三|bǎi fēn zhī sān}{的|de}{电|diàn}，{开|kāi}{不|bu}{了|liǎo}{付|fù}{钱|qián}{的|de}{软件|ruǎn jiàn}。{我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{带|dài}{现金|xiàn jīn}，{后面|hòu miàn}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{在|zài}{等|děng}。{怎么|zěn me}{办|bàn}{呢|ne}？{还好|hái hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{的|de}{包|bāo}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{银行卡|yín háng kǎ}，{超市|chāo shì}{也|yě}{收|shōu}{银行卡|yín háng kǎ}。{我|wǒ}{刷卡|shuā kǎ}{付|fù}{了|le}{钱|qián}，{收银员|shōu yín yuán}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}：“{现在|xiàn zài}{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{刷卡|shuā kǎ}{了|le}！”{从|cóng}{那|nà}{天|tiān}{起|qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{出门|chū mén}{都|dōu}{带|dài}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{卡|kǎ}{和|hé}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{现金|xiàn jīn}。

{软件|ruǎn jiàn} is an app (software); {还好|hái hǎo} is "luckily, fortunately"; {收银员|shōu yín yuán} is a cashier
("collect-silver-person"). {开|kāi}{不|bu}{了|liǎo} is "can't open":
{了|liǎo} as a potential complement, like {吃不了|chī bu liǎo} in lesson 06. {怎么|zěn me}{办|bàn}{呢|ne}？ (What could we do?) uses this
lesson's {办|bàn}; it's lesson 28's phrase {怎么办|zěn me bàn}.

1. How much did the shopping cost?
2. Why couldn't the writer pay by phone, and what about the friend's phone?
3. How did they pay in the end?
4. What does the writer do now?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. ¥128.50 ({一百二十八|yì bǎi èr shí bā}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ}).
2. The writer's phone was out of battery and had switched off; the friend's had only 3% left, not
   enough to open the payment app.
3. With a bank card from the writer's bag: the supermarket takes bank cards.
4. Always takes a card and a little cash when going out ({从|cóng}{那|nà}{天|tiān}{起|qǐ}…).

"Last Saturday my friend and I went to the supermarket. We bought fruit, milk and two bottles of
soft drinks: 128.50 altogether. I wanted to pay with my phone, but the battery was dead and it
had switched off! My friend's phone only had 3% battery left, not enough to open the payment app.
Neither of us had brought any cash, and lots of people were waiting behind us. What could we do? Luckily there was a bank card in my bag, and
the supermarket takes bank cards. I paid by card, and the cashier laughed: "Hardly anyone pays
by card these days!" Since that day, I've always taken a card and a bit of cash with
me when I go out."
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{一共|yí gòng}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？
= How much is it altogether?
{十二|shí èr}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ}。
= Twelve fifty.
{可以|kě yǐ}{刷卡|shuā kǎ}{吗|ma}？
= Can I pay by card?
{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{办|bàn}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{银行卡|yín háng kǎ}。
= I'd like to get a bank card.
{我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{没|méi}{电|diàn}{了|le}。
= My phone's battery is dead.
{你|nǐ}{收到|shōu dào}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{短信|duǎn xìn}{了|le}{吗|ma}？
= Did you get my text?
{没|méi}{办法|bàn fǎ}。
= It can't be helped.
```

## Pronunciation

- {卡|kǎ}: *k* with a strong puff of air, a dipping tone. {信用卡|xìn yòng kǎ}: 4 + 4 + 3.
- {银行|yín háng}: two rising tones. {行|háng} here, not *xíng*.
- {毛|máo} rises; {猫|māo} (cat) is level: the same syllable, one tone apart.
- {角|jiǎo} sounds like {饺|jiǎo} (dumpling); {叫|jiào} (to be called) falls.
- {收|shōu} is level, {手|shǒu} (hand) dips, {瘦|shòu} (thin, lesson 04) falls.
- {办|bàn} falls; {半|bàn} (half) is the same syllable, and {搬|bān} (move house, lesson 02) is level.
- {一共|yí gòng}: {一|yí} rises before the fourth tone of {共|gòng}.
- {三分之一|sān fēn zhī yī}: 一 keeps its first tone in numbers; {之|zhī} is level too.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{二|èr}{块|kuài}~~ for ¥2: before {块|kuài} and {毛|máo}, say {两|liǎng}: {两|liǎng}{块|kuài}, {两|liǎng}{毛|máo}.
- Mixing spoken and written: {十二|shí èr}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ}{角|jiǎo} is odd. Say {十二|shí èr}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ}({毛|máo}); write {十二|shí èr}{元|yuán}{五|wǔ}{角|jiǎo} or ¥12.50.
- ~~{一|yí}{个|gè}{银行卡|yín háng kǎ}~~: cards take {张|zhāng}: {一|yì}{张|zhāng}{银行卡|yín háng kǎ}.
- English order with {用|yòng}: ~~{我|wǒ}{付|fù}{钱|qián}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}~~. The tool comes first: {我|wǒ}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{付|fù}{钱|qián}.
- Fractions upside down: ~~{一|yī}{分之|fēn zhī}{三|sān}~~ for 1/3. The whole comes first: {三分之一|sān fēn zhī yī}.
- {收|shōu} vs {收到|shōu dào}: {这里|zhè lǐ}{不|bù}{收|shōu}{现金|xiàn jīn} (cash isn't accepted here) is the action; {我|wǒ}{收到|shōu dào}{了|le} (I've got it) is the
  result.

## Key points

- Spoken {块|kuài} / {毛|máo}, written {元|yuán} / {角|jiǎo}; {分|fēn} for 0.01. ¥12.50 = {十二|shí èr}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ} = {十二|shí èr}{元|yuán}{五|wǔ}{角|jiǎo}. {一共|yí gòng}: altogether.
- {一|yì}{张|zhāng}{卡|kǎ} / {票|piào} / {桌子|zhuō zi}: {张|zhāng} for flat things. {银行卡|yín háng kǎ}, {信用卡|xìn yòng kǎ}, {号码|hào mǎ} (digits one by one, 1 = yāo).
- {办|bàn}{卡|kǎ} (get a card), {有|yǒu}{办法|bàn fǎ} / {没|méi}{办法|bàn fǎ}; {带|dài} (bring), {查|chá} (check), {收|shōu} / {收到|shōu dào}, {用|yòng} + tool + verb, {有用|yǒu yòng}.
- {没|méi}{电|diàn}{了|le}, {开机|kāi jī} / {关机|guān jī}; {从|cóng}…{起|qǐ}: from… on.
- Decimals with {点|diǎn} ({三|sān}{点|diǎn}{五|wǔ}); fractions bottom first ({三分之一|sān fēn zhī yī}); percentages {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}…; discounts {打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé}.

lessons.title: The four seasons and the weather: 刮着风, 变冷了, 没有那么冷
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 1 gave you {天气|tiān qì}, {冷|lěng}, {热|rè}, {下雨|xià yǔ} and {下雪|xià xuě}; HSK 2 added sunny and cloudy days. This
lesson, the last core lesson of the module, adds the seasons and the language of change: weather
that turns, suddenly or slowly, and one season compared with another. You'll learn:

- {春天|chūn tiān}, {夏天|xià tiān}, {秋天|qiū tiān}, {冬天|dōng tiān}; {季节|jì jié}, {季|jì} and {四季|sì jì};
- {风|fēng} and {刮|guā} ({刮风|guā fēng}: the wind blows), {冰|bīng} (ice), {凉快|liáng kuai} (pleasantly cool), {太阳|tài yang} and
  {月亮|yuè liang}, {伞|sǎn} (umbrella);
- weather going on now with durative {着|zhe}: {外面|wài miàn}{下|xià}{着|zhe}{雨|yǔ};
- change: {变|biàn}, {变化|biàn huà}, {突然|tū rán} ({天气|tiān qì}{突然|tū rán}{变|biàn}{冷|lěng}{了|le});
- {一般|yì bān}: usually; ordinary;
- comparing seasons: how much colder, not as cold, the same, even colder.

## The four seasons

| Season | Word | Typical weather in much of China |
|---|---|---|
| spring | {春天|chūn tiān} | warmer, windy in the north, often rainy in the south |
| summer | {夏天|xià tiān} | hot, and the rainy season in most places |
| autumn | {秋天|qiū tiān} | cool, dry and clear: many people's favourite |
| winter | {冬天|dōng tiān} | cold and dry in the north, with snow and ice; mild and damp in the south |

China is so large that its weather can't be summed up in one table: in winter it can be below
minus twenty in Harbin, in the far north-east, and above twenty in Hainan, in the far south. The
table gives the broad pattern.

{季节|jì jié} is "season"; {季|jì} is its short form, used inside words. {四季|sì jì} is the four seasons, and
{一年四季|yì nián sì jì} means "all year round":

{你|nǐ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{哪|nǎ}{个|gè}{季节|jì jié}？ — Which season do you like best?

{北京|Běi jīng}{四季|sì jì}{很|hěn}{分明|fēn míng}。 — Beijing has four distinct seasons. ({分明|fēn míng}: clearly marked)

{昆明|Kūn míng}{一年四季|yì nián sì jì}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{冷|lěng}{不|bú}{热|rè}。 — Kunming is neither cold nor hot all year round.

Kunming, in Yunnan in the south-west, is nicknamed {春城|chūn chéng}, "spring city", for its mild weather.
The {天|tiān} in the season words is light in many people's speech, but we write it with its first
tone, as the word lists do.

## Weather words

**{风|fēng}** is wind, and the verb for wind is **{刮|guā}**, "to blow": {刮风|guā fēng} (the wind is blowing, it's windy).
Like {下雨|xià yǔ}, it's verb + noun, so adjectives go on the noun:

{今天|jīn tiān}{刮|guā}{大|dà}{风|fēng}。 — It's very windy today. (A big wind is blowing.)

{外面|wài miàn}{风|fēng}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。 — It's very windy outside. (The wind is strong.)

**{冰|bīng}** is ice, the {冰|bīng} of {冰箱|bīng xiāng} (fridge, lesson 02) and {冰激凌|bīng jī líng}. In winter rivers and lakes
{结冰|jié bīng} (freeze over; {结|jié}: to form).

**{凉快|liáng kuai}** is "pleasantly cool", the welcome coolness after heat. {冷|lěng} is cold, and not pleasant:

{秋天|qiū tiān}{很|hěn}{凉快|liáng kuai}，{不|bù}{冷|lěng}{也|yě}{不|bú}{热|rè}。 — Autumn is nice and cool, neither cold nor hot.

{树|shù}{下|xià}{很|hěn}{凉快|liáng kuai}。 — It's cool under the trees. ({树|shù}: tree, lesson 15)

**{太阳|tài yang}** is the sun and **{月亮|yuè liang}** the moon, both with a light second syllable. The sun "comes
out":

{出|chū}{太阳|tài yang}{了|le}！ — The sun's come out!

{今天|jīn tiān}{太阳|tài yang}{很|hěn}{大|dà}，{别|bié}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}。 — The sun's strong today: don't forget to drink water.

{今天|jīn tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{的|de}{月亮|yuè liang}{真|zhēn}{好看|hǎo kàn}。 — The moon's really beautiful tonight.

**{伞|sǎn}** is an umbrella, counted with {把|bǎ} (something you hold by a handle): {一|yì}{把|bǎ}{伞|sǎn}. You {带|dài}{伞|sǎn}
(take an umbrella, lesson 09) and {打|dǎ}{伞|sǎn} (hold one up):

{天|tiān}{阴|yīn}{了|le}，{带|dài}{上|shàng}{伞|sǎn}{吧|ba}。 — It's clouded over: take an umbrella.

{下|xià}{这么|zhè me}{大|dà}{的|de}{雨|yǔ}，{打|dǎ}{伞|sǎn}{也|yě}{没|méi}{用|yòng}。 — In rain this heavy, an umbrella's no use.

A temperature is {度|dù} (degree): {今天|jīn tiān}{二十五|èr shí wǔ}{度|dù} (it's 25 degrees today), {零下|líng xià}{五|wǔ}{度|dù} (minus five).

## Weather going on now: {下|xià}{着|zhe}{雨|yǔ}

HSK 2 taught durative {着|zhe}, a state that lasts ({门|mén}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}, the door is open). With weather verbs it
describes the scene: it's raining, the wind is blowing, as a lasting background.

{外面|wài miàn}{下|xià}{着|zhe}{雨|yǔ}，{你|nǐ}{带|dài}{伞|sǎn}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ — It's raining outside. Have you got an umbrella?

{外面|wài miàn}{刮|guā}{着|zhe}{大|dà}{风|fēng}，{别|bié}{出去|chū qù}{了|le}。 — There's a strong wind blowing out there: don't go out.

{下|xià}{着|zhe}{雨|yǔ}{呢|ne}，{我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān}{再|zài}{去|qù}{吧|ba}。 — It's raining: let's go tomorrow instead.

Compare the three ways of saying "it's raining":

| Sentence | What it says |
|---|---|
| {下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}。 | It has started raining. (A change: HSK 1's {了|le}.) |
| {在|zài}{下雨|xià yǔ}。 | It's raining at the moment. (An action in progress.) |
| {外面|wài miàn}{下|xià}{着|zhe}{雨|yǔ}。 | It's raining outside. (The scene, a lasting state; often with a place, and often followed by another clause.) |

{着|zhe} splits {下雨|xià yǔ} and {刮风|guā fēng}: it goes straight after the verb, {下|xià}{着|zhe}{雨|yǔ}, {刮|guā}{着|zhe}{风|fēng}.

## Change: {变|biàn}, {变化|biàn huà}, {突然|tū rán}

**{变|biàn}** is "to change, to become different". With an adjective and {了|le} it says what something has
become:

{天气|tiān qì}{变|biàn}{了|le}。 — The weather has changed.

{天|tiān}{变|biàn}{冷|lěng}{了|le}。 — It's turned cold.

{十|shí}{年|nián}{没|méi}{见|jiàn}，{你|nǐ}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{也|yě}{没|méi}{变|biàn}！ — Ten years, and you haven't changed a bit!

**{变化|biàn huà}** is "change" as a noun, and also a verb, a little more formal than {变|biàn}:

{这里|zhè lǐ}{的|de}{天气|tiān qì}{变化|biàn huà}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。 — The weather here changes a lot. (Its changes are big.)

{这|zhè}{几|jǐ}{年|nián}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{旁边|páng biān}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{变化|biàn huà}。 — There have been lots of changes around my home these last few years.

{变|biàn} is "become different"; lesson 08's {换|huàn} is "swap one thing for another". The weather {变|biàn}; you {换|huàn}
your clothes.

**{突然|tū rán}** is "sudden, suddenly". As an adverb it goes before the verb (or at the start of the
sentence); as an adjective it takes {很|hěn}:

{天气|tiān qì}{突然|tū rán}{变|biàn}{冷|lěng}{了|le}。 — The weather suddenly turned cold.

{突然|tū rán}，{外面|wài miàn}{下|xià}{起|qǐ}{雨|yǔ}{来|lái}{了|le}。 — Suddenly it started to rain outside.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{太|tài}{突然|tū rán}{了|le}！ — That's so sudden!

{下|xià}{起|qǐ}{雨|yǔ}{来|lái} is HSK 2's {起来|qǐ lái} for "start to", with the object {雨|yǔ} in the middle.

## {一般|yì bān}: usually, and ordinary

**{一般|yì bān}** before a verb is "usually, generally". As an adjective it's "ordinary, average, so-so". Its {一|yì}
is fourth tone, because {般|bān} is first tone.

{我|wǒ}{一般|yì bān}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。 — I usually get up at seven.

{这里|zhè lǐ}{冬天|dōng tiān}{一般|yì bān}{不|bú}{下雪|xià xuě}。 — It doesn't usually snow here in winter.

{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{的|de}{菜|cài}{很|hěn}{一般|yì bān}。 — The food at this restaurant is nothing special.

{很|hěn}{一般|yì bān} is a polite way to say "not great". {一般|yì bān} differs from HSK 1's {一半|yí bàn} (half) by its tones.

## Comparing seasons

You compared people in lesson 04: {比|bǐ}, {没有|méi yǒu}…{那么|nà me}, {跟|gēn}…{一样|yí yàng}. Comparing seasons and days is
where you'll use them most, and where the size of the difference matters. That's **comparison of
degree**: saying not only *which* is colder, but by how much.

| How much | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| a little | A {比|bǐ} B + adj. + {一点儿|yì diǎnr} | {今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{冷|lěng}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。 Today is a little colder than yesterday. |
| a lot | A {比|bǐ} B + adj. + {多|duō}{了|le} / {得|de}{多|duō} | {北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{比|bǐ}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{冷|lěng}{多|duō}{了|le}。 Beijing's winter is much colder than Shanghai's. |
| exactly | A {比|bǐ} B + adj. + amount | {今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{热|rè}{五|wǔ}{度|dù}。 Today is five degrees hotter than yesterday. |
| even more | A {比|bǐ} B {更|gèng} + adj. | {夏天|xià tiān}{很|hěn}{热|rè}，{但是|dàn shì}{七月|qī yuè}{比|bǐ}{六月|liù yuè}{更|gèng}{热|rè}。 Summer is hot, but July is even hotter than June. |
| not as… | A {没有|méi yǒu} B ({那么|nà me}) + adj. | {春天|chūn tiān}{没有|méi yǒu}{夏天|xià tiān}{那么|nà me}{热|rè}。 Spring isn't as hot as summer. |
| the same | A {跟|gēn} B {一样|yí yàng} + adj. | {今天|jīn tiān}{跟|gēn}{昨天|zuó tiān}{一样|yí yàng}{冷|lěng}。 Today is as cold as yesterday. |
| the most | {最|zuì} + adj. | {秋天|qiū tiān}{最|zuì}{舒服|shū fu}。 Autumn is the most comfortable. |

Two rules hold for every row with {比|bǐ}:

- The degree words come **after** the adjective ({冷|lěng}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}, {冷|lěng}{多|duō}{了|le}, {热|rè}{五|wǔ}{度|dù}); only {更|gèng} (or {还|hái},
  "even") goes before it.
- {很|hěn}, {非常|fēi cháng} and {太|tài} never go in a {比|bǐ} sentence: not ~~{今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}~~.

{更|gèng} (even more) is lesson 12's word; it says the second thing goes beyond something already
true: summer is hot, and July is *even* hotter.

### More and more: {越来越|yuè lái yuè}

A season is a change that keeps going, and Chinese has a pattern for it: **[[越…越]]**. {越来越|yuè lái yuè} +
adjective is "more and more", a change over time:

{十一月|shí yī yuè}{了|le}，{天|tiān}{越来越|yuè lái yuè}{冷|lěng}{了|le}。 — It's November: it's getting colder and colder.

{雨|yǔ}{越|yuè}{下|xià}{越|yuè}{大|dà}。 — The rain is getting heavier and heavier. (The more it rains, the heavier it gets.)

Like {更|gèng}, it takes no {很|hěn}. Lesson 12 teaches it properly, with the character {越|yuè}.

### Meaning stories

- **春**: the top is a later shape that once showed plants sprouting; 日 (sun) is underneath. The sun
  and new growth: spring.
- **秋**: grain 禾 + fire 火. A common explanation is the harvest, when grain is ripe and the stalks are
  burned in the fields.
- **夏** was once a drawing of a person; "summer" is a meaning it took on later.
- **季**: grain 禾 over 子 (child). Its old meaning is "youngest"; "season" came later.
- **节** first meant a joint in a bamboo stem, which is why traditional 節 has bamboo ⺮ on top. From
  "joint, section" it came to mean a section of the year, and then a festival.
- **风** is 几 with ㄨ inside; traditional 風 has 虫 (an insect, a small creature) inside instead.
- **刮** is knife 刂 + 舌: "to scrape", and in the mainland also "to blow" for the wind. Taiwan writes
  the wind sense with its own character, 颳, which has 風 on the left.
- **凉**: ice 冫 + 京 (*jīng*, once the sound; it has drifted). Traditional 涼 has water 氵 instead.
- **阳**: 阝 (here a hill, on the left) + 日 (sun): the sunny side of a hill. Traditional 陽 has 昜
  (*yáng*) for the sound.
- **化** is two people, one upright 亻 and one upside down 匕: turning into something else.
- **突** is a hole 穴 with a dog 犬 inside: a dog shooting out of its hole, suddenly.
- **伞** is a drawing of an open umbrella with its handle; traditional 傘 has four little people 人
  under the cover.

### Stroke order

- **春**: three horizontals (the third longest), the left-falling and right-falling strokes across
  them, then 日.
- **冬**: 夂 (left-falling, the turning stroke, the long right-falling stroke), then the two dots.
- **风**: 几 first (left-falling, then the horizontal that turns down with a hook), then the two
  strokes inside, left-falling then dot.
- **变**: the top (dot, horizontal, two short verticals, then a short left-falling stroke on the left and a dot on
  the right), then 又.
- **伞**: 人 on top, then a dot and a short left-falling stroke, the horizontal, and the long vertical last.
