## Pronunciation

- {北|běi} *běi* dips; {被|bèi} *bèi* (lesson 13) falls, and {杯|bēi} *bēi* (in {杯子|bēi zi}) is level.
- {南|nán} *nán* rises, like {男|nán} *nán* (male): the same syllable.
- {西|xī} *xī* is level; {洗|xǐ} *xǐ* (to wash) dips.
- {东|dōng} *dōng* is level; {懂|dǒng} *dǒng* (to understand) dips, {动|dòng} *dòng* (to move) falls.
- {地方|dì fang} *dìfang*: the *fang* is light. In {方向|fāng xiàng} *fāngxiàng* both syllables are full.
- {附近|fù jìn} *fùjìn*: two falling tones in a row. Make the first one shorter, then fall again.
- {城市|chéng shì} *chéngshì*: *ch* and *sh* with the tongue curled back; {有名|yǒu míng} *yǒumíng*: a low dip, then a rise.
- {街|jiē} *jiē* and {接|jiē} *jiē* (to meet, lesson 20) sound the same.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{北|běi}{南|nán}{东|dōng}{西|xī}~~ in the "north, south, east, west" order: Chinese starts with {东|dōng}: {东|dōng}{南|nán}{西|xī}{北|běi}.
- ~~{他|tā}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}{什么|shén me}~~ for "he knows everything": the question word goes first, then {都|dōu}: {他|tā}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{哪儿|nǎr}{不|bú}{去|qù}~~: keep {也|yě} / {都|dōu} before the negative: {我|wǒ}{哪儿|nǎr}{也|yě}{不|bú}{去|qù} / {我|wǒ}{哪儿|nǎr}{都|dōu}{不|bú}{去|qù}.
- ~~{银行|yín háng}{在|zài}{中间|zhōng jiān}{书店|shū diàn}{和|hé}{超市|chāo shì}~~: the two places come first: {银行|yín háng}{在|zài}{书店|shū diàn}{和|hé}{超市|chāo shì}{中间|zhōng jiān}.
- ~~{他|tā}{是|shì}{很|hěn}{有名|yǒu míng}~~: {有名|yǒu míng} is an adjective: {他|tā}{很|hěn}{有名|yǒu míng}, or with a noun, {他|tā}{是|shì}{很|hěn}{有名|yǒu míng}{的|de}{医生|yī shēng}.
- {地点|dì diǎn} in conversation: ~~{这个|zhè ge}{地点|dì diǎn}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}~~. Say {这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}; {地点|dì diǎn} is for notices.
- {附近|fù jìn} for "close": ~~{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{离|lí}{学校|xué xiào}{很|hěn}{附近|fù jìn}~~. Use {近|jìn}: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{离|lí}{学校|xué xiào}{很|hěn}{近|jìn}; or {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{附近|fù jìn}.

## Key points

- {东|dōng}{南|nán}{西|xī}{北|běi} (east, south, west, north) + {边|biān} / {面|miàn}: {银行|yín háng}{在|zài}{超市|chāo shì}({的|de}){北边|běi bian}; {往|wǎng}{东|dōng}{走|zǒu}.
- {在|zài} A {和|hé} B {中间|zhōng jiān}: between A and B. Place + {附近|fù jìn} (+ {有|yǒu}…): nearby.
- {马路|mǎ lù} (road), {街|jiē} (street), {路口|lù kǒu} (crossing), {路边|lù biān} (roadside), all with {条|tiáo}.
- {地方|dì fang} (place) vs {地点|dì diǎn} (location on a notice); {地图|dì tú}, {方向|fāng xiàng}; {地|dì}: the ground ({坐|zuò}{在|zài}{地|dì}{上|shàng}).
- {城市|chéng shì} (a city) vs {市|shì} (in names: {北京市|Běi jīng shì}); {有名|yǒu míng} (famous), {环境|huán jìng} (surroundings).
- Question word + {都|dōu} / {也|yě} + verb: {哪儿|nǎr}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}, {什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}, {谁|shéi}{都|dōu}{认识|rèn shi}; negative {哪儿|nǎr}{也|yě}{不|bú}{去|qù}, {什么|shén me}{也|yě}{没|méi}{买|mǎi}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: North, south and the world: 越…越, 更
topics: Degree: 越…越, 更, 极了, 比较
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 11 gave you {东|dōng}, {南|nán}, {西|xī} and {北|běi} in the city. Now you'll put them together and look further
out: at the regions of China, other countries and the world. You'll learn:

- the in-between directions {东北|dōng běi}, {东南|dōng nán}, {西北|xī běi}, {西南|xī nán}, and why Chinese says "east-north";
- {北方|běi fāng} and {南方|nán fāng} (the north and the south of China), {东方|dōng fāng} and {西方|xī fāng} (the East and the West);
- {外地|wài dì} (somewhere other than here), {来自|lái zì} (to come from), {国家|guó jiā} (country) and {世界|shì jiè} (world);
- **{越|yuè}…{越|yuè}** and {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}: "the more…, the more…" and "more and more";
- {更|gèng} (even more), {极|jí}{了|le} (extremely) and {比较|bǐ jiào} (fairly);
- {以上|yǐ shàng}, {以下|yǐ xià} and {以外|yǐ wài} with numbers: {十八|shí bā}{岁|suì}{以上|yǐ shàng} (eighteen and over).

## {东北|dōng běi}, {西南|xī nán}: directions in between

The four in-between directions put **east or west first**, and north or south second. English
does the opposite:

| Chinese | Literally | English |
|---|---|---|
| {东北|dōng běi} | east-north | northeast |
| {东南|dōng nán} | east-south | southeast |
| {西北|xī běi} | west-north | northwest |
| {西南|xī nán} | west-south | southwest |

~~{北|běi}{东|dōng}~~ and ~~{南|nán}{西|xī}~~ aren't Chinese. Like the four main directions, they take -{边|biān} / -{面|miàn} for a side ({城市|chéng shì}{的|de}{东|dōng}{北边|běi bian})
and follow {往|wǎng} ({往|wǎng}{西北|xī běi}{走|zǒu}).

They are also the names of regions of China. {东北|dōng běi} is the Northeast, the provinces in the far
north-east of the country, known for long cold winters; {东北人|Dōng běi rén} are people from there, and {东北菜|Dōng běi cài}
its cooking. {西北|xī běi} and {西南|xī nán} are the Northwest and the Southwest.

{我|wǒ}{朋友|péng you}{是|shì}{东北人|Dōng běi rén}，{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{饺子|jiǎo zi}。 — My friend is from the Northeast and loves dumplings.

{这个|zhè ge}{城市|chéng shì}{的|de}{西|xī}{南边|nán bian}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{新|xīn}{小区|xiǎo qū}。 — There are lots of new housing estates in the southwest of the city.

## {北方|běi fāng} and {南方|nán fāng}, {东方|dōng fāng} and {西方|xī fāng}

-{方|fāng} (side, region) makes bigger, vaguer areas than -{边|biān}:

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {北方|běi fāng} | the north; in China, the North |
| {南方|nán fāng} | the south; in China, the South |
| {东方|dōng fāng} | the east; the East (East Asia) |
| {西方|xī fāng} | the west; the West (Europe and the Americas) |

In China, {北方|běi fāng} and {南方|nán fāng} are a familiar way of dividing the country. Geographers usually draw the
line along the Qinling mountains and the Huai River, a little north of the Yangtze: Beijing is in
the North, Shanghai in the South. People talk about differences in weather, food and speech:

{北方|běi fāng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{比较|bǐ jiào}{冷|lěng}，{南方|nán fāng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{比较|bǐ jiào}{短|duǎn}。 — Winters in the North are fairly cold; in the South they're shorter.

{北方人|běi fāng rén}{吃|chī}{面条儿|miàn tiáor}{和|hé}{饺子|jiǎo zi}{比较|bǐ jiào}{多|duō}，{南方人|nán fāng rén}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}{比较|bǐ jiào}{多|duō}。 — Northerners eat more noodles and dumplings; southerners eat more rice.

These are broad tendencies, not rules: plenty of northerners eat rice every day. One surprise for
visitors: homes in the North have central heating in winter ({暖气|nuǎn qì}), and many homes in the South
don't, so a southern winter can feel colder indoors.

{东方|dōng fāng} and {西方|xī fāng} often mean the cultures of East and West: {西方国家|xī fāng guó jiā} (Western countries), {东方|dōng fāng}{文化|wén huà}
({文化|wén huà}, culture: a lesson 23 word). As plain directions they're used for the sky: {太阳|tài yang}{在|zài}{东方|dōng fāng} (the
sun is in the east).

## {外地|wài dì}, {来自|lái zì}, {国家|guó jiā}, {世界|shì jiè}

{外地|wài dì} is "another place": anywhere other than the city you're in or where you're from.

{他|tā}{是|shì}{外地人|wài dì rén}，{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{工作|gōng zuò}。 — He's not from here: he works in Beijing.

{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{外地|wài dì}，{下|xià}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{回来|huí lái}。 — My mum is away (in another city); she's back next week.

{来自|lái zì} is "to come from" (a place of origin), the written or formal way to say where someone or
something is from. In conversation, {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{英国|Yīng guó}{人|rén} ({英国|Yīng guó}, the UK) is still the natural
sentence; {来自|lái zì} is for introductions in public, forms and news:

{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{大卫|Dà wèi}，{来自|lái zì}{英国|Yīng guó}。 — My name is David, and I'm from the UK.

{我们|wǒ men}{学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}{来自|lái zì}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{国家|guó jiā}。 — The students at our school come from many countries.

{来自|lái zì} takes its place straight after it: ~~{来自|lái zì}{从|cóng}{英国|Yīng guó}~~ repeats "from".

{国家|guó jiā} is "a country, a nation". {国|guó} alone (HSK 1) is mostly used in words ({中国|Zhōng guó}, {外国|wài guó}, {出国|chū guó}, {回|huí}{国|guó}); for
"a country" on its own, say {国家|guó jiā}:

{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{国家|guó jiā}？ — How many countries have you been to?

{世界|shì jiè} is "the world". {世界上|shì jiè shàng} is "in the world":

{世界上|shì jiè shàng}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{国家|guó jiā}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{看|kàn}。 — There are lots of countries in the world, and I'd like to see them.

## {中|zhōng} and {园|yuán}

{中|zhōng} (in, among, in the middle of) is the {中|zhōng} of {中间|zhōng jiān}, {中午|zhōng wǔ} and {中国|Zhōng guó}. As a word of its own it is mostly
written, after a noun or in {在|zài}…{中|zhōng}:

{在|zài}{这些|zhè xiē}{城市|chéng shì}{中|zhōng}，{我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 — Of all these cities, I like Shanghai best.

{园|yuán} is "a garden, a park", mostly in words: {公园|gōng yuán} (park) and {动物园|dòng wù yuán} (zoo) come in lesson 15, {花园|huā yuán}
(garden) too. On its own it appears in names and in {园里|yuán lǐ} (in the garden, in the park):

{园里|yuán lǐ}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}。 — There are lots of flowers in the garden.

## {越|yuè}…{越|yuè}: the more…, the more…

{越|yuè} is "to go beyond", and as an adverb it builds two patterns.

**{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè} + adjective**: more and more. The change goes on over time, so {了|le} often ends the sentence:

{天气|tiān qì}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{冷|lěng}{了|le}。 — It's getting colder and colder.

{你|nǐ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！ — Your Chinese keeps getting better!

{来|lái}{北京|Běi jīng}{旅游|lǚ yóu}{的|de}{外国|wài guó}{人|rén}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}。 — More and more foreigners come to Beijing as tourists.

**A {越|yuè} + verb, {越|yuè} + adjective / verb**: the more you do A, the more B:

{雨|yǔ}{越|yuè}{下|xià}{越|yuè}{大|dà}。 — The more it rains, the heavier it gets. (The rain is getting heavier.)

{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{我|wǒ}{越|yuè}{看|kàn}{越|yuè}{喜欢|xǐ huan}。 — The more I read this book, the more I like it.

{他|tā}{越|yuè}{说|shuō}{越|yuè}{快|kuài}，{我|wǒ}{越|yuè}{听|tīng}{越|yuè}{不|bù}{懂|dǒng}。 — The faster he talks, the less I understand.

{越|yuè}{快|kuài}{越|yuè}{好|hǎo}。 — The sooner the better.

Each {越|yuè} is followed by a verb or adjective, never by a degree word: ~~{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}~~, ~~{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{非常|fēi cháng}{好|hǎo}~~.
The two halves can have different subjects: {东西|dōng xi}{越|yuè}{便宜|pián yi}，{买|mǎi}{的|de}{人|rén}{越|yuè}{多|duō} (the cheaper things are, the more
people buy).

## {更|gèng}, {极|jí}{了|le} and {比较|bǐ jiào}: how much?

Three ways to say how strong a quality is:

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {更|gèng} + adjective | even more (than another) | {东北|dōng běi}{更|gèng}{冷|lěng}。 The Northeast is even colder. |
| adjective + {极|jí}{了|le} | extremely (spoken) | {好|hǎo}{极|jí}{了|le}！ Excellent! |
| {比较|bǐ jiào} + adjective | fairly, rather, relatively | {这儿|zhèr}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}{比较|bǐ jiào}{便宜|pián yi}。 Things here are fairly cheap. |

**{更|gèng}** compares, like {比|bǐ}, but it adds "even": the other thing already has the quality.

{北京|Běi jīng}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{东北|dōng běi}{更|gèng}{冷|lěng}。 — Beijing is cold, and the Northeast is even colder.

{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{北方|běi fāng}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{更|gèng}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{南方|nán fāng}。 — I like the North, but I like the South even more.

In a {比|bǐ} sentence, {更|gèng} is fine where {很|hěn} isn't: {今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{更|gèng}{冷|lěng} (today is even colder than yesterday;
~~{今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}~~ is wrong). Compare {最|zuì} (the most): {我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{南方|nán fāng} (I like the South best of all).

**{极|jí}{了|le}** goes after an adjective (or a verb of feeling) and makes it extreme. It's spoken and
lively, and nothing goes before the adjective:

{这儿|zhèr}{的|de}{饺子|jiǎo zi}{好吃|hǎo chī}{极|jí}{了|le}！ — The dumplings here are absolutely delicious!

{那|nà}{天|tiān}{冷|lěng}{极|jí}{了|le}。 — That day it was freezing.

~~{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}{极|jí}{了|le}~~ says "very" twice. You'll meet more ways of making a description stronger in lesson 22.

**{比较|bǐ jiào}** before an adjective is "fairly, rather": milder than {很|hěn}, and often a polite way of saying
something less than perfect:

{这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{比较|bǐ jiào}{安静|ān jìng}。 — This place is fairly quiet.

{我|wǒ}{比较|bǐ jiào}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}。 — I prefer rice.

{比较|bǐ jiào} is also a verb, "to compare": {我们|wǒ men}{比较|bǐ jiào}{一下|yí xià}{这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{城市|chéng shì} (let's compare these two cities).

## {以上|yǐ shàng}, {以下|yǐ xià}, {以外|yǐ wài}: above, below, beyond

After a number, {以上|yǐ shàng} is "and above, or more" and {以下|yǐ xià} "and below, or less":

{十八|shí bā}{岁|suì}{以上|yǐ shàng} — eighteen and over

{六|liù}{岁|suì}{以下|yǐ xià}{的|de}{孩子|hái zi}{不要|bú yào}{门票|mén piào}。 — Children aged six and under don't need a ticket.

{这个|zhè ge}{城市|chéng shì}{的|de}{人口|rén kǒu}{在|zài}{一千万|yì qiān wàn}{以上|yǐ shàng}。 — This city has more than ten million people ({人口|rén kǒu}: population).

In everyday rules, signs and the law, {以上|yǐ shàng} and {以下|yǐ xià} normally include the number itself: {十八|shí bā}{岁|suì}{以上|yǐ shàng}
covers eighteen-year-olds. When it matters, check the small print.

{以外|yǐ wài} is "outside, beyond" a place or a limit:

{北京|Běi jīng}{以外|yǐ wài}{的|de}{城市|chéng shì} — the cities outside Beijing

{工作|gōng zuò}{以外|yǐ wài}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān} — time outside work

({除了|chú le}…{以外|yǐ wài}, "apart from…", is lesson 27's.)

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 世 | generation; world | shì | 一 | 5 | {世界|shì jiè} |
| 界 | boundary | jiè | 田 | 9 | {世界|shì jiè} |
| 园 (traditional 園) | garden; park | yuán | 囗 | 7 | {园|yuán}, and later {公园|gōng yuán}, {花园|huā yuán}, {动物园|dòng wù yuán} (15) |
| 越 | cross over; the more | yuè | 走 | 12 | {越|yuè}, {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè} |
| 更 | even more | gèng (and others) | 曰 | 7 | {更|gèng} |
| 极 (traditional 極) | extreme | jí | 木 | 7 | {极|jí}{了|le} |
| 较 (traditional 較) | compare | jiào | 车 | 10 | {比较|bǐ jiào} |

Four of these have a clear phonetic component, three of them characters you already know:

- {界|jiè}: 田 (field) on top for the meaning, a boundary between fields; below it {介|jiè}, the {介|jiè} of
  {介绍|jiè shào} (HSK 2), which gives the sound exactly.
- {园|yuán} ({園|yuán}): 囗 (an enclosure: a garden has a wall) with {元|yuán} (yuan, HSK 1) inside for the
  sound. The traditional form has 袁 inside instead, also read *yuán*: the same part as in
  traditional 遠 ({远|yuǎn}, far).
- {较|jiào} ({較|jiào}): 车 (vehicle) and {交|jiāo} *jiāo*, the {交|jiāo} of {公交车|gōng jiāo chē}. {交|jiāo} is a phonetic component in a
  family of characters: {校|xiào} *xiào* ({学校|xué xiào}), {饺|jiǎo} *jiǎo* ({饺子|jiǎo zi}, lesson 07), {较|jiào} *jiào* and 郊 jiāo (suburbs,
  not a course word). The sounds have drifted apart over the centuries, but all four still rhyme.
- {极|jí} ({極|jí}): 木 (tree, wood) and 及 jí (to reach; not a course character), which gives the sound.
  The traditional form keeps 木 with a different sound part, 亟, also read *jí*.

And the other three:

- {世|shì}: three {十|shí} (ten) joined at the bottom, the usual explanation goes: thirty years, a generation.
  From "generation" it came to mean "the age, the world".
- {越|yuè}: 走 (to walk, as in {走|zǒu}, {起|qǐ} and {超|chāo}) for the meaning, "to step over", and 戉 yuè (an old word
  for an axe) on the right for the sound.
- {更|gèng}: has another reading, *gēng*, in a few words outside this course. Its radical in our tables
  is 曰, as in the old Kangxi dictionary; some modern dictionaries file it under 一.

A family worth knowing: {元|yuán} also gives the sound in {远|yuǎn} and {园|yuán}, and once did in {完|wán}
(HSK 2), which has drifted further away.

### Stroke order

- **{越|yuè}**: {走|zǒu} first, all seven strokes, its long last stroke sweeping under the right side; then
  戉: the horizontal, a short vertical that flicks up, the long slanting hook, the
  left-falling stroke and the dot.
- **{更|gèng}**: the top horizontal, then the box (vertical, the turning horizontal, the middle
  horizontal and the short one inside), then the long left-falling stroke through the box and
  the right-falling stroke last.
- **{世|shì}**: the long horizontal, then two verticals, a short horizontal between them, and last the
  vertical on the left that turns along the bottom.
- **{较|jiào}**: 车 on the left, as in {辆|liàng} (lesson 13): horizontal, the bent stroke, the vertical, and the
  bottom stroke rises (it's written after the vertical). Then {交|jiāo}.
- **{极|jí}**: 木, then 及 in three strokes: left-falling, the stroke that turns twice, right-falling.

```trace
世界园越更极较
```

Write it: {更|gèng} is on the handwriting list. Write it three times from memory: seven strokes, and
the long left-falling stroke goes through the box.
=}

## Dialogue: north or south?

{宋佳|Sòng Jiā} (宋佳, a classmate whose family lives in Shanghai) and {大卫|Dà wèi} (大卫) are chatting after
class in Beijing.

```dialogue
# North or south?
大卫: {宋佳|Sòng Jiā}，{你|nǐ}{是|shì}{北京|Běi jīng}{人|rén}{吗|ma}？
= Song Jia, are you from Beijing?
宋佳: {不|bú}{是|shì}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{外地人|wài dì rén}，{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。{上海|Shàng hǎi}{在|zài}{南方|nán fāng}。
= No, I'm not from here: my family's in Shanghai. Shanghai is in the South.
大卫: {北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{比|bǐ}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{冷|lěng}{吗|ma}？
= Are winters in Beijing colder than in Shanghai?
宋佳: {冷|lěng}{多|duō}{了|le}！{外面|wài miàn}{冷|lěng}{极|jí}{了|le}，{但是|dàn shì}{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{暖气|nuǎn qì}，{比|bǐ}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{更|gèng}{舒服|shū fu}。
= Much colder! It's freezing outside, but rooms in Beijing have heating, so they're even more
  comfortable than rooms in Shanghai.
大卫: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{英国|Yīng guó}{的|de}{北边|běi bian}，{冬天|dōng tiān}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}。{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{比较|bǐ jiào}{短|duǎn}，{太阳|tài yang}{也|yě}{比较|bǐ jiào}{多|duō}。
= My home is in the north of the UK, and winters are cold there too. I think Beijing's winters
  are fairly short, and there's quite a lot of sun.
宋佳: {你|nǐ}{来|lái}{北京|Běi jīng}{多长时间|duō cháng shí jiān}{了|le}？
= How long have you been in Beijing?
大卫: {两|liǎng}{年|nián}{了|le}。{我|wǒ}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{这个|zhè ge}{城市|chéng shì}{了|le}。{北方|běi fāng}{的|de}{饺子|jiǎo zi}，{我|wǒ}{越|yuè}{吃|chī}{越|yuè}{喜欢|xǐ huan}！
= Two years. I like this city more and more. And the more northern dumplings I eat, the more I like them!
宋佳: {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{是|shì}。{我|wǒ}{来|lái}{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{不|bú}{太|tài}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{面条儿|miàn tiáor}，{现在|xiàn zài}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{吃|chī}。
= Me too. When I came to Beijing I didn't much like noodles; now I eat them every day.
大卫: {世界上|shì jiè shàng}{好吃|hǎo chī}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}{太|tài}{多|duō}{了|le}！
= There's so much good food in the world!
```

{冷|lěng}{多|duō}{了|le} (much colder) is lesson 04's {比|bǐ} + adjective + {多|duō}{了|le}, here without {比|bǐ} because the comparison
is clear. {暖气|nuǎn qì} is central heating. {多长时间|duō cháng shí jiān} (how long) asks about a length of time.

## Reading: a southerner in the North

> {赵军|Zhào Jūn}{是|shì}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{人|rén}。{三年前|sān nián qián}，{他|tā}{来|lái}{北京|Běi jīng}{工作|gōng zuò}。{北京|Běi jīng}{在|zài}{北方|běi fāng}，{冬天|dōng tiān}{比|bǐ}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{冷|lěng}{多|duō}{了|le}，{外面|wài miàn}{经常|jīng cháng}{刮|guā}{大|dà}{风|fēng}。{第|dì}{一|yī}{年|nián}{冬天|dōng tiān}，{赵军|Zhào Jūn}{觉得|jué de}{冷|lěng}{极|jí}{了|le}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{下|xià}{了|le}{班|bān}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{出门|chū mén}。{北方人|běi fāng rén}{吃|chī}{面条儿|miàn tiáor}、{饺子|jiǎo zi}{比较|bǐ jiào}{多|duō}，{他|tā}{也|yě}{不|bú}{太|tài}{喜欢|xǐ huan}。{但是|dàn shì}{公司|gōng sī}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}{都|dōu}{对|duì}{他|tā}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{星期天|xīng qī tiān}{经常|jīng cháng}{请|qǐng}{他|tā}{去|qù}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{吃|chī}{饺子|jiǎo zi}。{他|tā}{越|yuè}{吃|chī}{越|yuè}{喜欢|xǐ huan}，{还|hái}{学会|xué huì}{了|le}{自己|zì jǐ}{做|zuò}{饺子|jiǎo zi}。{现在|xiàn zài}{赵军|Zhào Jūn}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{住|zhù}{了|le}{三|sān}{年|nián}{了|le}，{他|tā}{觉得|jué de}{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{没有|méi yǒu}{那么|nà me}{冷|lěng}{了|le}。{他|tā}{说|shuō}：“{我|wǒ}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{北方|běi fāng}{了|le}。{上海|Shàng hǎi}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{家|jiā}，{北京|Běi jīng}{也|yě}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{家|jiā}。”

{三年前|sān nián qián} is "three years ago". {下|xià}{了|le}{班|bān} splits the separable verb {下班|xià bān}: "after work". {学会|xué huì} is "to
learn (how to do something)", with {会|huì} as a result: he learned until he could. {没有|méi yǒu}{那么|nà me}{冷|lěng} (not so cold)
is lesson 04's {没有|méi yǒu} comparison.

1. Why did Zhao Jun come to Beijing?
2. How did he feel in his first winter?
3. What changed his mind about northern food?
4. How does he feel now?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. For work ({他|tā}{来|lái}{北京|Běi jīng}{工作|gōng zuò}).
2. He felt it was freezing ({冷|lěng}{极|jí}{了|le}) and didn't want to go out after work.
3. His friends at work often invited him home for dumplings on Sundays; the more he ate, the more
   he liked them ({他|tā}{越|yuè}{吃|chī}{越|yuè}{喜欢|xǐ huan}), and he learned to make them himself.
4. He likes the North more and more ({我|wǒ}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{北方|běi fāng}{了|le}): Beijing is his home too.

"Zhao Jun is from Shanghai. Three years ago he came to Beijing to work. Beijing is in the North,
and its winters are much colder than Shanghai's, with strong winds outside. In his first winter
Zhao Jun found it freezing and didn't want to go out after work. Northerners eat a lot of noodles
and dumplings, and he didn't much like them. But his friends at the company were all very good to
him and often invited him home on Sundays to eat dumplings. The more he ate, the more he liked them,
and he even learned to make them himself. Now Zhao Jun has lived in Beijing for three years, and
he finds the winters aren't so cold. He says: 'I like the North more and more. Shanghai is my
home, and Beijing is my home too.'"
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{我|wǒ}{来自|lái zì}{英国|Yīng guó}。
= I'm from the UK.
{他|tā}{是|shì}{外地人|wài dì rén}，{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{工作|gōng zuò}。
= He's not from here; he works in Beijing.
{天气|tiān qì}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{冷|lěng}{了|le}。
= It's getting colder and colder.
{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{我|wǒ}{越|yuè}{看|kàn}{越|yuè}{喜欢|xǐ huan}。
= The more I read this book, the more I like it.
{北京|Běi jīng}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{东北|dōng běi}{更|gèng}{冷|lěng}。
= Beijing is cold, and the Northeast is even colder.
{好|hǎo}{极|jí}{了|le}！
= Excellent!
{十八|shí bā}{岁|suì}{以上|yǐ shàng}{的|de}{人|rén}{可以|kě yǐ}{参加|cān jiā}。
= People aged eighteen and over can take part.
```

({参加|cān jiā}, to take part, is a lesson 21 word.)

## Pronunciation

- {越|yuè} *yuè* and {月|yuè} *yuè* (month) sound the same: the *yu* is ü, with rounded lips.
- {更|gèng} *gèng* falls. Keep the *e* as in English "hung", not "gang".
- {极|jí} *jí* rises; so do {急|jí} *jí* (urgent, lesson 13) and the *jí* of {年级|nián jí} (lesson 16). {几|jǐ} *jǐ* dips.
- {比较|bǐ jiào} *bǐjiào*: the second syllable falls, *jiào*; don't say *jiǎo* (as in {饺子|jiǎo zi}).
- {世界|shì jiè} *shìjiè*: two falling tones; the first shorter, as in {附近|fù jìn}.
- {西南|xī nán} *xīnán* is *xī-nán*: two syllables, level then rising.
- {以上|yǐ shàng}, {以下|yǐ xià} and {以外|yǐ wài} all start with a low {以|yǐ} *yǐ*; before {上|shàng}, {下|xià} and {外|wài} (all falling) it stays low.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{北|běi}{东|dōng}~~, ~~{南|nán}{西|xī}~~: east or west comes first: {东北|dōng běi}, {西南|xī nán}.
- ~~{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}~~: nothing between {越|yuè} and the adjective: {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{冷|lěng}.
- ~~{他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}~~: in a {比|bǐ} sentence use {更|gèng} ({他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{更|gèng}{高|gāo}) or nothing ({他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{高|gāo}).
- ~~{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}{极|jí}{了|le}~~: {极|jí}{了|le} already says "extremely": {好|hǎo}{极|jí}{了|le}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{来自|lái zì}{从|cóng}{英国|Yīng guó}~~: {来自|lái zì} already contains "from": {我|wǒ}{来自|lái zì}{英国|Yīng guó}.
- ~~{一|yí}{个|gè}{国|guó}~~ for "a country": say {一|yí}{个|gè}{国家|guó jiā}.
- Using {比较|bǐ jiào} for "to compare" without an object: {比较|bǐ jiào} + two things, or {比较|bǐ jiào}{一下|yí xià}.

## Key points

- {东北|dōng běi}, {东南|dōng nán}, {西北|xī běi}, {西南|xī nán}: east or west first. Also regions of China ({东北人|Dōng běi rén}, {东北菜|Dōng běi cài}).
- {北方|běi fāng} / {南方|nán fāng} (the North / the South of China), {东方|dōng fāng} / {西方|xī fāng} (the East / the West).
- {外地|wài dì} (another place), {来自|lái zì} + place (written: to come from), {国家|guó jiā} (country), {世界|shì jiè} (world), {世界上|shì jiè shàng}.
- {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè} + adjective (more and more); A {越|yuè} + verb {越|yuè} + adjective (the more…, the more…).
- {更|gèng} + adjective (even more; fine in {比|bǐ} sentences); adjective + {极|jí}{了|le} (extremely); {比较|bǐ jiào} + adjective (fairly).
- Number + {以上|yǐ shàng} / {以下|yǐ xià} (and over / and under); place + {以外|yǐ wài} (outside).
- {中|zhōng}: in, among ({在|zài}…{中|zhōng}); {园|yuán}: garden ({公园|gōng yuán}, {花园|huā yuán}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Traffic: the 被 sentence
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

In lesson 03 the {把|bǎ} sentence put the thing you act on before the verb: {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}. This lesson
turns the same event round, so that the thing comes first and something happens **to** it:

- the **[[passive]]** with {被|bèi} ({我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}: my bike has been ridden off by someone);
- **existential {着|zhe} sentences**, which say what is standing, sitting or lying somewhere ({路口|lù kǒu}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén});
- the words of the road: {汽车|qì chē}, {自行车|zì xíng chē}, {骑|qí} and {辆|liàng}, {司机|sī jī}, {红绿灯|hóng lǜ dēng}, {安全|ān quán}, {船|chuán} and {高铁|gāo tiě}, and {米|mǐ} (metres);
- being late: {迟到|chí dào} (people) and {晚点|wǎn diǎn} (trains and planes); hurrying: {马上|mǎ shàng}, {急|jí}, {着急|zháo jí};
- {站|zhàn} as a verb: to stand.

## Vehicles: {骑|qí} or {坐|zuò}, and {辆|liàng}

You know {车|chē} (vehicle), {开车|kāi chē} (to drive) and {坐|zuò} (to sit; to take a vehicle) from HSK 1. Now:

| Word | Meaning | Goes with |
|---|---|---|
| {汽车|qì chē} | a motor vehicle, a car | {开|kāi} (drive), {坐|zuò} (ride in) |
| {自行车|zì xíng chē} | a bicycle | {骑|qí} (ride) |
| {船|chuán} | a boat, a ship | {坐|zuò} |
| {高铁|gāo tiě} | high-speed rail, a high-speed train | {坐|zuò} |
| {司机|sī jī} | a driver | |

{汽车|qì chē} is the full word; in speech people usually just say {车|chē}. {自行车|zì xíng chē} is literally "self-moving
vehicle", and in speech {骑车|qí chē} is "to ride a bike". {高铁|gāo tiě} is short for the high-speed railway, and
also the trains themselves: {坐|zuò}{高铁|gāo tiě}{去|qù}{上海|Shàng hǎi} (take the high-speed train to Shanghai).

**{骑|qí} or {坐|zuò}?** {骑|qí} is for things you sit astride, legs either side: a bicycle, a horse ({马|mǎ}, lesson 15).
{坐|zuò} is for things you sit inside: a car, a bus, a train, a boat, a plane.

{我|wǒ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{骑|qí}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{上班|shàng bān}。 — I cycle to work every day.

{我们|wǒ men}{坐|zuò}{船|chuán}{去|qù}{吧|ba}！ — Let's go by boat!

~~{骑|qí}{汽车|qì chē}~~ is wrong; you {开|kāi} a car (drive) or {坐|zuò} one (ride in it). ~~{坐|zuò}{自行车|zì xíng chē}~~ only works if
you're the passenger on the back.

**{辆|liàng}** is the measure word for vehicles with wheels: {一|yí}{辆|liàng}{汽车|qì chē}, {两|liǎng}{辆|liàng}{自行车|zì xíng chē}, {这|zhè}{辆|liàng}{车|chē}. Boats usually
take {条|tiáo} in everyday speech: {一|yì}{条|tiáo}{船|chuán}.

{门口|mén kǒu}{有|yǒu}{三|sān}{辆|liàng}{自行车|zì xíng chē}。 — There are three bikes at the door.

## Red lights and safety: {红绿灯|hóng lǜ dēng}, {安全|ān quán}, {米|mǐ}

{红绿灯|hóng lǜ dēng} is "traffic lights": literally "red-green lights". {红灯|hóng dēng} is a red light and {绿灯|lǜ dēng} a green one.
Children learn a rhyme: {红灯|hóng dēng}{停|tíng}，{绿灯|lǜ dēng}{行|xíng} ({停|tíng}, to stop; {行|xíng}, to go): "stop at red, go at
green".

{过|guò}{马路|mǎ lù}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{要|yào}{看|kàn}{红绿灯|hóng lǜ dēng}。 — When you cross the road, watch the lights.

{安全|ān quán} is "safe" and "safety". Two common phrases on signs and in warnings: {注意|zhù yì}{安全|ān quán} (be careful,
literally "pay attention to safety") and {安全第一|ān quán dì yī} (safety first).

{晚上|wǎn shang}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{骑车|qí chē}{不|bù}{安全|ān quán}。 — Cycling alone at night isn't safe.

{骑车|qí chē}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{要|yào}{注意|zhù yì}{安全|ān quán}！ — Be careful when you're cycling!

{米|mǐ} (the {米|mǐ} of {米饭|mǐ fàn}) is also the metre. The distance goes after the verb of moving:

{往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}{一百|yì bǎi}{米|mǐ}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}。 — Go a hundred metres straight on and you're there.

Heights use {米|mǐ} too, read the short way (lesson 04): 1.75{米|mǐ} is {一|yì}{米|mǐ}{七五|qī wǔ}.

## Late and in a hurry: {迟到|chí dào}, {晚点|wǎn diǎn}, {马上|mǎ shàng}, {急|jí}, {着急|zháo jí}

{迟到|chí dào} is "to arrive late", for people: for school, work, a meeting. How late goes after it:

{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{上班|shàng bān}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。 — I was late for work today.

{他|tā}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}{二十|èr shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。 — He was twenty minutes late.

{明天|míng tiān}{别|bié}{迟到|chí dào}！ — Don't be late tomorrow!

{晚点|wǎn diǎn} is "to run late", for trains, buses and planes:

{飞机|fēi jī}{晚点|wǎn diǎn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 — The plane was an hour late.

~~{我|wǒ}{晚点|wǎn diǎn}{了|le}~~ is wrong for a person. (In speech, {晚点儿|wǎn diǎnr} can also mean "a bit later": {我们|wǒ men}{晚点儿|wǎn diǎnr}{再|zài}{说|shuō}, let's
talk later.)

{马上|mǎ shàng} is "at once, right away", often with {就|jiù}: {我|wǒ}{马上|mǎ shàng}{来|lái}！ (I'm coming right now!) {马上|mǎ shàng}{就|jiù}{到|dào} (almost
there).

{急|jí} is "urgent" or "impatient": {急事|jí shì} is urgent business, {别|bié}{急|jí} is "no rush, take your time". {着急|zháo jí} is
"worried, anxious, in a hurry", the feeling inside you:

{别|bié}{着急|zháo jí}，{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}。 — Don't worry, there's still time.

{她|tā}{很|hěn}{着急|zháo jí}，{因为|yīn wèi}{火车|huǒ chē}{马上|mǎ shàng}{就|jiù}{要|yào}{开|kāi}{了|le}。 — She was anxious, because the train was about to leave.

Watch the reading: in {着急|zháo jí} the {着|zháo} is *zháo*, not the light *zhe* of {穿|chuān}{着|zhe} (HSK 2). Same character,
different word.

## {站|zhàn}: to stand

HSK 2's {站|zhàn} was a stop or station ({车站|chē zhàn}). As a verb it means "to stand":

{别|bié}{站|zhàn}{在|zài}{马路|mǎ lù}{中间|zhōng jiān}！ — Don't stand in the middle of the road!

{他|tā}{站|zhàn}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le}。 — He stood up. ({起来|qǐ lái}, lesson 12 of HSK 2: upwards.)

{在|zài}{公交车|gōng jiāo chē}{上|shàng}，{我|wǒ}{经常|jīng cháng}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}。 — On the bus I usually stand.

## The passive: {被|bèi}

A {被|bèi} sentence starts with the thing or person something happens to. {被|bèi} introduces who did it,
and the verb comes last:

**receiver + {被|bèi} + (doer) + verb + something more**

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 — My bike's been ridden off by someone. (Someone's taken my bike.)

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{被|bèi}{弟弟|dì di}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 — My phone's been taken by my little brother.

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{伞|sǎn}{被|bèi}{风|fēng}{刮|guā}{走|zǒu}{了|le}！ — My umbrella's been blown away by the wind!

How it works:

- **The doer is optional.** When you don't know who did it, or it doesn't matter, leave it out, or
  use {人|rén} (someone): {我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le} / {我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}.
- **The verb doesn't stand alone.** Like the {把|bǎ} sentence, it needs something after it: {了|le}, a result
  ({骑|qí}{走|zǒu}, {吃|chī}{完|wán}, {拿|ná}{走|zǒu}) or a place ({放|fàng}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}). ~~{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{骑|qí}~~ is incomplete.
- **Negatives and time words go before {被|bèi}**: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{没|méi}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu} (my bike wasn't taken), {昨天|zuó tiān}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{伞|sǎn}{被|bèi}{风|fēng}
  {刮|guā}{走|zǒu}{了|le}.
- **It's mostly for things you didn't want**: losing, breaking, getting caught in the rain. For
  ordinary events, an active sentence is more natural: say {老师|lǎo shī}{教|jiāo}{我们|wǒ men}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}, not ~~{我们|wǒ men}{被|bèi}{老师|lǎo shī}{教|jiāo}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}~~.
  (In news and writing {被|bèi} is used more widely.)

In everyday speech you'll also hear {让|ràng} or {叫|jiào} in place of {被|bèi}, with the doer then required: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{让|ràng}
{人|rén}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}.

### {被|bèi} and {把|bǎ}: one event, two ways

The {把|bǎ} sentence of lesson 03 starts with the doer; the {被|bèi} sentence starts with the receiver. The
rest stays the same:

| {把|bǎ} (doer first) | {被|bèi} (receiver first) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {弟弟|dì di}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{吃|chī}{了|le}。 | {我|wǒ}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{被|bèi}{弟弟|dì di}{吃|chī}{了|le}。 | My little brother ate my cake. |
| {风|fēng}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{伞|sǎn}{刮|guā}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 | {我|wǒ}{的|de}{伞|sǎn}{被|bèi}{风|fēng}{刮|guā}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 | The wind blew my umbrella away. |
| {他|tā}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 | {我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{他|tā}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 | He rode off on my bike. |

Choose by what you're talking about: if the story is about the cake, start with the cake.

## Existential {着|zhe} sentences: what is where

To describe a scene, Chinese puts the place first, then a verb with {着|zhe}, and then what is there:

**place + verb + {着|zhe} + (number + measure word) + thing or person**

{路口|lù kǒu}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}。 — There's someone standing at the crossing.

{门口|mén kǒu}{放|fàng}{着|zhe}{两|liǎng}{辆|liàng}{自行车|zì xíng chē}。 — There are two bikes standing by the door.

{车|chē}{上|shàng}{坐|zuò}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}。 — There are lots of people sitting on the bus.

{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}{放|fàng}{着|zhe}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}。 — There's a book lying on the table.

The {着|zhe} is HSK 2's durative {着|zhe}: a state that lasts ({门|mén}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}, the door is open). Here it tells you *how*
the thing is there: standing, sitting, lying. {有|yǒu} would only say that it's there: {路口|lù kǒu}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}.

Three points:

- The place comes first, usually without {在|zài} in front of it: {路口|lù kǒu}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}, not {在|zài}{路口|lù kǒu}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}.
- The thing or person is new to the listener, so it usually has a number and a measure word
  ({一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}, {两|liǎng}{辆|liàng}{自行车|zì xíng chē}). A known person goes the other way round: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}{站|zhàn}{在|zài}{路口|lù kǒu} (Wang Fang is standing
  at the crossing).
- Common verbs: {站|zhàn}, {坐|zuò}, {放|fàng}, {住|zhù} ({楼|lóu}{上|shàng}{住|zhù}{着|zhe}{一|yì}{家人|jiā rén}, a family lives upstairs) and {写|xiě} ({门|mén}{上|shàng}{写|xiě}{着|zhe}“{安全|ān quán}
  {出口|chū kǒu}”, the door says "Emergency exit").

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 汽 | steam, vapour | qì | 氵 | 7 | {汽车|qì chē} |
| 骑 (traditional 騎) | ride | qí | 马 | 11 | {骑|qí} |
| 辆 (traditional 輛) | (measure for vehicles) | liàng | 车 | 11 | {辆|liàng} |
| 全 | whole, complete | quán | 入 | 6 | {安全|ān quán} |
| 船 | boat | chuán | 舟 | 11 | {船|chuán} |
| 迟 (traditional 遲) | late, slow | chí | 辶 | 7 | {迟到|chí dào} |
| 急 | urgent | jí | 心 | 9 | {急|jí}, {着急|zháo jí} |
| 被 | (passive); quilt | bèi | 衤 | 10 | {被|bèi} |

Five of the eight have a sound part you can hear:

- {汽|qì}: 氵 (water) and {气|qì} (air, gas, as in {天气|tiān qì}): water turned into gas, steam. The sound is exact.
- {骑|qí}: 马 (horse: you ride it) and {奇|qí} (strange, in {奇怪|qí guài}, lesson 24). Exact again. On the left
  {马|mǎ}'s last stroke rises.
- {辆|liàng}: 车 and {两|liǎng} *liǎng* (two), with a change of tone. Traditional 輛 has the traditional forms of
  both parts, 車 and 兩.
- {迟|chí} ({遲|chí}): 辶 (walking) and {尺|chǐ} (a foot in length; not a course character) inside: late,
  slow walking. Traditional 遲 has a different inside, 犀, and no longer sounds like *chí*.
- {急|jí}: the top was once {及|jí}, the same sound part as in {极|jí} (lesson 12), with 心 (heart) below:
  a heart in a hurry. In today's shape the top no longer looks like {及|jí}.

The other three:

- {被|bèi}: 衤 (clothing, as in {裤子|kù zi} and {衬衫|chèn shān}) and {皮|pí} (skin). {被|bèi} first meant a quilt, something
  that covers you (a quilt is still a {被子|bèi zi}); from "covered by" came the passive. {皮|pí} once
  gave the sound.
- {船|chuán}: 舟, an old character for a boat, on the left; the right side is also in {铅|qiān} (the first character of {铅笔|qiān bǐ},
  pencil, lesson 16) and once gave the sound. On the left, 舟's horizontal becomes a rising stroke.
- {全|quán}: 王 under a roof that looks like 人. Our tables give its radical as 入 (to enter), as
  the old dictionaries do. A memory aid, not history: a king under one roof is the whole country.

### Stroke order

- **{迟|chí}**: {尺|chǐ} first (four strokes), then 辶 last: the dot, the bent stroke, and the long sweep along
  the bottom, as in {这|zhè}, {边|biān} and {远|yuǎn}.
- **{被|bèi}**: 衤 has five strokes: the dot, the bent stroke, the vertical, then two short strokes (a
  left-falling stroke and a dot) on its right. Compare 礻 (as in {礼物|lǐ wù}, a present, lesson 23), which has one stroke fewer.
  Then {皮|pí}.
- **{急|jí}**: the short left-falling stroke and the bent stroke on top, then the three strokes of
  the middle (like 彐), then {心|xīn}: the dot, the long curved hook, and the two dots.
- **{全|quán}**: {人|rén} first (left-falling, then right-falling), then 王 inside: the horizontals from top to
  bottom, the vertical before the last horizontal.
- **{船|chuán}**: 舟 first, in six strokes: a short left-falling stroke on top, a long one, the turning
  hook, a dot, the rising stroke and a last dot inside; then the right side: {几|jǐ}, then {口|kǒu}.

```trace
汽骑辆全船迟急被
```

Write it: {汽|qì}, {全|quán}, {急|jí} and {被|bèi} are on the handwriting list. Write each three times from memory.
Check the five strokes of 衤 in {被|bèi}, and the order of the strokes inside {急|jí}.
=}

## Dialogue: late for work

{李强|Lǐ Qiáng} (李强) phones his colleague {林红|Lín Hóng} (林红) on his way to work.

```dialogue
# Where are you?
林红: {喂|wèi}，{李强|Lǐ Qiáng}，{你|nǐ}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{了|le}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{等|děng}{你|nǐ}。
= Hello, Li Qiang, where are you? It's nine o'clock: everyone's waiting for you.
李强: {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{要|yào}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}！{我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。
= Sorry, I'm going to be late today! Someone's taken my bike.
林红: {啊|a}？{被|bèi}{谁|shéi}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}？
= What? Who took it?
李强: {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}。{我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{下|xià}{楼|lóu}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{门口|mén kǒu}{放|fàng}{着|zhe}{三|sān}{辆|liàng}{自行车|zì xíng chē}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{不见|bú jiàn}{了|le}。
= I don't know either. When I came downstairs this morning there were three bikes at the door,
  but mine had gone.
林红: {那|nà}{你|nǐ}{现在|xiàn zài}{怎么|zěn me}{来|lái}？
= So how are you getting here now?
李强: {我|wǒ}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{一|yí}{辆|liàng}{车|chē}，{但是|dàn shì}{路上|lù shang}{车|chē}{太|tài}{多|duō}{了|le}，{红绿灯|hóng lǜ dēng}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。
= I've got a taxi, but there's far too much traffic, and lots of lights.
林红: {别|bié}{着急|zháo jí}，{安全第一|ān quán dì yī}。{你|nǐ}{还|hái}{要|yào}{多长时间|duō cháng shí jiān}？
= Don't worry: safety first. How much longer will you be?
李强: {司机|sī jī}{说|shuō}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{公里|gōng lǐ}。{我|wǒ}{马上|mǎ shàng}{就|jiù}{到|dào}！
= The driver says two more kilometres. I'll be there right away!
林红: {好|hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{告诉|gào su}{大家|dà jiā}{你|nǐ}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{到|dào}。
= OK, I'll tell everyone you'll be here in ten minutes.
```

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{不见|bú jiàn}{了|le} is "mine had gone" ({不见|bú jiàn}, lesson 03): {我|wǒ}{的|de} stands for {我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}. {打|dǎ}{了|le}{一|yí}{辆|liàng}{车|chē} uses {辆|liàng} with
{打车|dǎ chē} (to take a taxi, HSK 2), split like a separable verb. {公里|gōng lǐ} is a kilometre.

## Reading: the train was late too

> {上|shàng}{个|gè}{月|yuè}，{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{要|yào}{坐|zuò}{高铁|gāo tiě}{去|qù}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。{火车|huǒ chē}{下午|xià wǔ}{两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{开|kāi}，{她|tā}{一|yī}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{出门|chū mén}。{那|nà}{天|tiān}{风|fēng}{很|hěn}{大|dà}，{她|tā}{刚|gāng}{走|zǒu}{到|dào}{路口|lù kǒu}，{她|tā}{的|de}{伞|sǎn}{就|jiù}{被|bèi}{风|fēng}{刮|guā}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。{她|tā}{在|zài}{路边|lù biān}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{一|yí}{辆|liàng}{车|chē}，{对|duì}{司机|sī jī}{说|shuō}：“{师傅|shī fu}，{我|wǒ}{两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{的|de}{高铁|gāo tiě}，{能|néng}{快点儿|kuài diǎnr}{吗|ma}？”{司机|sī jī}{说|shuō}：“{别|bié}{着急|zháo jí}，{路上|lù shang}{车|chē}{不|bù}{多|duō}，{马上|mǎ shàng}{就|jiù}{到|dào}。{但是|dàn shì}{安全第一|ān quán dì yī}，{红灯|hóng dēng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{我们|wǒ men}{不|bù}{能|néng}{走|zǒu}。”{路上|lù shang}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{红绿灯|hóng lǜ dēng}，{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{着急|zháo jí}。{一|yī}{点|diǎn}{五十|wǔ shí}{分|fēn}，{她|tā}{终于|zhōng yú}{到|dào}{了|le}{高铁站|gāo tiě zhàn}。{她|tā}{跑|pǎo}{进|jìn}{车站|chē zhàn}，{看见|kàn jiàn}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{等|děng}{车|chē}。{原来|yuán lái}，{那|nà}{天|tiān}{风|fēng}{太|tài}{大|dà}，{火车|huǒ chē}{晚点|wǎn diǎn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}！{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{笑|xiào}{了|le}：“{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{迟到|chí dào}，{火车|huǒ chē}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}！”

{师傅|shī fu} is a polite way to address a driver or a skilled worker. {才|cái} (only then, late), {刚|gāng}
(just) and {终于|zhōng yú} (at last) are words of lessons 25 and 21; {原来|yuán lái} is "it turned out
that". {两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{的|de}{高铁|gāo tiě} is "the two o'clock train".

1. Why did Wang Fang feel she might miss the train?
2. What happened to her umbrella?
3. Why wouldn't the driver go through every light?
4. Was she late? Why or why not?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. The train left at two, and she only left home at one.
2. It was blown away by the wind ({她|tā}{的|de}{伞|sǎn}{就|jiù}{被|bèi}{风|fēng}{刮|guā}{走|zǒu}{了|le}).
3. Safety first: they couldn't go at a red light ({红灯|hóng dēng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{我们|wǒ men}{不|bù}{能|néng}{走|zǒu}).
4. No: the train was an hour late ({火车|huǒ chē}{晚点|wǎn diǎn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}) because of the wind.

"Last month Wang Fang was going to take the high-speed train to Shanghai. The train left at two
in the afternoon, and she didn't leave home until one. It was very windy that day: she had just
reached the crossing when her umbrella was blown away by the wind. She got a taxi by the road and
said to the driver, 'My train's at two: could you go a bit faster?' The driver said, 'Don't
worry, there isn't much traffic; we'll be there in no time. But safety first: we can't go when
the light's red.' There were lots of traffic lights on the way, and Wang Fang got more and more
anxious. At ten to two she finally reached the high-speed rail station. She ran in and saw lots
of people standing, waiting for their train. It turned out that the wind was so strong that day
that the train was an hour late! Wang Fang laughed: 'I'm not late: the train is!'"

The last line is a joke: {迟到|chí dào} is the word for people being late, so Wang Fang uses it for the
train to be funny. For a train that is late, say {晚点|wǎn diǎn}, as the text does just before.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}！
= Someone's taken my bike!
{我|wǒ}{的|de}{伞|sǎn}{被|bèi}{风|fēng}{刮|guā}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。
= My umbrella's been blown away.
{对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。
= Sorry I'm late.
{飞机|fēi jī}{晚点|wǎn diǎn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。
= The plane is an hour late.
{别|bié}{着急|zháo jí}，{我|wǒ}{马上|mǎ shàng}{就|jiù}{到|dào}。
= Don't worry, I'll be there right away.
{骑车|qí chē}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{要|yào}{注意|zhù yì}{安全|ān quán}。
= Be careful when you're cycling.
{路口|lù kǒu}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
= There's someone standing at the crossing.
```

## Pronunciation

- {被|bèi} *bèi* falls; {北|běi} *běi* (north, lesson 11) dips, {杯|bēi} *bēi* (cup) is level.
- {骑|qí} *qí* rises; {起|qǐ} *qǐ* (to rise) dips and {汽|qì} *qì* falls. *q* is like "ch" in "cheese", lips spread.
- {船|chuán} *chuán* rises; {穿|chuān} *chuān* (to wear) is level.
- {辆|liàng} *liàng* falls; {两|liǎng} *liǎng* (two) dips: {两|liǎng}{辆|liàng}{车|chē} *liǎng liàng chē*.
- {着急|zháo jí} *zháojí*: two rising tones. In {站|zhàn}{着|zhe} and {穿|chuān}{着|zhe} the {着|zhe} is light: *zhe*.
- {红绿灯|hóng lǜ dēng} *hónglǜdēng*: the *lǜ* is ü, with rounded lips (as in {绿色|lǜ sè}).
- {自行车|zì xíng chē} *zìxíngchē*: *z* and *ch* are different sounds: *z* like the "ds" in "beds", *ch* with the
  tongue curled back.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{骑|qí}~~: the verb needs something after it: {被|bèi}{人|rén}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}.
- ~~{我们|wǒ men}{被|bèi}{老师|lǎo shī}{教|jiāo}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}~~: for an ordinary event, use the active: {老师|lǎo shī}{教|jiāo}{我们|wǒ men}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{没|méi}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}~~: {没|méi} goes before {被|bèi}: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{没|méi}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}.
- ~~{骑|qí}{汽车|qì chē}~~ / ~~{坐|zuò}{自行车|zì xíng chē}~~: {开|kāi} or {坐|zuò} a car; {骑|qí} a bike.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{晚点|wǎn diǎn}{了|le}~~: people {迟到|chí dào}; trains and planes {晚点|wǎn diǎn}.
- ~~{一|yí}{个|gè}{汽车|qì chē}~~: vehicles take {辆|liàng}: {一|yí}{辆|liàng}{汽车|qì chē}.
- {着急|zháo jí} read *zhejí*: it's *zháojí*.
- ~~{路口|lù kǒu}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}~~: a known person goes before the verb: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}{站|zhàn}{在|zài}{路口|lù kǒu}. The {着|zhe} sentence is for someone new:
  {路口|lù kǒu}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}.

## Key points

- {被|bèi}: receiver + {被|bèi} + (doer) + verb + more ({了|le}, a result, a place): {我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}. The doer can be
  left out; {没|méi} / {别|bié} / time words go before {被|bèi}; mostly for unwelcome events.
- {把|bǎ} ↔ {被|bèi}: {弟弟|dì di}{把|bǎ}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{吃|chī}{了|le} = {蛋糕|dàn gāo}{被|bèi}{弟弟|dì di}{吃|chī}{了|le}.
- Existential {着|zhe}: place + verb + {着|zhe} + number + measure + thing: {路口|lù kǒu}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}, {门口|mén kǒu}{放|fàng}{着|zhe}{两|liǎng}{辆|liàng}{自行车|zì xíng chē}.
- {骑|qí} (astride: {自行车|zì xíng chē}, {马|mǎ}) vs {坐|zuò} (inside: {汽车|qì chē}, {船|chuán}, {高铁|gāo tiě}); {辆|liàng} for vehicles.
- {迟到|chí dào} (people) vs {晚点|wǎn diǎn} (trains, planes); {马上|mǎ shàng} (right away); {急|jí} (urgent), {着急|zháo jí} (anxious) *zháojí*.
- {红绿灯|hóng lǜ dēng}, {安全|ān quán} ({注意|zhù yì}{安全|ān quán}), {米|mǐ} (metre), {站|zhàn} (to stand).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: A trip: 一边…一边, 是…的
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

You've travelled with HSK 2 ({旅游|lǚ yóu}, {酒店|jiǔ diàn}, {门票|mén piào}, {去|qù}{过|guo}) and got through the city with lessons 11–13. This
lesson packs your bags. You'll learn:

- **[[simultaneous actions]]** with {一边|yì biān}…{一边|yì biān} (doing two things at once);
- {是|shì}…{的|de} again, now for telling and asking about past trips;
- the words of a journey: {护照|hù zhào}, {行李|xíng li}, {宾馆|bīn guǎn}, {出发|chū fā}, {起飞|qǐ fēi}, {检票|jiǎn piào}, {游客|yóu kè};
- {经过|jīng guò} (to pass by), {离开|lí kāi} (to leave) and {到处|dào chù} (everywhere);
- photos: {拍照|pāi zhào}, {照相|zhào xiàng}, {相机|xiàng jī}, {照片|zhào piàn} and {照|zhào};
- {一块儿|yí kuàir}, the spoken "together".

## Getting ready: {护照|hù zhào}, {行李|xíng li}, {出发|chū fā}

{护照|hù zhào} is a passport and {行李|xíng li} luggage (the *li* is light: *xíngli*). Both are things you {带|dài} (bring, take
with you: lesson 09):

{护照|hù zhào}{带|dài}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ — Have you got your passport?

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{行李|xíng li}{不|bù}{多|duō}，{就|jiù}{一|yí}{个|gè}{箱子|xiāng zi}。 — I don't have much luggage, just one case.

In China a passport is also an ID for foreigners: you show it when you buy a train ticket or check
in at a hotel.

{出发|chū fā} is "to set off, to start a journey". It has no object, but a place of departure can go before
it with {从|cóng}:

{我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{出发|chū fā}。 — We're setting off at eight tomorrow morning.

{我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{出发|chū fā}{的|de}。 — We set off from Beijing.

## At the station and the airport: {检票|jiǎn piào}, {起飞|qǐ fēi}

{检票|jiǎn piào} is "to check tickets": at stations, the staff check tickets before you board, and the screens
say {开始|kāi shǐ}{检票|jiǎn piào} (boarding: tickets now being checked). The gate is the {检票口|jiǎn piào kǒu}.

{去|qù}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{的|de}{高铁|gāo tiě}{开始|kāi shǐ}{检票|jiǎn piào}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}。 — They've started checking tickets for the Shanghai train: let's go.

{起飞|qǐ fēi} is "to take off", for planes: {起|qǐ} (to rise) + {飞|fēi} (to fly).

{飞机|fēi jī}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{起飞|qǐ fēi}，{我们|wǒ men}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{机场|jī chǎng}{就|jiù}{行|xíng}。 — The plane takes off at ten, so it's fine if we're at the airport by eight.

## Hotels and tourists: {宾馆|bīn guǎn}, {游客|yóu kè}

{宾馆|bīn guǎn} is a hotel, a slightly older and more formal word than HSK 2's {酒店|jiǔ diàn}; many hotels are called
one or the other. {饭店|fàn diàn} (HSK 1's restaurant) is also in the names of some big old hotels. {游客|yóu kè} is a
tourist, a visitor at a sight:

{我们|wǒ men}{住|zhù}{的|de}{宾馆|bīn guǎn}{离|lí}{车站|chē zhàn}{很|hěn}{近|jìn}。 — The hotel we're staying in is close to the station.

{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{和|hé}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}，{这儿|zhèr}{的|de}{游客|yóu kè}{更|gèng}{多|duō}。 — On Saturdays and Sundays there are even more tourists here.

## {经过|jīng guò}, {离开|lí kāi}, {到处|dào chù}

{经过|jīng guò} is "to pass by, to go through" a place on the way:

{去|qù}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{的|de}{路上|lù shang}，{高铁|gāo tiě}{经过|jīng guò}{南京|Nán jīng}。 — On the way to Shanghai, the train goes through Nanjing.

{我|wǒ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{上班|shàng bān}{都|dōu}{经过|jīng guò}{这个|zhè ge}{超市|chāo shì}。 — I go past this supermarket every day on my way to work.

{经过|jīng guò} is also a noun, "the course of events": {事情|shì qing}{的|de}{经过|jīng guò} (what happened, step by step).

{离开|lí kāi} is "to leave" a place or a person, with the place as its object:

{我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān}{离开|lí kāi}{北京|Běi jīng}。 — We're leaving Beijing tomorrow.

{她|tā}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{离开|lí kāi}{家|jiā}。 — She doesn't want to leave home.

Compare: {走|zǒu} (HSK 2) is just "to go away", with no object ({我|wǒ}{走|zǒu}{了|le}); {出发|chū fā} is starting a journey;
{离开|lí kāi} says what you leave behind.

{到处|dào chù} is "everywhere, all over": {到处|dào chù}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{人|rén} (there are people everywhere), and before a verb, "around":
{到处|dào chù}{看|kàn}{看|kàn}, {到处|dào chù}{走|zǒu}{走|zǒu} (have a look around, walk around).

{这个|zhè ge}{城市|chéng shì}{到处|dào chù}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{好吃|hǎo chī}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}。 — There's good food all over this city.

{到处|dào chù} is a word of its own; lesson 11's {哪儿|nǎr}{都|dōu} says the same with a question word: {哪儿|nǎr}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{人|rén}.

## Photos: {拍照|pāi zhào}, {照相|zhào xiàng}, {相机|xiàng jī}, {照片|zhào piàn}, {照|zhào}

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {拍照|pāi zhào} | to take photos ({拍|pāi}, to pat; to shoot a photo) |
| {照相|zhào xiàng} | to take a photo; to have your photo taken |
| {相机|xiàng jī} | a camera |
| {照片|zhào piàn} | a photo (measure word {张|zhāng}) |
| {照|zhào} | to shine; to take (a photo); to look in (a mirror) |

{拍照|pāi zhào} and {照相|zhào xiàng} both mean taking photos; {拍照|pāi zhào} is the more common in signs and in talk about phones,
{照相|zhào xiàng} a little older. Both are separable: {拍个照|pāi ge zhào} (take a quick photo), {照|zhào}{了|le}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{相|xiàng}.

{这儿|zhèr}{可以|kě yǐ}{拍照|pāi zhào}{吗|ma}？ — Can I take photos here?

{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{给|gěi}{我们|wǒ men}{照|zhào}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{相|xiàng}，{好|hǎo}{吗|ma}？ — Could you take a photo of us, please?

{我|wǒ}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{拍|pāi}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{照片|zhào piàn}。 — I took lots of photos on my phone.

{照|zhào} on its own is "to shine": {太阳|tài yang}{照|zhào}{着|zhe}{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{街|jiē} (the sun is shining on this street). It's also the verb
in {照|zhào}{了|le}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{照片|zhào piàn} (took a photo).

## Simultaneous actions: {一边|yì biān}…{一边|yì biān}

To say that someone does two things at the same time, put {一边|yì biān} before each verb:

**subject + {一边|yì biān} + verb 1 + {一边|yì biān} + verb 2**

{他|tā}{一边|yì biān}{走|zǒu}{一边|yì biān}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。 — He's talking on the phone as he walks.

{我们|wǒ men}{一边|yì biān}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{一边|yì biān}{聊天|liáo tiān}。 — We chatted over dinner. ({聊天|liáo tiān}, to chat: lesson 22.)

{她|tā}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{一边|yì biān}{听|tīng}{歌|gē}{一边|yì biān}{做饭|zuò fàn}。 — She likes listening to music while she cooks.

- The subject comes once, before the first {一边|yì biān}.
- Both actions are things you *do*, going on at the same time. Words for states ({是|shì}, {有|yǒu}, {喜欢|xǐ huan})
  don't take {一边|yì biān}.
- In quick speech the {一|yī} is often dropped: {边|biān}{走|zǒu}{边|biān}{说|shuō} (talk as you walk).

Don't confuse it with {又|yòu}…{又|yòu} (lesson 08), which joins two qualities: {又|yòu}{便宜|pián yi}{又|yòu}{好看|hǎo kàn}. {一边|yì biān}…{一边|yì biān} joins two
actions.

({一边|yì biān} can also mean "one side": {马路|mǎ lù}{的|de}{一边|yì biān} is one side of the road.)

## {是|shì}…{的|de}: telling about a past trip

HSK 2 taught {是|shì}…{的|de} for the details of something that has already happened: when, where, how, who
with. It's the natural frame for questions about a trip:

{你们|nǐ men}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{时候|shí hou}{去|qù}{的|de}？ — When did you go?

{我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{高铁|gāo tiě}{去|qù}{的|de}。 — We went by high-speed train.

{你|nǐ}{是|shì}{跟|gēn}{谁|shéi}{一块儿|yí kuàir}{去|qù}{的|de}？ — Who did you go with?

{照片|zhào piàn}{是|shì}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}{拍|pāi}{的|de}？ — Where were the photos taken?

The event itself (that you went) is known; {是|shì}…{的|de} asks or tells about one detail. {是|shì} goes before the
detail, {的|de} after the verb, and the verb takes no {了|le}. In a positive sentence {是|shì} can be left out: {我们|wǒ men}
{坐|zuò}{高铁|gāo tiě}{去|qù}{的|de}.

## {一块儿|yí kuàir}: together

{一块儿|yí kuàir} (*yíkuàir*) means the same as {一起|yì qǐ} (HSK 2): together. It's spoken, and very common in the North:

{我们|wǒ men}{一块儿|yí kuàir}{去|qù}{吧|ba}！ — Let's go together!

{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{跟|gēn}{朋友|péng you}{一块儿|yí kuàir}{去|qù}{的|de}。 — I went with a friend.

In formal writing, use {一起|yì qǐ}; in a chatty narrative {一块儿|yí kuàir} is fine.

| 李 | plum; (surname) Li | li, lǐ | 木 | 7 | {行李|xíng li}, {李明|Lǐ Míng} |
| 宾 (traditional 賓) | guest | bīn | 宀 | 10 | {宾馆|bīn guǎn} |

- {护|hù} ({護|hù}): 扌 (hand) and {户|hù} *hù* (door, the top of {房|fáng}), which gives the sound exactly: a hand
  guarding the door. A {护照|hù zhào} is a "protection permit". The traditional form has 言 (speech) and a
  different right side.
- {拍|pāi}: 扌 again, and {白|bái} *bái* (white) for the sound. {白|bái} is the sound part of a small family: {拍|pāi} *pāi*,
  {怕|pà} *pà* (to fear, lesson 24), and {百|bǎi} *bǎi* (hundred) is built on it too. The vowels still rhyme
  more or less; the first sounds have moved.
- {宾|bīn} ({賓|bīn}): 宀 (roof): a guest under your roof. The simplified form put {兵|bīng} (soldier; not a
  course character) underneath as a near sound; the traditional form has 貝 (shell, money) at the
  bottom: as a memory aid, the gifts a guest brings.
- {李|Lǐ}: 木 (tree) over {子|zǐ}: a plum tree. {子|zǐ} once gave the sound. {李|Lǐ} is also one of the commonest
  surnames ({李明|Lǐ Míng}). In {行李|xíng li} it's light: *xíngli*.
- {相|xiàng}: 木 (tree) and 目 (eye): an eye looking at a tree, "to look closely". From there, "appearance"
  ({照相|zhào xiàng}, to take someone's likeness) and "each other" ({相信|xiāng xìn}, to trust, read *xiāng*).
- {片|piàn}: the right half of a tree trunk cut down the middle (compare 木): a slice, a flat piece. Its
  own radical; {照片|zhào piàn} is a "shining slice".
- {处|chù} ({處|chù}): 夂 and 卜. Also read *chǔ* in a few words outside this course. The traditional form is
  quite different, with 虍 (tiger) on top.

### Stroke order

- **{片|piàn}**: four strokes: the long left-falling stroke, the short vertical at the top right, the
  horizontal, and the stroke that goes right and then down.
- **{处|chù}**: 夂 first (left-falling, the bent stroke, and the long right-falling stroke that sweeps
  under), then 卜 (the vertical, then the dot).
- **{护|hù}** and **{拍|pāi}**: 扌 first: the horizontal, the vertical with its hook, then the rising stroke.
  Then the right side.
- **{相|xiàng}** and **{李|Lǐ}**: on the left or on top, 木's last stroke shrinks to a dot.
- **{宾|bīn}**: 宀 (dot, dot, the horizontal with its hook), then {兵|bīng}.

```trace
护李宾处拍相片
```
