worried. Wang Fang phoned the hotel right away. Someone at the hotel said, 'Don't worry, your
passport is on the table in your room: we'll bring it over straight away.' Half an hour later the
passport arrived. The plane took off at twelve, and they weren't late. On the plane, Anna looked
at the photos and laughed: 'You can skip the photos, but you can't skip the passport!'"
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{护照|hù zhào}{带|dài}{了|le}{吗|ma}？
= Have you got your passport?
{我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{出发|chū fā}。
= We're setting off at eight tomorrow morning.
{飞机|fēi jī}{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}{起飞|qǐ fēi}？
= What time does the plane take off?
{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{给|gěi}{我们|wǒ men}{照|zhào}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{相|xiàng}，{好|hǎo}{吗|ma}？
= Could you take a photo of us, please?
{我们|wǒ men}{一边|yì biān}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{一边|yì biān}{聊天|liáo tiān}{吧|ba}。
= Let's chat over dinner.
{你们|nǐ men}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{时候|shí hou}{去|qù}{的|de}？
= When did you go?
{我们|wǒ men}{一块儿|yí kuàir}{去|qù}{吧|ba}！
= Let's go together!
```

## Pronunciation

- {行李|xíng li} *xíngli*: the *li* is light. {行|xíng} is *xíng* here (walk, travel), not the *háng* of {银行|yín háng}.
- {护照|hù zhào} *hùzhào*: two falling tones; *zh* with the tongue curled back.
- {宾馆|bīn guǎn} *bīnguǎn*: level, then a dip. *bin* ends in *-n*, not *-ng*.
- {出发|chū fā} *chūfā* and {起飞|qǐ fēi} *qǐfēi*: in {出发|chū fā}, both level; in {起飞|qǐ fēi}, a dip and then level.
- {相机|xiàng jī} *xiàngjī*: {相|xiàng} falls here; in {相信|xiāng xìn} (lesson 24) it's level, *xiāng*.
- {一边|yì biān} *yìbiān* ({一|yī} before a first tone), {一块儿|yí kuàir} *yíkuàir* ({一|yī} before a fourth tone; *kuàir* with erhua).
- {照片|zhào piàn} *zhàopiàn* and {照相|zhào xiàng} *zhàoxiàng*: falling, falling.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{他|tā}{一边|yì biān}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}{一边|yì biān}{工作|gōng zuò}~~: {一边|yì biān}…{一边|yì biān} is for actions you do at the same time: {他|tā}{一边|yì biān}{学习|xué xí}{一边|yì biān}{工作|gōng zuò}.
- ~~{一边|yì biān}{他|tā}{走|zǒu}{一边|yì biān}{他|tā}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}~~: the subject comes once, first: {他|tā}{一边|yì biān}{走|zǒu}{一边|yì biān}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}.
- ~~{我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{高铁|gāo tiě}{去|qù}{了|le}~~: {是|shì}…{的|de} takes {的|de}, not {了|le}: {我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{高铁|gāo tiě}{去|qù}{的|de}.
- {离开|lí kāi} usually names what you leave: {我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān}{离开|lí kāi}{北京|Běi jīng}. When the place is clear, everyday speech
  more often just says {走|zǒu}: {我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān}{走|zǒu}.
- ~~{出发|chū fā}{北京|Běi jīng}~~: {出发|chū fā} has no object; {从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{出发|chū fā} (set off from Beijing), {去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng} (go to Beijing).
- ~~{一|yí}{个|gè}{照片|zhào piàn}~~: photos take {张|zhāng}: {一|yì}{张|zhāng}{照片|zhào piàn}.
- {行李|xíng li} read *xínglǐ*: the *li* is light.

## Key points

- {一边|yì biān} + verb + {一边|yì biān} + verb: two actions at once ({他|tā}{一边|yì biān}{走|zǒu}{一边|yì biān}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}); the subject once, first.
- {是|shì}…{的|de} for details of a past trip: {你们|nǐ men}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{时候|shí hou}{去|qù}{的|de}？ {我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{高铁|gāo tiě}{去|qù}{的|de}。
- {护照|hù zhào}, {行李|xíng li} ({带|dài}), {出发|chū fā} ({从|cóng}…{出发|chū fā}), {起飞|qǐ fēi} (planes), {检票|jiǎn piào} (boarding), {宾馆|bīn guǎn}, {游客|yóu kè}.
- {经过|jīng guò} (to pass through), {离开|lí kāi} + place (to leave), {到处|dào chù} (everywhere: {到处|dào chù}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{人|rén}).
- {拍照|pāi zhào} / {照相|zhào xiàng} (to take photos), {相机|xiàng jī} (camera), {照片|zhào piàn} (photo, {张|zhāng}), {照|zhào} (to shine; to take).
- {一块儿|yí kuàir} = {一起|yì qǐ} (spoken).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Mountains, parks and animals
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This module has taken you through the city, across the country and on a trip. Now you leave the
roads behind. You'll learn:

- landscape words: {山|shān}, {河|hé}, {海|hǎi}, {草|cǎo}, {草地|cǎo dì}, {树|shù}, and {爬|pá}{山|shān} (to go hiking);
- parks and gardens: {公园|gōng yuán}, {花园|huā yuán}, {动物园|dòng wù yuán}, and {开花|kāi huā} (to bloom);
- animals: {动物|dòng wù}, {大熊猫|dà xióng māo}, {马|mǎ}, {牛|niú}, {羊|yáng}, {鸡|jī}, and {养|yǎng} (to keep, to raise);
- the measure words that go with them: {一|yì}{只|zhī}{鸡|jī}, {一|yì}{头|tóu}{牛|niú}, {一|yì}{条|tiáo}{河|hé}, {一|yì}{棵|kē}{树|shù};
- the natural environment ({环境|huán jìng} again), and the existential {着|zhe} sentence of lesson 13 for
  describing a landscape: {山上|shān shàng}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}.

## Mountains, rivers and the sea: {山|shān}, {河|hé}, {海|hǎi}

{山|shān} is a mountain or a hill, {河|hé} a river and {海|hǎi} the sea. They make many everyday words:

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {山上|shān shàng} / {山下|shān xià} | on the mountain / at the foot of the mountain |
| {爬|pá}{山|shān} | to climb a mountain; to go hiking |
| {河边|hé biān} | the riverside |
| {海边|hǎi biān} | the seaside |
| {大海|dà hǎi} | the sea, the ocean |

{爬|pá} is "to climb" (on hands and feet, or up steps) and also "to crawl": {孩子|hái zi}{会|huì}{爬|pá}{了|le} (the baby can
crawl now). {爬|pá}{山|shān} is a popular weekend activity in China, and it often means
climbing the steps of a mountain path rather than real climbing.

{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}{吧|ba}！ — Let's go hiking on Saturday!

{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{河边|hé biān}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{河边|hé biān}{跑步|pǎo bù}。 — My home is by the river; every morning I go running along it.

{夏天|xià tiān}{我们|wǒ men}{经常|jīng cháng}{去|qù}{海边|hǎi biān}。 — In summer we often go to the seaside.

Measure words: a river is long and thin, so {一|yì}{条|tiáo}{河|hé}. A mountain takes {座|zuò} ({一|yí}{座|zuò}{山|shān}), a measure word
for big, solid things like mountains and buildings.

## Grass and trees: {草|cǎo}, {草地|cǎo dì}, {树|shù}, {开花|kāi huā}

{草|cǎo} is grass (or any small plant), and {草地|cǎo dì} a lawn or a meadow: "grass ground". {树|shù} is a tree, and its
measure word is {棵|kē} (for plants: {一|yì}{棵|kē}{树|shù}).

{公园|gōng yuán}{的|de}{草地|cǎo dì}{上|shàng}{坐|zuò}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}。 — There are lots of people sitting on the grass in the park.

{请|qǐng}{别|bié}{在|zài}{草地|cǎo dì}{上|shàng}{走|zǒu}。 — Please keep off the grass.

{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{门口|mén kǒu}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{棵|kē}{大|dà}{树|shù}。 — There's a big tree outside my home.

{开花|kāi huā} is "to bloom, to flower": {开|kāi} (to open) + {花|huā} (flower). It's a verb with its own object, so it can
split: {开|kāi}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā} (lots of flowers came out). Or say {花|huā}{开|kāi}{了|le} (the flowers are out).

{春天|chūn tiān}{到|dào}{了|le}，{花|huā}{都|dōu}{开|kāi}{了|le}。 — Spring has come and the flowers are all out.

{这|zhè}{棵|kē}{树|shù}{四|sì}{月|yuè}{开花|kāi huā}。 — This tree flowers in April.

## Parks and gardens: {公园|gōng yuán}, {花园|huā yuán}, {动物园|dòng wù yuán}

{园|yuán} (lesson 12) is the garden in all three words:

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {公园|gōng yuán} | a park (a public garden) |
| {花园|huā yuán} | a garden (with flowers) |
| {动物园|dòng wù yuán} | a zoo (an animal garden) |

{我们|wǒ men}{小区|xiǎo qū}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{花园|huā yuán}。 — There's a little garden on our estate.

{公园|gōng yuán}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{老人|lǎo rén}{在|zài}{跑步|pǎo bù}、{跳舞|tiào wǔ}。 — In the park lots of older people are running and dancing.

## Animals and their measure words

{动物|dòng wù} is an animal. You know {狗|gǒu}, {猫|māo} and {鸟|niǎo} from HSK 1 and 2, and how to count animals: {一|yì}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}, {两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{鸟|niǎo}. Here are four farm animals and China's best-known wild one:

| Word | Meaning | Measure word |
|---|---|---|
| {马|mǎ} | horse | {一|yì}{匹|pǐ}{马|mǎ} ({匹|pǐ}) |
| {牛|niú} | cow, ox | {一|yì}{头|tóu}{牛|niú} ({头|tóu}, head) |
| {羊|yáng} | sheep, goat | {一|yì}{只|zhī}{羊|yáng} |
| {鸡|jī} | chicken | {一|yì}{只|zhī}{鸡|jī} |
| {大熊猫|dà xióng māo} | giant panda | {一|yì}{只|zhī}{大熊猫|dà xióng māo} |

- {一|yì}{只|zhī} is the general way to count animals ({一|yì}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}, {一|yì}{只|zhī}{羊|yáng}); {头|tóu} is used for cattle (and pigs), as English says
  "fifty head of cattle"; {条|tiáo} for long animals ({一|yì}{条|tiáo}{鱼|yú}, and also {一|yì}{条|tiáo}{狗|gǒu}).
- {羊|yáng} covers sheep and goats. When it matters, {绵羊|mián yáng} is a sheep and {山羊|shān yáng} ("mountain
  sheep") a goat.
- {牛|niú} covers cows, bulls and oxen. In slang, {牛|niú} also means "awesome": {你|nǐ}{太|tài}{牛|niú}{了|le}！ (you're amazing!).
  Use it with friends, not in an exam essay.
- {鸡|jī} is the bird and the meat: {我|wǒ}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{鸡|jī} (I love chicken). {鸡蛋|jī dàn} (HSK 1) is "chicken egg".
- {大熊猫|dà xióng māo} is "big bear-cat": {熊|xióng} is a bear and {猫|māo} a cat. People often just say {熊猫|xióng māo}. You'll read more
  about pandas in the honors lesson of this module.

{动物园|dòng wù yuán}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{大熊猫|dà xióng māo}。 — There are two giant pandas at the zoo.

{骑|qí}{马|mǎ}{很|hěn}{好玩儿|hǎo wánr}。 — Horse riding is great fun.

## {养|yǎng}: to keep, to raise

{养|yǎng} is "to keep" animals or plants and "to raise" children:

{你|nǐ}{养|yǎng}{过|guo}{狗|gǒu}{吗|ma}？ — Have you ever had a dog?

{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{养|yǎng}{花|huā}。 — My mum loves growing flowers.

{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{养|yǎng}{了|le}{一|yì}{头|tóu}{牛|niú}{和|hé}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{羊|yáng}。 — My grandpa keeps a cow and lots of sheep.

In the city, {养|yǎng} + pet is the usual way to say "have a pet": {我|wǒ}{养|yǎng}{了|le}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{猫|māo} (I've got a cat).

## Describing a landscape: the existential {着|zhe} sentence again

The pattern from lesson 13, place + verb + {着|zhe} + thing, is how you paint a scene:

{山上|shān shàng}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}。 — Lots of flowers are blooming on the mountain.

{河边|hé biān}{坐|zuò}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{钓鱼|diào yú}{的|de}{人|rén}。 — There are lots of people sitting by the river fishing. ({钓鱼|diào yú}, to fish)

{树|shù}{下|xià}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{鸡|jī}。 — A chicken is standing under the tree.

{草地|cǎo dì}{上|shàng}{住|zhù}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{小|xiǎo}{动物|dòng wù}。 — Lots of little animals live in the meadow.

Start with the place, then say how the thing is there ({开|kāi}{着|zhe}, {坐|zuò}{着|zhe}, {站|zhàn}{着|zhe}, {住|zhù}{着|zhe}), then the thing, with a
number or {很|hěn}{多|duō}.

## The environment: {环境|huán jìng}

Lesson 11's {环境|huán jìng} (surroundings) is also the natural environment. {保护环境|bǎo hù huán jìng} ({保护|bǎo hù}, to protect)
is "to protect the environment", a phrase you'll see on posters and in schools.

{这儿|zhèr}{的|de}{环境|huán jìng}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{山上|shān shàng}{树|shù}{很|hěn}{多|duō}，{河|hé}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{水|shuǐ}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{干净|gān jìng}。 — The environment here is very good: lots of trees on the
hills, and the water in the river is clean too.

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 山 | mountain | shān | 山 | 3 | {山|shān}, {爬|pá}{山|shān} |
| 河 | river | hé | 氵 | 8 | {河|hé} |
| 海 | sea | hǎi | 氵 | 10 | {海|hǎi} |
| 爬 | climb; crawl | pá | 爪 | 8 | {爬|pá} |
| 草 | grass | cǎo | 艹 | 9 | {草|cǎo}, {草地|cǎo dì} |
| 树 (traditional 樹) | tree | shù | 木 | 9 | {树|shù} |
| 物 | thing | wù | 牛 | 8 | {动物|dòng wù}, {动物园|dòng wù yuán}, and later {礼物|lǐ wù} (23) |
| 熊 | bear | xióng | 灬 | 14 | {大熊猫|dà xióng māo} |
| 羊 | sheep | yáng | 羊 | 6 | {羊|yáng} |
| 养 (traditional 養) | raise; keep | yǎng | 丷 | 9 | {养|yǎng} |

Two pictures: {山|shān} is three peaks, and {羊|yáng} a sheep's head, with two horns on top. {羊|yáng} is also a sound
part: {样|yàng} (in {怎么样|zěn me yàng}) and {养|yǎng} both say *yang*.

The others are mostly meaning + sound:

- {河|hé}: 氵 (water) and {可|kě} for the sound. The same part is in {哥|gē} *gē* and {歌|gē} *gē* ({唱歌|chàng gē}): the sounds
  have drifted, but {可|kě}, {哥|gē} and {河|hé} still share their vowel.
- {海|hǎi}: 氵 and {每|měi} *měi* (every, HSK 2), which once gave the sound and no longer does.
- {爬|pá}: 爪 (claw) and {巴|bā}. {巴|bā} is the sound part of a family you already know: {把|bǎ} *bǎ* (lesson 03),
  {爸|bà} *bà*, {吧|ba} *ba*, and now {爬|pá} *pá*.
- {草|cǎo}: 艹 (grass) and {早|zǎo} *zǎo* (early, HSK 1), which once gave the sound.
- {物|wù}: 牛 (ox) and {勿|wù}, which gives the sound. On the left, {牛|niú}'s last stroke rises.
- {树|shù} ({樹|shù}): 木 (tree). The simplified right side looks like {对|duì}, but only the shape is borrowed;
  the traditional right side gave the sound.
- {熊|xióng}: the usual explanation is that {能|néng} (can, HSK 1) first meant "bear"; when it came to mean "can",
  fire dots 灬 were added underneath to write the animal.
- {养|yǎng} ({養|yǎng}): in the traditional form, {羊|yáng} on top gives the sound and {食|shí} (food) below the meaning:
  to feed. The simplified form keeps a squeezed {羊|yáng} on top. Our tables give its radical as 丷;
  many dictionaries file it under {羊|yáng}.

### Stroke order

- **{山|shān}**: the middle vertical first, then the left vertical that turns along the bottom, then
  the right vertical.
- **{爬|pá}**: 爪 first (four strokes), its last stroke sweeping right underneath; then {巴|bā}, ending with
  the vertical that curves into a hook.
- **{羊|yáng}**: a dot and a short left-falling stroke on top, three horizontals, and the long vertical last, through them all.
- **{养|yǎng}**: the dot and the short left-falling stroke, the three horizontals, then the long left-falling and right-falling
  strokes, and last the short left-falling stroke and the vertical at the bottom.
- **{物|wù}**: {牛|niú} on the left (left-falling, horizontal, vertical, rising stroke), then {勿|wù}.
- **{树|shù}**: 木, then {又|yòu}, then 寸 (its dot last).

```trace
山河海爬草
```

```trace
树物熊羊养
```

Write it: {山|shān}, {河|hé}, {海|hǎi}, {草|cǎo}, {树|shù}, {物|wù}, {羊|yáng} and {养|yǎng} are all on the handwriting list. Write each three
times from memory. {河|hé} and {海|hǎi} share 氵; {羊|yáng} and {养|yǎng} share the sheep on top.
=}

## Dialogue: mountains or pandas?

{王芳|Wáng Fāng} (王芳) and {安娜|Ān nà} (安娜) are planning the weekend.

```dialogue
# This Saturday
王芳: {安娜|Ān nà}，{这个|zhè ge}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{吗|ma}？{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}{吧|ba}！
= Anna, are you free this Saturday? Let's go hiking!
安娜: {爬|pá}{山|shān}？{山上|shān shàng}{冷|lěng}{不|bu}{冷|lěng}？
= Hiking? Is it cold up on the mountain?
王芳: {不|bù}{冷|lěng}。{现在|xiàn zài}{是|shì}{春天|chūn tiān}，{山上|shān shàng}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}，{漂亮|piào liang}{极|jí}{了|le}。
= No. It's spring now: there are lots of flowers out on the mountain, it's gorgeous.
安娜: {好|hǎo}{啊|a}！{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{更|gèng}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{动物园|dòng wù yuán}{看|kàn}{大熊猫|dà xióng māo}。
= OK! But I'd rather go to the zoo to see the pandas.
王芳: {那|nà}{我们|wǒ men}{上午|shàng wǔ}{爬|pá}{山|shān}，{下午|xià wǔ}{去|qù}{动物园|dòng wù yuán}，{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？{动物园|dòng wù yuán}{就|jiù}{在|zài}{山下|shān xià}。
= Then we'll go hiking in the morning and to the zoo in the afternoon, how's that? The zoo is
  right at the foot of the mountain.
安娜: {太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！{你|nǐ}{养|yǎng}{过|guo}{动物|dòng wù}{吗|ma}？
= Great! Have you ever kept animals?
王芳: {我|wǒ}{小时候|xiǎo shí hou}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{养|yǎng}{了|le}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}{和|hé}{两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{鸡|jī}。{我|wǒ}{外公|wài gōng}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{外地|wài dì}，{他|tā}{养|yǎng}{了|le}{一|yì}{头|tóu}{牛|niú}{和|hé}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{羊|yáng}。
= When I was little we had a dog and two chickens. My grandpa (my mum's father) lives in another part of the
  country: he keeps a cow and lots of sheep.
安娜: {真|zhēn}{的|de}？{我|wǒ}{还|hái}{没|méi}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}{真|zhēn}{的|de}{牛|niú}{呢|ne}！
= Really? I've never even seen a real cow!
王芳: {那|nà}{下|xià}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{我们|wǒ men}{一块儿|yí kuàir}{去|qù}{我|wǒ}{外公|wài gōng}{家|jiā}{吧|ba}，{那儿|nàr}{有山有河|yǒu shān yǒu hé}，{环境|huán jìng}{好|hǎo}{极|jí}{了|le}。
= Then let's go to my grandpa's together next month. There are mountains and a river there:
  it's a wonderful place.
```

{有山有河|yǒu shān yǒu hé} is "with mountains and rivers": {有|yǒu} A {有|yǒu} B lists what a place has. {还|hái}{没|méi}…{呢|ne} is "not yet, not
even".

## Reading: the old man and his sheep

> {上|shàng}{个|gè}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}，{天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{李明|Lǐ Míng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}。{山上|shān shàng}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}，{树|shù}{也|yě}{绿|lǜ}{了|le}。{他|tā}{一边|yì biān}{爬|pá}{一边|yì biān}{拍照|pāi zhào}。{在|zài}{一|yì}{棵|kē}{大|dà}{树|shù}{下|xià}，{他|tā}{看见|kàn jiàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}{的|de}{鸟|niǎo}，{就|jiù}{跟着|gēn zhe}{鸟|niǎo}{往|wǎng}{山|shān}{里|lǐ}{走|zǒu}。{他|tā}{越|yuè}{走|zǒu}{越|yuè}{远|yuǎn}，{鸟|niǎo}{不见|bú jiàn}{了|le}，{他|tā}{也|yě}{找|zhǎo}{不|bú}{到|dào}{路|lù}{了|le}。{天|tiān}{快要|kuài yào}{黑|hēi}{了|le}，{李明|Lǐ Míng}{很|hěn}{着急|zháo jí}。{这时候|zhè shí hou}，{他|tā}{看见|kàn jiàn}{山下|shān xià}{的|de}{草地|cǎo dì}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{羊|yáng}，{旁边|páng biān}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{个|gè}{老人|lǎo rén}。{老人|lǎo rén}{养|yǎng}{了|le}{三十|sān shí}{多|duō}{只|zhī}{羊|yáng}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{带|dài}{它们|tā men}{来|lái}{这儿|zhèr}{吃|chī}{草|cǎo}。{他|tā}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}：“{这|zhè}{座|zuò}{山|shān}{我|wǒ}{爬|pá}{了|le}{五十|wǔ shí}{年|nián}{了|le}，{哪儿|nǎr}{都|dōu}{认识|rèn shi}，{跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}！”{老人|lǎo rén}{带|dài}{李明|Lǐ Míng}{下|xià}{了|le}{山|shān}。{回到|huí dào}{家|jiā}，{李明|Lǐ Míng}{说|shuō}：“{我|wǒ}{拍|pāi}{了|le}{一百|yì bǎi}{张|zhāng}{照片|zhào piàn}，{最|zuì}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{是|shì}{老人|lǎo rén}{和|hé}{他|tā}{的|de}{羊|yáng}！”

{跟着|gēn zhe} is "following" ({跟|gēn} + {着|zhe}). {天|tiān}{快要|kuài yào}{黑|hēi}{了|le} is "it was about to get dark" ({快要|kuài yào}…{了|le}, HSK 2). {这时候|zhè shí hou} is "at
that moment". {座|zuò} is the measure word for mountains.

1. What made Li Ming go further into the mountains?
2. Why did he get worried?
3. Who helped him, and why could that person help?
4. Which photo did he like best?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. He was following a beautiful bird ({跟着|gēn zhe}{鸟|niǎo}{往|wǎng}{山|shān}{里|lǐ}{走|zǒu}).
2. The bird had gone, he couldn't find the path, and it was about to get dark.
3. An old man with his sheep: he had climbed that mountain for fifty years and knew every part of it.
4. The one of the old man and his sheep ({最|zuì}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{是|shì}{老人|lǎo rén}{和|hé}{他|tā}{的|de}{羊|yáng}).

"Last Sunday the weather was lovely, and Li Ming went hiking on his own. There were lots of
flowers out on the mountain, and the trees had turned green. He took photos as he climbed. Under
a big tree he saw a beautiful bird, and he followed it further into the mountains. The further he
walked, the further away he got; the bird disappeared, and he couldn't find the path. It was
about to get dark, and Li Ming was worried. Just then he saw lots of sheep on the meadow below,
with an old man standing beside them. The old man kept more than thirty sheep and brought them
here every day to graze. He smiled and said, 'I've been climbing this mountain for fifty years: I
know every bit of it. Follow me!' The old man took Li Ming down the mountain. Back home, Li Ming
said, 'I took a hundred photos, and the best one is of the old man and his sheep!'"
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}{吧|ba}！
= Let's go hiking on Saturday!
{山上|shān shàng}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}。
= There are lots of flowers out on the mountain.
{动物园|dòng wù yuán}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{大熊猫|dà xióng māo}。
= There are two giant pandas at the zoo.
{你|nǐ}{养|yǎng}{过|guo}{狗|gǒu}{吗|ma}？
= Have you ever had a dog?
{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{养|yǎng}{了|le}{一|yì}{头|tóu}{牛|niú}{和|hé}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{羊|yáng}。
= My grandpa keeps a cow and lots of sheep.
{请|qǐng}{别|bié}{在|zài}{草地|cǎo dì}{上|shàng}{走|zǒu}。
= Please keep off the grass.
{春天|chūn tiān}{到|dào}{了|le}，{花|huā}{都|dōu}{开|kāi}{了|le}。
= Spring has come and the flowers are all out.
```

## Pronunciation

- {山|shān} *shān* (mountain) and {三|sān} *sān* (three): *sh* with the tongue curled back, *s* with it flat.
- {河|hé} *hé* rises, like {和|hé} *hé* (and); {喝|hē} *hē* (to drink) is level.
- {海|hǎi} *hǎi* dips; {还|hái} *hái* (still) rises.
- {草|cǎo} *cǎo*: *c* is "ts" with a puff of air. {早|zǎo} *zǎo* (early) has no puff.
- {树|shù} *shù* falls; {书|shū} *shū* (book) is level.
- {羊|yáng} *yáng* rises, {养|yǎng} *yǎng* dips: {养|yǎng}{羊|yáng} *yǎng yáng*, to keep sheep.
- {爬|pá} *pá* rises; {怕|pà} *pà* (to fear, lesson 24) falls.
- {大熊猫|dà xióng māo} *dàxióngmāo*: falling, rising, level. *xiong* rhymes roughly with "young".

## Common mistakes

- ~~{一|yí}{个|gè}{牛|niú}~~, ~~{一|yí}{个|gè}{树|shù}~~: animals and plants have their own measure words: {一|yì}{头|tóu}{牛|niú}, {一|yì}{棵|kē}{树|shù} (and {一|yì}{只|zhī}{羊|yáng},
  {一|yì}{条|tiáo}{河|hé}).
- ~~{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{狗|gǒu}~~ for a pet: {我|wǒ}{养|yǎng}{了|le}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu} (or {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}).
- ~~{在|zài}{山上|shān shàng}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}~~: in the existential sentence the place comes first without {在|zài}: {山上|shān shàng}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}.
- {爬|pá}{山|shān} isn't rock-climbing: in everyday Chinese it's a hike up a hill or a mountain, often on steps.
- ~~{花|huā}{开花|kāi huā}{了|le}~~: either {花|huā}{开|kāi}{了|le} or {开|kāi}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}.
- {树|shù} *shū* or {草|cǎo} *zǎo*: watch the tones and the initials.

## Key points

- {山|shān} ({座|zuò}), {河|hé} ({条|tiáo}), {海|hǎi}, {草|cǎo}, {草地|cǎo dì}, {树|shù} ({棵|kē}); {爬|pá} (to climb, to crawl), {爬|pá}{山|shān} (to go hiking).
- {公园|gōng yuán}, {花园|huā yuán}, {动物园|dòng wù yuán}; {开花|kāi huā} (to bloom: {花|huā}{开|kāi}{了|le}, {开|kāi}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}).
- {动物|dòng wù}: {一|yì}{匹|pǐ}{马|mǎ}, {一|yì}{头|tóu}{牛|niú}, {一|yì}{只|zhī}{羊|yáng}, {一|yì}{只|zhī}{鸡|jī}, {一|yì}{只|zhī}{大熊猫|dà xióng māo}. {一|yì}{只|zhī} is the general way to count animals.
- {养|yǎng} + animal or plant: to keep, to raise ({养|yǎng}{狗|gǒu}, {养|yǎng}{花|huā}).
- Existential {着|zhe}: {山上|shān shàng}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}, {河边|hé biān}{坐|zuò}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}.
- {环境|huán jìng}: the natural environment too ({保护环境|bǎo hù huán jìng}, to protect the environment).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: The Silk Road
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This module has been about roads, directions and travel. Its first honors lesson follows the most
famous set of roads in Chinese history: the routes that, from about two thousand years ago,
linked China with Central Asia and the lands beyond. You'll read about the name, the envoy who
opened the way, what travelled along the roads, and the oasis town of Dunhuang. You'll meet a few
words outside the course; they're glossed where they come and listed at the end.

## Many roads, and a young name

The Silk Road was never one road. It was a network of routes, over mountains and along the edges
of deserts, from the old Chinese capital Chang'an ({长安|Cháng'ān}, today's Xi'an, lesson 14) westwards
to Central Asia, Persia, India and the Mediterranean, with sea routes too. Few traders went the
whole way: goods passed from hand to hand, city to city.

The name is much younger than the roads. It became popular after the German geographer Ferdinand
von Richthofen used *Seidenstraße*, "silk road", in 1877; historians have since found the word in
German books some decades earlier. Chinese took the name over as {丝绸之路|sī chóu zhī lù} ({丝绸|sī chóu} is
silk, and {之|zhī} is the written {的|de}). So when you read that "people travelled the Silk Road" two
thousand years ago, remember that they didn't call it that.

## Zhang Qian opens the way

The roads begin, in the Chinese telling, with {张骞|Zhāng Qiān} (Zhang Qian), an official of the Han
dynasty. In 138 BCE Emperor Wu of Han sent him west to find allies against the Xiongnu, a
powerful people of the northern steppes. On the way the Xiongnu captured him and held him for
more than ten years. He escaped, went on west and reached the kingdoms of Central Asia: Dayuan (in
the Ferghana valley), Kangju and Daxia (Bactria), and the Yuezhi he had been sent to find. They
didn't want a war, but Zhang Qian came home in about 126 or 125 BCE with what the court had never had:
first-hand reports of rich, settled countries in the west.

He told of the fine horses of Dayuan, which the emperor wanted badly. Missions and trade
followed, and so did armies. Chinese histories credit Zhang Qian with opening up the way to the
"Western Regions".

## What travelled

| Westwards | Eastwards |
|---|---|
| silk (the cloth the West couldn't make) | horses from Central Asia |
| later, paper and the ways to make it | alfalfa (horse fodder), grapes and other plants |
| | glass, silver, and spices |
| | Buddhism, which came to China along these routes |

Ideas, religions, music and art travelled with the goods. Buddhism reached China from India by
these roads in the first centuries CE, and Buddhist monks and pilgrims went along them in both
directions.

## Dunhuang and the Mogao Caves

{敦煌|Dūn huáng} (Dunhuang) is an oasis town in Gansu province, in the northwest of China, where
the routes divided to go round the deserts. Travellers stopped there to rest and pray before the
hard part of the journey.

Near the town, in a cliff, are the Mogao Caves ({莫高窟|Mò gāo kū}). Buddhist monks began cutting caves
there in 366 CE, and for about a thousand years, to the 14th century, people kept making new ones
and painting them. UNESCO counts 492 caves with art, about 45,000 square metres of wall
paintings and more than 2,000 painted statues; the caves became a World Heritage Site in 1987. In
1900 a sealed room full of old manuscripts was found there, among them a copy of the Diamond
Sutra printed in 868, the oldest dated printed book known.

In 2014 UNESCO also listed a network of 33 Silk Road sites along about 5,000 kilometres of routes
between Chang'an and the Tianshan mountains, shared by China, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.

## Reading: the roads to the west

> {两千多年前|liǎng qiān duō nián qián}，{从|cóng}{中国|Zhōng guó}{的|de}{长安|Cháng'ān}{往|wǎng}{西|xī}，{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{条|tiáo}{路|lù}。{商人们|shāng rén men}{骑|qí}{着|zhe}{马|mǎ}{和|hé}{骆驼|luò tuo}，{带|dài}{着|zhe}{丝绸|sī chóu}{往|wǎng}{西|xī}{走|zǒu}，{经过|jīng guò}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{国家|guó jiā}。{路上|lù shang}{有|yǒu}{山|shān}，{有|yǒu}{河|hé}，{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{沙漠|shā mò}，{白天|bái tiān}{热|rè}{极|jí}{了|le}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}。{他们|tā men}{从|cóng}{西方|xī fāng}{带回来|dài huí lai}{马|mǎ}、{葡萄|pú tao}{和|hé}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{新东西|xīn dōng xi}。{敦煌|Dūn huáng}{是|shì}{路上|lù shang}{一|yí}{个|gè}{有名|yǒu míng}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}，{那儿|nàr}{的|de}{山|shān}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{洞|dòng}，{洞里|dòng lǐ}{有|yǒu}{一千多年前|yì qiān duō nián qián}{的|de}{画儿|huàr}。{现在|xiàn zài}，{世界上|shì jiè shàng}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{游客|yóu kè}{都|dōu}{来|lái}{敦煌|Dūn huáng}{看|kàn}{这些|zhè xiē}{画儿|huàr}。“{丝绸之路|sī chóu zhī lù}”{这个|zhè ge}{名字|míng zi}{没有|méi yǒu}{那么|nà me}{老|lǎo}，{是|shì}{一百多年前|yì bǎi duō nián qián}{的|de}{人|rén}{起|qǐ}{的|de}。

New words: {商人|shāng rén} (trader, merchant), {骆驼|luò tuo} (camel), {丝绸|sī chóu} (silk), {沙漠|shā mò}
(desert), {葡萄|pú tao} (grapes), {洞|dòng} (cave), {起|qǐ} (here: to give a name). {两千多年前|liǎng qiān duō nián qián} is "more than two
thousand years ago"; {带回来|dài huí lai} is "to bring back".

1. What did the traders ride?
2. What was the weather like on the way?
3. What is in the caves at Dunhuang?
4. What does the last sentence say about the name?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Horses and camels ({骑|qí}{着|zhe}{马|mǎ}{和|hé}{骆驼|luò tuo}).
2. Very hot in the day and cold at night ({白天|bái tiān}{热|rè}{极|jí}{了|le}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}).
3. Paintings more than a thousand years old ({一千多年前|yì qiān duō nián qián}{的|de}{画儿|huàr}).
4. That it isn't so old: people gave it a little over a hundred years ago ({是|shì}{一百多年前|yì bǎi duō nián qián}{的|de}{人|rén}{起|qǐ}{的|de}).

"More than two thousand years ago, there were many roads going west from Chang'an in China.
Traders rode horses and camels, carrying silk westwards and passing through many countries. On
the way there were mountains, rivers and great deserts, scorching by day and cold at night. From
the West they brought back horses, grapes and many new things. Dunhuang was a famous place on the
way: in its hills there are many caves, and in the caves there are paintings more than a
thousand years old. Today, lots of tourists from all over the world come to Dunhuang to see these
paintings. The name 'Silk Road' isn't so old: people gave it a little over a hundred years ago."
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{丝绸之路|sī chóu zhī lù}{不|bú}{是|shì}{一|yì}{条|tiáo}{路|lù}，{是|shì}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{条|tiáo}{路|lù}。
= The Silk Road wasn't one road but many.
{商人们|shāng rén men}{骑|qí}{着|zhe}{骆驼|luò tuo}{往|wǎng}{西|xī}{走|zǒu}。
= The traders rode west on camels.
{敦煌|Dūn huáng}{的|de}{洞里|dòng lǐ}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{画儿|huàr}。
= There are many paintings in the caves at Dunhuang.
```

## Words in this lesson

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {丝绸之路|sī chóu zhī lù} | the Silk Road |
| {丝绸|sī chóu} | silk |
| {长安|Cháng'ān} | Chang'an (today's Xi'an) |
| {张骞|Zhāng Qiān} | Zhang Qian |
| {敦煌|Dūn huáng} | Dunhuang |
| {莫高窟|Mò gāo kū} | the Mogao Caves |
| {商人|shāng rén} | trader, merchant |
| {骆驼|luò tuo} | camel |
| {沙漠|shā mò} | desert |
| {葡萄|pú tao} | grapes |
| {洞|dòng} | cave, hole |

These words aren't part of your vocabulary reviews; the lesson's own words are all from the core
lessons.

## Key points

- The Silk Road was a network of routes from Chang'an (Xi'an) to Central Asia and beyond, from
  about two thousand years ago; the name dates from the 19th century.
- Zhang Qian, sent west by Emperor Wu of Han in 138 BCE, was held by the Xiongnu for more than
  ten years and came back in about 126–125 BCE with reports of the western kingdoms.
- Silk went west; horses, plants such as alfalfa and grapes, and Buddhism came east.
- Dunhuang, an oasis in Gansu, has the Mogao Caves: begun in 366 CE, painted for a thousand years,
  a World Heritage Site since 1987.

lessons.title: Giant pandas
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 15 gave you {大熊猫|dà xióng māo}, "the big bear-cat". This honors lesson is about the animal itself: where
it lives, what it eats, how its numbers fell and rose, and where you can see one. The figures
come from surveys and conservation bodies, with their dates, because numbers like these change.
A few words outside the course are glossed where they come and listed at the end.

## A bear that eats bamboo

The giant panda is a black-and-white bear. In the wild it lives only in China, in the mountains
of three provinces of western and central China: Sichuan
({四川|Sì chuān}), Shaanxi ({陕西|Shǎn xī}) and Gansu ({甘肃|Gān sù}). Its home is the cool, wet bamboo forest on the
mountain slopes.

Pandas belong to the order of meat-eaters, but bamboo ({竹子|zhú zi}) makes up about 99 percent of what
they eat. Bamboo gives little energy, so a panda spends around twelve hours a day eating, and
much of the rest resting. They climb trees well and can swim.

In Chinese the name is {大熊猫|dà xióng māo} or just {熊猫|xióng māo}. Don't confuse it with the {小熊猫|xiǎo xióng māo} ("little bear-cat"), the
red panda, a smaller reddish animal of the same mountains that isn't a bear at all.

## Fewer, then more

In the 20th century pandas lost much of their forest to farms, roads and logging, and their
numbers fell. China has counted its wild pandas in national surveys since the 1970s. The fourth
survey, announced in 2015, found 1,864 in the wild (a minimum estimate). Later official reports
speak of nearly 1,900.

What changed things was protecting the forests: nature reserves, a ban on logging in much of the
pandas' range, and replanting. In 2021 several reserves were joined into the Giant Panda National
Park ({大熊猫国家公园|Dà xióng māo Guó jiā Gōng yuán}), across Sichuan, Shaanxi and Gansu, which takes in about 70 percent of the
pandas' wild habitat.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) moved the giant panda on its Red List
from "endangered" to "vulnerable" in 2016, and China's own Ministry of Ecology and Environment did
the same in July 2021. "Vulnerable" still means at risk: the forests are split into separate
patches, and a warmer climate could make bamboo harder to find.

## Breeding centres

Many pandas live in breeding and research centres, where scientists study them and raise cubs;
some young pandas are later trained for life in the wild and released. The best-known centre is
in Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan: the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding
({成都大熊猫繁育研究基地|Chéng dū Dà xióng māo Fán yù Yán jiū Jī dì}, "the panda base" for short), founded in 1987 with six pandas rescued
from the wild. Today it is one of the city's most visited sights. Pandas also live in zoos in
other countries, on loan from China for research and breeding programmes.

## Reading: a visit to the panda base

> {上|shàng}{个|gè}{月|yuè}，{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{朋友|péng you}{一块儿|yí kuàir}{去|qù}{了|le}{四川|Sì chuān}{的|de}{成都|Chéng dū}。{成都|Chéng dū}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{很|hěn}{有名|yǒu míng}{的|de}{城市|chéng shì}，{那儿|nàr}{的|de}{菜|cài}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}，{大熊猫|dà xióng māo}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{有名|yǒu míng}。{我们|wǒ men}{早上|zǎo shang}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}{熊猫基地|xióng māo jī dì}，{因为|yīn wèi}{大熊猫|dà xióng māo}{早上|zǎo shang}{吃|chī}{东西|dōng xi}，{下午|xià wǔ}{常常|cháng cháng}{在|zài}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。{基地|jī dì}{里|lǐ}{树|shù}{很|hěn}{多|duō}，{环境|huán jìng}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{很|hěn}{安静|ān jìng}。{我们|wǒ men}{看见|kàn jiàn}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{大熊猫|dà xióng māo}{坐|zuò}{在|zài}{地|dì}{上|shàng}，{一边|yì biān}{吃|chī}{竹子|zhú zi}{一边|yì biān}{看|kàn}{我们|wǒ men}，{好像|hǎo xiàng}{在|zài}{说|shuō}：“{你们|nǐ men}{好|hǎo}！”{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{熊猫宝宝|xióng māo bǎo bao}{在|zài}{树|shù}{上|shàng}{玩儿|wánr}。{朋友|péng you}{拍|pāi}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{照片|zhào piàn}。{基地|jī dì}{的|de}{人|rén}{告诉|gào su}{我们|wǒ men}，{野生|yě shēng}{的|de}{大熊猫|dà xióng māo}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{四川|Sì chuān}、{陕西|Shǎn xī}{和|hé}{甘肃|Gān sù}{的|de}{山|shān}{里|lǐ}，{现在|xiàn zài}{比|bǐ}{以前|yǐ qián}{多|duō}{了|le}。{我们|wǒ men}{越|yuè}{看|kàn}{越|yuè}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{它们|tā men}！

New words: {成都|Chéng dū} (Chengdu), {熊猫基地|xióng māo jī dì} (the panda base), {竹子|zhú zi} (bamboo), {野生|yě shēng}
(wild), {四川|Sì chuān}, {陕西|Shǎn xī} and {甘肃|Gān sù} (three provinces), and {熊猫宝宝|xióng māo bǎo bao} (panda cubs: "panda babies"). {常常|cháng cháng} (often) and
{以前|yǐ qián} (before) are words of lessons 27 and 25.

1. Why did the writer arrive at eight in the morning?
2. What was the giant panda doing?
3. Where do wild pandas live?
4. How did the visit make the writer and the friend feel?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Pandas eat in the morning and often sleep in the afternoon ({大熊猫|dà xióng māo}{早上|zǎo shang}{吃|chī}{东西|dōng xi}，{下午|xià wǔ}{常常|cháng cháng}{在|zài}{睡觉|shuì jiào}).
2. Sitting on the ground, eating bamboo and looking at them ({坐|zuò}{在|zài}{地|dì}{上|shàng}，{一边|yì biān}{吃|chī}{竹子|zhú zi}{一边|yì biān}{看|kàn}{我们|wǒ men}).
3. In the mountains of Sichuan, Shaanxi and Gansu.
4. The more they watched, the more they liked the pandas ({我们|wǒ men}{越|yuè}{看|kàn}{越|yuè}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{它们|tā men}).

"Last month a friend and I went to Chengdu in Sichuan. Chengdu is a famous city: the food there is
delicious, and its giant pandas are famous too. We got to the panda base at eight in the morning,
because pandas eat in the morning and are often asleep in the afternoon. There are lots of trees
at the base; it's a lovely, quiet place. We saw a giant panda sitting on the ground, eating
bamboo and looking at us, as if to say, 'Hello!' Two panda cubs were playing in a tree. My
friend took lots of photos. The people at the base told us that wild giant pandas live in the
mountains of Sichuan, Shaanxi and Gansu, and that there are more of them now than before. The
more we watched them, the more we liked them!"
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{大熊猫|dà xióng māo}{很|hěn}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{竹子|zhú zi}。
= Giant pandas love bamboo.
{野生|yě shēng}{的|de}{大熊猫|dà xióng māo}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{四川|Sì chuān}、{陕西|Shǎn xī}{和|hé}{甘肃|Gān sù}{的|de}{山|shān}{里|lǐ}。
= Wild giant pandas live in the mountains of Sichuan, Shaanxi and Gansu.
{我们|wǒ men}{越|yuè}{看|kàn}{越|yuè}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{它们|tā men}！
= The more we watched them, the more we liked them!
```

## Words in this lesson

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {竹子|zhú zi} | bamboo |
| {野生|yě shēng} | wild |
| {小熊猫|xiǎo xióng māo} | red panda |
| {熊猫宝宝|xióng māo bǎo bao} | panda cub |
| {熊猫基地|xióng māo jī dì} | the panda base (breeding centre) |
| {四川|Sì chuān} | Sichuan |
| {陕西|Shǎn xī} | Shaanxi |
| {甘肃|Gān sù} | Gansu |
| {成都|Chéng dū} | Chengdu |

These words aren't part of your vocabulary reviews.

## Key points

- Giant pandas ({大熊猫|dà xióng māo}, {熊猫|xióng māo}) live in the wild only in the mountains of Sichuan, Shaanxi and Gansu.
- Bamboo is about 99 percent of their food; they eat for around twelve hours a day.
- The fourth national survey (announced 2015) counted 1,864 wild pandas; later reports say nearly 1,900.
- The IUCN moved them from "endangered" to "vulnerable" in 2016; China did the same in 2021, the
  year the Giant Panda National Park was set up.
- The Chengdu panda base was founded in 1987 with six rescued pandas.

lessons.title: In the classroom: verb measure words
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This module is about school, work and messages: the classroom, school subjects and results,
understanding and giving opinions, the office, and emails and the news. It starts in the
classroom. In HSK 1 and HSK 2 you learned {上课|shàng kè}, {下课|xià kè}, {课|kè}, {同学|tóng xué}, {教室|jiào shì}, {班|bān}, {本子|běn zi}, {笔|bǐ} and {作|zuò} in {工作|gōng zuò}.
Now you get the rest of a school day: the textbook and its pages, the text and its sentences,
dictionaries, notes and homework, and the moment school is out.

The grammar is a small set of words that count actions instead of things. HSK 2 gave you one of
them, {次|cì} ({我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}, "I've been twice"). This lesson adds {遍|biàn} and {下|xià} and shows where all three go in a
sentence:

- **[[verb measure words]]** {次|cì}, {遍|biàn} and {下|xià}: {去|qù}{过|guo}{三|sān}{次|cì}, {读|dú}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}, {看|kàn}{一下|yí xià};
- {遍|biàn}: one time through, from beginning to end ({再|zài}{说|shuō}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}, "say it again");
- where the object goes: {读|dú}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}{课文|kè wén}, {见|jiàn}{过|guo}{他|tā}{一|yí}{次|cì}, {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn};
- {页|yè} (page: {第|dì}{十|shí}{页|yè}), {年级|nián jí}, {班级|bān jí}, {学期|xué qī} and {初中|chū zhōng};
- {课本|kè běn}, {课文|kè wén}, {句子|jù zi} and {句|jù} ({一|yí}{句|jù}{话|huà}, "one sentence");
- {词典|cí diǎn} and {字典|zì diǎn}, {笔记|bǐ jì} and {笔记本|bǐ jì běn}, {铅笔|qiān bǐ}, {黑板|hēi bǎn}, {纸|zhǐ}, {作业|zuò yè} and {放学|fàng xué}.

## Counting actions: verb measure words

A measure word for things goes between a number and a noun: {一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}, {三|sān}{个|gè}{人|rén}. Chinese also counts
actions, and for that it has verb measure words. They go after the verb, with the number in
front of them, and say how many times the action happens. You already know the commonest one:

{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}{北京|Běi jīng}。 — I've been to Beijing twice.

{这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{过|guo}{三|sān}{次|cì}。 — I've seen this film three times.

The number + measure word comes after the verb and after {了|le} or {过|guo}. That's the opposite of English
word order in one way: English can put "twice" at the very end, Chinese keeps it next to the
verb. HSK 3 has three verb measure words:

| Verb measure word | Counts | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {次|cì} | times, occasions | {我|wǒ}{来|lái}{过|guo}{三|sān}{次|cì}。 I've been here three times. |
| {遍|biàn} | times through, from beginning to end | {请|qǐng}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。 Please say it again. |
| {下|xià} | quick, short actions (with {一|yī}: "briefly, have a go") | {你|nǐ}{看|kàn}{一下|yí xià}。 Have a look. |

### {遍|biàn}: from beginning to end

{遍|biàn} counts an action done all the way through: reading a text, listening to a recording, saying
a sentence, watching a film from start to finish.

{这|zhè}{篇|piān}{课文|kè wén}{我|wǒ}{读|dú}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}。 — I read this text three times (through).

{老师|lǎo shī}，{请|qǐng}{您|nín}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。 — Could you say that again, please?

{这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}，{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}。 — This film is great: I watched it twice.

({篇|piān} *piān* is the measure word for texts and articles; it isn't in HSK 3, so you'll mostly see
{这个|zhè ge}{课文|kè wén} or just {课文|kè wén} in this course.)

{次|cì} and {遍|biàn} both translate as "times". The difference is what they count. {次|cì} counts occasions: each
time something happens, whether it's finished or not. {遍|biàn} counts complete runs through something
that has a beginning and an end. So you can go somewhere three {次|cì}, but never three {遍|biàn}, because a
visit has no "start to finish" to go through:

{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{三|sān}{次|cì}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 — I've been to Shanghai three times. (×{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}{上海|Shàng hǎi})

{这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi}{我|wǒ}{写|xiě}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}。 — I wrote this sentence out three times.

With a text or a film either word can be right, with a small difference: {这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì} says
"on two occasions", {这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn} "twice through".

The most useful sentence with {遍|biàn} is the request to hear something again: {请|qǐng}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{一|yí}{遍|biàn} (please say
it again). {再|zài} (again) goes before the verb, {一|yí}{遍|biàn} after it. In class you'll also hear {再|zài}{读|dú}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}
(read it again) and {再|zài}{听|tīng}{一|yí}{遍|biàn} (listen again).

### {下|xià}: a quick action

{下|xià} counts short, quick actions: knocks, claps, taps. {他|tā}{拍|pāi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{下|xià}{手|shǒu} is "he clapped twice" ({拍|pāi}
*pāi*: to clap, to pat; you know the character from {拍照|pāi zhào}). Most often you'll meet it with {一|yī}, as
{一下|yí xià} (HSK 1): after a verb it makes the action brief and the request softer.

{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}{一下|yí xià}{这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi}。 — Have a look at this sentence.

{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{一下|yí xià}。 — Let me think for a moment.

{请|qǐng}{等|děng}{一下|yí xià}。 — Wait a moment, please.

{一下|yí xià} doesn't count anything here: it means "a bit, for a moment". It works like the verb
reduplication of HSK 2: {看|kàn}{一下|yí xià} and {看|kàn}{看|kàn} are both "have a look".

### Where the object goes

When the verb has an object, the number + measure word can go before it or after it, depending
on what the object is.

- An ordinary noun object usually goes after the measure word: verb + {了|le} / {过|guo} + number +
  measure word + object.

  {我|wǒ}{读|dú}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}{课文|kè wén}。 — I read the text twice.

  {他|tā}{去|qù}{过|guo}{一|yí}{次|cì}{中国|Zhōng guó}。 — He's been to China once.

- A pronoun object ({我|wǒ}, {你|nǐ}, {他|tā}, {它|tā}…) goes before the number: verb + pronoun + number +
  measure word.

  {我|wǒ}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}{他|tā}{一|yí}{次|cì}。 — I've met him once.

  {老师|lǎo shī}{叫|jiào}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}。 — The teacher called you twice.

- A place name can go either way: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{北京|Běi jīng}{两|liǎng}{次|cì} and {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}{北京|Běi jīng} are both fine.

- A longer object, or one with {这|zhè} / {那|nà}, often moves to the front as the topic, or goes after
  {把|bǎ} (lesson 03):

  {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}。 — I've read this book three times.

  {请|qǐng}{把|bǎ}{这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi}{读|dú}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。 — Please read this sentence once (through).

To ask "how many times?", put {几|jǐ} in front of the measure word: {你|nǐ}{看|kàn}{了|le}{几|jǐ}{遍|biàn}？ (how many times did you
read it?), {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{几|jǐ}{次|cì}？ (how many times have you been?). And {第|dì} makes an ordinal of it: {第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}
(the first time), {第|dì}{二|èr}{遍|biàn} (the second time through).

{这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{来|lái}{中国|Zhōng guó}。 — This is my first time in China.

## A school day

### Grades, classes and terms

Most of China's schools have six years of {小学|xiǎo xué} (primary school), three of {初中|chū zhōng} (junior high school) and
three of {高中|gāo zhōng} (senior high school). {初中|chū zhōng} is short for {初级中学|chū jí zhōng xué} ("first-level secondary school"):
{初|chū} means "beginning". The years are counted with {年级|nián jí} (grade, year):

{我|wǒ}{上|shàng}{初中|chū zhōng}{二|èr}{年级|nián jí}。 — I'm in the second year of junior high.

{她|tā}{是|shì}{三|sān}{年级|nián jí}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}。 — She's in year three.

People shorten these in speech: {初二|chū èr} is the second year of junior high, {高一|gāo yī} the first year of
senior high.

{班级|bān jí} is a class as a unit of the school, the group a student belongs to; {班|bān} (HSK 2) means the same
and is the usual word in speech. {班级|bān jí} is the more formal, written word; in counting and names
you say {班|bān}: {我们|wǒ men}{班|bān}, {三|sān}{年级|nián jí}{二|èr}{班|bān} (year three, class two).

{学期|xué qī} is a school term or semester. Chinese schools and universities have two in a year:

{这个|zhè ge}{学期|xué qī}{我们|wǒ men}{有|yǒu}{六|liù}{门|mén}{课|kè}。 — We have six subjects this term. ({门|mén} *mén*: the measure word for courses)

### Textbooks, texts and sentences

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {课本|kè běn} | textbook | {请|qǐng}{打开|dǎ kāi}{课本|kè běn}。 Please open your textbooks. |
| {课文|kè wén} | the text of a lesson | {我们|wǒ men}{一起|yì qǐ}{读|dú}{课文|kè wén}。 Let's read the text together. |
| {页|yè} | page (a measure word) | {请|qǐng}{看|kàn}{第|dì}{二十|èr shí}{页|yè}。 Please look at page twenty. |
| {句子|jù zi} | sentence | {这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}。 This sentence is very long. |
| {句|jù} | measure word for sentences and lines | {他|tā}{说|shuō}{了|le}{一|yí}{句|jù}{话|huà}。 He said a sentence (a few words). |

{页|yè} counts pages and numbers them: {一|yí}{页|yè} (one page), {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{有|yǒu}{三百|sān bǎi}{页|yè} (this book has three hundred pages),
{第|dì}{十|shí}{页|yè} (page ten). Unlike {次|cì} or {遍|biàn} it's a measure word for things, before a noun or alone.

{句|jù} is a measure word: {一|yí}{句|jù}{话|huà} is "one sentence, a remark", and {我|wǒ}{说|shuō}{两|liǎng}{句|jù} is a modest "let me say a few
words". {句子|jù zi} is the noun: {这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi} (this sentence), {写|xiě}{句子|jù zi} (write sentences). Don't put a measure word
in front of {句|jù}: you say {一|yí}{句|jù}{话|huà} or {一|yí}{个|gè}{句子|jù zi}, never ×{一|yí}{个|gè}{句|jù}.

### Dictionaries

| Word | What it lists | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {词典|cí diǎn} | words (and their meanings) | {这个|zhè ge}{词|cí}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{词典|cí diǎn}{里|lǐ}{查|chá}{了|le}。 I looked this word up in the dictionary. |
| {字典|zì diǎn} | characters, one by one | {这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{字典|zì diǎn}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}。 This character is in the character dictionary. |

Since a {字|zì} is a single character and a {词|cí} a word (HSK 2), a {字典|zì diǎn} explains characters and a {词典|cí diǎn} explains
words. Most learners use a {词典|cí diǎn}, today usually an app on the phone ({手机|shǒu jī}{词典|cí diǎn}). {查|chá} (lesson 09) is
"to look up".

### Notes, paper, pencils and the board

- {笔记|bǐ jì} are notes you write while studying: {记|jì}{笔记|bǐ jì} or {做|zuò}{笔记|bǐ jì} is "to take notes" ({记|jì} is lesson 18's word).
- {笔记本|bǐ jì běn} is a notebook for notes, and also a laptop ({笔记本|bǐ jì běn}{电脑|diàn nǎo}, "notebook computer"): context
  tells you which. {本子|běn zi} (HSK 2) is any notebook or exercise book.
- {铅笔|qiān bǐ} is a pencil: {铅|qiān} is lead, {笔|bǐ} a pen. Its measure word is {支|zhī} *zhī* ({一|yì}{支|zhī}{铅笔|qiān bǐ}), outside HSK 3.
- {纸|zhǐ} is paper; a sheet is {一|yì}{张|zhāng}{纸|zhǐ} ({张|zhāng}: lesson 09).
- {黑板|hēi bǎn} is the blackboard: {老师|lǎo shī}{在|zài}{黑板|hēi bǎn}{上|shàng}{写|xiě}{字|zì} (the teacher writes on the board).

### Homework and the end of the day

{作业|zuò yè} is homework, and {做|zuò}{作业|zuò yè} or {写|xiě}{作业|zuò yè} is "to do homework". {放学|fàng xué} is "school is out" (to finish
school for the day): its subject is the pupils or the school, never a teacher.

{我们|wǒ men}{下午|xià wǔ}{四|sì}{点|diǎn}{放学|fàng xué}。 — We finish school at four in the afternoon.

{放学|fàng xué}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{回家|huí jiā}{吧|ba}！ — School's out: let's go home!

{放学|fàng xué} is for school pupils. Students at university just say {下课|xià kè} (class is over) or {没|méi}{课|kè}{了|le} (no more
classes).

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 级 (traditional 級) | grade, level | jí | 纟 | 6 | {年级|nián jí}, {班级|bān jí} |
| 初 | beginning | chū | 刀 | 7 | {初中|chū zhōng} |
| 句 | sentence | jù | 口 | 5 | {句子|jù zi}, {句|jù} |
| 典 | standard work; dictionary | diǎn | 八 | 8 | {词典|cí diǎn}, {字典|zì diǎn} |
| 铅 (traditional 鉛) | lead (the metal) | qiān | 钅 | 10 | {铅笔|qiān bǐ} |
| 板 | board | bǎn | 木 | 8 | {黑板|hēi bǎn} |
| 业 (traditional 業) | work, business | yè | 一 | 5 | {作业|zuò yè} |
| 页 (traditional 頁) | page | yè | 页 | 6 | {页|yè} |

| 纸 (traditional 紙) | paper | zhǐ | 纟 | 7 | {纸|zhǐ}, {报纸|bào zhǐ} (lesson 20) |

- {级|jí}: 纟 (silk) on the left and {及|jí} on the right, which gives the sound: jí. The same part is in {极|jí}
  (extremely, lesson 12). Silk threads come in grades: a memory aid for the meaning.
- {初|chū}: 衤 (clothing) and {刀|dāo} (knife). Cutting the cloth is the first step in making clothes, and
  that is the old explanation of the character: "the beginning". Make Me a Hanzi files it under
  {刀|dāo}; most dictionaries put it under 衤. Don't confuse 衤 (clothing: five strokes) with 礻
  (four strokes).
- {句|jù}: 勹 (a wrapping stroke) around 口 (mouth). Dictionaries file it under 口 or 勹.
- {典|diǎn}: the oldest forms show books (bundles of bamboo strips) on a stand or held in two hands: an
  important book, a classic. That's why it ends both {词典|cí diǎn} and {字典|zì diǎn}.
- {铅|qiān}: 钅 (metal) on the left: lead is a metal. Pencils were once thought to have lead in them, and
  the name stuck.
- {板|bǎn}: 木 (wood) and {反|fǎn}, which gives the sound -an. {反|fǎn} is also in {饭|fàn} (meal): with the food radical
  饣 it's fàn, with wood it's bǎn. In {黑板|hēi bǎn} the traditional form is the same, {板|bǎn}; the {板|bǎn} of {老板|lǎo bǎn}
  (boss) is {闆|bǎn} in traditional writing, a different character.
- {业|yè}: the simplified form keeps the top of traditional {業|yè} and drops the rest. Make Me a Hanzi files
  it under 一; many dictionaries give {业|yè} a radical of its own.
- {页|yè}: in its oldest forms a drawing of a head with hair on top. It is the radical of {题|tí} (HSK 1) and
  {颜|yán} ({颜色|yán sè}, HSK 2), characters that once had to do with the head or the face; "page" is a later
  meaning that borrowed the character.
- {遍|biàn}: 辶 (walking) around {扁|biǎn} (flat), which gives the sound: biàn. "Walking all over a place" is
  the old meaning, and "once through" comes from it.
- {纸|zhǐ}: 纟 (silk) and {氏|shì}. The character is older than paper as we know it: it first meant a sheet
  of silk waste, which is why it has the silk radical. {氏|shì} gave the sound in old Chinese, but it
  doesn't match zhǐ today, so don't rely on it.

### Phonetic components: {反|fǎn} and {及|jí}

A character with a meaning part and a sound part is the most common kind (HSK 1 honors 05h2).
As in the earlier modules, the character sections point out sound parts that come back again
and again. Two from this lesson:

| Sound part | Characters | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| 反 fǎn | {饭|fàn} (meal), {板|bǎn} (board) | fàn, bǎn |
| 及 jí | {级|jí} (grade), {极|jí} (extremely) | jí, jí |

The sound part gives the syllable, sometimes with a different initial or tone (fǎn, fàn, bǎn).
It's a hint for remembering, not a rule: always learn the reading with the word.

### Stroke order

- **级**: 纟 first (two bent strokes and a rising stroke), then 及: the slash, a stroke that
  turns back and forth, and the long falling stroke to the right.
- **业**: the two short verticals in the middle first, then the dot on the left and the slash on the
  right, and the long horizontal at the bottom last.
- **页**: the top horizontal first, then the short slash, the box-like part (vertical, turn), the
  inner slash and the dot.
- **遍**: 扁 first (户 on top, then the part below with its short verticals), and 辶 last:
  dot, the bent stroke, the long sweep, as in {这|zhè} and {边|biān}.

These HSK 1 handwriting characters are all over this lesson. Write each three times from

In traditional script the pads show {+{写|xiě}+} (15 strokes) and {+{习|xí}+} (11); {作|zuò} and {文|wén} are the same.

## Dialogue: in class

{王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī} (王老师, Teacher Wang) is starting a lesson. {大卫|Dà wèi} (大卫, David) and {安娜|Ān nà} (安娜, Anna) are
in her class.

```dialogue
# In class
王老师: {同学们|tóng xué men}{好|hǎo}！{今天|jīn tiān}{我们|wǒ men}{学习|xué xí}{第|dì}{十六|shí liù}{课|kè}。{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{打开|dǎ kāi}{课本|kè běn}，{看|kàn}{第|dì}{一百二十|yì bǎi èr shí}{页|yè}。
= Good morning, everyone! Today we're doing lesson sixteen. Please open your textbooks at page one hundred and twenty.
大卫: {老师|lǎo shī}，{对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{的|de}{课本|kè běn}{忘|wàng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{了|le}。
= Sorry, I've left my textbook at home.
王老师: {没关系|méi guān xi}，{你|nǐ}{跟|gēn}{安娜|Ān nà}{一起|yì qǐ}{看|kàn}{吧|ba}。{我们|wǒ men}{听|tīng}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}{课文|kè wén}。
= That's all right: share with Anna. We'll listen to the text twice.
王老师: {怎么样|zěn me yàng}？{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}{吗|ma}？
= Well? Did you understand it?
安娜: {听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。{老师|lǎo shī}，{请|qǐng}{您|nín}{再|zài}{放|fàng}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}，{好|hǎo}{吗|ma}？
= A little. Could you play it once more, please?
王老师: {好|hǎo}。……{这|zhè}{次|cì}{呢|ne}？
= All right. … How about this time?
大卫: {这|zhè}{次|cì}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}。
= This time I got it.
王老师: {很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。{现在|xiàn zài}{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{把|bǎ}{这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi}{写|xiě}{在|zài}{本子|běn zi}{上|shàng}。
= Very good. Now please write this sentence in your notebooks.
安娜: {老师|lǎo shī}，{这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{怎么|zěn me}{写|xiě}？{我|wǒ}{的|de}{词典|cí diǎn}{里|lǐ}{没有|méi yǒu}。
= How do you write this character? It isn't in my dictionary.
王老师: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{黑板|hēi bǎn}{上|shàng}{写|xiě}{一下|yí xià}。{你们|nǐ men}{看|kàn}，{一共|yí gòng}{九|jiǔ}{笔|bǐ}。
= I'll write it on the board. Look, nine strokes in all.
大卫: {老师|lǎo shī}，{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{作业|zuò yè}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}？
= What's today's homework?
王老师: {把|bǎ}{课文|kè wén}{读|dú}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}，{再|zài}{把|bǎ}{第|dì}{一百二十一|yì bǎi èr shí yī}{页|yè}{的|de}{句子|jù zi}{写|xiě}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}。{好|hǎo}，{今天|jīn tiān}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{这儿|zhèr}。{下课|xià kè}！
= Read the text three times, and write out the sentences on page one hundred and twenty-one twice. All right, that's it for today. Class dismissed!
```

- {同学们|tóng xué men} (classmates, students) is how teachers address a class, and {大家|dà jiā} (everyone) is in the next
  sentence too.
- {忘|wàng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{了|le}: {忘|wàng} (to forget) + {在|zài} + place, "left it at home".
- {再|zài}{放|fàng}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}: {放|fàng} is "to put", and also "to play" a recording. {再|zài} + verb + {一|yí}{遍|biàn} is "once more".
- {一共|yí gòng}{九|jiǔ}{笔|bǐ}: {笔|bǐ} (pen) also counts the strokes of a character.
- {今天|jīn tiān}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{这儿|zhèr} ("today it gets as far as here") is how a teacher ends a class.

## Reading: my dictionary

> {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{大卫|Dà wèi}，{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{一|yí}{个|gè}{学校|xué xiào}{学习|xué xí}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。{我们|wǒ men}{班|bān}{有|yǒu}{十二|shí èr}{个|gè}{学生|xué sheng}，{从|cóng}{星期|xīng qī}{一|yī}{到|dào}{星期|xīng qī}{五|wǔ}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{课|kè}，{上午|shàng wǔ}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{上课|shàng kè}，{十二|shí èr}{点|diǎn}{放学|fàng xué}。
>
> {上|shàng}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{三|sān}，{老师|lǎo shī}{让|ràng}{我们|wǒ men}{读|dú}{课本|kè běn}{第|dì}{四十五|sì shí wǔ}{页|yè}{的|de}{课文|kè wén}。{课文|kè wén}{不|bù}{长|cháng}，{一共|yí gòng}{十|shí}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{句子|jù zi}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{句子|jù zi}{也|yě}{看|kàn}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}。{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{查|chá}{词典|cí diǎn}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{词典|cí diǎn}{忘|wàng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{着急|zháo jí}。{我|wǒ}{旁边|páng biān}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}{安娜|Ān nà}{看见|kàn jiàn}{了|le}，{把|bǎ}{她|tā}{的|de}{词典|cí diǎn}{给|gěi}{了|le}{我|wǒ}。{她|tā}{还|hái}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}："{新|xīn}{的|de}{课文|kè wén}{要|yào}{多|duō}{读|dú}{几|jǐ}{遍|biàn}。{读|dú}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}，{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}；{读|dú}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}、{四|sì}{遍|biàn}，{你|nǐ}{就|jiù}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}。"
>
> {那|nà}{天|tiān}{放学|fàng xué}{回家|huí jiā}，{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{课文|kè wén}{读|dú}{了|le}{五|wǔ}{遍|biàn}，{还|hái}{把|bǎ}{不|bú}{认识|rèn shi}{的|de}{词|cí}{写|xiě}{在|zài}{了|le}{笔记本|bǐ jì běn}{上|shàng}，{一共|yí gòng}{写|xiě}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{页|yè}。{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{上课|shàng kè}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{老师|lǎo shī}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{读|dú}{课文|kè wén}。{我|wǒ}{读|dú}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}："{大卫|Dà wèi}，{你|nǐ}{读|dú}{得|de}{真|zhēn}{不错|bú cuò}！"{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。{现在|xiàn zài}{我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}{把|bǎ}{课文|kè wén}{读|dú}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}，{还|hái}{做|zuò}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{笔记|bǐ jì}，{我|wǒ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{好|hǎo}{了|le}。

1. What was the problem in class last Wednesday?
2. Why couldn't David look the words up?
3. What did he do at home that day?
4. What does he do every day now?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. The text wasn't long, but he couldn't understand a single sentence ({我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{句子|jù zi}{也|yě}{看|kàn}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}).
2. He had left his dictionary at home ({我|wǒ}{的|de}{词典|cí diǎn}{忘|wàng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{了|le}). Anna lent him hers.
3. He read the text five times and wrote the words he didn't know in his notebook: two pages.
4. He reads each text three times and takes lots of notes; his Chinese is getting better and better.

"My name is David, and I'm studying Chinese at a school in Beijing. There are twelve students in
our class. We have lessons from Monday to Friday: classes start at eight in the morning and
we finish at twelve.

Last Wednesday the teacher had us read the text on page forty-five of the textbook. The text
wasn't long, just a dozen or so sentences, but I couldn't understand a single one. I wanted to
look the words up, but I'd left my dictionary at home, and I got worried. My classmate Anna, who
sits next to me, saw this and gave me her dictionary. She also told me: 'You need to read a new
text several times. Read it once and you won't understand it; read it three or four times and
you will.'

When school finished that day I went home and read the text five times, and I wrote the words I
didn't know in my notebook: two pages in all. The next day in class the teacher asked me to read
the text. I read it well, and the teacher said: 'David, you read that really well!' I was very
happy. Now I read every text three times and take lots of notes, and my Chinese is getting
better and better."
</details>

## Write it: one or two sentences

Write one or two sentences in characters about your own studies. Use a verb measure word in
each: how many times you read or listen to a text, or how many times you've been somewhere.

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {每|měi}{个|gè}{课文|kè wén}{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{读|dú}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}。 — I read every text three times.
- {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}{中国|Zhōng guó}，{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{是|shì}{去年|qù nián}。 — I've been to China twice; the first time was last year.
- {我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{了|le}{四|sì}{遍|biàn}{课文|kè wén}，{现在|xiàn zài}{都|dōu}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}。 — I listened to the text four times, and now I understand all of it.

Check: is the number + {次|cì} / {遍|biàn} after the verb (and after {了|le} or {过|guo})? A pronoun object goes before
it ({见|jiàn}{过|guo}{他|tā}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}).
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# In class
{老师|lǎo shī}，{请|qǐng}{您|nín}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。
= Could you say that again, please?
{请|qǐng}{打开|dǎ kāi}{课本|kè běn}，{看|kàn}{第|dì}{二十|èr shí}{页|yè}。
= Please open your books at page twenty.
{这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi}{我|wǒ}{读|dú}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}。
= I read this sentence three times.
{这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{怎么|zěn me}{写|xiě}？
= How do you write this character?
{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{作业|zuò yè}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}？
= What's today's homework?
{我们|wǒ men}{四|sì}{点|diǎn}{放学|fàng xué}。
= We finish school at four.
```

## Pronunciation

- {遍|biàn} biàn and {变|biàn} biàn (to change, lesson 10) are the same syllable; {边|biān} biān is first tone.
- {页|yè} yè and {也|yě} yě (also): a falling tone for the page, a dipping one for "also".
- {句|jù} jù: the *u* after j is ü (lips rounded, tongue as for "ee").
- {纸|zhǐ} zhǐ: the same syllable as the first syllable of {只有|zhǐ yǒu} (only if, lesson 26). {词典|cí diǎn} cí diǎn and {字典|zì diǎn} zì diǎn differ in
  the first syllable's initial and tone: c (ts with a puff) rising, z (ts) falling.
- {笔记本|bǐ jì běn} bǐ jì běn: two third tones with a fourth between them, so no 3+3 change: {笔|bǐ} is a low half-third before {记|jì}, and {本|běn} at the end can dip fully.
- {铅笔|qiān bǐ} qiān bǐ, {黑板|hēi bǎn} hēi bǎn: first tone, then a dip.

## Common mistakes

- A pronoun after the measure word: ×{我|wǒ}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}{一|yí}{次|cì}{他|tā}. A pronoun object comes first: {我|wǒ}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}{他|tā}{一|yí}{次|cì}. An
  ordinary noun usually comes after: {我|wǒ}{读|dú}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}{课文|kè wén}.
- ×{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}{北京|Běi jīng}: a visit is counted with {次|cì}. {遍|biàn} is for things you go through from start to end.
- Putting the number before the verb, as with time words: ×{我|wǒ}{三|sān}{次|cì}{去|qù}{过|guo}{北京|Běi jīng}. "When" goes before the
  verb; "how many times" goes after it.
- ×{一|yí}{个|gè}{句|jù}: {句|jù} is itself a measure word ({一|yí}{句|jù}{话|huà}); the noun is {句子|jù zi} ({一|yí}{个|gè}{句子|jù zi}).
- {放学|fàng xué} for a teacher or an office: ×{老师|lǎo shī}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}{放学|fàng xué}. Pupils and schools {放学|fàng xué}; adults {下班|xià bān} (finish work).
- Mixing up {字典|zì diǎn} (characters) and {词典|cí diǎn} (words).

## Key points

- Verb measure words count actions: verb (+ {了|le} / {过|guo}) + number + {次|cì} / {遍|biàn} / {下|xià}.
- {次|cì}: occasions ({去|qù}{过|guo}{三|sān}{次|cì}); {遍|biàn}: once through from start to finish ({读|dú}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}, {请|qǐng}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}); {一下|yí xià}: briefly
  ({看|kàn}{一下|yí xià}).
- Object: ordinary nouns after the measure word ({读|dú}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}{课文|kè wén}); pronouns before it ({见|jiàn}{过|guo}{他|tā}{一|yí}{次|cì}); long
  or definite objects first ({这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}) or with {把|bǎ}.
- {几|jǐ}{遍|biàn} / {几|jǐ}{次|cì} ask how many times; {第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì} is "the first time".
- {页|yè} ({第|dì}{十|shí}{页|yè}), {年级|nián jí} ({二|èr}{年级|nián jí}), {班级|bān jí} / {班|bān}, {学期|xué qī}, {初中|chū zhōng}; {课本|kè běn}, {课文|kè wén}, {句子|jù zi} / {句|jù}; {词典|cí diǎn} / {字典|zì diǎn}; {笔记|bǐ jì},
  {笔记本|bǐ jì běn}, {铅笔|qiān bǐ}, {黑板|hēi bǎn}, {纸|zhǐ}; {作业|zuò yè}; {放学|fàng xué}.
- {=Sound parts: {反|fǎn} in {饭|fàn} and {板|bǎn}, {及|jí} in {级|jí} and {极|jí}.=}
