lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 16 was the classroom. This one is about what you study there and how well it goes: school
subjects, results, raising your level, and the ways people work at it. The grammar answers a
question HSK 2 left half open: what do you do when a verb has an object and also something after
it, such as {得|de} + "how well" or a length of time?

You'll learn:

- school subjects: {数学|shù xué}, {历史|lì shǐ}, {体育|tǐ yù}, {外语|wài yǔ} and {语言|yǔ yán};
- {成绩|chéng jì} (results), {水平|shuǐ píng} (level) and {提高|tí gāo} (to raise, to improve);
- {努力|nǔ lì} and {认真|rèn zhēn}: working hard and working carefully;
- {方法|fāng fǎ} (a method) and how it differs from {办法|bàn fǎ} (lesson 09);
- {复习|fù xí}, {练习|liàn xí} and {练|liàn}: revising and practising;
- **[[verb repetition with 得]]**: {他|tā}{学|xué}{数学|shù xué}{学|xué}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}, or without the first verb, {他|tā}{数学|shù xué}{学|xué}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo};
- the same repetition with a length of time or a number of times: {我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{历史|lì shǐ}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}.

## School subjects

| Subject | Pinyin | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| {数学|shù xué} | shù xué | maths: {数|shù} (number) + {学|xué} (study) |
| {历史|lì shǐ} | lì shǐ | history |
| {体育|tǐ yù} | tǐ yù | PE, physical education; also "sport" in general |
| {外语|wài yǔ} | wài yǔ | a foreign language: {外|wài} (outside) + {语|yǔ} (language) |
| {汉语|Hàn yǔ} / {中文|Zhōng wén} | Hàn yǔ / Zhōng wén | Chinese (HSK 1) |

Chinese pupils call their own Chinese class {语文|yǔ wén} *yǔ wén* (language and literature), and English is
{英语|Yīng yǔ} *Yīng yǔ*; neither is an HSK 3 word. A lesson in a subject is the subject + {课|kè}: {数学|shù xué}{课|kè} (a maths
lesson), {体育|tǐ yù}{课|kè} (PE).

{我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{历史|lì shǐ}{课|kè}。 — History is my favourite lesson.

{星期|xīng qī}{三|sān}{上午|shàng wǔ}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{节|jié}{数学|shù xué}{课|kè}。 — There are two maths lessons on Wednesday morning. ({节|jié} *jié*: the measure
word for lessons, lesson 23's word)

{语言|yǔ yán} is "language" in general, the thing all languages are examples of; {三|sān}{种|zhǒng}{语言|yǔ yán} is "three
languages". For one particular language, say {汉语|Hàn yǔ}, {外语|wài yǔ} or {中文|Zhōng wén}.

{他|tā}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{三|sān}{种|zhǒng}{语言|yǔ yán}。 — He speaks three languages.

{学|xué}{外语|wài yǔ}，{方法|fāng fǎ}{很|hěn}{重要|zhòng yào}。 — In learning a foreign language, method matters. ({重要|zhòng yào}, important, is lesson 28's word.)

## Results and level: {成绩|chéng jì}, {水平|shuǐ píng}, {提高|tí gāo}

{成绩|chéng jì} is your results or grades: in an exam, in a subject, or at school in general.

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{考试|kǎo shì}{她|tā}{的|de}{成绩|chéng jì}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 — She did very well in this exam. (her results were very good)

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{数学|shù xué}{成绩|chéng jì}{不|bú}{太|tài}{好|hǎo}。 — My maths results aren't very good.

{水平|shuǐ píng} is a level or standard: how good you are at something. It goes with {高|gāo} / {低|dī} *dī* (low) and
with {提高|tí gāo} (to raise):

{她|tā}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{水平|shuǐ píng}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}。 — Her Chinese is very good. (her level is high)

{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{提高|tí gāo}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{水平|shuǐ píng}。 — I want to improve my Chinese.

{提高|tí gāo} is "to raise": {提|tí} (lift) + {高|gāo} (high). It works with {水平|shuǐ píng}, {成绩|chéng jì} and other things that can go
up. It's the usual word for "improve" with these nouns. {提高|tí gāo}{汉语|Hàn yǔ} on its own is heard in casual
speech, but the standard phrase raises the {水平|shuǐ píng}: {提高|tí gāo}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{水平|shuǐ píng}.

{这个|zhè ge}{学期|xué qī}{他|tā}{的|de}{成绩|chéng jì}{提高|tí gāo}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。 — His results went up a lot this term.

The question is often {怎么|zěn me}{提高|tí gāo}？ (how can I improve it?), and the answer is a {方法|fāng fǎ}.

## Working at it: {努力|nǔ lì} and {认真|rèn zhēn}

{努力|nǔ lì} is effort: working hard, trying hard. It's a verb ({努力|nǔ lì} + verb, "work hard at") and an
adjective ({很|hěn}{努力|nǔ lì}, "hard-working"):

{我|wǒ}{会|huì}{努力|nǔ lì}{学习|xué xí}。 — I'll study hard.

{他|tā}{学习|xué xí}{非常|fēi cháng}{努力|nǔ lì}。 — He works very hard at his studies.

{我们|wǒ men}{一起|yì qǐ}{努力|nǔ lì}{吧|ba}！ — Let's all do our best!

{认真|rèn zhēn} is "conscientious, serious, careful": doing something properly, paying attention.

{她|tā}{做|zuò}{作业|zuò yè}{很|hěn}{认真|rèn zhēn}。 — She does her homework carefully.

{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{认真|rèn zhēn}{听|tīng}。 — Everyone, please listen carefully.

{认真|rèn zhēn} is also "serious" in the sense of "not joking": {他|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{认真|rèn zhēn} (he said it seriously). Before a verb
both words can take {地|de} (HSK 2): {认真|rèn zhēn}{地|de}{听|tīng}, {努力|nǔ lì}{地|de}{学习|xué xí}. The {地|de} is often left out.

A hard-working student may still not be a careful one: {努力|nǔ lì} is how much effort, {认真|rèn zhēn} how much care.

## Methods: {方法|fāng fǎ} and {办法|bàn fǎ}

Both are "way, method", but they answer different questions:

| Word | Means | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {方法|fāng fǎ} | a method: how to do something, as a technique | {学习|xué xí}{方法|fāng fǎ} study methods |
| {办法|bàn fǎ} (lesson 09) | a way out: what can be done about a problem | {没|méi}{办法|bàn fǎ} there's nothing to be done |

{你|nǐ}{学|xué}{汉字|hàn zì}{的|de}{方法|fāng fǎ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 — Your way of learning characters is very good.

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{丢|diū}{了|le}，{有|yǒu}{没有|méi yǒu}{办法|bàn fǎ}？ — I've lost my phone: is there anything I can do? (×{有|yǒu}{没有|méi yǒu}{方法|fāng fǎ})

## Revising and practising: {复习|fù xí}, {练习|liàn xí}, {练|liàn}

| Word | Means | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {复习|fù xí} | to revise, go over what you've learned | {明天|míng tiān}{考试|kǎo shì}，{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{复习|fù xí}{数学|shù xué}。 There's a maths exam tomorrow: I need to revise. |
| {练习|liàn xí} | to practise; an exercise | {我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{练习|liàn xí}{写|xiě}{汉字|hàn zì}。 I practise writing characters every day. {做|zuò}{练习|liàn xí} do exercises |
| {练|liàn} | to practise (short form) | {练|liàn}{字|zì} practise handwriting; {练|liàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí} practised for an hour |

{复|fù} is "again": {复习|fù xí} is "study again". {练习|liàn xí} is both a verb and a noun: a textbook's {练习|liàn xí} are its exercises.
{练|liàn} is the short form, used with a one-character object ({练|liàn}{字|zì}, practising handwriting) or with a
time or number after it ({练|liàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}, {再|zài}{练|liàn}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}). Before a longer object use {练习|liàn xí}: {练习|liàn xí}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}.

## Verb repetition with {得|de}

In HSK 2 you learned the degree complement: {得|de} after a verb, then how well the action goes.

{他|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 — He speaks well.

That's simple when the verb has no object. But {得|de} has to follow the verb directly, so when there
is an object there's a problem: ×{他|tā}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} is wrong, because {得|de} is stuck after {汉语|Hàn yǔ}. Chinese
solves it in one of two ways.

1. Say the verb twice: verb + object, then the verb again + {得|de} + how well. This is verb
repetition with {得|de}:

{他|tā}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 — He speaks Chinese well.

{她|tā}{学|xué}{数学|shù xué}{学|xué}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 — She does very well at maths.

{我|wǒ}{写|xiě}{汉字|hàn zì}{写|xiě}{得|de}{很|hěn}{慢|màn}。 — I write characters slowly.

2. Drop the first verb, and put the object first, as a topic:

{他|tā}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 — He speaks Chinese well. (Chinese, he speaks it well)

{她|tā}{数学|shù xué}{学|xué}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 — She's good at maths.

Both are correct and common. The second is a little shorter and puts the object forward ("as for
maths…"). What you can't do is keep the object after the verb and add {得|de} straight after it.

| | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| no object | verb + {得|de} + how | {他|tā}{跑|pǎo}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}。 |
| with object (1) | verb + object + verb + {得|de} + how | {他|tā}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 |
| with object (2) | object + verb + {得|de} + how | {他|tā}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 |
| ✗ | ×verb + object + {得|de} + how | ×{他|tā}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 |

The negative goes on the part after {得|de}, never before the verb:

{他|tā}{打|dǎ}{球|qiú}{打|dǎ}{得|de}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}。 — He doesn't play ball well. (×{他|tā}{不|bù}{打|dǎ}{球|qiú}{打|dǎ}{得|de}{好|hǎo})

And the question asks about the same part: {他|tā}{汉字|hàn zì}{写|xiě}{得|de}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ (how well does he write
characters?), {他|tā}{汉字|hàn zì}{写|xiě}{得|de}{好|hǎo}{不|bu}{好|hǎo}？

### The same repetition with time and numbers

The same problem comes up with a length of time or a verb measure word (lesson 16) after a verb
with an object, and the same repetition solves it:

{我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{历史|lì shǐ}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 — I revised history for three hours.

{他|tā}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{学|xué}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{年|nián}。 — He studied Chinese for two years.

{她|tā}{看|kàn}{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{看|kàn}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}。 — She read this book three times.

Here there is also a third way, without repeating: put the time or number between the verb and
its object, as in lesson 16: {我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{历史|lì shǐ}, {他|tā}{学|xué}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{年|nián}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}, {我|wǒ}{读|dú}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}{课文|kè wén}. All of
these are correct. A pronoun object still comes before the number: {我|wǒ}{等|děng}{他|tā}{等|děng}{了|le}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí} or {我|wǒ}{等|děng}{了|le}{他|tā}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}
(I waited half an hour for him).

Only the second verb takes {了|le}: {我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{历史|lì shǐ}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}, not ×{我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{历史|lì shǐ}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}.

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 成 | become; complete | chéng | 戈 | 6 | {成绩|chéng jì}, {完成|wán chéng} (lesson 19) |
| 绩 (traditional 績) | achievement | jì | 纟 | 11 | {成绩|chéng jì} |
| 数 (traditional 數) | number; count | shù (and others) | 攵 | 13 | {数学|shù xué} |
| 历 (traditional 歷) | go through; history | lì | 厂 | 4 | {历史|lì shǐ} |
| 史 | history | shǐ | 口 | 5 | {历史|lì shǐ} |
| 育 | raise, educate | yù | ⺼ | 8 | {体育|tǐ yù} |
| 言 | speech | yán | 言 | 7 | {语言|yǔ yán} |
| 复 (traditional 複) | again; repeat | fù | 夊 | 9 | {复习|fù xí} |
| 练 (traditional 練) | practise | liàn | 纟 | 8 | {练习|liàn xí}, {练|liàn} |
| 提 | lift | tí | 扌 | 12 | {提高|tí gāo} |
| 平 | flat, level | píng | 广 | 5 | {水平|shuǐ píng} |
| 努 | exert | nǔ | 力 | 7 | {努力|nǔ lì} |
| 力 | strength | lì | 力 | 2 | {努力|nǔ lì} |

- {成|chéng}: the radical is 戈 (an old weapon, a halberd), as in {我|wǒ}.
- {绩|jì}: 纟 (silk) and {责|zé}. {绩|jì} first meant twisting hemp into thread; then the result of work,
  "achievement". {责|zé} *zé* doesn't give the sound jì any more.
- {数|shù}: the left part is {娄|lóu}, the same part as in {楼|lóu} (building, HSK 2), and 攵 (a hand at work) on the
  right. {娄|lóu} gives lóu in {楼|lóu}; in {数|shù} the sound has changed to shù. As the verb "to count" it is {数|shǔ} shǔ
  ({数|shǔ}{一|yi}{数|shǔ}, count them): another reading of the same character.
- {历|lì}: 厂 (a cliff or shelter) over {力|lì} (strength), which gives the sound: lì. The simplified {历|lì}
  stands for two traditional characters, {歷|lì} (going through: {歷史|lì shǐ}, history) and {曆|lì} (the calendar:
  {日曆|rì lì}). In {历史|lì shǐ} the Traditional switch shows {歷|lì}.
- {史|shǐ}: a common reading of the old form is a hand holding a record: the official who kept the
  records. From "record-keeper" came "history".
- {育|yù}: on top, an upside-down child (子 turned over: a birth); below, ⺼, the "meat" form of 月.
  "To give birth to, to raise", then "to educate". Make Me a Hanzi files it under ⺼;
  some dictionaries use 亠 or 月.
- {言|yán}: speech. This is the full form of the radical 讠 that you know from {说|shuō}, {语|yǔ} and {话|huà} (HSK 1); in
  traditional writing the left side is 言 too ({說|shuō}, {語|yǔ}).
- {复|fù}: the simplified {复|fù} stands for {復|fù} (again, return) and {複|fù} (double, repeated). Taiwan writes
  {复习|fù xí} as {複習|fù xí}, and that's what the Traditional switch shows; you may also see {復習|fù xí} in older texts.
  Make Me a Hanzi files {复|fù} under 夊, the "slow walk" at the bottom; dictionaries often use 夂 or
  丿.
- {练|liàn}: 纟 (silk) and a right side that looks like {东|dōng} (east) but isn't: it's a simplified {柬|jiǎn}
  (traditional {練|liàn}). It first meant boiling raw silk to make it soft and white, a process repeated
  until it was done well, which is one memory aid for "practise".
- {提|tí}: 扌 (hand) and {是|shì}, which gives the sound tí, as in {题|tí} (question, HSK 1). Lift with the hand.
- {平|píng}: an old drawing of something level, like a balance. Make Me a Hanzi files it under 广, which
  is unusual; dictionaries give 干 or 一. It gives the sound in {苹|píng} ({苹果|píng guǒ}, apple).
- {努|nǔ}: {奴|nú} *nú* (servant) gives the sound, and {力|lì} (strength) at the bottom the meaning: putting in
  your strength.
- {力|lì}: most scholars read the old form as a drawing of a plough, the tool of hard work. It is the
  radical of {努|nǔ} and of {办|bàn} (lesson 09) and {动|dòng} (HSK 2), and the lower part of {男|nán} (HSK 1), which is
  filed under 田.

### Phonetic components: {是|shì}, {平|píng}, {力|lì}

| Sound part | Characters | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| 是 shì | {题|tí} (question), {提|tí} (lift) | tí, tí |
| 平 píng | {苹|píng} ({苹果|píng guǒ}, apple) | píng |
| 力 lì | {历|lì} (go through) | lì |
| 娄 lóu | {楼|lóu} (building); {数|shù} (sound changed) | lóu; shù |

{是|shì} is a surprise: shì gives tí in {题|tí} and {提|tí}, a different initial and tone (the sounds were closer
in old Chinese). Use these as hints, never as rules.

### Stroke order

- **成**: the first horizontal, the slash down to the left, the horizontal-turn-hook inside, then
  the long slanting hook of 戈, its slash, and the dot last, as in {我|wǒ}.
- **力**: the horizontal-turn-hook first, then the slash through it. Two strokes only.
- **平**: the top horizontal, the two short strokes below it (a dot on the left, then a short left-falling stroke on
  the right), the second horizontal,
  and the long vertical last, through the middle.
- **复**: the short slash and the horizontal on top, then 日, then 夊 at the bottom: a slash, a
  stroke that turns, and the long falling stroke.
- **言**: the dot, three horizontals (the first longest), then 口 at the bottom.
- **育**: the dot and the horizontal, the turning stroke and the dot of the upside-down child,
  then 月 below.

```trace
成绩数历史育言
```

```trace trad=複練提平努力
复练提平努力
```

Write it: {成|chéng}, {育|yù}, {言|yán}, {复|fù}, {练|liàn}, {平|píng}, {努|nǔ} and {力|lì} are on the HSK 3 handwriting list. Write each three
times from memory, then check the strokes on the pad.

### Handwriting review

From HSK 1 and HSK 2: {学|xué} (8 strokes), {汉|hàn} (5), {语|yǔ} (9), {比|bǐ} (4).

```trace
学汉语比
```
=}

In traditional script the pads show {+{学|xué}+} (16 strokes), {+{汉|hàn}+} (14) and {+{语|yǔ}+} (14); {比|bǐ} is the same.

## Dialogue: after the exam

{徐亮|Xú Liàng} (徐亮) and {谢丽|Xiè Lì} (谢丽) are junior high school pupils. The maths results are out.

```dialogue
# After the exam
徐亮: {谢丽|Xiè Lì}，{你|nǐ}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{数学|shù xué}{考|kǎo}{得|de}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
= Xie Li, how did you do in maths this time?
谢丽: {还|hái}{不错|bú cuò}，{九十二|jiǔ shí èr}{分|fēn}。{你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？
= Not bad, ninety-two. And you?
徐亮: {别|bié}{说|shuō}{了|le}，{六十五|liù shí wǔ}{分|fēn}。{我|wǒ}{学|xué}{数学|shù xué}{学|xué}{得|de}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}，{每|měi}{次|cì}{考试|kǎo shì}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{着急|zháo jí}。
= Don't ask. Sixty-five. I'm bad at maths: every exam I panic.
谢丽: {你|nǐ}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{吗|ma}？
= Did you revise?
徐亮: {复习|fù xí}{了|le}！{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{数学|shù xué}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{四|sì}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}，{但是|dàn shì}{题|tí}{还是|hái shi}{不|bú}{会|huì}{做|zuò}。
= I did! Last night I revised maths for four hours, but I still couldn't do the questions.
谢丽: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{怎么|zěn me}{复习|fù xí}{的|de}？
= How did you revise?
徐亮: {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{课本|kè běn}{看|kàn}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}。
= I read the textbook three times.
谢丽: {数学|shù xué}{光|guāng}{看|kàn}{课本|kè běn}{没|méi}{有用|yǒu yòng}，{要|yào}{多|duō}{做|zuò}{题|tí}。{我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{做|zuò}{二十|èr shí}{个|gè}{练习|liàn xí}，{做|zuò}{错|cuò}{的|de}{题|tí}{再|zài}{做|zuò}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。
= Just reading the textbook is no use for maths; you need to do lots of questions. I do twenty exercises a day, and do the ones I got wrong again.
徐亮: {每天|měi tiān}{二十|èr shí}{个|gè}？{你|nǐ}{真|zhēn}{努力|nǔ lì}！
= Twenty a day? You really work hard!
谢丽: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我们|wǒ men}{老师|lǎo shī}{教|jiāo}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{方法|fāng fǎ}。{你|nǐ}{试|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{月|yuè}，{成绩|chéng jì}{会|huì}{提高|tí gāo}{的|de}。
= It's the method our teacher taught me. Try it for a month: your results will go up.
徐亮: {好|hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{试|shì}{试|shì}。{谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}！
= OK, I'll try it. Thanks!
```

- {考|kǎo}{得|de}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}: {考|kǎo} (to take an exam) + {得|de} + {怎么样|zěn me yàng}, "how did the exam go?". No object, so no repetition.
- {我|wǒ}{学|xué}{数学|shù xué}{学|xué}{得|de}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}: verb repetition with {得|de}, negative after {得|de}.
- {我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{数学|shù xué}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{四|sì}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}: the same repetition with a length of time.
- {光|guāng}{看|kàn}{课本|kè běn}{没|méi}{有用|yǒu yòng}: {光|guāng} *guāng* (only, just) is spoken; {没|méi}{有用|yǒu yòng} is "no use" ({有用|yǒu yòng}, lesson 09).
- {成绩|chéng jì}{会|huì}{提高|tí gāo}{的|de}: {会|huì}…{的|de} makes a confident prediction, "it will, you'll see".

## Reading: how my results went up

> {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{徐亮|Xú Liàng}，{是|shì}{初中|chū zhōng}{二|èr}{年级|nián jí}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}。{我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{体育|tǐ yù}{和|hé}{历史|lì shǐ}，{最|zuì}{不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{的|de}{是|shì}{数学|shù xué}。{上|shàng}{个|gè}{学期|xué qī}，{我|wǒ}{的|de}{数学|shù xué}{成绩|chéng jì}{很|hěn}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}，{考试|kǎo shì}{考|kǎo}{了|le}{六十五|liù shí wǔ}{分|fēn}。
>
> {为什么|wèi shén me}？{我|wǒ}{学|xué}{数学|shù xué}{学|xué}{得|de}{很|hěn}{认真|rèn zhēn}，{每|měi}{次|cì}{考试|kǎo shì}{前|qián}{都|dōu}{复习|fù xí}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{方法|fāng fǎ}{不|bú}{对|duì}：{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{课本|kè běn}{看|kàn}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{遍|biàn}，{但是|dàn shì}{不|bú}{做|zuò}{题|tí}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}{谢丽|Xiè Lì}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}，{数学|shù xué}{要|yào}{多|duō}{练|liàn}。{她|tā}{每天|měi tiān}{做|zuò}{二十|èr shí}{个|gè}{练习|liàn xí}，{做|zuò}{错|cuò}{的|de}{题|tí}，{她|tā}{再|zài}{做|zuò}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}、{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}，{做|zuò}{到|dào}{会|huì}{做|zuò}。
>
> {这个|zhè ge}{学期|xué qī}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{用|yòng}{了|le}{她|tā}{的|de}{方法|fāng fǎ}。{每天|měi tiān}{放学|fàng xué}{回家|huí jiā}，{我|wǒ}{做|zuò}{二十|èr shí}{个|gè}{数学|shù xué}{题|tí}，{做|zuò}{完|wán}{了|le}{再|zài}{做|zuò}{老师|lǎo shī}{给|gěi}{的|de}{作业|zuò yè}。{我|wǒ}{做|zuò}{题|tí}{做|zuò}{得|de}{很|hěn}{慢|màn}，{有|yǒu}{时候|shí hou}{一|yí}{个|gè}{题|tí}{要|yào}{做|zuò}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{坚持|jiān chí}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}。{上|shàng}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{考试|kǎo shì}，{我|wǒ}{考|kǎo}{了|le}{八十八|bā shí bā}{分|fēn}！{老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}："{徐亮|Xú Liàng}，{你|nǐ}{的|de}{数学|shù xué}{水平|shuǐ píng}{提高|tí gāo}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}，{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}！{要|yào}{坚持|jiān chí}{下去|xià qù}！"
>
> {现在|xiàn zài}{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}，{学习|xué xí}{要|yào}{努力|nǔ lì}，{要|yào}{认真|rèn zhēn}，{也|yě}{要|yào}{有|yǒu}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{方法|fāng fǎ}。

1. Which subjects does Xu Liang like most?
2. What was wrong with the way he studied maths?
3. What does he do now when he gets home?
4. What did he score in last week's exam?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. PE and history ({我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{体育|tǐ yù}{和|hé}{历史|lì shǐ}).
2. He was conscientious and revised before every exam, but his method was wrong: he read the
   textbook many times but didn't do any questions ({我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{课本|kè běn}{看|kàn}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{遍|biàn}，{但是|dàn shì}{不|bú}{做|zuò}{题|tí}).
3. He does twenty maths questions first, and then the homework the teacher gave.
4. Eighty-eight ({我|wǒ}{考|kǎo}{了|le}{八十八|bā shí bā}{分|fēn}), up from sixty-five last term.

"My name is Xu Liang and I'm in the second year of junior high. My favourite subjects are PE and
history; the one I like least is maths. Last term my maths results were very bad: I got
sixty-five in the exam.

Why? I studied maths very conscientiously and always revised before an exam, but my method was
wrong: I read the textbook over and over, but I didn't do any questions. My classmate Xie Li told me that
maths takes a lot of practice. She does twenty exercises every day, and the questions she gets
wrong she does again, once, twice, until she can do them.

This term I've used her method too. Every day when I get home from school, I do twenty maths
questions, and when I've finished them I do the homework the teacher gave. I'm slow at them:
sometimes one question takes me half an hour, but I've kept at it. In last week's exam I got
eighty-eight! The teacher said: 'Xu Liang, your maths has improved a lot. Well done! Keep it up!'

Now I think that in studying you have to work hard and be careful, and you also need a good
method."
</details>

## Write it: one or two sentences

Write one or two sentences in characters about a subject you study: how well you do it, and how
long or how often you practise. Use verb repetition (or the topic form) in at least one.

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {我|wǒ}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{不错|bú cuò}，{但是|dàn shì}{汉字|hàn zì}{写|xiě}{得|de}{很|hěn}{慢|màn}。 — I speak Chinese quite well, but I write characters slowly.
- {我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{练|liàn}{汉字|hàn zì}{练|liàn}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 — I practise characters for an hour every day.
- {我|wǒ}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{学|xué}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{年|nián}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{提高|tí gāo}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{水平|shuǐ píng}。 — I've been learning Chinese for two years, and I want to
  raise my level.

Check: is {得|de} straight after a verb ({说|shuō}{得|de}, {写|xiě}{得|de}), not after the object? Does only the second verb
take {了|le}?
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Talking about school
{你|nǐ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{什么|shén me}{课|kè}？
= What's your favourite subject?
{我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{历史|lì shǐ}{课|kè}。
= History is my favourite.
{她|tā}{数学|shù xué}{学|xué}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。
= She's good at maths.
{我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。
= I revised for three hours.
{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{提高|tí gāo}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{水平|shuǐ píng}。
= I want to improve my Chinese.
{你|nǐ}{学习|xué xí}{的|de}{方法|fāng fǎ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。
= Your study method is very good.
```

## Pronunciation

- {水平|shuǐ píng} shuǐ píng: a dip, then a rising tone. Don't confuse it with {睡|shuì} shuì (to sleep).
- {努力|nǔ lì} nǔ lì: the *u* of nǔ is a plain "oo" (not ü): nǔ, not nǚ ({女|nǚ}).
- {练|liàn} liàn and {脸|liǎn} liǎn (face, lesson 04): a falling tone for "practise", a dip for "face".
- {历史|lì shǐ} lì shǐ: lì falls, shǐ dips; and the two *i* sounds differ: "ee" after l, the buzzing vowel of {是|shì} after sh.
- {体育|tǐ yù} tǐ yù: the *yu* is ü.
- {复习|fù xí} fù xí and {服务|fú wù} fú wù (service, lesson 19) start with the same syllable in different tones:
  fù falls, fú rises.

## Common mistakes

- ×{他|tā}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}: {得|de} can't follow the object. Say {他|tā}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} or {他|tā}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}.
- ×{我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{数学|shù xué}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}: only the second verb takes {了|le} ({我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{数学|shù xué}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}).
- ×{他|tā}{不|bù}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{好|hǎo}: the negative goes after {得|de}: {他|tā}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}.
- {提高|tí gāo}{汉语|Hàn yǔ} on its own: it's heard in speech, but the standard phrase raises the level, {提高|tí gāo}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{水平|shuǐ píng}.
- {方法|fāng fǎ} for "a way out": ×{没有|méi yǒu}{方法|fāng fǎ}. A problem that can't be solved is {没|méi}{办法|bàn fǎ}.
- {练|liàn} with a long object: {练|liàn}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ} is heard in casual speech but sounds clipped; {练习|liàn xí}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ} is more natural.

## Key points

- Subjects: {数学|shù xué}, {历史|lì shǐ}, {体育|tǐ yù}, {外语|wài yǔ} ({语言|yǔ yán} is language in general). A lesson: subject + {课|kè}.
- {成绩|chéng jì} (results), {水平|shuǐ píng} (level), {提高|tí gāo} + {水平|shuǐ píng} / {成绩|chéng jì} (raise, improve).
- {努力|nǔ lì}: effort (verb and adjective); {认真|rèn zhēn}: care, conscientiousness.
- {方法|fāng fǎ}: a method ({学习|xué xí}{方法|fāng fǎ}); {办法|bàn fǎ}: a way out ({没|méi}{办法|bàn fǎ}).
- {复习|fù xí} (revise), {练习|liàn xí} (practise; exercises), {练|liàn} (short form: {练|liàn}{字|zì}, {练|liàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}).
- Verb repetition with {得|de}: {他|tā}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} = {他|tā}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}; never ×{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{得|de}.
- With time or times: {我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{历史|lì shǐ}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí} = {我|wǒ}{复习|fù xí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{历史|lì shǐ}.
- {=Sound parts: {是|shì} in {题|tí} and {提|tí}, {平|píng} in {苹|píng}, {力|lì} in {历|lì}.=}

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Do you understand? 听得懂, 以为 and 认为
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

A learner spends a lot of time not quite understanding, and the rest of the time trying to say
what they think. This lesson gives you the words for both: understanding (and not), remembering
and forgetting, things that are hard or easy, and giving an opinion with a reason, one of the
HSK 3 speaking and writing tasks.

You'll learn:

- potential complements with {懂|dǒng}, {清楚|qīng chu} and {明白|míng bai}: {听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng}, {听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}, {看|kàn}{不|bu}{清楚|qīng chu}, {说|shuō}{不|bu}{明白|míng bai};
- the verbs of understanding and knowing: {懂|dǒng}, {明白|míng bai}, {了解|liǎo jiě}, {懂得|dǒng de}, {认得|rèn de}, beside {知道|zhī dào} and {认识|rèn shi};
- {以为|yǐ wéi} (to think, wrongly) and {认为|rèn wéi} (to hold the opinion), beside {觉得|jué de};
- {听说|tīng shuō} (to hear that), {记|jì} (to note down) and {忘记|wàng jì} (to forget);
- {难|nán}, {容易|róng yì} and {简单|jiǎn dān}, also before a verb: {难|nán}{写|xiě}, {容易|róng yì}{懂|dǒng};
- {聪明|cōng ming}, {难题|nán tí}, {回答|huí dá}, {对话|duì huà} and {讲|jiǎng};
- question words that don't ask anything: {我|wǒ}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng};
- giving an opinion: {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}…，{因为|yīn wèi}….

## Can you understand? Potential complements with {懂|dǒng}, {清楚|qīng chu}, {明白|míng bai}

In lesson 06 you learned the potential complement: verb + {得|de} / {不|bù} + result, for what can or
can't happen. {吃|chī}{得|de}{完|wán} is "can finish (eating)", {买|mǎi}{不|bu}{到|dào} "can't get (to buy)". The commonest ones of
all are about understanding:

| Can | Can't | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng} | {听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng} | can / can't understand (by listening) |
| {看|kàn}{得|de}{懂|dǒng} | {看|kàn}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng} | can / can't understand (by reading) |
| {看|kàn}{得|de}{清楚|qīng chu} | {看|kàn}{不|bu}{清楚|qīng chu} | can / can't see clearly |
| {听|tīng}{得|de}{清楚|qīng chu} | {听|tīng}{不|bu}{清楚|qīng chu} | can / can't hear clearly |
| {说|shuō}{得|de}{清楚|qīng chu} | {说|shuō}{不|bu}{清楚|qīng chu} | can / can't put it clearly |
| {听|tīng}{得|de}{明白|míng bai} | {听|tīng}{不|bu}{明白|míng bai} | can / can't follow (make sense of what you hear) |

The {不|bù} in the middle is light, *bu*. The {得|de} is light too, *de*.

{你|nǐ}{听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng}{上海话|Shàng hǎi huà}{吗|ma}？ — Can you understand Shanghainese? ({上海话|Shàng hǎi huà}: the Shanghai dialect)

{老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}{得|de}{太|tài}{快|kuài}，{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}。 — The teacher speaks too fast; I can't understand.

{字|zì}{太|tài}{小|xiǎo}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{不|bu}{清楚|qīng chu}。 — The characters are too small: I can't see them clearly.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{说|shuō}{不|bu}{清楚|qīng chu}。 — I can't really explain this either. (I can't say it clearly)

The question is the verb + {得|de} + complement + {吗|ma}, or both forms side by side:

{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}{得|de}{懂|dǒng}{吗|ma}？ / {你|nǐ}{看|kàn}{得|de}{懂|dǒng}{看|kàn}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}？ — Can you understand it? (reading)

### Three ways to use {懂|dǒng}

Compare three sentences that all have {懂|dǒng} or {清楚|qīng chu} after a verb. They look alike but say different
things:

| Sentence | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}。 | result complement (HSK 2) | I understood (what was said just now). |
| {我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng}。 | potential complement (lesson 06) | I can understand (it's within my ability). |
| {老师|lǎo shī}{讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{清楚|qīng chu}。 | degree complement (HSK 2) | The teacher explains very clearly. |

The result complement reports what happened, with {了|le} or {没|méi}: {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng} (I didn't understand). The
potential complement says what is possible, with {得|de} / {不|bù} and no {了|le} after the verb: {我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng} (I can't understand).
A {了|le} at the end can still mark a change: {现在|xiàn zài}{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng}{了|le} (now I can understand).
The degree complement describes how well something is done, and almost always has {很|hěn} or another
degree word: {讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{清楚|qīng chu}. Without {很|hěn}, {讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{清楚|qīng chu} is usually the potential "can explain clearly" (in a contrast, such as {他|tā}{讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{清楚|qīng chu}，{你|nǐ}{讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{不|bù}{清楚|qīng chu}, it can also be the degree complement).

## Understanding and knowing

Chinese has more words here than English. You know three from HSK 1 and HSK 2:

| Word | Meaning | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| {知道|zhī dào} | know (a fact) | {我|wǒ}{知道|zhī dào}{他|tā}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}。 I know his name. |
| {认识|rèn shi} | know (a person, a character, a place) | {我|wǒ}{认识|rèn shi}{他|tā}。 I know him. |
| {懂|dǒng} | understand (language, meaning) | {我|wǒ}{懂|dǒng}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{意思|yì si}。 I understand what you mean. |
| {明白|míng bai} | understand clearly, get it; clear | {我|wǒ}{明白|míng bai}{了|le}！ I've got it! |
| {了解|liǎo jiě} | know well, know about; find out about | {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{了解|liǎo jiě}{他|tā}。 I know him well. |
| {懂得|dǒng de} | grasp (a principle), know how to | {他|tā}{懂得|dǒng de}{怎么|zěn me}{学习|xué xí}。 He knows how to study. |
| {认得|rèn de} | recognise (by sight) | {这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{我|wǒ}{认得|rèn de}。 I recognise this character. |

- {明白|míng bai} is close to {懂|dǒng}, and the two often swap: {我|wǒ}{懂|dǒng}{了|le} and {我|wǒ}{明白|míng bai}{了|le} both mean "I understand now". {明白|míng bai}
  is about the meaning becoming clear, often suddenly ("oh, I see!"), and it's also an adjective:
  {讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{明白|míng bai} (explained clearly). The {白|bái} is light: *míng bai*.
- {了解|liǎo jiě} is deeper and wider: knowing a lot about a person, a place, a subject or a situation, or
  finding out about it. {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{了解|liǎo jiě}{一下|yí xià}{中国|Zhōng guó}{的|de}{历史|lì shǐ} is "I'd like to learn something about Chinese
  history". Notice the {了|le}: here it's *liǎo*, not *le*.
- {懂得|dǒng de} is for understanding a principle, knowing how to behave or how to do something: {懂得|dǒng de}{学习|xué xí}{的|de}{方法|fāng fǎ},
  {他|tā}{很|hěn}{懂得|dǒng de}{关心|guān xīn}{别人|bié ren} (he knows how to show he cares about others: {关心|guān xīn} is lesson 20's word). It's more serious
  and less common than {懂|dǒng}.
- {认得|rèn de} is spoken: you recognise something when you see it again. {这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{我|wǒ}{认得|rèn de}，{但是|dàn shì}{不|bú}{会|huì}{写|xiě} is the
  everyday learner's sentence: "I know this character when I see it, but I can't write it". {认识|rèn shi}
  can say the same; {认得|rèn de} is narrower (recognising).

## {以为|yǐ wéi} and {认为|rèn wéi}: wrong beliefs and opinions

Both are "to think", but in different senses.

{认为|rèn wéi} gives an opinion, a view you hold. It's a little more formal than {觉得|jué de} (HSK 1), and it
fits discussions, essays and opinions with reasons:

{我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}，{听|tīng}{和|hé}{说|shuō}{很|hěn}{有用|yǒu yòng}。 — I think that in learning Chinese, listening and speaking are very useful.

{你|nǐ}{认为|rèn wéi}{这个|zhè ge}{方法|fāng fǎ}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ — What do you think of this method?

{以为|yǐ wéi} is "to think (wrongly)": a belief that turned out not to be true. The next sentence usually
says what was really the case:

{我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{今天|jīn tiān}{有|yǒu}{课|kè}，{但是|dàn shì}{今天|jīn tiān}{没有|méi yǒu}{课|kè}。 — I thought there was class today, but there isn't.

{我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{他|tā}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}，{他|tā}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}！ — I thought he was a teacher; he's a student!

{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{了|le}！{我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{来|lái}{了|le}。 — You've come! I thought you weren't coming.

So {我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{他|tā}{会|huì}{来|lái} almost always means "I thought he'd come (but he didn't)". For a simple opinion, use
{认为|rèn wéi} or {觉得|jué de}: {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}{他|tā}{会|huì}{来|lái} (I think he'll come).

| Word | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {觉得|jué de} | feeling or opinion (everyday) | {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{冷|lěng}。 / {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{这个|zhè ge}{方法|fāng fǎ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 |
| {认为|rèn wéi} | opinion (more considered, formal) | {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}{这个|zhè ge}{方法|fāng fǎ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 |
| {以为|yǐ wéi} | belief that was wrong | {我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{这个|zhè ge}{方法|fāng fǎ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{但是|dàn shì}{没|méi}{有用|yǒu yòng}。 |
| {想|xiǎng} | think about; would like to | {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{一下|yí xià}。 / {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}。 |

The {为|wéi} in {认为|rèn wéi} and {以为|yǐ wéi} is *wéi*, second tone (in {为什么|wèi shén me} it's *wèi*).

## {听说|tīng shuō}: hearing that…

{听说|tīng shuō} is "to hear (it said) that": news you got from someone else. It usually goes at the start, and
the speaker can be put in the middle:

{听说|tīng shuō}{明天|míng tiān}{要|yào}{考试|kǎo shì}。 — I hear there's an exam tomorrow.

{听|tīng}{老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}，{下|xià}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{有|yǒu}{考试|kǎo shì}。 — The teacher says (I heard from the teacher that) there's an exam next week.

{我|wǒ}{听说|tīng shuō}{过|guo}{这个|zhè ge}{人|rén}，{但是|dàn shì}{不|bú}{认识|rèn shi}{他|tā}。 — I've heard of this person, but I don't know him.

## Remembering and forgetting: {记|jì} and {忘记|wàng jì}

{记|jì} is "to note down, to remember": to put something in your memory or on paper.

{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{她|tā}{的|de}{电话|diàn huà}{号码|hào mǎ}{记|jì}{在|zài}{本子|běn zi}{上|shàng}{了|le}。 — I wrote her phone number down in my notebook.

{上课|shàng kè}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{我|wǒ}{记|jì}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{笔记|bǐ jì}。 — I took lots of notes in class.

{这些|zhè xiē}{字|zì}{我|wǒ}{记|jì}{不|bu}{住|zhù}。 — I can't remember these characters. ({记|jì}{住|zhù}: to fix in memory; a potential
complement with {住|zhù} *zhù*)

{记得|jì de} (HSK 2) is "to remember" as a state: {我|wǒ}{记得|jì de}{他|tā} (I remember him). {忘记|wàng jì} is "to forget", the same as
{忘|wàng} (HSK 2) and a little more formal; in speech people mostly say {忘|wàng}{了|le}:

{别|bié}{忘记|wàng jì}{带|dài}{课本|kè běn}。 / {别|bié}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{带|dài}{课本|kè běn}。 — Don't forget to bring your textbook.

{我|wǒ}{忘记|wàng jì}{他|tā}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}{名字|míng zi}{了|le}。 — I've forgotten his name.

## Hard and easy: {难|nán}, {容易|róng yì}, {简单|jiǎn dān}

{难|nán} (difficult) and {容易|róng yì} (easy) are adjectives: {这个|zhè ge}{题|tí}{很|hěn}{难|nán} (this question is hard), {这个|zhè ge}{题|tí}{很|hěn}{容易|róng yì}. {简单|jiǎn dān} is
"simple": not complicated. Something can be {简单|jiǎn dān} but not {容易|róng yì} (a simple rule that's hard to keep),
and {容易|róng yì} is about the effort it takes.

The useful thing is that {难|nán} and {容易|róng yì} go straight before a verb, like {好|hǎo} in {好吃|hǎo chī} and {好看|hǎo kàn}:

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {难|nán} + verb | {难|nán}{写|xiě}, {难|nán}{懂|dǒng}, {难|nán}{说|shuō} | hard to write, hard to understand, hard to say |
| {容易|róng yì} + verb | {容易|róng yì}{懂|dǒng}, {容易|róng yì}{忘|wàng} | easy to understand, easy to forget |

{这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{很|hěn}{难|nán}{写|xiě}。 — This character is hard to write.

{他|tā}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{很|hěn}{容易|róng yì}{懂|dǒng}。 — His Chinese is easy to understand.

{明天|míng tiān}{天气|tiān qì}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？{很|hěn}{难|nán}{说|shuō}。 — What will the weather be like tomorrow? Hard to say.

{容易|róng yì} + verb also means "likely to": {冬天|dōng tiān}{容易|róng yì}{感冒|gǎn mào} (it's easy to catch a cold in winter), {这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{很|hěn}{容易|róng yì}{写|xiě}{错|cuò}
(people often write this character wrongly). {难题|nán tí} is a hard problem or question, and {聪明|cōng ming} is
"clever": {他|tā}{很|hěn}{聪明|cōng ming}，{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{学|xué}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài} (he's clever: he learns everything quickly).

## Questions and answers: {回答|huí dá}, {对话|duì huà}, {讲|jiǎng}

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {回答|huí dá} | to answer; an answer | {请|qǐng}{回答|huí dá}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{问题|wèn tí}。 Please answer my question. |
| {对话|duì huà} | a dialogue, a conversation | {我们|wǒ men}{听|tīng}{一下|yí xià}{这个|zhè ge}{对话|duì huà}。 Let's listen to this dialogue. |
| {讲|jiǎng} | to explain, tell, speak | {老师|lǎo shī}{讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{清楚|qīng chu}。 The teacher explains very clearly. |

{回答|huí dá} takes the question as its object: {回答|huí dá}{问题|wèn tí}. {讲|jiǎng} is "to explain" ({讲课|jiǎng kè}, to give a lecture; {讲|jiǎng}{语法|yǔ fǎ},
to explain grammar: {语法|yǔ fǎ} *yǔ fǎ*) and in speech often just "to say, to tell": {你|nǐ}{讲|jiǎng}{一下|yí xià} (tell us).
{对话|duì huà} is mostly a noun in textbooks ({听|tīng}{对话|duì huà}, {读|dú}{对话|duì huà}); as a verb it is formal ("to hold a dialogue").

## Question words that don't ask: {什么|shén me}{都|dōu}, {谁|shéi}{都|dōu}

In lesson 11 you met question words used without asking anything: {什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào} (knows everything),
{谁|shéi}{都|dōu}{认识|rèn shi} (knows everyone). These are **[[non-interrogative question words]]**: the question word stands for
"any" or "every", with {都|dōu} or {也|yě} after it, and with a negative it means "none at all". They're very
common when you talk about understanding:

{我|wǒ}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}。 — I can't understand anything.

{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{谁|shéi}{都|dōu}{会|huì}{回答|huí dá}。 — Anyone can answer this question.

{我|wǒ}{哪儿|nǎr}{都|dōu}{找|zhǎo}{不|bu}{到|dào}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{词典|cí diǎn}。 — I can't find my dictionary anywhere.

Without {都|dōu} / {也|yě}, {什么|shén me} in a question often means "any": {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{问题|wèn tí}{吗|ma}？ is "Do you have any
questions?", not "What questions do you have?" The {吗|ma} at the end shows it's a yes/no question. Every
teacher ends a class with it.

## Giving an opinion: {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}…，{因为|yīn wèi}…

An opinion is stronger with a reason. The simplest frame is {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi} / {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de} + opinion, then {因为|yīn wèi} +
reason (HSK 2), or the other way round with {所以|suǒ yǐ}:

{我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}{学|xué}{汉字|hàn zì}{很|hěn}{有意思|yǒu yì si}，{因为|yīn wèi}{每|měi}{个|gè}{字|zì}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{故事|gù shi}。 — I think learning characters is interesting,
because every character has its own story. ({故事|gù shi}: story, lesson 22's word)

{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{这个|zhè ge}{方法|fāng fǎ}{不|bú}{太|tài}{好|hǎo}，{因为|yīn wèi}{很|hěn}{容易|róng yì}{忘|wàng}。 — I don't think this method is very good, because it's easy to
forget things.

{因为|yīn wèi}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{的|de}{声调|shēng diào}{很|hěn}{难|nán}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{听|tīng}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{遍|biàn}。 — Because Chinese tones are hard, I listen many times every
day. ({声调|shēng diào} *shēng diào*: tone)

To ask someone's opinion: {你|nǐ}{认为|rèn wéi}{呢|ne}？ / {你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ (what do you think?). Notice that in Chinese {不|bù}
goes in the reason or in the opinion itself: {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{这个|zhè ge}{方法|fāng fǎ}{不|bù}{好|hǎo} is the normal way to say "I don't think
this method is good". {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{认为|rèn wéi}… exists, but sounds strong ("I don't accept that…").

  meaning. Make Me a Hanzi files {难|nán} under {又|yòu}; many dictionaries put it under 隹.
- {答|dá}: ⺮ (bamboo) over {合|hé} (to fit together). A memory aid: an answer fits the question.
- {讲|jiǎng}: 讠 (speech) and {井|jǐng} *jǐng* (a well), which gives the sound: jiǎng. Traditional {講|jiǎng} has a
  different right side, 冓.
- {解|jiě}: {角|jiǎo} (horn) on the left, {刀|dāo} (knife) and {牛|niú} (ox) on the right: cutting the horns off an ox,
  taking it apart. From "take apart, untie" come "explain" and "understand" ({了解|liǎo jiě}).
- {清|qīng}: 氵 (water) and {青|qīng} *qīng*, which gives the sound: clear water. See the {青|qīng} family below.
- {楚|chǔ}: two trees 林 over 疋 (a foot). It was also the name of an ancient state in the south. In
  {清楚|qīng chu} it's light, *chu*.
- {聪|cōng}: {耳|ěr} (ear) on the left: {聪|cōng} first meant "sharp of hearing". The right side of simplified {聪|cōng} looks
  like {总|zǒng} (always, lesson 27), but in traditional {聰|cōng} it's 悤 *cōng*, which gave the sound.

  were written on strips of bamboo, {简|jiǎn}; "simple" is a later meaning. The traditional form is {簡|jiǎn}
  (with {間|jiān}).
- {容|róng}: 宀 (roof) over 谷 (valley): a space that holds things. "To contain", then "face, looks".

### Phonetic components: the {青|qīng} family

{青|qīng} *qīng* (blue-green) is one of the most useful sound parts in Chinese. You now know five of its
characters, all read *qing* or *jing*, and the radical tells you which one you're looking at:

| Character | Radical | Reading | Word |
|---|---|---|---|
| 请 | 讠 speech | qǐng | {请|qǐng} (please) |
| 情 | 忄 heart | qíng | {事情|shì qing} (matter) |
| 晴 | {日|rì} sun | qíng | {晴|qíng} (sunny) |
| 清 | 氵 water | qīng | {清楚|qīng chu} (clear) |
| 睛 | {目|mù} eye | jīng | {眼睛|yǎn jing} (eye) |

Two more sound parts from this lesson: {井|jǐng} *jǐng* in {讲|jiǎng} *jiǎng*, and {间|jiān} *jiān* in {简|jiǎn} *jiǎn*.

### Stroke order

- **难**: {又|yòu} first (the turning stroke, then the long falling one), then 隹: the slash, the
  vertical, the dot, three horizontals, the second vertical, and the bottom horizontal last.
- **答**: ⺮ (two sets of three: slash, short horizontal, dot), then {合|hé}: the slash and the falling
  stroke, the short horizontal, and {口|kǒu}.
- **讲**: 讠 (the dot, then the turning stroke with its rising end), then {井|jǐng}: the two horizontals,
  the slash on the left, and the vertical on the right last.
- **解**: {角|jiǎo} first (7 strokes), then {刀|dāo}, then {牛|niú} with its long vertical last.

## Dialogue: I thought I understood

{安娜|Ān nà} (安娜, Anna) stays behind after class to ask {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī} (王老师, Teacher Wang) about a question.

```dialogue
# I thought I understood
安娜: {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}，{您|nín}{现在|xiàn zài}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{吗|ma}？{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{问题|wèn tí}。
= Do you have a moment now, Teacher Wang? I have a question.
王老师: {有|yǒu}，{你|nǐ}{说|shuō}{吧|ba}。
= Yes, go ahead.
安娜: {今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{语法|yǔ fǎ}，{上课|shàng kè}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}，{但是|dàn shì}{回家|huí jiā}{做|zuò}{作业|zuò yè}，{我|wǒ}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{不|bú}{会|huì}{做|zuò}。
= Today's grammar: in class I thought I'd understood it, but at home doing the homework I couldn't do any of it.
王老师: {是|shì}{哪个|nǎ ge}{题|tí}？
= Which question is it?
安娜: {第|dì}{三|sān}{个|gè}。"{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng}"{和|hé}"{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}"{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}？
= The third one. What's the difference between {我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng} and {我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}?
王老师: "{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}"{是|shì}{说|shuō}，{老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}{的|de}{话|huà}，{你|nǐ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}。"{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng}"{是|shì}{说|shuō}，{你|nǐ}{的|de}{水平|shuǐ píng}{可以|kě yǐ}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}。
= {我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le} says that you've understood what was said. {我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng} says that your level is good enough to understand.
安娜: {哦|ò}，{我|wǒ}{明白|míng bai}{了|le}！"{他|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{太|tài}{快|kuài}，{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}"{是|shì}{说|shuō}，{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{办法|bàn fǎ}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}。
= Oh, I see! {他|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{太|tài}{快|kuài}，{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng} means there's no way I can understand.
王老师: {对|duì}！{你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{聪明|cōng ming}。{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{问题|wèn tí}{吗|ma}？
= Right! You're clever. Any other questions?
安娜: {没有|méi yǒu}{了|le}。{谢谢|xiè xie}{老师|lǎo shī}，{您|nín}{讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{真|zhēn}{清楚|qīng chu}！
= No, that's all. Thank you, you explain things really clearly!
王老师: {不客气|bú kè qi}。{听说|tīng shuō}{你们|nǐ men}{明天|míng tiān}{考试|kǎo shì}，{好好|hǎo hǎo}{复习|fù xí}{吧|ba}。
= You're welcome. I hear you have an exam tomorrow: revise well.
```

- {我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}: {以为|yǐ wéi} for a belief that turned out wrong.
- {我|wǒ}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{不|bú}{会|huì}{做|zuò}: a non-interrogative {什么|shén me} with {都|dōu} and a negative, "nothing at all".
- {哦|ò} *ò* is "oh!" (a sudden understanding).
- {好好|hǎo hǎo} (properly, well) is {好|hǎo} said twice, before a verb: {好好|hǎo hǎo}{复习|fù xí}, {好好|hǎo hǎo}{休息|xiū xi}.

## Reading: is Chinese hard?

> {很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{问|wèn}{我|wǒ}："{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{难|nán}{不|bu}{难|nán}？"
>
> {我|wǒ}{开始|kāi shǐ}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{以为|yǐ wéi}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{很|hěn}{难|nán}，{因为|yīn wèi}{汉字|hàn zì}{很|hěn}{多|duō}，{声调|shēng diào}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{难|nán}。{第|dì}{一|yī}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}，{老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}{的|de}{话|huà}{我|wǒ}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}，{课本|kè běn}{上|shàng}{的|de}{字|zì}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{一|yí}{个|gè}{都|dōu}{不|bú}{认识|rèn shi}。{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{着急|zháo jí}，{想|xiǎng}{换|huàn}{一|yì}{种|zhǒng}{语言|yǔ yán}{学习|xué xí}。{我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{都|dōu}{复习|fù xí}，{但是|dàn shì}{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{还是|hái shi}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。
>
> {我|wǒ}{的|de}{老师|lǎo shī}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}："{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{没有|méi yǒu}{你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{的|de}{那么|nà me}{难|nán}。{每天|měi tiān}{听|tīng}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}{课文|kè wén}，{读|dú}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}，{写|xiě}{十|shí}{个|gè}{字|zì}，{坚持|jiān chí}{三|sān}{个|gè}{月|yuè}，{你|nǐ}{就|jiù}{能|néng}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{了|le}。"{我|wǒ}{用|yòng}{了|le}{老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{方法|fāng fǎ}。{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{每天|měi tiān}{学|xué}{的|de}{新|xīn}{词|cí}{都|dōu}{记|jì}{在|zài}{笔记本|bǐ jì běn}{上|shàng}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{睡觉|shuì jiào}{前|qián}{看|kàn}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。{三|sān}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{过去|guò qù}{了|le}，{老师|lǎo shī}{讲课|jiǎng kè}，{我|wǒ}{差不多|chà bu duō}{都|dōu}{能|néng}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}；{路上|lù shang}{的|de}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{字|zì}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{认得|rèn de}{了|le}。
>
> {现在|xiàn zài}，{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{问|wèn}{我|wǒ}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{难|nán}{不|bu}{难|nán}，{我|wǒ}{会|huì}{回答|huí dá}："{汉字|hàn zì}{难|nán}{写|xiě}，{但是|dàn shì}{不|bù}{难|nán}{认|rèn}；{声调|shēng diào}{不|bù}{容易|róng yì}，{但是|dàn shì}{多|duō}{听|tīng}{就|jiù}{好|hǎo}{了|le}。{我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}，{方法|fāng fǎ}{和|hé}{坚持|jiān chí}{比|bǐ}{聪明|cōng ming}{更|gèng}{有用|yǒu yòng}。"

1. What did the writer think of Chinese at first, and why?
2. What happened in the first week?
3. What method did the teacher suggest?
4. In the writer's opinion, what matters most in learning Chinese?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. That it was very hard ({以为|yǐ wéi}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{很|hěn}{难|nán}), because there are many characters and the tones are hard.
2. The writer couldn't understand anything the teacher said, couldn't read a single character in
   the textbook, got worried and thought of changing to another language.
3. Listen to the text twice a day, read it three times, write ten characters, and keep it up for
   three months.
4. Method and keeping at it are more useful than being clever ({方法|fāng fǎ}{和|hé}{坚持|jiān chí}{比|bǐ}{聪明|cōng ming}{更|gèng}{有用|yǒu yòng}).

"Lots of people ask me: 'Is Chinese hard?'

When I first started learning Chinese, I thought it was very hard, because there are so many
characters, and the tones are hard too. In the first week I couldn't understand anything the
teacher said, and I didn't know a single character in the textbook. I got worried and thought
about switching to another language. I revised every evening, but the next day I'd still
forgotten a lot.

My teacher told me: 'Chinese isn't as hard as you think. Listen to the text twice a day, read it
three times, write ten characters, keep that up for three months, and you'll understand a lot.' I
used my teacher's method. I wrote all the new words of each day in my notebook and looked
through them once before going to bed. Three months went by, and I could understand almost everything
when the teacher taught, and I recognised a lot of the characters in the street too.

Now, when someone asks me whether Chinese is hard, I answer: 'Characters are hard to write, but not
hard to recognise; the tones aren't easy, but they get better if you listen a lot. I think that
in learning Chinese, method and keeping at it are more useful than being clever.'"
</details>

## Write it: your opinion

Write one or two sentences in characters giving your opinion about learning Chinese, with a
reason: {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}… / {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}…，{因为|yīn wèi}….

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{的|de}{声调|shēng diào}{很|hěn}{难|nán}，{因为|yīn wèi}{有|yǒu}{时候|shí hou}{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{清楚|qīng chu}。 — I think Chinese tones are hard, because sometimes I
  can't hear them clearly.
- {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{汉字|hàn zì}{不|bù}{难|nán}，{因为|yīn wèi}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{字|zì}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{像|xiàng}{图画|tú huà}。 — I don't think characters are hard, because lots of them
  look like pictures.
- {我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{语法|yǔ fǎ}{很|hěn}{难|nán}，{但是|dàn shì}{它|tā}{很|hěn}{简单|jiǎn dān}！ — I thought Chinese grammar was hard, but it's very simple!

Check: {认为|rèn wéi} or {觉得|jué de} for your opinion; {以为|yǐ wéi} only if you were wrong.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Understanding
{对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}。
= Sorry, I didn't understand.
{老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}{得|de}{太|tài}{快|kuài}，{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}。
= The teacher speaks too fast: I can't understand.
{您|nín}{讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{真|zhēn}{清楚|qīng chu}！
= You explain things really clearly!
{我|wǒ}{明白|míng bai}{了|le}！
= I've got it!
{我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{来|lái}{了|le}。
= I thought you weren't coming.
{我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}{这个|zhè ge}{方法|fāng fǎ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{因为|yīn wèi}{很|hěn}{简单|jiǎn dān}。
= I think this method is good, because it's simple.
```

## Pronunciation

- {了解|liǎo jiě} liǎo jiě: two third tones, said *liáo jiě*. The {了|le} is liǎo here, never le.
- {认为|rèn wéi} rèn wéi, {以为|yǐ wéi} yǐ wéi: the {为|wéi} rises. {为什么|wèi shén me} has wèi.
- {明白|míng bai} míng bai, {清楚|qīng chu} qīng chu, {聪明|cōng ming} cōng ming: the second syllable is light in all three.
- {讲|jiǎng} jiǎng and {将|jiāng} jiāng (outside HSK 3) sound alike except for the tone; listen for the dip.
- {难|nán} nán (difficult) and {男|nán} nán (male) are the same syllable; {南|nán} nán (south) too.
- {听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng} tīng bu dǒng: the {不|bù} is light and short.

## Common mistakes

- {以为|yǐ wéi} for an ordinary opinion: ×{我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{这个|zhè ge}{方法|fāng fǎ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} (unless it turned out bad). Use {认为|rèn wéi} or {觉得|jué de}.
- ×{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{能|néng}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}: "can't understand" is {听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}, a potential complement, not {不|bù}{能|néng} + verb.
- ×{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng}{了|le} for "I understood (just now)": that is {我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}. ({现在|xiàn zài}{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}, "now I can understand", with the {了|le} of a change, is fine.)
- {讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{清楚|qīng chu} vs {讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{清楚|qīng chu}: with {很|hěn} it's how well (degree); without it, it's whether someone can.
- ×{了解|liǎo jiě} read le jiě: it's liǎo jiě.
- ×{我|wǒ}{什么|shén me}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}: the non-interrogative {什么|shén me} needs {都|dōu} or {也|yě}: {我|wǒ}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}.

## Key points

- Potential complements of understanding: {听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng} / {听|tīng}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}, {看|kàn}{得|de}{清楚|qīng chu} / {看|kàn}{不|bu}{清楚|qīng chu}, {说|shuō}{不|bu}{清楚|qīng chu}, {听|tīng}{不|bu}{明白|míng bai}.
- {听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le} (did understand), {听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng} (can understand), {讲|jiǎng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{清楚|qīng chu} (explains clearly).
- {懂|dǒng} / {明白|míng bai} (understand), {了解|liǎo jiě} (know well, find out about), {懂得|dǒng de} (grasp a principle), {认得|rèn de} (recognise),
  {知道|zhī dào} (a fact), {认识|rèn shi} (a person).
- {认为|rèn wéi}: an opinion; {以为|yǐ wéi}: a wrong belief; {觉得|jué de}: feeling or opinion.
- {听说|tīng shuō} (I hear that), {记|jì} (note down; {记|jì}{住|zhù}, {记|jì}{笔记|bǐ jì}), {忘记|wàng jì} = {忘|wàng}.
- {难|nán} / {容易|róng yì} + verb: {难|nán}{写|xiě}, {容易|róng yì}{懂|dǒng}, {很|hěn}{难|nán}{说|shuō}; {简单|jiǎn dān} (simple), {聪明|cōng ming} (clever), {难题|nán tí} (hard problem).
- Non-interrogative question words: {什么|shén me}{都|dōu} / {谁|shéi}{都|dōu} / {哪儿|nǎr}{都|dōu} (+ negative: nothing, nobody, nowhere).
- Opinion + reason: {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}…，{因为|yīn wèi}…; {你|nǐ}{认为|rèn wéi}{呢|ne}？
- The {青|qīng} family: {请|qǐng} {情|qíng} {晴|qíng} {清|qīng} {睛|jīng}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: At work: 需要, 要求 and separable verbs with a quantity
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

From school to the office. This lesson gives you the words of a working day: the office, the
manager and your colleagues, meetings, problems to solve and work to finish, days off and
holidays. The grammar picks up the separable verbs of HSK 1 and HSK 2 ({睡觉|shuì jiào}, {帮忙|bāng máng}) and shows where
a quantity goes inside them: {请|qǐng}{了|le}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{假|jià}, {开|kāi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{会|huì}. It also adds two verbs you'll use in every
workplace, {需要|xū yào} (to need) and {要求|yāo qiú} (to require).

You'll learn:

- {需要|xū yào} as a modal verb, a verb and a noun: {你|nǐ}{需要|xū yào}{休息|xiū xi}, {需要|xū yào}{时间|shí jiān}, {我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{需要|xū yào};
- {要求|yāo qiú}: to require; a requirement;
- separable verbs with a quantity inside: {请|qǐng}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{假|jià}, {开|kāi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{的|de}{会|huì}, {放|fàng}{几|jǐ}{天|tiān}{假|jià};
- {会|huì} (a meeting) and {会议|huì yì}, {开会|kāi huì}, {办公室|bàn gōng shì} and {室|shì};
- {经理|jīng lǐ}, {同事|tóng shì} and {工作日|gōng zuò rì};
- {解决|jiě jué} (to solve) and {完成|wán chéng} (to complete);
- {服务|fú wù}, {决定|jué dìng}, and the spoken verb {干|gàn} (to do);
- holidays: {放假|fàng jià}, {休假|xiū jià}, {请假|qǐng jià} and {假期|jià qī}.

## {需要|xū yào}: need

{需要|xū yào} is "to need", and it works three ways.

Before a verb it's a modal verb, like {想|xiǎng} or {要|yào}: "need to, have to".

{你|nǐ}{需要|xū yào}{休息|xiū xi}。 — You need to rest.

{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{需要|xū yào}{马上|mǎ shàng}{解决|jiě jué}。 — This problem needs to be solved right away.

Before a noun it's an ordinary verb: "to need something".

{我|wǒ}{需要|xū yào}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{的|de}{笔记本|bǐ jì běn}。 — I need a new laptop.

{学|xué}{外语|wài yǔ}{需要|xū yào}{时间|shí jiān}。 — Learning a foreign language takes time.

As a noun it's "a need": {我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{需要|xū yào} (our needs).

The negative is {不|bù}{需要|xū yào}. Before a verb, {不用|bú yòng} (lesson 05) is the more usual spoken "no need to":

{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{需要|xū yào}{来|lái}。 / {你|nǐ}{不用|bú yòng}{来|lái}。 — You don't need to come.

{你|nǐ}{需要|xū yào}{我|wǒ}{帮忙|bāng máng}{吗|ma}？——{不用|bú yòng}，{谢谢|xiè xie}！ — Do you need my help? No, thanks!

{需要|xū yào} and {要|yào} overlap: {我|wǒ}{要|yào}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{笔记本|bǐ jì běn} is also "I need (want) a new laptop". {需要|xū yào} is more about what is
necessary, {要|yào} more about what you want.

## {要求|yāo qiú}: require, requirement

{要求|yāo qiú} is "to require, to demand, to ask (someone to do something)" and also "a requirement".
Notice the first syllable: *yāo*, first tone, not the *yào* of {要|yào}.

As a verb, it takes a person and then what they must do, like {让|ràng} (HSK 2):

{经理|jīng lǐ}{要求|yāo qiú}{我们|wǒ men}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{办公室|bàn gōng shì}。 — The manager requires us to be in the office by eight.

{老师|lǎo shī}{要求|yāo qiú}{大家|dà jiā}{每天|měi tiān}{写|xiě}{一百|yì bǎi}{个|gè}{字|zì}。 — The teacher asks everyone to write a hundred characters a day.

As a noun, a {要求|yāo qiú} can be high or low, and you can have one:

{这个|zhè ge}{工作|gōng zuò}{要求|yāo qiú}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}。 — This job's requirements are very high. (the job demands a lot)

{你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{要求|yāo qiú}？ — What do you require? (Do you have any requests?)

## Separable verbs with a quantity inside

Many common verbs are a verb + its object: {睡觉|shuì jiào} (sleep + a sleep), {帮忙|bāng máng} (help + a favour), {开会|kāi huì} (hold +
a meeting), {请假|qǐng jià} (request + leave). They're **[[separable verbs]]**: other words can go between the two
parts. You know {帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{忙|máng} (do me a favour) from HSK 2. Now the rule:

- {了|le} and {过|guo} go after the first part (the verb): {开|kāi}{了|le}{会|huì}, {请|qǐng}{过|guo}{假|jià}.
- A quantity (how many, how long) goes before the second part (the object), often with {的|de}
  for a length of time: {开|kāi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{会|huì}, {开|kāi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{的|de}{会|huì}, {请|qǐng}{了|le}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{假|jià}.

| Verb | With a quantity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {请假|qǐng jià} | {请|qǐng}{了|le}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{假|jià} | took three days' leave |
| {开会|kāi huì} | {开|kāi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{会|huì} / {开|kāi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{的|de}{会|huì} | had a meeting / had a two-hour meeting |
| {放假|fàng jià} | {放|fàng}{五|wǔ}{天|tiān}{假|jià} | have five days off (school or work closes) |
| {休假|xiū jià} | {休|xiū}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{的|de}{假|jià} | took a week's holiday |
| {睡觉|shuì jiào} | {睡|shuì}{了|le}{八|bā}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{的|de}{觉|jiào} | slept for eight hours |
| {帮忙|bāng máng} | {帮|bāng}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{忙|máng} / {帮|bāng}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{忙|máng} | did me a favour / helped me a lot |

{我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{请|qǐng}{了|le}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{假|jià}。 — I took a day off yesterday.

{下午|xià wǔ}{我们|wǒ men}{开|kāi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{的|de}{会|huì}。 — We had a two-hour meeting this afternoon.

{下|xià}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{学校|xué xiào}{放|fàng}{五|wǔ}{天|tiān}{假|jià}。 — The school has five days off next week.

A typical learner mistake is to put the quantity after the whole verb, as with ordinary verbs:
×{请假|qǐng jià}{了|le}{三|sān}{天|tiān}, ×{开会|kāi huì}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}. The verb-object inside the word doesn't allow that: the quantity goes
inside.

To ask how many or how long, put the question words in the same place:

{你|nǐ}{请|qǐng}{了|le}{几|jǐ}{天|tiān}{假|jià}？ — How many days off did you take?

{你们|nǐ men}{开|kāi}{了|le}{多|duō}{长|cháng}{时间|shí jiān}{的|de}{会|huì}？ — How long was your meeting?

The person you ask goes before the verb with {跟|gēn} or {向|xiàng} ({向|xiàng} is lesson 26's word): {跟|gēn}{经理|jīng lǐ}{请假|qǐng jià} (ask the
manager for leave).

## Meetings and the office

{会|huì} (a meeting) is the noun behind {开会|kāi huì}. It's the spoken short form; {会议|huì yì} is the full, more formal
word, also for conferences:

{明天|míng tiān}{上午|shàng wǔ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{会|huì}。 — There's a meeting tomorrow morning.

{这|zhè}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{会议|huì yì}，{有|yǒu}{三百|sān bǎi}{人|rén}。 — It's a big conference: there are three hundred people.

{经理|jīng lǐ}{正在|zhèng zài}{开会|kāi huì}{呢|ne}。 — The manager is in a meeting.

Don't confuse the noun {会|huì} (meeting) with the HSK 1 verb {会|huì} (can, will): {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{开车|kāi chē} (I can drive) vs
{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{开会|kāi huì} (I'm going to a meeting). They're written and said the same: *huì*.

{室|shì} is "room" in words: {教室|jiào shì} (classroom), {办公室|bàn gōng shì} (office), {会议|huì yì}{室|shì} (meeting room). On its own it's
written style, mostly on door signs: 302{室|shì} (room 302). {办公室|bàn gōng shì} is the office as a room or a floor;
the company is {公司|gōng sī}.

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {办公室|bàn gōng shì} | office | {我|wǒ}{的|de}{办公室|bàn gōng shì}{在|zài}{五|wǔ}{楼|lóu}。 My office is on the fifth floor. |
| {经理|jīng lǐ} | manager | {王|Wáng}{经理|jīng lǐ}{不|bú}{在|zài}{办公室|bàn gōng shì}。 Manager Wang isn't in the office. |
| {同事|tóng shì} | colleague | {我|wǒ}{和|hé}{同事|tóng shì}{一起|yì qǐ}{吃|chī}{午饭|wǔ fàn}。 I have lunch with my colleagues. |
| {工作日|gōng zuò rì} | working day | {五|wǔ}{个|gè}{工作日|gōng zuò rì} five working days |

{经理|jīng lǐ} is also a title, after the surname: {王|Wáng}{经理|jīng lǐ}, {李|Lǐ}{经理|jīng lǐ}. Colleagues often call each other {小|xiǎo}{王|Wáng} or {老|lǎo}{李|Lǐ}
(lesson 01).

## Getting it done: {解决|jiě jué} and {完成|wán chéng}

{解决|jiě jué} is "to solve": a problem, a question, a difficulty.

{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{我们|wǒ men}{怎么|zěn me}{解决|jiě jué}？ — How shall we solve this problem?

{问题|wèn tí}{解决|jiě jué}{了|le}！ — The problem's solved!

{完成|wán chéng} is "to complete": a task, a plan, a piece of work. It's the word for finishing something you
were given to do:

{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{完成|wán chéng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{工作|gōng zuò}。 — I got a lot of work done today.

{作业|zuò yè}{你|nǐ}{完成|wán chéng}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ — Have you finished your homework?

{完|wán} (HSK 2) is mostly used after a verb, as a result complement: {做|zuò}{完|wán}, {写|xiě}{完|wán}, {吃|chī}{完|wán}. {完成|wán chéng} is a verb on its
own: {完成|wán chéng}{工作|gōng zuò}, not ×{完|wán}{工作|gōng zuò}. {解决|jiě jué} and {完成|wán chéng} both often take {了|le} for a done job, and both have the
potential forms you know: {解决|jiě jué}{不|bu}{了|liǎo} (can't be solved: {了|le} here is *liǎo*), {完成|wán chéng}{不|bu}{了|liǎo}.

## Serving and deciding: {服务|fú wù}, {决定|jué dìng}, {干|gàn}

{服务|fú wù} is "to serve; service". A {服务员|fú wù yuán} is a waiter, waitress or attendant. The restaurant's service
is its {服务|fú wù}:

{这个|zhè ge}{饭店|fàn diàn}{的|de}{服务|fú wù}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 — The service in this restaurant is very good.

{决定|jué dìng} is "to decide" and "a decision". Before a verb it's "decide to":

{我|wǒ}{决定|jué dìng}{明年|míng nián}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}。 — I've decided to go to China next year.

{这|zhè}{是|shì}{经理|jīng lǐ}{的|de}{决定|jué dìng}。 — It's the manager's decision.

{干|gàn} *gàn* is a spoken "to do": {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{干|gàn}{什么|shén me}？ (what are you doing?) is the same as {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}？, a little
more casual. It's common in {干活儿|gàn huór} (to work, do a job: {活儿|huór} *huór*, work) and {干|gàn}{得|de}{不错|bú cuò} (doing well):

{今天|jīn tiān}{你|nǐ}{干|gàn}{了|le}{什么|shén me}？ — What did you do today?

{小|xiǎo}{王|Wáng}{干|gàn}{得|de}{不错|bú cuò}。 — Xiao Wang is doing a good job.

{=Careful with the character: {干|gàn} is *gàn* (to do) here, but *gān* (dry) in {干净|gān jìng} (clean). Traditional
characters write them differently: {幹|gàn} for "do", {乾|gān} for "dry" and "clean". The Traditional switch
shows {幹|gàn} in this lesson and {乾淨|gān jìng} for {干净|gān jìng}.=}

## Holidays and leave: {放假|fàng jià}, {休假|xiū jià}, {请假|qǐng jià}, {假期|jià qī}

All four have {假|jià} *jià*, "time off".

| Word | Who decides | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| {放假|fàng jià} | the school, the company, the country | have a holiday (everyone is off) | {学校|xué xiào}{七|qī}{月|yuè}{放假|fàng jià}。 School breaks up in July. |
| {休假|xiū jià} | you take your own holiday | take a holiday, be on leave | {经理|jīng lǐ}{下|xià}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{休假|xiū jià}。 The manager is on holiday next week. |
| {请假|qǐng jià} | you ask for it | ask for leave, take time off | {我|wǒ}{病|bìng}{了|le}，{要|yào}{请假|qǐng jià}。 I'm ill: I'll take the day off. |
| {假期|jià qī} | (a noun) | the holiday period | {这个|zhè ge}{假期|jià qī}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}？ Where are you going this holiday? |

{放假|fàng jià} is when everyone has the day off: a public holiday, the school holidays. {休假|xiū jià} is time off you have
from work, the days of holiday you take. {请假|qǐng jià} is asking to be absent, often for illness or a family
matter. {假期|jià qī} is the time itself.

A leave request ({请假条|qǐng jià tiáo}, *qǐng jià tiáo*) is one of the short texts you should be able to read and
write at this level. A simple one looks like this:

> {王|Wáng}{经理|jīng lǐ}：
>
> {您|nín}{好|hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{发烧|fā shāo}{了|le}，{需要|xū yào}{去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}{检查|jiǎn chá}{一下|yí xià}，{想|xiǎng}{请|qǐng}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{假|jià}。{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}，{我|wǒ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{让|ràng}{同事|tóng shì}{小|xiǎo}{王|Wáng}{帮忙|bāng máng}{完成|wán chéng}{了|le}。
>
> {李强|Lǐ Qiáng}
>
> {九|jiǔ}{月|yuè}{十五|shí wǔ}{日|rì}

"Dear Manager Wang, I've had a fever since this morning and need to go to the hospital for a
check-up, so I'd like to take a day off. I've asked my colleague Xiao Wang to help finish today's
work. Li Qiang, 15 September."

The parts: the name with a colon, {您|nín}{好|hǎo}, the reason ({发烧|fā shāo}, {去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}), the request ({想|xiǎng}{请|qǐng}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{假|jià}), what you've
arranged, then your name and the date at the bottom right (written with {日|rì}, not {号|hào}).

  jade along its grain; from that, "reason, order" and "to manage". So a {经理|jīng lǐ} is "one who manages".
- {决|jué}: 冫 (ice) and {夬|guài} *guài*, a part that gives the -uai / -ue sounds: jué here, and kuài in {快|kuài}

  {一|yī}.
- {需|xū}: {雨|yǔ} (rain) over {而|ér} *ér*. One old reading: waiting for the rain to stop, "to need".
- {务|wù}: 夂 over {力|lì} (strength): work needs strength. Traditional {務|wù} adds {矛|máo} (a spear) on the left.

### Phonetic components: {里|lǐ}, {义|yì}, {夬|guài}

| Sound part | Characters | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| 里 lǐ | {理|lǐ} (reason) | lǐ |
| 义 yì | {议|yì} (discuss) | yì |
| 夬 guài | {决|jué} (decide), {快|kuài} (fast) | jué, kuài |

{里|lǐ} is an easy one: {理|lǐ} sounds exactly like it. {夬|guài} shows how a sound part can drift: {决|jué} and {快|kuài} share it,
but no longer rhyme.

### Stroke order

- **求**: the horizontal, the vertical hook, the dot on the left, the rising stroke below it, then
  the slash and the long falling stroke on the right, and the last dot at the top right.
- **务**: 夂 first (slash, the turning stroke, the falling stroke), then {力|lì} (horizontal-turn-hook,
  then the slash).
- **定**: 宀, then the horizontal, the short vertical and the short horizontal, the slash and the
  long falling stroke.
- **决**: the two ice dots first, then {夬|guài}: the horizontal-turn, the long horizontal, the slash and the
  falling stroke.
