stopped working. I got very worried: without a computer, how was I going to finish the job?

My colleague Xiao Wang saw this and said: 'Don't worry, let me have a look.' She checked it and
said she couldn't solve the problem; we needed the company's computer service. The service person
came at eleven and solved the problem within an hour.

By then it was already twelve. I decided not to go to lunch and to write in the office.
Xiao Wang bought me a bread roll and a bottle of water. At half past one I finished.

The afternoon meeting went on for two hours. When I'd finished speaking, the manager said: 'Xiao
Li, you explained that very clearly: good work!' After the meeting I treated Xiao Wang to dinner.
I think it's really good to have a good colleague."
</details>

## Write it: a leave request

Write a short leave request to a teacher or a manager, in two or three sentences: the reason,
how many days, and your name and the date.

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

> {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}：
>
> {您|nín}{好|hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{感冒|gǎn mào}{了|le}，{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{发烧|fā shāo}，{明天|míng tiān}{想|xiǎng}{请|qǐng}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{假|jià}。{明天|míng tiān}{的|de}{作业|zuò yè}{我|wǒ}{会|huì}{让|ràng}{同学|tóng xué}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}。
>
> {安娜|Ān nà}
>
> {十|shí}{月|yuè}{八|bā}{日|rì}

"Dear Teacher Wang, I've got a cold and a bit of a temperature, so I'd like to take tomorrow off.
I'll ask a classmate to tell me tomorrow's homework. Anna, 8 October."

Check: {请|qǐng} + number + {天|tiān} + {假|jià}, with the number inside; the date with {日|rì}.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# At work
{经理|jīng lǐ}{正在|zhèng zài}{开会|kāi huì}{呢|ne}。
= The manager is in a meeting.
{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{请|qǐng}{两|liǎng}{天|tiān}{假|jià}。
= I'd like to take two days off.
{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{我们|wǒ men}{需要|xū yào}{马上|mǎ shàng}{解决|jiě jué}。
= We need to solve this problem right away.
{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}{我|wǒ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{完成|wán chéng}{了|le}。
= I've already finished today's work.
{你|nǐ}{在|zài}{干|gàn}{什么|shén me}{呢|ne}？
= What are you up to?
{我|wǒ}{决定|jué dìng}{明年|míng nián}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}。
= I've decided to go to China next year.
```

## Pronunciation

- {要求|yāo qiú} yāo qiú: the {要|yào} is first tone here. {需要|xū yào} xū yào has the usual yào.
- {经理|jīng lǐ} jīng lǐ, {理|lǐ} lǐ: the same syllable as {里|lǐ} (inside) and {李|Lǐ} (the surname).
- {假|jià} jià (time off) and {家|jiā} jiā (home): the same syllable with different tones.
- {解决|jiě jué} jiě jué: the *ue* after j is üe, lips rounded.
- {干|gàn} gàn (to do) falls; {干净|gān jìng} gān jìng starts level.
- {服务|fú wù} fú wù: two syllables that both have *u*, rising then falling.

## Common mistakes

- ×{请假|qǐng jià}{了|le}{三|sān}{天|tiān}, ×{开会|kāi huì}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}: the quantity goes inside the separable verb: {请|qǐng}{了|le}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{假|jià}, {开|kāi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{的|de}{会|huì}.
- Offering help with ×{我|wǒ}{需要|xū yào}{你|nǐ}{帮忙|bāng máng}{吗|ma} (that asks whether *you* should help *me*): the offer is {你|nǐ}{需要|xū yào}{我|wǒ}{帮忙|bāng máng}{吗|ma}？ (do you need me to help?).
- {要求|yāo qiú} said yào qiú: it's yāo qiú.
- ×{完|wán}{工作|gōng zuò}: use {完成|wán chéng}{工作|gōng zuò} or {做|zuò}{完|wán}{工作|gōng zuò}.
- {放假|fàng jià} for your own leave: {我|wǒ}{下|xià}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{放假|fàng jià} means your school or workplace is off; for leave you take yourself,
  say {休假|xiū jià} or {请假|qǐng jià}.
- {=Reading the {干|gān} of {干净|gān jìng} as gàn, or the {干|gàn} of "do" as gān: one simplified character, two words.=}

## Key points

- {需要|xū yào} + verb (need to), + noun (need something), and as a noun (needs); negative {不|bù}{需要|xū yào} / {不用|bú yòng}.
- {要求|yāo qiú} *yāo qiú*: require (someone to do), a requirement ({要求|yāo qiú}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}).
- Separable verbs: {了|le} after the verb part, the quantity before the object part: {请|qǐng}{了|le}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{假|jià}, {开|kāi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{的|de}{会|huì},
  {帮|bāng}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{忙|máng}.
- {会|huì} (meeting, spoken) / {会议|huì yì} (formal, conference); {开会|kāi huì}; {办公室|bàn gōng shì}, {会议|huì yì}{室|shì}, {室|shì}.
- {解决|jiě jué} (solve) a problem; {完成|wán chéng} (complete) a task.
- {服务|fú wù}, {决定|jué dìng} (+ verb), {干|gàn} *gàn* (spoken "do"; traditional {幹|gàn}).
- {放假|fàng jià} (everyone's off), {休假|xiū jià} (your holiday), {请假|qǐng jià} (ask for leave), {假期|jià qī} (the holiday period).
- {=Sound parts: {里|lǐ} in {理|lǐ}, {义|yì} in {议|yì}, {夬|guài} in {决|jué} and {快|kuài}.=}

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Emails, letters and news: 关于, 有关, 根据
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The last core lesson of the module is about messages: emails and letters, notices, the news and
the programmes you watch. Reading an email or a notice and understanding its point is one of the
HSK 3 reading tasks, so this lesson gives you the words that such texts are built from, and
three useful words for saying what something is about and what it's based on.

You'll learn:

- {关于|guān yú} (about, concerning) and {有关|yǒu guān} (to have to do with): {关于|guān yú}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}, {跟|gēn}{天气|tiān qì}{有关|yǒu guān};
- {根据|gēn jù} (according to): {根据|gēn jù}{老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{要求|yāo qiú};
- sending and receiving: {发|fā}, {接|jiē}, {收|shōu} and {收到|shōu dào}; {封|fēng} for letters and emails;
- {邮件|yóu jiàn}, {邮箱|yóu xiāng}, {网站|wǎng zhàn}, {信|xìn}, {电子书|diàn zǐ shū};
- the news: {新闻|xīn wén}, {报纸|bào zhǐ}, {节目|jié mù};
- {影响|yǐng xiǎng} (to affect; influence), {关心|guān xīn} (to care about), {关注|guān zhù} (to follow closely);
- {心里|xīn li} (in your heart, in your mind);
- how a Chinese email and a notice are laid out.

## About: {关于|guān yú} and {有关|yǒu guān}

### {关于|guān yú}: about, on the subject of

{关于|guān yú} introduces the topic: "about, concerning, on". It goes before a noun, and the whole phrase
either opens the sentence or describes a noun with {的|de}. ({关于|guān yú} is lesson 28's vocabulary word; its
grammar comes here, where you'll need it to read emails and notices.)

{关于|guān yú}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}，{我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān}{再|zài}{开会|kāi huì}。 — We'll have another meeting about this question tomorrow.

{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{看|kàn}{一|yì}{本|běn}{关于|guān yú}{中国|Zhōng guó}{历史|lì shǐ}{的|de}{书|shū}。 — I'd like to read a book about Chinese history.

{这|zhè}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{关于|guān yú}{学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{新闻|xīn wén}。 — This is a news story about the school.

At the start of a sentence, {关于|guān yú}… puts the topic up front, then the comment follows after a comma.
In front of a noun, it needs {的|de}: {关于|guān yú}{历史|lì shǐ}{的|de}{书|shū} (a book about history). It doesn't go straight after a
verb as English "about" does: "talk about the problem" is {谈|tán}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí} ({谈|tán} *tán*: to talk about) or {说|shuō}{一下|yí xià}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}, not
×{说|shuō}{关于|guān yú}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}.

### {有关|yǒu guān}: to have to do with

{有关|yǒu guān} is a verb: A {跟|gēn} B {有关|yǒu guān} is "A has to do with B, A is related to B".

{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{跟|gēn}{天气|tiān qì}{有关|yǒu guān}。 — This problem has to do with the weather.

{他|tā}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}{跟|gēn}{电脑|diàn nǎo}{有关|yǒu guān}。 — His work is computer-related.

The negative is {跟|gēn}…{没有|méi yǒu}{关系|guān xi} ({关系|guān xi} *guān xi*, relation, is lesson 29's word; you know it from {没关系|méi guān xi}):

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{关系|guān xi}。 — This has nothing to do with me.

{有关|yǒu guān} also goes before a noun + {的|de}, like {关于|guān yú}:

{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{上|shàng}{看|kàn}{了|le}{有关|yǒu guān}{这个|zhè ge}{节目|jié mù}{的|de}{新闻|xīn wén}。 — I read news about this programme on a website.

Before a noun the two are close: {有关|yǒu guān}{学习|xué xí}{的|de}{书|shū} and {关于|guān yú}{学习|xué xí}{的|de}{书|shū} are both "books on studying". At the
start of a sentence, use {关于|guān yú}. To say that two things are connected, use {跟|gēn}…{有关|yǒu guān}.

| Word | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {关于|guān yú} | {关于|guān yú} + topic，… / {关于|guān yú} + topic + {的|de} + noun | {关于|guān yú}{考试|kǎo shì}，{老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}{了|le}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}。 / {关于|guān yú}{考试|kǎo shì}{的|de}{问题|wèn tí} |
| {有关|yǒu guān} | A {跟|gēn} B {有关|yǒu guān} / {有关|yǒu guān} + topic + {的|de} + noun | {这|zhè}{跟|gēn}{考试|kǎo shì}{有关|yǒu guān}。 / {有关|yǒu guān}{考试|kǎo shì}{的|de}{问题|wèn tí} |

## According to: {根据|gēn jù}

{根据|gēn jù} is "according to, on the basis of". It usually opens the sentence:

{根据|gēn jù}{老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{要求|yāo qiú}，{我们|wǒ men}{每天|měi tiān}{写|xiě}{一百|yì bǎi}{个|gè}{字|zì}。 — As the teacher requires, we write a hundred characters a day.

{根据|gēn jù}{天气预报|tiān qì yù bào}，{明天|míng tiān}{会|huì}{下雨|xià yǔ}。 — According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow. ({天气预报|tiān qì yù bào} *tiān qì yù bào*)

It's also a noun, "basis, grounds": {你|nǐ}{这么|zhè me}{说|shuō}，{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{根据|gēn jù}？ (what grounds do you have for saying
that?). In notices it's very common: {根据|gēn jù}{学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{安排|ān pái} (according to the school's arrangements: {安排|ān pái} *ān
pái*).

## Sending and receiving

| Word | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| {发|fā} | to send | {发|fā}{邮件|yóu jiàn} send an email, {发|fā}{短信|duǎn xìn} send a text, {发|fā}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ} send it to me |
| {收|shōu} / {收到|shōu dào} | to receive (lesson 09) | {收|shōu}{邮件|yóu jiàn}, {我|wǒ}{收到|shōu dào}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{信|xìn} |
| {接|jiē} | to pick up; to answer (the phone); to receive | {接|jiē}{电话|diàn huà}, {去|qù}{机场|jī chǎng}{接|jiē}{人|rén}, {接|jiē}{到|dào}{通知|tōng zhī} (get a notice) |
| {封|fēng} | measure word for letters and emails | {一|yì}{封|fēng}{信|xìn}, {两|liǎng}{封|fēng}{邮件|yóu jiàn} |

{我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{经理|jīng lǐ}{发|fā}{了|le}{一|yì}{封|fēng}{邮件|yóu jiàn}。 — I sent the manager an email.

{你|nǐ}{收到|shōu dào}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{邮件|yóu jiàn}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ — Did you get my email?

{他|tā}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{响|xiǎng}{了|le}，{但是|dàn shì}{他|tā}{没|méi}{接|jiē}。 — His phone rang, but he didn't answer. ({响|xiǎng}: to ring)

{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{机场|jī chǎng}{接|jiē}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}。 — I'm going to the airport to pick up my mother.

{发|fā} + thing + {给|gěi} + person is the common order with a person: {你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{照片|zhào piàn}{发|fā}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ} (send me the photos), {我|wǒ}{发|fā}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}
(I'll send it to you). {接|jiē} is about the moment something reaches you (a call, a person, a notice: {接|jiē}{到|dào}),
{收到|shōu dào} about having it.

{=A note on the character: the {发|fā} of "to send" is {發|fā} in traditional writing, while the {发|fà} of {头发|tóu fa} (hair) is
{髮|fà}. The Traditional switch handles both: {发|fā}{邮件|yóu jiàn} shows as {發郵件|fā yóu jiàn}, {头发|tóu fa} as {頭髮|tóu fa}.=}

## Emails, letters and the internet

- {邮件|yóu jiàn} is an email (the full word is {电子邮件|diàn zǐ yóu jiàn}, "electronic mail"), and also post sent by mail. {邮箱|yóu xiāng}
  is an email address or a mailbox: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{邮箱|yóu xiāng}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}？ (what's your email address?).
- {信|xìn} is a letter: {写|xiě}{信|xìn}, {一|yì}{封|fēng}{信|xìn}. As a verb, {信|xìn} is "to believe": {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{信|xìn} (I don't believe it). The full verb
  "to believe" is {相信|xiāng xìn}, lesson 24's word.
- {网站|wǎng zhàn} is a website ({网|wǎng} net + {站|zhàn} station), and an {电子书|diàn zǐ shū} is an e-book ({电子|diàn zǐ} *diàn zǐ*, electronic).

{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{写|xiě}{信|xìn}，{一般|yì bān}{发|fā}{邮件|yóu jiàn}。 — I rarely write letters; I usually send emails.

{这个|zhè ge}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{电子书|diàn zǐ shū}。 — There are lots of e-books on this website.

## The news: {新闻|xīn wén}, {报纸|bào zhǐ}, {节目|jié mù}

{新闻|xīn wén} is the news, or one news story ({一|yì}{条|tiáo}{新闻|xīn wén}). {报纸|bào zhǐ} is a newspaper; {看|kàn}{报纸|bào zhǐ} is "read the paper". {节目|jié mù} is
a programme on TV or the radio, or one item in a show.

{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{新闻|xīn wén}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ — Have you seen today's news?

{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{每天|měi tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{看|kàn}{报纸|bào zhǐ}。 — My grandfather reads the paper every morning.

{这个|zhè ge}{电视|diàn shì}{节目|jié mù}{很|hěn}{有意思|yǒu yì si}。 — This TV programme is very interesting.

Today most people read {新闻|xīn wén} on a {网站|wǎng zhàn} or on their phone; the words are the same.

## {影响|yǐng xiǎng}, {关心|guān xīn} and {关注|guān zhù}

{影响|yǐng xiǎng} is "to affect" as a verb and "influence, effect" as a noun:

{晚上|wǎn shang}{玩|wán}{手机|shǒu jī}{会|huì}{影响|yǐng xiǎng}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。 — Using your phone at night affects your sleep.

{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{对|duì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{影响|yǐng xiǎng}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。 — This book had a big influence on me.

As a noun it goes with {对|duì}…{有|yǒu}{影响|yǐng xiǎng} (to have an effect on) and {影响|yǐng xiǎng}{很|hěn}{大|dà} (a big influence).

{关心|guān xīn} is "to care about, to be concerned about": people, their health, their studies.

{谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{关心|guān xīn}！ — Thank you for your concern!

{爸爸|bà ba}{妈妈|mā ma}{很|hěn}{关心|guān xīn}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{学习|xué xí}。 — My parents care a lot about my studies.

{关注|guān zhù} is "to follow closely, to pay attention to": the news, a matter, an event; online, also "to
follow" an account.

{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{关注|guān zhù}{这个|zhè ge}{新闻|xīn wén}。 — Lots of people are following this news story.

{关心|guān xīn} is warm, about people you care for; {关注|guān zhù} is attention, about events and news.

## {心里|xīn li}: in your heart

{心里|xīn li} is "in your heart, in your mind": what you feel or think inside, even if you don't say it.

{他|tā}{嘴|zuǐ}{上|shàng}{不|bù}{说|shuō}，{心里|xīn li}{很|hěn}{着急|zháo jí}。 — He doesn't say so, but inside he's very worried.

{我|wǒ}{心里|xīn li}{想|xiǎng}："{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{真|zhēn}{难|nán}！" — I thought to myself: "This question is really hard!"

{收到|shōu dào}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{信|xìn}，{我|wǒ}{心里|xīn li}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 — I was very happy to get your letter.

The {里|lǐ} is light: *xīn li*.

## How an email and a notice look

A Chinese email (or letter) opens with the name and a colon, then {您|nín}{好|hǎo} or {你好|nǐ hǎo} on a new line. The body
follows, and it ends with a greeting such as {祝好|zhù hǎo} (best wishes: *zhù hǎo*), then the name and the
date on the right:

> {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}：
>
> {您|nín}{好|hǎo}！
>
> {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{您|nín}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}{安娜|Ān nà}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{电脑|diàn nǎo}{坏|huài}{了|le}，{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{作业|zuò yè}{没有|méi yǒu}{完成|wán chéng}，{明天|míng tiān}{发|fā}{给|gěi}{您|nín}，{可以|kě yǐ}{吗|ma}？
>
> {祝好|zhù hǎo}！
>
> {安娜|Ān nà}
>
> {十一|shí yī}{月|yuè}{三|sān}{日|rì}

A notice ({通知|tōng zhī} *tōng zhī*) usually has a title with {关于|guān yú}…{的|de}{通知|tōng zhī} ("notice about…"), then the facts:
when, where, who, what to do.

> {关于|guān yú}{开会|kāi huì}{的|de}{通知|tōng zhī}
>
> {根据|gēn jù}{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{要求|yāo qiú}，{本|běn}{星期|xīng qī}{五|wǔ}{下午|xià wǔ}{两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{在|zài}{三|sān}{楼|lóu}{会议|huì yì}{室|shì}{开会|kāi huì}，{时间|shí jiān}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{准时|zhǔn shí}{到|dào}。{有|yǒu}{问题|wèn tí}{的|de}{同事|tóng shì}，{请|qǐng}{发|fā}{邮件|yóu jiàn}{给|gěi}{小|xiǎo}{李|Lǐ}。
>
> {办公室|bàn gōng shì}
>
> {十|shí}{月|yuè}{十二|shí èr}{日|rì}

### Stroke order

- **目**: the left vertical, the top and right side (one turning stroke), then the three
  horizontals inside and at the bottom, top to bottom.
- **报**: 扌 (horizontal, vertical hook, rising stroke), then the right side: the turning stroke
  with its hook, the long vertical, and 又 last.
- **闻**: 门 first (the dot, the left vertical, then the right side with its hook), then 耳 inside.
- **响**: 口, then {向|xiàng}: the slash, the left vertical, the hooked right side, and the small 口 inside.
- **封**: the left 土 twice (smaller on top, the bottom one's last stroke rises), then 寸.

## Pronunciation

- {影响|yǐng xiǎng} yǐng xiǎng: two third tones, said *yíng xiǎng*.
- {新闻|xīn wén} xīn wén and {心里|xīn li} xīn li: the same first syllable.
- {关心|guān xīn} guān xīn, {关注|guān zhù} guān zhù: guān (level) in both; {注|zhù} falls.
- {邮|yóu} yóu rises, like {由|yóu} yóu and {油|yóu} (oil); don't dip it as in {有|yǒu} yǒu.
- {接|jiē} jiē (receive) and {街|jiē} jiē (street, lesson 11): the same syllable.
- {根据|gēn jù} gēn jù: the *u* after j is ü.

## Common mistakes

- ×{说|shuō}{关于|guān yú}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}: {关于|guān yú} doesn't follow a verb. Say {说|shuō}{一下|yí xià}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}, or {关于|guān yú}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{说|shuō}….
- ×{关于|guān yú}{历史|lì shǐ}{书|shū} for "a book about history": {关于|guān yú} + topic + {的|de} + noun, {关于|guān yú}{历史|lì shǐ}{的|de}{书|shū}.
- {这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{有关|yǒu guān}{天气|tiān qì} is formal written style at best; the everyday pattern is A {跟|gēn} B {有关|yǒu guān}: {这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{跟|gēn}{天气|tiān qì}{有关|yǒu guān}.
- {关心|guān xīn} for news: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{关心|guān xīn}{这个|zhè ge}{新闻|xīn wén} is possible but means you're concerned; to follow it, say {关注|guān zhù}.
- ×{一|yí}{个|gè}{信|xìn}: letters take {封|fēng}, and so do emails ({一|yí}{个|gè}{邮件|yóu jiàn} is heard in speech, but {一|yì}{封|fēng}{邮件|yóu jiàn} is the standard).
- Confusing {收|shōu} / {收到|shōu dào} (receive) with {接|jiē} (pick up, answer the phone).

## Key points

- {关于|guān yú} + topic，…: about; {关于|guān yú} + topic + {的|de} + noun ({关于|guān yú}{历史|lì shǐ}{的|de}{书|shū}).
- A {跟|gēn} B {有关|yǒu guān}: A has to do with B; {跟|gēn}…{没有|méi yǒu}{关系|guān xi} (nothing to do with).
- {根据|gēn jù}…，…: according to ({根据|gēn jù}{天气预报|tiān qì yù bào}, {根据|gēn jù}{老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{要求|yāo qiú}).
- {发|fā} (send), {收|shōu} / {收到|shōu dào} (receive), {接|jiē} (pick up, answer the phone; {接|jiē}{到|dào} receive); {封|fēng} (letters, emails).
- {邮件|yóu jiàn}, {邮箱|yóu xiāng}, {信|xìn} (letter; to believe), {网站|wǎng zhàn}, {电子书|diàn zǐ shū}.
- {新闻|xīn wén} (news), {报纸|bào zhǐ} (newspaper), {节目|jié mù} (programme).
- {影响|yǐng xiǎng}: to affect; influence ({对|duì}…{有|yǒu}{影响|yǐng xiǎng}); {关心|guān xīn} (care about people); {关注|guān zhù} (follow news and events).
- {心里|xīn li}: in your heart / mind.
- An email: name + colon, {您|nín}{好|hǎo}, body, {祝好|zhù hǎo}, name, date. A notice: {关于|guān yú}…{的|de}{通知|tōng zhī}, then when, where, who, what.
- {=Sound parts: {门|mén} in {们|men} {问|wèn} {闻|wén}, {艮|gèn} in {根|gēn} {跟|gēn}, {居|jū} in {据|jù}, {向|xiàng} in {响|xiǎng}, {由|yóu} in {邮|yóu}.=}

lessons.title: Confucius and the Analects
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This module has been about school and learning, so its first honors lesson goes back to the most
famous teacher in Chinese history. You'll find out who Confucius was, what the book of his sayings
is, and read three of its shortest and best-known lines in the original classical Chinese, with
pinyin, a modern Chinese paraphrase and our own translation. The lines are about learning, and
Chinese pupils still learn them by heart. This is history and literature: what Confucius taught,
and how it has been remembered, not a judgement on it.

## Who Confucius was

"Confucius" is a Latin form, made by European writers several centuries ago, of {孔夫子|Kǒng fū zǐ},
"Master Kong". In Chinese he is usually called {孔子|Kǒng zǐ}: {孔|Kǒng} is his family name and {子|zǐ} *zǐ* a title of
respect, "master". His own name was {孔丘|Kǒng Qiū}.

By Chinese tradition he was born in 551 BCE and died in 479 BCE. The dates are traditional: the
sources for his life were written later, and they mix history with stories. He lived in the
state of {鲁|Lǔ}, one of many small states of the time, near today's Qufu in Shandong province. He
held office there for a time, travelled from state to state hoping a ruler would put his ideas
into practice, and came back to Lu late in life.

Above all he was a teacher. Tradition says he had a great many students ({弟子|dì zǐ}, disciples), and
he taught people who were not from noble families, which was unusual then. His teaching was about
how to live and how to govern: being humane to others ({仁|rén}), keeping the proper forms of
behaviour ({礼|lǐ}), and learning, which he valued very highly.

## The Analects: {论语|Lún yǔ}

The book of his sayings is the 《{论语|Lún yǔ}》 (*Lún yǔ*), in English the *Analects*. Confucius didn't write
it. It was put together after his death by his students and their students, from what they
remembered him saying and doing, and it probably reached roughly its present form a few
centuries later. It has twenty short books, and most passages are a few lines long. Many begin
with {子曰|zǐ yuē}: "The Master said".

The *Analects* is written in classical Chinese ({文言|wén yán}), the written language of
ancient China. It uses the same characters as modern Chinese, but the grammar is much more
compact, many words are one character long, and some characters have old meanings. That's why the
lines below come with a modern paraphrase: Chinese readers use one too.

## Three lines about learning

The quotations are given in simplified characters, checked character by character against two
published texts (see the notes of this module). The pinyin is the reading used in schools today.

### 1. Learning and practising

> {子曰|zǐ yuē}：{学而时习之|xué ér shí xí zhī}，{不亦说乎|bú yì yuè hū}？{有朋自远方来|yǒu péng zì yuǎn fāng lái}，{不亦乐乎|bú yì lè hū}？

Modern Chinese: {老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}：{学|xué}{了|le}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}，{经常|jīng cháng}{复习|fù xí}，{不|bú}{是|shì}{很|hěn}{快乐|kuài lè}{的|de}{事|shì}{吗|ma}？{有|yǒu}{朋友|péng you}{从|cóng}{很|hěn}{远|yuǎn}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}{来|lái}，{不|bú}{是|shì}{很|hěn}{快乐|kuài lè}{的|de}{事|shì}{吗|ma}？

Our translation: The Master said: "To learn something and practise it at the right times: isn't
that a pleasure? To have a friend come from far away: isn't that a joy?"

- {而|ér} *ér* (and), {时|shí} (at the proper time, often), {习|xí} (to practise, to go over: the {习|xí} of {学习|xué xí} and {复习|fù xí}), {之|zhī}
  *zhī* (it).
- {不|bú}{亦|yì}…{乎|hū} is "isn't it also…?": {亦|yì} *yì* is "also", and {乎|hū} *hū* is a question particle, like {吗|ma}.
- {说|yuè} here is read *yuè*, not shuō: it is an old way of writing {悦|yuè} *yuè* (pleased, glad). It's the most
  famous reading trap in the *Analects*, and every Chinese pupil learns it.
- {乐|lè} is *lè* (joy), as in {快乐|kuài lè}. {朋|péng} is a friend, as in {朋友|péng you}, and {自|zì} *zì* means "from" here.

These are the opening lines of the whole book. The passage goes on for one more line, about not
being upset when others don't recognise you.

### 2. A teacher in every group

> {三人行|sān rén xíng}，{必有我师焉|bì yǒu wǒ shī yān}。

Modern Chinese: {三|sān}{个|gè}{人|rén}{一起|yì qǐ}{走|zǒu}，{里面|lǐ miàn}{会|huì}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{可以|kě yǐ}{做|zuò}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{老师|lǎo shī}。

Our translation: "When three people walk together, there is sure to be a teacher of mine among
them."

- {行|xíng} *xíng*: to walk, to go. {必|bì} *bì*: certainly, must (as in {必须|bì xū}, lesson 27).
- {师|shī} is a teacher, as in {老师|lǎo shī}. {焉|yān} *yān* is "among them, there".

The passage continues: pick out their good points and follow them, and their bad points and
correct them in yourself. Today {三人行|sān rén xíng}，{必有我师|bì yǒu wǒ shī} is used as a saying: you can learn from anyone.

### 3. Reviewing the old

> {温故而知新|wēn gù ér zhī xīn}，{可以为师矣|kě yǐ wéi shī yǐ}。

Modern Chinese: {复习|fù xí}{学|xué}{过|guo}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}，{能|néng}{知道|zhī dào}{新|xīn}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}，{这样|zhè yàng}{就|jiù}{可以|kě yǐ}{做|zuò}{老师|lǎo shī}{了|le}。

Our translation: "Go over the old and learn something new from it, and you can be a teacher."

- {温|wēn} *wēn* is literally "to warm up": to go over again. {故|gù} *gù* is "old, what is known".
- {知|zhī} *zhī* is "to know", as in {知道|zhī dào}. {为|wéi} is *wéi*, "to be, to become", as in {认为|rèn wéi} and {以为|yǐ wéi}.
- {矣|yǐ} *yǐ* is a final particle, a little like {了|le}.

The short form {温故知新|wēn gù zhī xīn} is a four-character saying: "review the old to understand the new".

## Reading: the teacher Confucius

> {孔子|Kǒng zǐ}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{很|hěn}{有名|yǒu míng}{的|de}{老师|lǎo shī}。{两千五百|liǎng qiān wǔ bǎi}{多|duō}{年|nián}{前|qián}，{他|tā}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{鲁国|Lǔ guó}。{他|tā}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{学生|xué sheng}，{他|tā}{教|jiāo}{学生|xué sheng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{不|bú}{看|kàn}{学生|xué sheng}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{没有|méi yǒu}{钱|qián}。{他|tā}{认为|rèn wéi}{学习|xué xí}{很|hěn}{有用|yǒu yòng}，{也|yě}{经常|jīng cháng}{跟|gēn}{学生|xué sheng}{讲|jiǎng}："{学|xué}{了|le}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}{要|yào}{经常|jīng cháng}{复习|fù xí}。"{孔子|Kǒng zǐ}{死|sǐ}{了|le}，{他|tā}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}{把|bǎ}{他|tā}{说|shuō}{的|de}{话|huà}{记|jì}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}，{这|zhè}{就|jiù}{是|shì}《{论语|Lún yǔ}》。{现在|xiàn zài}，{中国|Zhōng guó}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}{还|hái}{在|zài}{读|dú}《{论语|Lún yǔ}》{里|lǐ}{的|de}{句子|jù zi}，{像|xiàng}"{三人行|sān rén xíng}，{必有我师焉|bì yǒu wǒ shī yān}"。

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

"Confucius is a famous teacher in China. More than two thousand five hundred years ago he lived
in the state of Lu. He had many students, and when he taught them he didn't look at whether
their families had money or not. He thought learning was very useful, and he often told his
students: 'You should regularly go over what you've learned.' When Confucius died, his students
wrote down what he had said, and that is the *Analects*. Today Chinese pupils still read
sentences from the *Analects*, such as 'When three people walk together, there is sure to be a
teacher of mine among them.'"
</details>

{死|sǐ} *sǐ* is "to die", and {像|xiàng} (lesson 04) here means "such as".

## Why these lines are still known

The *Analects* was one of the books every candidate in the imperial examinations had to know
(the next honors lesson), and for many centuries it was among the first books children studied.
Today a few passages are in Chinese school textbooks, and lines like {学而时习之|xué ér shí xí zhī} and {温故知新|wēn gù zhī xīn} are part of
everyday Chinese: you'll see them on classroom walls and hear them in speeches about education.

Confucius's ideas have been admired, argued over and reinterpreted for more than two thousand
years, in China and in Korea, Japan and Vietnam. This lesson doesn't take sides on them: knowing
the lines is part of knowing the language and its history.

## Key points

- {孔子|Kǒng zǐ} (Confucius, "Master Kong"), traditional dates 551–479 BCE, from the state of Lu; a teacher
  above all.
- 《{论语|Lún yǔ}》, the *Analects*: his sayings, put together by his students and their students after his
  death; many passages begin {子曰|zǐ yuē} (the Master said).
- {学而时习之|xué ér shí xí zhī}，{不亦说乎|bú yì yuè hū}？ ({说|yuè} = *yuè*, pleased) — learning and practising is a pleasure.
- {三人行|sān rén xíng}，{必有我师焉|bì yǒu wǒ shī yān}。 — you can learn from anyone.
- {温故而知新|wēn gù ér zhī xīn}，{可以为师矣|kě yǐ wéi shī yǐ}。 — review the old and learn the new ({温故知新|wēn gù zhī xīn}).
- Classical Chinese: compact grammar, old meanings ({乎|hū} like {吗|ma}, {矣|yǐ} like {了|le}, {之|zhī} "it").

lessons.title: Exams in Chinese history
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

China has a long history of choosing people by examination. For about thirteen hundred years,
the way into government service went through the imperial examinations, and they left their mark
on Chinese education, literature and everyday language. This lesson tells their story in brief,
retells a famous scene from a novel about them, and ends with one paragraph on the national
university entrance exam of today, the {高考|gāo kǎo}.

## The imperial examinations: {科举|kē jǔ}

The imperial examinations are called {科举|kē jǔ} (*kē jǔ*) in Chinese. Before them, officials were mostly
chosen by recommendation, and family background counted for a great deal. The examinations put a
written test in the middle: in principle, a man who studied hard and wrote well could become an
official whatever his family.

| Period | What happened |
|---|---|
| Sui dynasty ({隋朝|Suí cháo}, 581–618) | Examinations for officials begin. The year usually given is 605; some historians prefer 607 or earlier dates. |
| Tang dynasty ({唐朝|Táng cháo}, 618–907) | The system grows. The most valued degree, the {进士|jìn shì}, becomes a main road into government. |
| Song dynasty ({宋朝|Sòng cháo}, 960–1279) | Many more candidates take part. A final palace examination, presided over by the emperor himself, becomes a regular step. |
| Ming and Qing ({明朝|Míng cháo}, {清朝|Qīng cháo}) | The exams follow a fixed form: answers on the Confucian classics, written as an "eight-legged essay" ({八股文|bā gǔ wén}). |
| 1905 | The Qing court ends the examinations. |

Only men could take them, and in practice it took years of study, so families with money had a
great advantage. Still, the idea that study, not birth, should open the door to office was very
influential, in China and beyond.

### What they tested

The candidates had to know the Confucian classics, among them the *Analects* (the last lesson),
almost by heart, and write about them in a strict style. From the Ming dynasty on, the answers
were written as an eight-legged essay: an essay in a fixed number of parts, with rules for each
part. Critics, then and later, said the form had become more important than the thinking.

### The levels

A candidate climbed step by step, and each level had its own title:

| Title | Pinyin | Level (Ming and Qing) |
|---|---|---|
| {秀才|xiù cai} | xiù cai | passed the local examination |
| {举人|jǔ rén} | jǔ rén | passed the provincial examination |
| {进士|jìn shì} | jìn shì | passed the metropolitan and palace examinations in the capital |
| {状元|zhuàng yuan} | zhuàng yuan | came first in the palace examination |

Only a few candidates passed each level, and many people took the same examination again and
again for most of their lives. The provincial and capital examinations lasted several days, and
the candidates wrote their answers alone in small cells, with their food and their brushes.

Some of these words are still in use. {状元|zhuàng yuan} means "the best in the field": the top student of a
province in today's university entrance exam is often called a {状元|zhuàng yuan} in the press, and the saying
{行行出状元|háng háng chū zhuàng yuan} means "every trade has its champions".

## A story: Fan Jin passes the exam

The most famous story about the examinations is from the 18th-century novel 《{儒林外史|Rú lín wài shǐ}》
(*Rú lín wài shǐ*, *The Scholars*) by {吴敬梓|Wú Jìng zǐ} (1701–1754), a book that makes fun of
scholars and the examination system. Here is one scene, retold in our own words:

> {范进|Fàn Jìn}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{很|hěn}{穷|qióng}{的|de}{读书人|dú shū rén}。{他|tā}{考|kǎo}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{年|nián}，{考|kǎo}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{次|cì}，{都|dōu}{没有|méi yǒu}{考|kǎo}{上|shàng}{举人|jǔ rén}。{他|tā}{的|de}{岳父|yuè fù}{胡屠户|Hú tú hù}{很|hěn}{看|kàn}{不|bu}{起|qǐ}{他|tā}，{经常|jīng cháng}{说|shuō}{他|tā}{没|méi}{用|yòng}。
>
> {那|nà}{年|nián}{范进|Fàn Jìn}{五十|wǔ shí}{多|duō}{岁|suì}，{他|tā}{还是|hái shi}{去|qù}{考试|kǎo shì}{了|le}。{考|kǎo}{完|wán}{回家|huí jiā}，{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{没有|méi yǒu}{米|mǐ}{了|le}，{他|tā}{就|jiù}{拿|ná}{了|le}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{鸡|jī}{去|qù}{街|jiē}{上|shàng}{卖|mài}。{这|zhè}{时候|shí hou}，{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{跑|pǎo}{来|lái}{告诉|gào su}{他|tā}："{你|nǐ}{考|kǎo}{上|shàng}{了|le}！{你|nǐ}{是|shì}{举人|jǔ rén}{了|le}！"{范进|Fàn Jìn}{不|bú}{信|xìn}，{回家|huí jiā}{一|yí}{看|kàn}，{真|zhēn}{的|de}{考|kǎo}{上|shàng}{了|le}。{他|tā}{太|tài}{高兴|gāo xìng}{了|le}，{大|dà}{笑|xiào}{起来|qǐ lái}，{一边|yì biān}{笑|xiào}{一边|yì biān}{往|wǎng}{外|wài}{跑|pǎo}，{他|tā}{疯|fēng}{了|le}！
>
> {大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{着急|zháo jí}，{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{要|yào}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}。{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{说|shuō}："{他|tā}{最|zuì}{怕|pà}{谁|shéi}？{让|ràng}{那个|nà ge}{人|rén}{打|dǎ}{他|tā}{一下|yí xià}，{告诉|gào su}{他|tā}{他|tā}{没|méi}{考|kǎo}{上|shàng}，{他|tā}{就|jiù}{好|hǎo}{了|le}。"{范进|Fàn Jìn}{最|zuì}{怕|pà}{他|tā}{的|de}{岳父|yuè fù}。{胡屠户|Hú tú hù}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{打|dǎ}，{因为|yīn wèi}{范进|Fàn Jìn}{已经|yǐ jīng}{是|shì}{举人|jǔ rén}{了|le}。{但是|dàn shì}{大家|dà jiā}{要求|yāo qiú}{他|tā}{打|dǎ}，{他|tā}{就|jiù}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{范进|Fàn Jìn}{一下|yí xià}。{范进|Fàn Jìn}{真|zhēn}{的|de}{不|bù}{疯|fēng}{了|le}。
>
> {范进|Fàn Jìn}{的|de}{事|shì}{很|hěn}{有名|yǒu míng}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{中国|Zhōng guó}{学生|xué sheng}{在|zài}{课本|kè běn}{上|shàng}{读|dú}{过|guo}。

{穷|qióng} *qióng* (poor), {读书人|dú shū rén} *dú shū rén* (a scholar), {岳父|yuè fù} *yuè fù* (father-in-law), {胡屠户|Hú tú hù} *Hú tú hù*
(Butcher Hu), {看|kàn}{不|bu}{起|qǐ} (to look down on), {疯|fēng} *fēng* (mad), {怕|pà} (to fear, lesson 24). {信|xìn} is "to believe" (lesson 20).

1. How old was Fan Jin when he finally passed?
2. What was he doing when the news came?
3. How did the people around him cure him?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Over fifty ({五十|wǔ shí}{多|duō}{岁|suì}).
2. He was in the street trying to sell a chicken, because there was no rice left at home.
3. His father-in-law, the person he feared most, hit him once ({打|dǎ}{了|le}{范进|Fàn Jìn}{一下|yí xià}).

"Fan Jin was a very poor scholar. He had taken the exam for many years, many times, and never
passed as a juren. His father-in-law, Butcher Hu, looked down on him and often said he was
useless.

That year Fan Jin was over fifty, and he still went to take the exam. When he got home afterwards there
was no rice left in the house, so he took a chicken to sell in the street. Just then someone came
running to tell him: 'You've passed! You're a juren!' Fan Jin didn't believe it, but he went home
to look, and he really had passed. He was so happy that he burst out laughing and ran outside
laughing all the way: he had gone mad!

Everyone was worried and didn't know what to do. Someone said: 'Who is he most afraid of? Get
that person to hit him and tell him he didn't pass, and he'll be all right.' Fan Jin was most
afraid of his father-in-law. Butcher Hu didn't want to hit him, because Fan Jin was now a juren.
But everyone insisted, so he hit Fan Jin once. And Fan Jin really did come to his senses.

Fan Jin's story is very well known: many Chinese pupils have read it in their textbooks."
</details>

The novel's point is sharp: a whole life spent on one exam, and the people around a man change
completely the moment he passes.

## Today: the {高考|gāo kǎo}

China's national college entrance examination, the {高考|gāo kǎo} (*gāo kǎo*: short for the entrance examination to
higher education, {高等教育|gāo děng jiào yù}), was first held in 1952. It was cancelled in 1966 and brought back in late 1977.
Today it begins on 7 June every year and lasts two to four days depending on the province. Every
candidate takes Chinese ({语文|yǔ wén}), mathematics and a foreign language, plus other subjects
they choose, and the results decide which universities they can apply to. The days of the {高考|gāo kǎo} are
a big event: families, schools and whole cities organise themselves around the candidates.

## Key points

- {科举|kē jǔ}, the imperial examinations: from the Sui dynasty (605 is the year usually given) to 1905.
- They tested the Confucian classics; from the Ming on, in the "eight-legged essay" ({八股文|bā gǔ wén}).
- Titles: {秀才|xiù cai} (local), {举人|jǔ rén} (provincial), {进士|jìn shì} (capital), {状元|zhuàng yuan} (first place).
- 《{儒林外史|Rú lín wài shǐ}》 (*The Scholars*) by {吴敬梓|Wú Jìng zǐ}: Fan Jin passes after a lifetime of trying, and goes mad
  with joy.
- {高考|gāo kǎo}: the national university entrance exam, first held in 1952, held from 7 June each year.

lessons.title: Matches and competitions: 比赛, 得 dé, 终于
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 5 is about the things people do for fun and the feelings that go with them: sport, music
and shows, festivals, and the way we tell what happened first and what happened next. It starts
on the sports field. You already play ball games with {打|dǎ} and {踢|tī} ({打|dǎ}{篮球|lán qiú}, {踢|tī}{足球|zú qiú}: HSK 2) and know
{运动|yùn dòng} (sport, exercise). This lesson adds the words of a competition:

- {比赛|bǐ sài} (a match; to compete) and {参加|cān jiā} (to take part in);
- {得|dé} (to get, to win: a score, a prize) and {得到|dé dào} (to get, to receive), and {得分|dé fēn} (to score);
- {一直|yì zhí} (all along, the whole time) and {终于|zhōng yú} (at last);
- three time words: {半天|bàn tiān} (half a day; "ages"), {段|duàn} (a stretch, a period) and {刻|kè} (a quarter of an
  hour);
- the places and people of sport: {球场|qiú chǎng}, {体育馆|tǐ yù guǎn}, {运动会|yùn dòng huì}, {运动员|yùn dòng yuán}, and {网球|wǎng qiú}, {羽毛球|yǔ máo qiú} and {跳|tiào}.

At the end you can read and write a short match report: why someone took part, how the match
went, and how it ended. Telling an event with its cause, its process and its result is one of
the HSK 3 tasks, and this module practises it in every lesson.

## {比赛|bǐ sài} and {参加|cān jiā}

{比赛|bǐ sài} is both a noun, "a match, a competition", and a verb, "to compete, to play a match":

{我们|wǒ men}{学校|xué xiào}{明天|míng tiān}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{足球|zú qiú}{比赛|bǐ sài}。 — Our school has a football match tomorrow.

{这个|zhè ge}{比赛|bǐ sài}{很|hěn}{有意思|yǒu yì si}。 — This competition is very interesting.

{我们|wǒ men}{跟|gēn}{三|sān}{班|bān}{比赛|bǐ sài}。 — We're playing against Class 3.

The verb takes the other side with {跟|gēn} (with, against), not as an object: {我们|wǒ men}{跟|gēn}{三|sān}{班|bān}{比赛|bǐ sài}, never
~~{我们|wǒ men}{比赛|bǐ sài}{三|sān}{班|bān}~~. Matches are counted with the measure word {场|chǎng} (a measure for matches,
shows and films; you know the character from {机场|jī chǎng}): {一|yì}{场|chǎng}{比赛|bǐ sài} (a match), {两|liǎng}{场|chǎng}{比赛|bǐ sài}. A
competition that runs over several days, such as a sports meeting, is often just {一|yí}{个|gè}{比赛|bǐ sài}.

{参加|cān jiā} is "to take part in, to join, to attend". Its object is an event or an activity, never a
person:

{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{参加|cān jiā}{这个|zhè ge}{比赛|bǐ sài}。 — I'd like to enter this competition.

{明天|míng tiān}{的|de}{运动会|yùn dòng huì}{你|nǐ}{参加|cān jiā}{吗|ma}？ — Are you taking part in tomorrow's sports meeting?

{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{参加|cān jiā}{了|le}{考试|kǎo shì}。 — Lots of people took the exam.

To say you went with someone, use {跟|gēn} / {和|hé}…{一起|yì qǐ}: {我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{朋友|péng you}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{了|le} (I went with my friend), not
~~{我|wǒ}{参加|cān jiā}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}~~.

What happens in a match: someone {得分|dé fēn} (scores), and in the end one side wins. "To win" is
{赢|yíng} and "to lose" {输|shū}; they're everyday words but not HSK 3 words, so this lesson
writes them with their meaning when it uses them. Scores are read with {比|bǐ} ("compared with", HSK
2): {三|sān}{比|bǐ}{一|yī} is three–one, {二十一|èr shí yī}{比|bǐ}{十九|shí jiǔ} is 21–19.

{我们|wǒ men}{三|sān}{比|bǐ}{一|yī}{赢|yíng}{了|le}。 — We won three–one.

{他|tā}{在|zài}{比赛|bǐ sài}{里|lǐ}{得|dé}{了|le}{十|shí}{分|fēn}。 — He scored ten points in the match.

## {得|dé}, {得到|dé dào} and {得分|dé fēn}: getting and winning

You know {得|de} as the particle of degree complements, read light: {他|tā}{跑|pǎo}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài} (he runs fast, HSK 2
lesson 18). The same character is also a full verb, read {得|dé}, second tone: "to get, to
gain, to win". In lesson 27 you'll meet a third reading, {得|děi}, "must". The meaning decides the
reading:

| Written | Read | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| 得 | de | particle before a degree complement | {他|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 He speaks well. |
| 得 | dé | to get, to win (a score, a prize, an illness) | {他|tā}{得|dé}{了|le}{第|dì}{一|yī}{名|míng}。 He came first. |
| 得 | děi | must, have to (lesson 27) | {我|wǒ}{得|děi}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 I have to go. |

{得|dé} goes with things you earn or come down with: points, places, prizes, and also illnesses:

{她|tā}{得|dé}{了|le}{第|dì}{一|yī}{名|míng}。 — She came first. (She got first place: {名|míng} counts places in a ranking, HSK 2.)

{我|wǒ}{考试|kǎo shì}{得|dé}{了|le}{九十|jiǔ shí}{分|fēn}。 — I got ninety points in the exam.

{他|tā}{得|dé}{了|le}{感冒|gǎn mào}。 — He's caught a cold.

{得到|dé dào} is "to get, to receive, to obtain", with the result complement {到|dào} (reaching). It's the
word for things that come to you, often things other people give or allow you:

{我|wǒ}{得到|dé dào}{了|le}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{比赛|bǐ sài}{的|de}{票|piào}。 — I got a ticket for the match.

{她|tā}{的|de}{画儿|huàr}{得到|dé dào}{了|le}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{喜爱|xǐ ài}。 — Her painting was loved by everyone. ({喜爱|xǐ ài}: to love, be fond of, lesson
22.)

{他|tā}{得到|dé dào}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{的|de}{关心|guān xīn}。 — He received a lot of people's care. ({关心|guān xīn}: lesson 20.)

{得分|dé fēn} is the sports verb, "to score": {得|dé} + {分|fēn} (point). It can be split by a number, like
other verb–object words: {他|tā}{得|dé}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{分|fēn} (he scored two points), {我们|wǒ men}{一直|yì zhí}{没|méi}{得分|dé fēn} (we didn't score the whole
time).

How {得到|dé dào} differs from {收到|shōu dào} (lesson 09): {收到|shōu dào} is receiving something sent to you, such as a letter or a
message ({我|wǒ}{收到|shōu dào}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{邮件|yóu jiàn}: I've received your email); {得到|dé dào} is getting something you wanted, won or
were given: a ticket, a chance, help, care, love.

## {一直|yì zhí} and {终于|zhōng yú}

{一直|yì zhí} means "the whole time, all along, continuously". It goes before the verb or the
adjective, and the sentence says the state or action didn't stop:

{雨|yǔ}{一直|yì zhí}{下|xià}，{比赛|bǐ sài}{不|bù}{能|néng}{开始|kāi shǐ}。 — It kept raining, so the match couldn't start.

{他|tā}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{练习|liàn xí}。 — He's been practising the whole time.

{我|wǒ}{一直|yì zhí}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{网球|wǎng qiú}。 — I've always liked tennis.

With {没|méi} or {不|bù} after it, {一直|yì zhí} says that something has not happened for the whole time:
{我们|wǒ men}{一直|yì zhí}{没|méi}{得分|dé fēn} (we didn't score at all, the whole time). You met its other use in HSK 2: {一直|yì zhí}{往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu},
"go straight ahead", where {一直|yì zhí} is "straight on". {一直|yì zhí}{到|dào} + time is "right up to": {我|wǒ}{一直|yì zhí}{工作|gōng zuò}{到|dào}{晚上|wǎn shang}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}
(I worked right through until ten in the evening).

{终于|zhōng yú} is "at last, finally": something you waited for or worked for has happened. Like
"at last", it carries relief or joy. The sentence usually ends in {了|le}:

{等|děng}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}，{他|tā}{终于|zhōng yú}{来|lái}{了|le}。 — After waiting ages, at last he came.

{我们|wǒ men}{终于|zhōng yú}{赢|yíng}{了|le}！ — We've won at last!

{雨|yǔ}{终于|zhōng yú}{停|tíng}{了|le}。 — The rain has finally stopped. ({停|tíng}: to stop.)

Put the two together and you have the shape of many match reports: something went one way the
whole time ({一直|yì zhí}), then at last it changed ({终于|zhōng yú}):

{一|yì}{开始|kāi shǐ}，{他们|tā men}{一直|yì zhí}{得分|dé fēn}；{后来|hòu lái}{我们|wǒ men}{终于|zhōng yú}{赢|yíng}{了|le}。 — At the start they kept scoring; later we won at
last. ({后来|hòu lái}, "later on", is lesson 25's word.)

## Time words: {半天|bàn tiān}, {段|duàn} and {刻|kè}

### {半天|bàn tiān}

{半天|bàn tiān} is "half a day": a morning or an afternoon.

{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{我们|wǒ men}{上|shàng}{半天|bàn tiān}{课|kè}。 — On Saturdays we have lessons for half a day.

In speech it's also an exaggeration for "a long time, ages", like English "for ages":

{我|wǒ}{等|děng}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{半天|bàn tiān}！ — I've been waiting for you for ages!

{他|tā}{说|shuō}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}，{我|wǒ}{还是|hái shi}{不|bù}{懂|dǒng}。 — He talked for ages and I still don't understand.

Like other lengths of time, {半天|bàn tiān} goes after the verb ({等|děng}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}): it's a quantity complement.

### {段|duàn}

{段|duàn} is a measure word for a part of something long: a stretch of road, a period of time, a
section of a text or of a piece of music.

{一|yí}{段|duàn}{路|lù} — a stretch of road

{一|yí}{段|duàn}{时间|shí jiān} — a period of time

{这|zhè}{段|duàn}{课文|kè wén} — this section of the text

{这|zhè}{段|duàn}{时间|shí jiān}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}。 — I've been busy these days. (During this period I'm busy.)

### {刻|kè}

{刻|kè} is a quarter of an hour. It tells the time with {点|diǎn}, the way English says "a quarter past":

| Time | Chinese | Or |
|---|---|---|
| 2:15 | {两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{一|yí}{刻|kè} | {两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{十五|shí wǔ}({分|fēn}) |
| 2:30 | {两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn} | {两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{三十|sān shí}({分|fēn}) |
| 2:45 | {两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{三|sān}{刻|kè} | {两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{四十五|sì shí wǔ}({分|fēn}) |
| 15 minutes | {一|yí}{刻|kè}{钟|zhōng} | {十五|shí wǔ}{分钟|fēn zhōng} |
| 45 minutes | {三|sān}{刻|kè}{钟|zhōng} | {四十五|sì shí wǔ}{分钟|fēn zhōng} |

There is no {两|liǎng}{刻|kè}: half past is {半|bàn}. A length of time is {一|yí}{刻|kè}{钟|zhōng}, "a quarter of an hour", built like {分钟|fēn zhōng}.
You'll also hear {差|chà}{一|yí}{刻|kè}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}, "a quarter to three" ({差|chà}:
short of, as in {差不多|chà bu duō}). Many people, the young especially, now just say the minutes ({两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{十五|shí wǔ}),
but {一|yí}{刻|kè} is everywhere in timetables, stories and the HSK.

{比赛|bǐ sài}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{一|yí}{刻|kè}{开始|kāi shǐ}。 — The match starts at a quarter past three.

{从|cóng}{这儿|zhèr}{到|dào}{体育馆|tǐ yù guǎn}{走路|zǒu lù}{要|yào}{一|yí}{刻|kè}{钟|zhōng}。 — It's a fifteen-minute walk from here to the sports hall.

## Where sport happens

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {球场|qiú chǎng} | court, pitch (for ball games) | {学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{球场|qiú chǎng}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。 The school's sports field is big. |
| {体育馆|tǐ yù guǎn} | sports hall, indoor gym | {体育馆|tǐ yù guǎn}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}。 There are lots of people in the sports hall. |
| {运动会|yùn dòng huì} | sports meeting, school sports day | {我们|wǒ men}{学校|xué xiào}{每年|měi nián}{都|dōu}{开|kāi}{运动会|yùn dòng huì}。 Our school holds a sports day every year. |
| {运动员|yùn dòng yuán} | athlete, sportsperson | {他|tā}{是|shì}{网球|wǎng qiú}{运动员|yùn dòng yuán}。 He's a tennis player. |
| {网球|wǎng qiú} | tennis | {你|nǐ}{会|huì}{打|dǎ}{网球|wǎng qiú}{吗|ma}？ Can you play tennis? |
| {羽毛球|yǔ máo qiú} | badminton | {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{打|dǎ}{羽毛球|yǔ máo qiú}{吧|ba}！ Let's go and play badminton! |
| {跳|tiào} | to jump | {他|tā}{跳|tiào}{得|de}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}。 He jumps very high. |

- {球场|qiú chǎng} is any court or pitch: a {足球|zú qiú}{场|chǎng}, {篮球|lán qiú}{场|chǎng} or {网球|wǎng qiú}{场|chǎng} is built from the ball game + {场|chǎng}.
  {体育馆|tǐ yù guǎn} is a building; {馆|guǎn} is the "hall, building" of {饭馆|fàn guǎn}.
- {运动会|yùn dòng huì} is {运动|yùn dòng} + {会|huì} (a meeting, lesson 19): a sports day or sports meeting with many events.
  Schools "hold" one with {开|kāi}: {开|kāi}{运动会|yùn dòng huì}. {运动员|yùn dòng yuán} has the suffix -{员|yuán} (a member, a person with a job:
  lesson 01).
- {羽毛球|yǔ máo qiú} is "feather ball": {羽毛|yǔ máo} is a feather, and the shuttlecock has feathers. You play it, like
  {网球|wǎng qiú} and {篮球|lán qiú}, with {打|dǎ}.
- {跳|tiào} is to jump; {跳舞|tiào wǔ} (to dance) is HSK 2. Two athletics events are built from it: {跳高|tiào gāo}
  (high jump) and {跳远|tiào yuǎn} (long jump).

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 赛 (traditional 賽) | compete; match | sài | 贝 | 14 | {比赛|bǐ sài} |
| 参 (traditional 參) ✎ | take part; join | cān (and others) | 厶 | 8 | {参加|cān jiā} |
| 羽 | feather | yǔ | 羽 | 6 | {羽毛球|yǔ máo qiú} |
| 直 ✎ | straight | zhí | 目 | 8 | {一直|yì zhí}, {直到|zhí dào} |
| 终 (traditional 終) | end; finally | zhōng | 纟 | 8 | {终于|zhōng yú} |
| 于 (traditional 於) ✎ | at; in (written) | yú | {二|èr} | 3 | {终于|zhōng yú}, {关于|guān yú} |
| 段 ✎ | section; period | duàn | 殳 | 9 | {段|duàn} |
| 刻 ✎ | quarter hour; carve | kè | 刂 | 8 | {刻|kè}, {一|yí}{刻|kè}{钟|zhōng} |

- 赛: 贝 (shell, the old money) at the bottom, as in {贵|guì} and {卖|mài}. The top is the top of {塞|sāi} ({塞|sāi}, to
  stuff), which gave the sound: sài. A match was first a thanks-offering, and 贝 stands for what was
  given. Traditional 賽 has the full 貝.
- 参: 厶 on top, {大|dà} in the middle and three slanting strokes 彡 below. Memory aid: a big person
  ({大|dà}) with three flags, joining the parade. In words like {人参|rén shēn} (ginseng) it is read shēn:
  learn cān for now.
- 羽: two feathers side by side; each half looks like 习 (HSK 1). It's also a radical, at the top of
  characters to do with wings.
- 直: {十|shí} on top, 目 (eye) below and a long horizontal at the bottom. A memory aid, close to the old
  meaning: looking (目) straight along a line. You'll meet it again in {直到|zhí dào} (until, lesson 25).
- 终: 纟 (silk) gives the meaning "the end of a thread", and {冬|dōng} (winter: lesson 10) gives the
  sound. Winter is the end of the year: a good memory aid, and the sound part is real.
- 于: three strokes, horizontal, horizontal and a vertical with a hook. It's a written preposition
  "at, in, to" in {终于|zhōng yú} and {关于|guān yú} (about, lesson 28). Its traditional form is 於 (8 strokes), a
  different character that simplified Chinese merged into 于; in traditional text 終於 has 於.
- {段|duàn}: 殳 on the right is a hand holding a tool (as in {没|méi}), and the left side looks like a cliff with
  steps. Memory aid: hitting a rock into sections.
- {刻|kè}: 刂 (knife) on the right: to carve, to cut a mark. Old water clocks measured time by marks cut
  on a rod, and {刻|kè} became the name of a unit of time: today a quarter of an hour. 亥 on the left
  gives the sound (it's read hài on its own).

### Stroke order

- **赛**: 宀 first, then the three horizontals with the two verticals between them (two short
  verticals cross the horizontals), then {八|bā} (left-falling, right-falling), and 贝 last.
- **参**: 厶 (the bent stroke, then the dot), then {大|dà} (horizontal, left-falling, right-falling),
  then the three left-falling strokes of 彡, top to bottom.
- **直**: {十|shí} (horizontal, short vertical), then 目 (the left vertical, the bent stroke on the
  right, the three inner horizontals), and the long horizontal along the bottom last.
- **于**: horizontal, horizontal, then the long vertical with the hook to the left. Don't write it
  like {千|qiān} (which starts with a left-falling stroke) or {干|gàn} (no hook).
- **刻**: 亥 first (dot, horizontal, then the four strokes below it), then 刂 (short vertical, long
  vertical with hook).

```trace
赛参羽直终于段刻
```

{大卫|Dà wèi} (David) and {李明|Lǐ Míng} (Li Ming) are classmates. The school sports meeting is coming up.

- {加油|jiā yóu} ("add fuel") is what fans shout: "Come on!" {给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{加油|jiā yóu} is "cheer you on".
- {比赛|bǐ sài}{完|wán}{了|le} is the result complement {完|wán} (finished, HSK 2): "when the match has finished".

## Reading: the badminton final

> {上|shàng}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}，{我们|wǒ men}{学校|xué xiào}{开|kāi}{运动会|yùn dòng huì}，{我|wǒ}{参加|cān jiā}{了|le}{羽毛球|yǔ máo qiú}{比赛|bǐ sài}。{比赛|bǐ sài}{前|qián}{的|de}{一|yí}{个|gè}{月|yuè}，{我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{下午|xià wǔ}{都|dōu}{去|qù}{体育馆|tǐ yù guǎn}{练|liàn}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}{大卫|Dà wèi}{也|yě}{参加|cān jiā}{了|le}{运动会|yùn dòng huì}，{他|tā}{参加|cān jiā}{的|de}{是|shì}{跳远|tiào yuǎn}{比赛|bǐ sài}。
>
> {运动会|yùn dòng huì}{那|nà}{天|tiān}，{我|wǒ}{一共|yí gòng}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{三|sān}{场|chǎng}{比赛|bǐ sài}。{第|dì}{一|yī}{场|chǎng}{很|hěn}{容易|róng yì}，{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{刻|kè}{钟|zhōng}{就|jiù}{赢|yíng}{了|le}。{第|dì}{二|èr}{场|chǎng}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{难|nán}，{我们|wǒ men}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{多|duō}{小时|xiǎo shí}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{赢|yíng}{了|le}。{第|dì}{三|sān}{场|chǎng}{我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{三|sān}{班|bān}{的|de}{韩雪|Hán Xuě}{比赛|bǐ sài}。{她|tā}{去年|qù nián}{得|dé}{过|guo}{第|dì}{一|yī}{名|míng}，{打|dǎ}{得|de}{非常|fēi cháng}{好|hǎo}。{一|yì}{开始|kāi shǐ}，{她|tā}{一直|yì zhí}{得分|dé fēn}，{我|wǒ}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{着急|zháo jí}。{老师|lǎo shī}{在|zài}{旁边|páng biān}{说|shuō}：“{别|bié}{急|jí}，{慢|màn}{慢|màn}{打|dǎ}！”{我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{了|le}{老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{话|huà}，{开始|kāi shǐ}{打|dǎ}{得|de}{好|hǎo}{多|duō}{了|le}。{我们|wǒ men}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}，{到|dào}{了|le}{二十|èr shí}{比|bǐ}{二十|èr shí}。{这|zhè}{时候|shí hou}，{我|wǒ}{又|yòu}{得|dé}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{分|fēn}，{终于|zhōng yú}{赢|yíng}{了|le}！
>
> {那|nà}{天|tiān}{我|wǒ}{得|dé}{了|le}{第|dì}{一|yī}{名|míng}，{还|hái}{得到|dé dào}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{的|de}{羽毛球|yǔ máo qiú}{拍|pāi}。{韩雪|Hán Xuě}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}：“{你|nǐ}{打|dǎ}{得|de}{真|zhēn}{好|hǎo}！{明年|míng nián}{我们|wǒ men}{再|zài}{比赛|bǐ sài}{吧|ba}。”{那|nà}{天|tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}，{我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{妈妈|mā ma}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}，{她|tā}{听|tīng}{了|le}{也|yě}{非常|fēi cháng}{高兴|gāo xìng}。

{话|huà} is "words, what someone says": {老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{话|huà} is "what the teacher said". {球拍|qiú pāi} is a racket
({拍|pāi}: to pat, the character of {拍照|pāi zhào}). {又|yòu} (again: lesson 26) says it happened once more.

1. What did the writer do to get ready?
2. Why was the third match hard?
3. What did the writer do after hearing the teacher, and how did the match end?
4. What did the writer get?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. For a month before the meeting, the writer practised in the sports hall for an hour every
   afternoon ({比赛|bǐ sài}{前|qián}{的|de}{一|yí}{个|gè}{月|yuè}，{我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{下午|xià wǔ}{都|dōu}{去|qù}{体育馆|tǐ yù guǎn}{练|liàn}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}).
2. Han Xue came first last year and plays very well ({她|tā}{去年|qù nián}{得|dé}{过|guo}{第|dì}{一|yī}{名|míng}，{打|dǎ}{得|de}{非常|fēi cháng}{好|hǎo}), and at the start
   she kept scoring.
3. The writer started playing much better; at 20–20 the writer scored two more points and won at
   last ({这|zhè}{时候|shí hou}，{我|wǒ}{又|yòu}{得|dé}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{分|fēn}，{终于|zhōng yú}{赢|yíng}{了|le}).
4. First place and a new badminton racket ({我|wǒ}{得|dé}{了|le}{第|dì}{一|yī}{名|míng}，{还|hái}{得到|dé dào}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{的|de}{羽毛球|yǔ máo qiú}{拍|pāi}).

"Last Saturday our school held its sports meeting, and I took part in the badminton. For a month
before the competition I went to the sports hall every afternoon to practise for an hour. My
friend David took part in the sports meeting too: he did the long jump.

On the day, I played three matches altogether. The first was easy: I won in a quarter of an hour.
The second was a bit harder; we played for over half an hour, and I won that too. In the third I
played Han Xue from Class 3. She came first last year and plays extremely well. At the start
she kept scoring, and I got a bit anxious. The teacher said from the side, 'Don't panic, take
your time!' I listened to the teacher and began to play much better. We played for ages and got
to twenty–twenty. Then I scored two more points and won at last!

That day I came first, and I also got a new badminton racket. Han Xue said with a smile, 'You
played really well! Let's play each other again next year.' That evening I phoned my mum, and she was
delighted to hear it too."
</details>

## Write it: a match you remember

Write one or two sentences in characters about a match or a competition you took part in or
watched: what it was, how it went, and how it ended. Use {参加|cān jiā} or {比赛|bǐ sài}, and {一直|yì zhí} or {终于|zhōng yú}.

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {去年|qù nián}{我|wǒ}{参加|cān jiā}{了|le}{学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{网球|wǎng qiú}{比赛|bǐ sài}。{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{开始|kāi shǐ}{一直|yì zhí}{输|shū}，{后来|hòu lái}{终于|zhōng yú}{赢|yíng}{了|le}{一|yì}{场|chǎng}。 — Last year I
  entered the school tennis competition. At first I kept losing; later I won a match at last.
- {昨天|zuó tiān}{的|de}{足球|zú qiú}{比赛|bǐ sài}{我们|wǒ men}{等|děng}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}，{雨|yǔ}{终于|zhōng yú}{停|tíng}{了|le}，{比赛|bǐ sài}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{一|yí}{刻|kè}{开始|kāi shǐ}{了|le}。 — For yesterday's football match we
  waited for ages; at last the rain stopped, and the match began at a quarter past three.

Check: {参加|cān jiā} + the event; {一直|yì zhí} and {终于|zhōng yú} before the verb; {了|le} after the change.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{你|nǐ}{参加|cān jiā}{这个|zhè ge}{比赛|bǐ sài}{吗|ma}？
= Are you taking part in this competition?
{我们|wǒ men}{跟|gēn}{三|sān}{班|bān}{比赛|bǐ sài}。
= We're playing against Class 3.
{比赛|bǐ sài}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{一|yí}{刻|kè}{开始|kāi shǐ}。
= The match starts at a quarter past three.
{他|tā}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{练习|liàn xí}。
= He's been practising the whole time.
{我们|wǒ men}{终于|zhōng yú}{赢|yíng}{了|le}！
= We've won at last!
{她|tā}{得|dé}{了|le}{第|dì}{一|yī}{名|míng}。
= She came first.
```

## Pronunciation

- {得|dé}, to get, rises; the particle {得|de} is light. In {得到|dé dào} and {得分|dé fēn} it's always dé.
- {参加|cān jiā}: two first tones, high and level. The *c* is "ts" with a puff of air, as in "cats".
- {赛|sài} falls; don't confuse it with {三|sān}.
- {羽毛球|yǔ máo qiú}: *yu* is ü, lips rounded. A falling-rising tone, then two rising ones: the
  first is usually said short and low.
- {一直|yì zhí} and {一刻|yí kè}: {一|yī} changes before the next tone, yì before the second tone of 直,
  yí before the fourth tone of {刻|kè}. In {三|sān}{刻|kè} sān kè there's nothing to change.
- {终于|zhōng yú}: *zh* is retroflex, tongue curled back; 于 is ü, rising.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我们|wǒ men}{比赛|bǐ sài}{三|sān}{班|bān}~~: the other side takes {跟|gēn}: {我们|wǒ men}{跟|gēn}{三|sān}{班|bān}{比赛|bǐ sài}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{参加|cān jiā}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}~~: {参加|cān jiā} takes an event ({参加|cān jiā}{比赛|bǐ sài}, {参加|cān jiā}{运动会|yùn dòng huì}). With a friend: {我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{朋友|péng you}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{了|le}.
- Reading 得 the wrong way: {他|tā}{得|dé}{了|le}{第|dì}{一|yī}{名|míng} is dé; {他|tā}{跑|pǎo}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài} is de. If 得 means "get" or "win", it's dé.
- ~~{两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{两|liǎng}{刻|kè}~~: there's no {两|liǎng}{刻|kè}. Say {两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{终于|zhōng yú}{到|dào}~~: a "finally" that has happened ends in {了|le}: {我|wǒ}{终于|zhōng yú}{到|dào}{了|le}.
- {一直|yì zhí} after the verb: ~~{他|tā}{练习|liàn xí}{一直|yì zhí}~~. Like other adverbs, {一直|yì zhí} goes before the verb: {他|tā}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{练习|liàn xí}.

## Key points

- {比赛|bǐ sài}: a match; to compete ({跟|gēn}…{比赛|bǐ sài}). Count matches with {场|chǎng}. {参加|cān jiā} + event: to take part in.
- {得|dé}: to get, to win ({得|dé}{第|dì}{一|yī}{名|míng}, {得|dé}{了|le}{九十|jiǔ shí}{分|fēn}, {得|dé}{了|le}{感冒|gǎn mào}). {得到|dé dào}: to get, to receive ({得到|dé dào}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{票|piào}). {得分|dé fēn}:
  to score. Three readings of 得: de (particle), dé (get), děi (must, lesson 27).
- {一直|yì zhí}: all along, the whole time ({一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{练习|liàn xí}, {一直|yì zhí}{没|méi}{得分|dé fēn}); also "straight on". {终于|zhōng yú} + verb + {了|le}: at last.
- {半天|bàn tiān}: half a day; "ages" ({等|děng}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}). {段|duàn}: a stretch, a period ({一|yí}{段|duàn}{时间|shí jiān}). {刻|kè}: a quarter of an hour
  ({两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{一|yí}{刻|kè}, {三|sān}{刻|kè}{钟|zhōng}; no {两|liǎng}{刻|kè}).
- Places and people: {球场|qiú chǎng}, {体育馆|tǐ yù guǎn}, {运动会|yùn dòng huì}, {运动员|yùn dòng yuán}; games {网球|wǎng qiú}, {羽毛球|yǔ máo qiú}; {跳|tiào}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Music, games and shows: 对…感兴趣, 极了, 挺…的
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 21 was about sport. This one is about the other things people do in their free time:
music, games, stories and shows. You'll learn to say what you're interested in and how much you
like something, from "quite" to "extremely":

- {对|duì}…{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù} (to be interested in…) and {有|yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù} / {兴趣|xìng qù} (interest);
- the **[[intensifying complement]]**: {好听|hǎo tīng}{极|jí}{了|le} (extremely nice to hear), {热|rè}{得|de}{很|hěn} (very hot);
- {挺|tǐng}…{的|de} (quite, pretty: spoken) and {特别|tè bié} (especially; special);
- shows and stories: {表演|biǎo yǎn}, {晚会|wǎn huì}, {节目|jié mù}, {音乐|yīn yuè}, {故事|gù shi}, {游戏|yóu xì}, {画家|huà jiā};
- sounds and talk: {声音|shēng yīn} / {声|shēng}, {耳机|ěr jī}, {聊|liáo} / {聊天儿|liáo tiānr};
- the opposites of {好看|hǎo kàn} and {好听|hǎo tīng}: {难看|nán kàn} and {难听|nán tīng}; and {喜爱|xǐ ài}, a written "love".

## {对|duì}…{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}: being interested

{兴趣|xìng qù} is a noun, "interest". {感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù} is "to feel interest": {感|gǎn} (to feel, as in {感冒|gǎn mào}, lesson 05) + {兴趣|xìng qù}.
The thing you're interested in goes in front, with {对|duì} ("towards", HSK 1):

A {对|duì} B ({很|hěn}) {感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù} — A is (very) interested in B

{我|wǒ}{对|duì}{音乐|yīn yuè}{很|hěn}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}。 — I'm very interested in music.

{他|tā}{对|duì}{游戏|yóu xì}{不|bù}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}。 — He isn't interested in games.

{你|nǐ}{对|duì}{什么|shén me}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}？ — What are you interested in?

English puts the topic after "interested in"; Chinese puts it before {感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}, with {对|duì}. {感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù} can't
take an object: ~~{我|wǒ}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}{音乐|yīn yuè}~~ is a typical mistake.

With {有|yǒu} the pattern is the same, and {兴趣|xìng qù} is a plain noun: {对|duì} B {有|yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù} / {没有|méi yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù}.

{我|wǒ}{对|duì}{画画儿|huà huàr}{有|yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù}。 — I'm interested in painting.

{我|wǒ}{妹妹|mèi mei}{对|duì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{文化|wén huà}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù}。 — My younger sister is very interested in Chinese culture. ({文化|wén huà}, culture, is
lesson 23's word.)

{兴趣|xìng qù} on its own is "interest, interests": {他|tā}{的|de}{兴趣|xìng qù}{很|hěn}{多|duō} (he has many interests). Don't mix it up with
{爱好|ài hào} (hobby: HSK 2): an {爱好|ài hào} is something you do, a {兴趣|xìng qù} can be anything you find interesting.

## How much? The intensifying complement

You know the degree words that go before an adjective: {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} (a bit, usually negative), {比较|bǐ jiào}
(fairly, lesson 12), {很|hěn}, {非常|fēi cháng}, {太|tài}…{了|le}. Chinese has two more ways to say "extremely", and both go
**after** the adjective. They're **[[intensifying complements]]**: a complement that only says "very,
very much".

### Adjective + {极|jí}{了|le}

{极|jí} (extreme: lesson 12) + {了|le}, straight after the adjective, is "extremely, really":

{这|zhè}{首|shǒu}{歌|gē}{好听|hǎo tīng}{极|jí}{了|le}！ — This song is just wonderful! ({首|shǒu}: the measure word for songs and poems.)

{今天|jīn tiān}{热|rè}{极|jí}{了|le}。 — It's extremely hot today.

{我|wǒ}{累|lèi}{极|jí}{了|le}。 — I'm absolutely exhausted.

Three rules: nothing comes before the adjective (~~{很|hěn}{好听|hǎo tīng}{极|jí}{了|le}~~), there's no {得|de} (~~{好听|hǎo tīng}{得|de}{极|jí}{了|le}~~),
and {了|le} is part of the phrase, not the change-of-state {了|le}. It's lively spoken Chinese and the most
common of the two.

### Adjective + {得|de}{很|hěn}

{得|de}{很|hěn}, with the light {得|de} of degree complements (HSK 2 lesson 18), is "very, very much". It's a
little more formal or old-fashioned than {极|jí}{了|le}, and you'll meet it in stories and in northern
speech:

{外面|wài miàn}{冷|lěng}{得|de}{很|hěn}。 — It's very cold outside.

{这个|zhè ge}{故事|gù shi}{有意思|yǒu yì si}{得|de}{很|hěn}。 — This story is very interesting indeed.

Compare {得|de}{很|hěn} with an ordinary degree complement: {他|tā}{唱|chàng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} is "he sings well", about the action
({唱|chàng}); {好|hǎo}{得|de}{很|hěn} is just "very good", about the quality itself.

| Before the adjective | After the adjective |
|---|---|
| {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{冷|lěng} (a bit too cold) | {冷|lěng}{极|jí}{了|le} (extremely cold) |
| {比较|bǐ jiào}{冷|lěng} (fairly cold) | {冷|lěng}{得|de}{很|hěn} (very cold) |
| {很|hěn}{冷|lěng} / {非常|fēi cháng}{冷|lěng} / {太|tài}{冷|lěng}{了|le} | {冷|lěng}{多|duō}{了|le} (much colder: comparisons, lesson 04) |

## {挺|tǐng}…{的|de} and {特别|tè bié}

{挺|tǐng} is a spoken "quite, pretty, rather". It often has {的|de} at the end of the phrase, which makes
it friendlier:

{这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{挺|tǐng}{好看|hǎo kàn}{的|de}。 — This film is pretty good.

{他|tā}{的|de}{声音|shēng yīn}{挺|tǐng}{好听|hǎo tīng}{的|de}。 — His voice is quite nice.

{我|wǒ}{最近|zuì jìn}{挺|tǐng}{忙|máng}{的|de}。 — I've been pretty busy lately. ({最近|zuì jìn}, recently, is lesson 25's.)

{挺|tǐng} is weaker than {非常|fēi cháng} and warmer than {比较|bǐ jiào}, the word for an everyday opinion. {挺|tǐng}{好|hǎo}{的|de} alone is a
common answer: "pretty good, fine".

{特别|tè bié} is an adverb, "especially, particularly", and an adjective, "special, unusual":

{她|tā}{唱|chàng}{得|de}{特别|tè bié}{好|hǎo}。 — She sings especially well.

{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{音乐|yīn yuè}，{特别|tè bié}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{音乐|yīn yuè}。 — I like music, especially Chinese music.

{他|tā}{的|de}{声音|shēng yīn}{很|hěn}{特别|tè bié}。 — His voice is unusual. (special, different from others')

{特别|tè bié}{是|shì} + noun is "especially…" at the start of the part you want to stress.

## Shows, stories and games

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {表演|biǎo yǎn} | to perform; a performance | {他们|tā men}{表演|biǎo yǎn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{节目|jié mù}。 They put on an act. |
| {晚会|wǎn huì} | evening party, gala | {学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{晚会|wǎn huì} the school gala |
| {音乐|yīn yuè} | music | {你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{什么|shén me}{音乐|yīn yuè}？ What music do you like? |
| {故事|gù shi} | story | {奶奶|nǎi nai}{给|gěi}{我们|wǒ men}{讲|jiǎng}{故事|gù shi}。 Grandma tells us stories. |
| {游戏|yóu xì} | game | {孩子|hái zi}{们|men}{在|zài}{玩|wán}{游戏|yóu xì}。 The children are playing a game. |
| {画家|huà jiā} | painter | {她|tā}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{有名|yǒu míng}{的|de}{画家|huà jiā}。 She's a well-known painter. |

- {表演|biǎo yǎn} is a verb ({表演|biǎo yǎn}{节目|jié mù}, {表演|biǎo yǎn}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}) and a noun ({他|tā}{的|de}{表演|biǎo yǎn}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}). {节目|jié mù} (lesson 20) is one item on the
  programme: a song, a dance, a short play.
- {晚会|wǎn huì} is {晚|wǎn} (evening) + {会|huì} (gathering): an evening party with performances, at school, at work, on
  television. {开|kāi}{晚会|wǎn huì} is to hold one; {参加|cān jiā}{晚会|wǎn huì}, to attend.
- {故事|gù shi} is gù shi, with a light second syllable. You {讲|jiǎng} (tell, lesson 18) a story: {讲|jiǎng}{故事|gù shi}.
- {游戏|yóu xì} is any game: a party game, a children's game or a computer game ({玩|wán}{游戏|yóu xì}, to play a game).
  Ball games are {运动|yùn dòng} or {比赛|bǐ sài}, not {游戏|yóu xì}.
- {画家|huà jiā} has the suffix -{家|jiā} (lesson 01): a person who is an expert in something. {音乐家|yīn yuè jiā} is a musician,
  {作家|zuò jiā} a writer.
- {喜爱|xǐ ài} is "to love, to be fond of", mostly in writing: {很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{喜爱|xǐ ài}{的|de}{音乐|yīn yuè} (music many people love). In
  speech people say {喜欢|xǐ huan} or {爱|ài}.

## Sounds, headphones and chatting

{声音|shēng yīn} is any sound and, for people, the voice: {我|wǒ}{听见|tīng jiàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{奇怪|qí guài}{的|de}{声音|shēng yīn} (I heard a strange sound; {奇怪|qí guài} is
lesson 24's), {她|tā}{的|de}{声音|shēng yīn}{很|hěn}{好听|hǎo tīng} (she has a lovely voice). {声|shēng} is the short form, in fixed phrases:

{大|dà}{声|shēng} — loudly: {请|qǐng}{大|dà}{声|shēng}{说|shuō}！ (Please speak up!)

{小|xiǎo}{声|shēng} — quietly: {我们|wǒ men}{小|xiǎo}{声|shēng}{说|shuō}{吧|ba}。 (Let's talk quietly.)

{声|shēng} is also a measure word for sounds and calls: {他|tā}{叫|jiào}{了|le}{一|yì}{声|shēng} (he gave a shout), {跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}{一|yì}{声|shēng} (let me
know: "say one sound to me").

{耳机|ěr jī} is headphones or earphones: {耳|ěr} (ear) + {机|jī} (machine). {用|yòng}{耳机|ěr jī}{听|tīng}{音乐|yīn yuè} is to listen to music on
headphones, and {戴|dài} {耳机|ěr jī} is to put them on ({戴|dài} is "to wear" for things on the head, ears or
wrists).

{聊天儿|liáo tiānr} is "to chat": {我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{聊天儿|liáo tiānr} (we're chatting). It's a verb + object ({天|tiān}, "the sky": chatting
about everything), so time goes after {聊|liáo}: {我们|wǒ men}{聊|liáo}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí} (we chatted for an hour). {聊|liáo} on its own
takes what you chat about:

{我们|wǒ men}{聊聊|liáo liao}{吧|ba}。 — Let's have a chat.

{你们|nǐ men}{在|zài}{聊|liáo}{什么|shén me}？ — What are you talking about?

{我们|wǒ men}{聊|liáo}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{音乐|yīn yuè}{的|de}{事|shì}。 — We talked a lot about music.

So "chat about films" is {聊|liáo}{电影|diàn yǐng}, never ~~{聊天儿|liáo tiānr}{电影|diàn yǐng}~~.

## Opposites: {难看|nán kàn} and {难听|nán tīng}

{难|nán} (difficult) before a verb of the senses makes the opposite of {好|hǎo}: {好看|hǎo kàn} / {难看|nán kàn}, {好听|hǎo tīng} / {难听|nán tīng}. You'll
also hear {难吃|nán chī} (tastes bad).

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{真|zhēn}{难看|nán kàn}！ — This piece of clothing is really ugly!

{他|tā}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}{很|hěn}{难听|nán tīng}。 — His singing is awful.

They're strong words. To be polite about someone's singing, Chinese speakers prefer {不|bú}{太|tài}{好听|hǎo tīng} (not
very nice to hear).

### Sound components

Most of these characters are a meaning part plus a sound part, and the sound part is easy to see:

- 故 = {古|gǔ} ({古|gǔ}, old) + 攵 (a hand tapping, as in {教|jiāo}). {古|gǔ} gives the sound gù. 故 itself means
  "old; former; reason": a {故事|gù shi} is an old matter, a story.
- 趣 = {走|zǒu} (walking) + {取|qǔ} ({取|qǔ}, to take). {取|qǔ} gives the sound qù. You know {走|zǒu} as a radical from {起|qǐ}
  and 超.
- {挺|tǐng} = 扌 (hand) + {廷|tíng} ({廷|tíng}, court). {廷|tíng} gives the sound tǐng; the hand is the meaning part. {挺|tǐng}
  also means "straight, upright".
- 演 = 氵 (water) + {寅|yín} ({寅|yín}, a sign of the old calendar). {寅|yín} once gave the sound; today yín and
  yǎn are only close. The first meaning was water flowing far.
- {聊|liáo} = 耳 (ear) + {卯|mǎo} ({卯|mǎo}, a sign of the old calendar, like {寅|yín}). {卯|mǎo} once gave the sound, but liáo and mǎo no longer match. The ear is
  a good memory aid for chatting.
- 特 = {牛|niú} (ox) + {寺|sì} ({寺|sì}, temple). {寺|sì} is a sound part in several characters, but the sounds have
  drifted apart: 特 tè, 持 chí ({坚持|jiān chí}, lesson 05), {诗|shī} (poem), and 時 shí, the traditional form
  of {时|shí}. Remember the family by its shape, not its sound. {牛|niú} on the left is squeezed: its bottom horizontal becomes a
  rising stroke, as in 物.

Three characters are not of this kind:

- 音: 立 on top, {日|rì} below. The old form was 言 (speech) with a mark in the mouth: a sound. 音 is a
  radical of its own and the top of 意 ({意思|yì si}). Memory aid: stand (立) in the sun ({日|rì}) and sing.
- {声|shēng}: 士 on top and a "door" shape below. Traditional 聲 adds 殳 and 耳 (ear): what the ear hears.
  Simplified Chinese kept only the top left corner.
- 戏: {又|yòu} (a hand) + 戈 (an old weapon, the dagger-axe). Memory aid: play-fighting on a stage. Traditional 戲 has
  a different left side; 戈 stays.

### Stroke order

- **音**: 立 first (dot, horizontal, dot, left-falling, the long horizontal), then {日|rì}.
- **{声|shēng}**: 士 (horizontal, vertical, horizontal), then the bent stroke, the short vertical inside and
  the horizontal, and the long left-falling stroke on the left last.
- **戏**: {又|yòu} first (the bent stroke, then the long dot), then 戈: horizontal, the long slanting
  hook, the left-falling stroke, and the dot at the top right last.
- **{挺|tǐng}**: 扌 first, then 壬 (left-falling, horizontal, vertical, horizontal), and 廴, the long
  "walking" stroke under it, last, as in {建|jiàn}.
- **特**: {牛|niú} (left-falling, horizontal, the long vertical, the rising stroke), then 土, then 寸
  (horizontal, vertical with a hook, dot).
