## Pronunciation

- {兴趣|xìng qù} and {感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}: two falling tones in {兴趣|xìng qù}. 兴 is xìng, fourth tone, as in
  {高兴|gāo xìng}; in some other words it's read xīng.
- {故事|gù shi}: falling, then light. {游戏|yóu xì}: rising, then falling.
- {音乐|yīn yuè}: 乐 is yuè, "music". In {快乐|kuài lè} it's lè, "happy": the same character.
- {挺|tǐng}: a dipping third tone. {特别|tè bié}: falling, then rising.
- {聊天儿|liáo tiānr}: the -r joins the second syllable, *tiānr*, said like "tyar".
- {耳机|ěr jī}: *er* with the tongue curled back, then a high, level *ji*.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}{音乐|yīn yuè}~~: the topic goes before, with {对|duì}: {我|wǒ}{对|duì}{音乐|yīn yuè}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}.
- ~~{很|hěn}{好听|hǎo tīng}{极|jí}{了|le}~~: {极|jí}{了|le} already means "extremely"; nothing goes before the adjective: {好听|hǎo tīng}{极|jí}{了|le}.
- ~~{好听|hǎo tīng}{得|de}{极|jí}{了|le}~~: no {得|de} with {极|jí}{了|le}. {得|de} goes with {很|hěn}: {好|hǎo}{得|de}{很|hěn}.
- ~~{聊天儿|liáo tiānr}{电影|diàn yǐng}~~: {聊天儿|liáo tiānr} has its own object. Chat about films: {聊|liáo}{电影|diàn yǐng}.
- {游戏|yóu xì} for sports: ~~{足球|zú qiú}{游戏|yóu xì}~~ for a football match. A match is {比赛|bǐ sài}: {足球|zú qiú}{比赛|bǐ sài}.
- {难听|nán tīng} to someone's face: it's blunt. {不|bú}{太|tài}{好听|hǎo tīng} is kinder.

## Key points

- A {对|duì} B {感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù} / {有|yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù}: A is interested in B ({不|bù}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}, {没有|méi yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù}). {兴趣|xìng qù}: interest.
- Intensifying complements after an adjective: {好听|hǎo tīng}{极|jí}{了|le} (extremely; no {很|hěn}, no {得|de}), {冷|lěng}{得|de}{很|hěn} (very).
- {挺|tǐng}…{的|de}: quite, pretty (spoken; {挺|tǐng}{好|hǎo}{的|de}). {特别|tè bié}: especially ({特别|tè bié}{好|hǎo}, {特别|tè bié}{是|shì}…); special.
- {表演|biǎo yǎn} (perform; performance), {晚会|wǎn huì}, {节目|jié mù}, {音乐|yīn yuè}, {故事|gù shi} ({讲|jiǎng}{故事|gù shi}), {游戏|yóu xì} ({玩|wán}{游戏|yóu xì}), {画家|huà jiā} (-{家|jiā}), {喜爱|xǐ ài} (written).
- {声音|shēng yīn} (sound, voice), {声|shēng} ({大|dà}{声|shēng}, {小|xiǎo}{声|shēng}; {说|shuō}{一|yì}{声|shēng}), {耳机|ěr jī}; {聊|liáo} + topic, {聊天儿|liáo tiānr} (chat).
- {难看|nán kàn} / {难听|nán tīng}: opposites of {好看|hǎo kàn} / {好听|hǎo tīng}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Festivals and life events: 过节, 结婚, invitations
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lessons 21 and 22 were about sport, music and shows. This lesson is about the days that are
different from the others: festivals and holidays, and the big events of a life, being born and
getting married. Then it turns to ordinary days, habits and how long things take:

- {节日|jié rì}, {节|jié}, {过节|guò jié} and {新年|xīn nián}: festivals and celebrating them; {礼物|lǐ wù}, {欢迎|huān yíng}, {文化|wén huà};
- {出生|chū shēng} and {结婚|jié hūn} (a verb that splits: {结|jié}{了|le}{婚|hūn}, {跟|gēn}…{结婚|jié hūn});
- {生活|shēng huó} (life; to live), {平时|píng shí} (normally, on ordinary days) and {习惯|xí guàn} (habit; to be used to);
- {久|jiǔ}, {好久|hǎo jiǔ} and {不久|bù jiǔ} (a long time, ages, soon after);
- {发生|fā shēng} (to happen) and {发展|fā zhǎn} (to develop);
- the HSK 3 task of writing and answering a formal invitation: {欢迎|huān yíng}…{参加|cān jiā}.

## Festivals: {节日|jié rì}, {节|jié} and {过节|guò jié}

{节日|jié rì} is a festival or a public holiday. Each festival has its own name ending in {节|jié} (festival):
{春节|Chūn jié} (the Spring Festival, the lunar new year), {中秋节|Zhōng qiū jié} (the Mid-Autumn
Festival), {国庆节|Guó qìng jié} (National Day). {新年|xīn nián} is the New Year of the calendar, 1 January,
and the greeting is the same one you know from birthdays: {新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè}！

{春节|Chūn jié}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{最|zuì}{大|dà}{的|de}{节日|jié rì}。 — The Spring Festival is China's biggest festival.

{你们|nǐ men}{国家|guó jiā}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{节日|jié rì}？ — What festivals does your country have?

{过节|guò jié} is "to celebrate a festival, to spend the holiday": {过|guò} (to pass, spend: HSK 2) + {节|jié}. It works
like {过年|guò nián} and {过|guò}{生日|shēng rì} (HSK 2):

{你们|nǐ men}{怎么|zěn me}{过节|guò jié}？ — How do you celebrate (the holiday)?

{我们|wǒ men}{每年|měi nián}{都|dōu}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{过节|guò jié}。 — We go home for the festival every year.

{节|jié} is also a measure word for school lessons, "a period": {今天|jīn tiān}{我们|wǒ men}{有|yǒu}{四|sì}{节|jié}{课|kè} (we have four lessons
today), {第|dì}{一|yī}{节|jié}{课|kè} (first period).

Festivals bring {礼物|lǐ wù} (presents) and {欢迎|huān yíng} (welcome):

{我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{妈妈|mā ma}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{礼物|lǐ wù}。 — I bought my mum a present. (A present is counted with {件|jiàn} or {个|gè}.)

{欢迎|huān yíng}！{欢迎|huān yíng}！ — Welcome! Welcome!

{欢迎|huān yíng}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{过节|guò jié}！ — You're welcome to spend the holiday at our home!

{欢迎|huān yíng} + person + verb is the polite way to invite: {欢迎|huān yíng}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}, {欢迎|huān yíng}{大家|dà jiā}{参加|cān jiā}. {文化|wén huà} is "culture": {中国|Zhōng guó}{文化|wén huà},
{节日|jié rì}{文化|wén huà} (the culture of festivals).

## Life events: {出生|chū shēng} and {结婚|jié hūn}

{出生|chū shēng} is "to be born". English uses a passive, "I was born"; Chinese uses an ordinary verb. Say
where and when with the patterns you know:

{我|wǒ}{是|shì}2005{年|nián}{出生|chū shēng}{的|de}。 — I was born in 2005. ({是|shì}…{的|de} for the time of a past event: HSK 2.)

{她|tā}{出生|chū shēng}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}。 / {她|tā}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{出生|chū shēng}。 — She was born in Beijing.

Years are read digit by digit: 2005{年|nián} is èr líng líng wǔ nián.

{结婚|jié hūn} is "to get married". It's a separable verb: {结|jié} (to tie) + {婚|hūn} (marriage). That has three
consequences:

1. The person you marry comes with {跟|gēn} (or {和|hé}), never as an object:

   {他|tā}{跟|gēn}{张丽|Zhāng Lì}{结婚|jié hūn}{了|le}。 — He married Zhang Li.

   ~~{他|tā}{结婚|jié hūn}{张丽|Zhāng Lì}~~ is wrong.

2. {了|le} and {过|guo} can go in the middle, as with {睡觉|shuì jiào} and {帮忙|bāng máng}: {他们|tā men}{结|jié}{了|le}{婚|hūn}{就|jiù}{去|qù}{旅游|lǚ yóu}{了|le} (they went travelling
   as soon as they were married), {他|tā}{没|méi}{结|jié}{过|guo}{婚|hūn} (he has never been married).

3. A length of time after it says how long since the event: {他们|tā men}{结婚|jié hūn}{十|shí}{年|nián}{了|le} (they've been married ten
   years: literally "married, ten years now").

{你|nǐ}{结婚|jié hūn}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ — Are you married? The answer is {结婚|jié hūn}{了|le} or {还|hái}{没|méi}{结婚|jié hūn} (not yet), and {没|méi}{结婚|jié hūn} for "not
married".

## Everyday life: {生活|shēng huó}, {平时|píng shí}, {习惯|xí guàn}

{生活|shēng huó} is a noun, "life (everyday life)", and a verb, "to live (one's life)":

{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}{很|hěn}{有意思|yǒu yì si}。 — Life in Beijing is very interesting.

{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{中国|Zhōng guó}{生活|shēng huó}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{年|nián}。 — I lived in China for two years.

{住|zhù} (HSK 1) is "to live" as in "to stay, to have your home somewhere" ({我|wǒ}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{三|sān}{楼|lóu}); {生活|shēng huó} is about the
way you live and how long: {生活|shēng huó} in a place, {生活|shēng huó}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}, {生活|shēng huó}{习惯|xí guàn} (living habits).

{平时|píng shí} is "normally, on ordinary days", and it often contrasts ordinary days with special ones:

{我|wǒ}{平时|píng shí}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}，{周末|zhōu mò}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。 — Normally I get up at seven; at weekends, at nine. ({周末|zhōu mò}: weekend,
lesson 25.)

{平时|píng shí}{她|tā}{不|bù}{喝|hē}{酒|jiǔ}，{过节|guò jié}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{喝|hē}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。 — She doesn't usually drink, but at festivals she has a little.

{一般|yì bān} (lesson 10) is "usually, as a rule"; {平时|píng shí} is "on normal days, as opposed to holidays or this
time". They often fit the same sentence.

{习惯|xí guàn} is a noun, "a habit, a custom", and a verb, "to be used to":

{早|zǎo}{睡|shuì}{早|zǎo}{起|qǐ}{是|shì}{好|hǎo}{习惯|xí guàn}。 — Going to bed early and getting up early is a good habit.

{我|wǒ}{习惯|xí guàn}{了|le}{这儿|zhèr}{的|de}{天气|tiān qì}。 — I've got used to the weather here.

{我|wǒ}{还|hái}{不|bù}{习惯|xí guàn}{吃|chī}{辣|là}{的|de}。 — I'm still not used to spicy food. ({辣|là}: spicy.)

{习惯|xí guàn} + noun or verb phrase, with {了|le} for "has got used to" and {不|bù}{习惯|xí guàn} for "isn't used to".

## How long? {久|jiǔ}, {好久|hǎo jiǔ}, {不久|bù jiǔ}

{久|jiǔ} is "long" in time ({长|cháng} is "long" in space or in time). It's used in a few common patterns:

{你|nǐ}{等|děng}{了|le}{多|duō}{久|jiǔ}？ — How long did you wait?

{我们|wǒ men}{很|hěn}{久|jiǔ}{没|méi}{见|jiàn}{了|le}。 — We haven't seen each other for a long time.

{好久|hǎo jiǔ} is "a very long time": {好|hǎo} before an adjective is "very, so" ({好多|hǎo duō}, lesson 07). Its best-known use is
the greeting {好久|hǎo jiǔ}{不见|bú jiàn}！ ("Long time no see!").

{我|wǒ}{好久|hǎo jiǔ}{没|méi}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{了|le}。 — I haven't been home for ages.

{不久|bù jiǔ} is "soon, before long, not long after": {他们|tā men}{结婚|jié hūn}{不久|bù jiǔ}{就|jiù}{有|yǒu}{了|le}{孩子|hái zi} (not long after they married, they
had a child), {不久|bù jiǔ}，{天|tiān}{就|jiù}{黑|hēi}{了|le} (soon it got dark).

## {发生|fā shēng} and {发展|fā zhǎn}

{发生|fā shēng} is "to happen, to take place", for events, usually unplanned ones:

{发生|fā shēng}{了|le}{什么|shén me}{事|shì}？ — What happened?

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{是|shì}{去年|qù nián}{发生|fā shēng}{的|de}。 — This happened last year.

{发展|fā zhǎn} is "to develop, to grow", for places, things and people over time, and also the noun
"development":

{这个|zhè ge}{城市|chéng shì}{发展|fā zhǎn}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}。 — This city has developed very fast.

{中国|Zhōng guó}{的|de}{发展|fā zhǎn} — China's development

Both start with {={发|fā}=} (to send out; also in {发烧|fā shāo}, lesson 05). In traditional characters they are
{+{发生|fā shēng}+} and {+{发展|fā zhǎn}+}, like {+{发烧|fā shāo}+}; {头发|tóu fa} (hair) is the one word of the course with the
other form: {+{头发|tóu fa}+}.

## Invitations: {欢迎|huān yíng}…{参加|cān jiā}

An invitation at level 3 is short and formal: what, when, where, and {欢迎|huān yíng} or {请|qǐng}. Here's a class
invitation:

> **{新年|xīn nián}{晚会|wǎn huì}**
>
> {新年|xīn nián}{快|kuài}{到|dào}{了|le}！{三|sān}{年级|nián jí}{二|èr}{班|bān}12{月|yuè}30{号|hào}{晚上|wǎn shang}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{体育馆|tǐ yù guǎn}{开|kāi}{新年|xīn nián}{晚会|wǎn huì}。{晚会|wǎn huì}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{音乐|yīn yuè}、{游戏|yóu xì}{和|hé}{表演|biǎo yǎn}，{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{礼物|lǐ wù}{送|sòng}{给|gěi}{大家|dà jiā}。{欢迎|huān yíng}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{参加|cān jiā}！
>
> {时间|shí jiān}：12{月|yuè}30{号|hào}{晚上|wǎn shang}7:00—9:30
>
> {地点|dì diǎn}：{学校|xué xiào}{体育馆|tǐ yù guǎn}
>
> {请|qǐng}{在|zài}12{月|yuè}26{号|hào}{以前|yǐ qián}{告诉|gào su}{王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{不|bù}{来|lái}。

The invitation is called {邀请|yāo qǐng} (to invite; an invitation). {以前|yǐ qián} (before) is lesson 25's
word, and {快|kuài}{到|dào}{了|le} is "is almost here".

A reply thanks, says yes or no, and adds a wish:

> {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}：{您|nín}{好|hǎo}！{谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}{的|de}{邀请|yāo qǐng}。{我|wǒ}{一定|yí dìng}{去|qù}{参加|cān jiā}{晚会|wǎn huì}，{还|hái}{想|xiǎng}{表演|biǎo yǎn}{一|yí}{个|gè}{节目|jié mù}。{安娜|Ān nà}

> {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}：{您|nín}{好|hǎo}！{谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}{的|de}{邀请|yāo qǐng}。{对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{那|nà}{天|tiān}{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{回|huí}{国|guó}{过节|guò jié}，{不|bù}{能|néng}{参加|cān jiā}。{祝|zhù}{大家|dà jiā}{新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè}！{大卫|Dà wèi}

{一定|yí dìng} (certainly) is lesson 27's word. {祝|zhù} is "to wish": {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{生日|shēng rì}{快乐|kuài lè}, {祝|zhù}{大家|dà jiā}{新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè}.

| To invite | To accept | To decline |
|---|---|---|
| {欢迎|huān yíng}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{参加|cān jiā}！ | {谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}{的|de}{邀请|yāo qǐng}，{我|wǒ}{一定|yí dìng}{参加|cān jiā}。 | {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{那|nà}{天|tiān}{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{事|shì}，{不|bù}{能|néng}{参加|cān jiā}。 |
| {请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{过节|guò jié}。 | {好|hǎo}{啊|a}，{我|wǒ}{一定|yí dìng}{来|lái}！ | {太|tài}{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{那|nà}{天|tiān}{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù}。 |

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 礼 (traditional 禮) ✎ | ceremony; gift; manners | lǐ | 礻 | 5 | {礼物|lǐ wù} |
| 迎 | welcome; meet | yíng | 辶 | 7 | {欢迎|huān yíng} |
| 结 (traditional 結) ✎ | tie; knot | jié | 纟 | 9 | {结婚|jié hūn}, {结束|jié shù} |
| 婚 | marriage | hūn | {女|nǚ} | 11 | {结婚|jié hūn} |
| 活 ✎ | live; alive | huó | 氵 | 9 | {生活|shēng huó} |
| 惯 (traditional 慣) | used to | guàn | 忄 | 11 | {习惯|xí guàn} |
| 久 ✎ | long (time) | jiǔ | 丿 | 3 | {久|jiǔ}, {好久|hǎo jiǔ}, {不久|bù jiǔ} |
| 展 | unfold; show | zhǎn | 尸 | 10 | {发展|fā zhǎn} |

### Sound components

- {婚|hūn} = {女|nǚ} (woman) + {昏|hūn} ({昏|hūn}, dusk). {昏|hūn} gives the sound exactly: hūn. A traditional explanation
  (from an old dictionary, the Shuowen) is that weddings took place at dusk.
- 惯 = 忄 (heart) + {贯|guàn} ({贯|guàn}, to pass through). {贯|guàn} gives the sound exactly, and the heart the
  meaning: what you're used to is in your mind.
- {结|jié} = 纟 (silk thread) + {吉|jí} ({吉|jí}, lucky). {吉|jí} gives a close sound, jí for jié; the thread gives the
  meaning, "to tie a knot". It's also the {结|jié} of {结束|jié shù} (to end: lesson 28).
- 迎 = {卬|áng} ({卬|áng}, an old word for "I; to look up") + 辶 (walking). {卬|áng} once gave the sound, but áng
  and yíng no longer match. Going (辶) out to meet someone is to welcome them.

### The others

- 礼: 礻 is {示|shì} (an altar) on the left, the radical of things to do with gods and ceremonies. 礼 was
  first a ceremony, then good manners, then a gift. Traditional 禮 has {豊|lǐ} (a ritual vessel) on the
  right; the short form 礼 is very old, not a 20th-century invention.
- 活: 氵 (water) + a right side that looks like {舌|shé} (tongue). In older forms the right side was a
  different part that gave the sound, so treat "water and a tongue: alive" as a memory aid.
- {久|jiǔ}: three strokes. Don't confuse it with {么|me} (in {什么|shén me}) or {夕|xī}.
- 展: 尸 (a body lying down: the radical of {层|céng} and 屋, lesson 02) over the rest. 展 is to spread out,
  open up: {发展|fā zhǎn} is to send out and spread, to develop.

### Stroke order

- **礼**: 礻 (dot, the bent stroke, vertical, short dot), then the long 乚 on the right in one
  stroke.
- **迎**: {卬|áng} first (the left part, then the right part with its long vertical), 辶 last.
- **{久|jiǔ}**: left-falling stroke, then the bent stroke (horizontal turning into a long left-falling
  stroke), then the right-falling stroke.
- **展**: 尸 (the bent stroke, horizontal, long left-falling stroke), then the inside: horizontal,
  two verticals, horizontal, and the three strokes of the bottom.
- **活**: 氵 (dot, dot, rising stroke), then the right: left-falling, horizontal, vertical, then {口|kǒu}.

```trace
礼迎结婚活惯久展
```

Write it: 礼, {结|jié}, 活 and {久|jiǔ} are characters to know by hand. Write each three times from memory.
For 礼, the right side is one stroke.
=}

## Dialogue: going home for the Spring Festival

{安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) meets {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) after the winter exams.

```dialogue
# Going home for the festival
安娜: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}，{好久|hǎo jiǔ}{不见|bú jiàn}！{考试|kǎo shì}{考|kǎo}{得|de}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
= Wang Fang, long time no see! How did your exams go?
王芳: {还|hái}{不错|bú cuò}。{马上|mǎ shàng}{要|yào}{过|guò}{春节|Chūn jié}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{过节|guò jié}。
= Not bad. It's almost the Spring Festival: I'm going home for the holiday tomorrow.
安娜: {你们|nǐ men}{家|jiā}{一般|yì bān}{怎么|zěn me}{过节|guò jié}？
= How does your family usually spend the festival?
王芳: {我们|wǒ men}{全家|quán jiā}{人|rén}{一起|yì qǐ}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}、{聊天儿|liáo tiānr}，{给|gěi}{孩子|hái zi}{们|men}{送|sòng}{礼物|lǐ wù}。{你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？{你|nǐ}{习惯|xí guàn}{在|zài}{中国|Zhōng guó}{过节|guò jié}{了|le}{吗|ma}？
= The whole family eats together and chats, and we give the children presents. And you? Are you used to the festivals in China?
安娜: {还|hái}{不|bú}{太|tài}{习惯|xí guàn}。{我们|wǒ men}{国家|guó jiā}{没有|méi yǒu}{春节|Chūn jié}。
= Not quite yet. We don't have the Spring Festival in my country.
王芳: {那|nà}{你|nǐ}{跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{吧|ba}！{欢迎|huān yíng}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{过节|guò jié}！
= Then come home with me! You're welcome to spend the festival with us!
安娜: {真|zhēn}{的|de}{吗|ma}？{太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！{我|wǒ}{对|duì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{的|de}{节日|jié rì}{文化|wén huà}{特别|tè bié}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}。
= Really? Great! I'm really interested in Chinese festival culture.
王芳: {我|wǒ}{表姐|biǎo jiě}{也|yě}{来|lái}，{她|tā}{去年|qù nián}{刚|gāng}{结婚|jié hūn}，{你们|nǐ men}{可以|kě yǐ}{一起|yì qǐ}{聊聊|liáo liao}。
= My cousin is coming too. She only got married last year: you two can have a chat.
```

- {全家|quán jiā}{人|rén} is "the whole family" ({全|quán}: whole, as in {安全|ān quán}, lesson 13).
- {马上|mǎ shàng}{要|yào}{过|guò}{春节|Chūn jié}{了|le} uses {要|yào}…{了|le} (about to: HSK 2) with {马上|mǎ shàng} (right away, lesson 13).
- {刚|gāng} (only just) is lesson 25's word: {刚|gāng}{结婚|jié hūn} is "only just got married".
- {表姐|biǎo jiě} is an older female cousin, like the {表妹|biǎo mèi} and {表哥|biǎo gē} of lesson 04.

## Reading: how my grandparents met

> {我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{是|shì}1950{年|nián}{在|zài}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{城市|chéng shì}{出生|chū shēng}{的|de}。{他|tā}{年轻|nián qīng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{在|zài}{火车|huǒ chē}{站|zhàn}{工作|gōng zuò}。{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{年|nián}{春节|Chūn jié}，{车站|chē zhàn}{的|de}{人|rén}{特别|tè bié}{多|duō}。{一|yí}{个|gè}{女|nǚ}{孩子|hái zi}{找|zhǎo}{不|bú}{到|dào}{她|tā}{的|de}{行李|xíng li}{了|le}，{非常|fēi cháng}{着急|zháo jí}，{在|zài}{那儿|nàr}{哭|kū}。{爷爷|yé ye}{帮|bāng}{她|tā}{找|zhǎo}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}，{终于|zhōng yú}{在|zài}{一|yì}{把|bǎ}{椅子|yǐ zi}{下面|xià miàn}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{了|le}。{那个|nà ge}{女|nǚ}{孩子|hái zi}{就|jiù}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{奶奶|nǎi nai}！
>
> {过|guò}{了|le}{不久|bù jiǔ}，{奶奶|nǎi nai}{给|gěi}{爷爷|yé ye}{送|sòng}{了|le}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{礼物|lǐ wù}，{谢谢|xiè xie}{他|tā}。{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{开始|kāi shǐ}{一起|yì qǐ}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}、{聊天儿|liáo tiānr}。{爷爷|yé ye}{说|shuō}，{他|tā}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{看见|kàn jiàn}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{就|jiù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{她|tā}{了|le}。1975{年|nián}，{他们|tā men}{结婚|jié hūn}{了|le}。{结|jié}{了|le}{婚|hūn}，{他们|tā men}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{这个|zhè ge}{城市|chéng shì}{生活|shēng huó}。
>
> {这|zhè}{几|jǐ}{十|shí}{年|nián}，{城市|chéng shì}{发展|fā zhǎn}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}，{可是|kě shì}{爷爷|yé ye}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}{习惯|xí guàn}{没有|méi yǒu}{变|biàn}：{他们|tā men}{平时|píng shí}{早上|zǎo shang}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{公园|gōng yuán}{走走|zǒu zou}。{每年|měi nián}{过节|guò jié}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{我们|wǒ men}{全家|quán jiā}{都|dōu}{去|qù}{他们|tā men}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}，{热闹|rè nao}{极|jí}{了|le}。{奶奶|nǎi nai}{还|hái}{会|huì}{给|gěi}{每|měi}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{小|xiǎo}{礼物|lǐ wù}。{奶奶|nǎi nai}{常|cháng}{说|shuō}：“{没有|méi yǒu}{那|nà}{天|tiān}{发生|fā shēng}{的|de}{事|shì}，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{我们|wǒ men}{这个|zhè ge}{家|jiā}！”

{热闹|rè nao} is "lively, bustling". {可是|kě shì} (but) is lesson 27's word and {常|cháng} (often) lesson 27's too.
{哭|kū} (to cry) is next lesson's.

1. Where and when was the grandfather born?
2. What happened at the station, and how did it end?
3. What happened not long after?
4. What hasn't changed?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. In a small city, in 1950 (1950{年|nián}{在|zài}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{城市|chéng shì}{出生|chū shēng}{的|de}).
2. A girl couldn't find her luggage and was crying; he helped her look for ages and at last found
   it under a chair ({终于|zhōng yú}{在|zài}{一|yì}{把|bǎ}{椅子|yǐ zi}{下面|xià miàn}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{了|le}). The girl was the writer's grandmother.
3. She gave him a present to thank him, they started going to films and chatting, and they married
   in 1975.
4. Their habits: normally they get up at six and go for a walk in the park in the evening
   ({他们|tā men}{平时|píng shí}{早上|zǎo shang}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{公园|gōng yuán}{走走|zǒu zou}).

"My grandfather was born in 1950 in a small city. When he was young he worked at the railway
station. One Spring Festival, the station was especially crowded. A girl couldn't find her
luggage; she was very anxious and stood there crying. Grandpa helped her look for ages, and at
last they found it under a chair. That girl was my grandmother!

Not long after, Grandma gave Grandpa a present to thank him. The two of them began going to films
and chatting together. Grandpa says he liked her from the first time he saw her. In 1975 they got married. Once married, they lived in this city the whole
time.

In these few decades the city has developed very fast, but my grandparents' habits haven't
changed: normally they get up at six in the morning and go for a walk in the park together in the
evening. Every year at festival time, the whole family goes to their home to eat, and it's
wonderfully lively. Grandma always gets a little present ready for each of the children. Grandma often says, 'Without what happened that day, there'd be no family of
ours!'"
</details>

## Write it: an invitation and a reply

Write a short invitation in characters (one or two sentences, with {欢迎|huān yíng} or {请|qǐng}, a time and a
place), then a one-sentence reply that accepts or declines.

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{晚上|wǎn shang}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{生日|shēng rì}{晚会|wǎn huì}，{欢迎|huān yíng}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{参加|cān jiā}！ — There's a birthday party at my home at six on
  Saturday evening: you're very welcome to come!
- {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{邀请|yāo qǐng}，{我|wǒ}{一定|yí dìng}{来|lái}！ / {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{事|shì}，{不|bù}{能|néng}{参加|cān jiā}。 — Thank you for the invitation,
  I'll definitely come! / Sorry, I'm busy on Saturday and can't come.

Check: {欢迎|huān yíng} + person + verb; time before place; a thank-you in the reply.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{好久|hǎo jiǔ}{不见|bú jiàn}！
= Long time no see!
{你们|nǐ men}{怎么|zěn me}{过节|guò jié}？
= How do you celebrate the festival?
{欢迎|huān yíng}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{过节|guò jié}！
= You're welcome to spend the festival at our home!
{我|wǒ}{是|shì}2005{年|nián}{出生|chū shēng}{的|de}。
= I was born in 2005.
{他们|tā men}{结婚|jié hūn}{十|shí}{年|nián}{了|le}。
= They've been married for ten years.
{我|wǒ}{还|hái}{不|bù}{习惯|xí guàn}{这儿|zhèr}{的|de}{天气|tiān qì}。
= I'm still not used to the weather here.
{发生|fā shēng}{了|le}{什么|shén me}{事|shì}？
= What happened?
```

## Pronunciation

- {节日|jié rì}: rising, then the retroflex *ri*, falling. {过节|guò jié}: falling, then rising.
- {礼物|lǐ wù}: dipping, then falling. Don't let 礼 rise into {离|lí} (away from).
- {结婚|jié hūn}: rising, then level. {欢迎|huān yíng}: level, then rising.
- {生活|shēng huó}: two clear tones; *huo* rises.
- {习惯|xí guàn}: rising, then falling: xí guàn.
- {久|jiǔ} and {酒|jiǔ} (alcohol) sound the same: {好久|hǎo jiǔ} is said háo jiǔ (two third tones).
- {发生|fā shēng}, {发展|fā zhǎn}: {={发|fā}=} is first tone, fā. Its other reading, fà, is only in {头发|tóu fa}.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{他|tā}{结婚|jié hūn}{张丽|Zhāng Lì}~~: {结婚|jié hūn} doesn't take an object. {他|tā}{跟|gēn}{张丽|Zhāng Lì}{结婚|jié hūn}{了|le}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{出生|chū shēng}2005{年|nián}~~ in English order: the time goes before the verb. {我|wǒ}2005{年|nián}{出生|chū shēng}, or with
  {是|shì}…{的|de}: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}2005{年|nián}{出生|chū shēng}{的|de}.
- {住|zhù} for "life": ~~{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{住|zhù}{很|hěn}{有意思|yǒu yì si}~~. Life is {生活|shēng huó}.
- ~~{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{时间|shí jiān}{不见|bú jiàn}~~ as a greeting: the set phrase is {好久|hǎo jiǔ}{不见|bú jiàn}.
- {发生|fā shēng} for planned events: a party doesn't {发生|fā shēng}; it {开|kāi} or {有|yǒu}: {星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{有|yǒu}{晚会|wǎn huì}.
- {欢迎|huān yíng} with the guest after the verb: ~~{欢迎|huān yíng}{参加|cān jiā}{你|nǐ}~~. {欢迎|huān yíng}{你|nǐ}{参加|cān jiā}.

## Key points

- {节日|jié rì}: festival; names end in {节|jié} ({春节|Chūn jié}). {过节|guò jié}: to celebrate a festival. {节|jié}: also a class period
  ({四|sì}{节|jié}{课|kè}). {新年|xīn nián}, {礼物|lǐ wù}, {欢迎|huān yíng} ({欢迎|huān yíng}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}…), {文化|wén huà}.
- {出生|chū shēng}: to be born ({是|shì}2005{年|nián}{出生|chū shēng}{的|de}, {出生|chū shēng}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}). {结婚|jié hūn}: separable ({跟|gēn}…{结婚|jié hūn}, {结|jié}{了|le}{婚|hūn}, {结婚|jié hūn}{十|shí}{年|nián}{了|le}).
- {生活|shēng huó}: life; to live. {平时|píng shí}: on ordinary days. {习惯|xí guàn}: habit; to be used to ({习惯|xí guàn}{了|le}, {不|bù}{习惯|xí guàn}).
- {久|jiǔ}: long (time). {好久|hǎo jiǔ}: ages ({好久|hǎo jiǔ}{不见|bú jiàn}). {不久|bù jiǔ}: soon after.
- {发生|fā shēng}: to happen. {发展|fā zhǎn}: to develop; development.
- Invitations: what, when ({时间|shí jiān}), where ({地点|dì diǎn}), {欢迎|huān yíng}…{参加|cān jiā}; reply {谢谢|xiè xie}…, {一定|yí dìng}{来|lái} / {不|bù}{能|néng}{参加|cān jiā}, {祝|zhù}….

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Feelings: 怕, 生气, 让 + feeling
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 1 and 2 gave you the first words for feelings: {高兴|gāo xìng}, {快乐|kuài lè}, {累|lèi}, {舒服|shū fu}, {有意思|yǒu yì si}. This lesson adds
the ones you need to tell a story with feeling in it, and to react to what other people say:

- fear: {怕|pà} and {害怕|hài pà}; worry and relief: {担心|dān xīn} (lesson 05) and {放心|fàng xīn};
- anger: {生气|shēng qì} ({对|duì}…{生气|shēng qì}); happiness and sadness: {开心|kāi xīn}, {难过|nán guò}, {哭|kū};
- {奇怪|qí guài} (strange) and {热情|rè qíng} (warm, friendly);
- {相信|xiāng xìn} (to believe), {同意|tóng yì} (to agree) and the modal verb {愿意|yuàn yì} (to be willing);
- {感到|gǎn dào} (to feel) and {受|shòu} / {受到|shòu dào} (to receive, to meet with);
- {让|ràng} + person + feeling: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{开心|kāi xīn} (this made me very happy);
- {身边|shēn biān} (by someone's side) and {面前|miàn qián} (in front of someone).

## Fear: {怕|pà} and {害怕|hài pà}

{怕|pà} and {害怕|hài pà} both mean "to be afraid". {害怕|hài pà} is the fuller word for real fear; {怕|pà} is shorter, very
common in speech, and has a few extra uses.

Both can take a noun or a verb phrase:

{我|wǒ}{怕|pà}{狗|gǒu}。 / {我|wǒ}{害怕|hài pà}{狗|gǒu}。 — I'm afraid of dogs.

{她|tā}{害怕|hài pà}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。 — She's scared of being home alone.

{孩子|hái zi}{们|men}{别|bié}{害怕|hài pà}！ — Don't be scared, children!

Only {怕|pà} has these:

- {怕|pà} + a condition you can't stand: {我|wǒ}{怕|pà}{冷|lěng} (I really feel the cold), {他|tā}{怕|pà}{热|rè} (he can't stand the heat).
- {怕|pà} + a clause, "I'm afraid that, I worry that": {我|wǒ}{怕|pà}{他|tā}{不|bù}{来|lái} (I'm worried he won't come), {我|wǒ}{怕|pà}{下雨|xià yǔ}
  (I'm afraid it'll rain).
- {怕|pà} alone, in the reassurance {别|bié}{怕|pà}！ (don't be afraid!) and {不|bú}{怕|pà} (I'm not afraid; never mind).

{害怕|hài pà} is the usual word when the fear itself is the point: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{害怕|hài pà} (I'm very scared), {别|bié}{害怕|hài pà}
(don't be scared).

## Worry and relief: {担心|dān xīn} and {放心|fàng xīn}

{担心|dān xīn} (to worry, lesson 05) and {放心|fàng xīn} (to stop worrying, to feel at ease) are opposites:

{妈妈|mā ma}{很|hěn}{担心|dān xīn}{你|nǐ}。 — Mum's very worried about you.

{你|nǐ}{放心|fàng xīn}{吧|ba}，{我|wǒ}{会|huì}{照顾|zhào gù}{自己|zì jǐ}。 — Don't worry, I'll look after myself.

{你|nǐ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{去|qù}，{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{放心|fàng xīn}。 — I'm not easy about you going alone.

{放心|fàng xīn} is {放|fàng} (to put down: lesson 03) + {心|xīn} (heart): "put your heart down". {你|nǐ}{放心|fàng xīn} / {放心|fàng xīn}{吧|ba} is the
everyday "don't worry, rest assured". {不|bú}{放心|fàng xīn} is "feel uneasy (about someone or something)".

## Anger: {生气|shēng qì}

{生气|shēng qì} is "to get angry, to be angry": {生|shēng} (to produce) + {气|qì} (air, breath). The person you're angry with
takes {对|duì} or {跟|gēn}:

{他|tā}{生气|shēng qì}{了|le}。 — He's angry. (He's got angry.)

{妈妈|mā ma}{对|duì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{生气|shēng qì}。 — Mum is very angry with me.

{别|bié}{生气|shēng qì}！ — Don't be angry!

{生气|shēng qì} is a verb + object word, so you'll also hear the person in the middle: {别|bié}{生|shēng}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{气|qì} (don't be
angry with me), {她|tā}{在|zài}{生|shēng}{谁|shéi}{的|de}{气|qì}？ (who's she angry with?). For now, use {对|duì}…{生气|shēng qì}; just recognise the
split form.

## Happy and sad: {开心|kāi xīn}, {难过|nán guò}, {哭|kū}

{开心|kāi xīn} is "cheerful, happy, having fun": {开|kāi} (open) + {心|xīn} (heart). It's the everyday spoken word for
feeling good:

{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{特别|tè bié}{开心|kāi xīn}。 — I'm really happy today.

{我们|wǒ men}{玩|wán}{得|de}{很|hěn}{开心|kāi xīn}。 — We had a great time.

{祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{开心|kāi xīn}！ — Have fun! / Be happy!

{高兴|gāo xìng} (HSK 1) is close: "glad, pleased", often about a piece of news ({认识|rèn shi}{你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}). {快乐|kuài lè} (HSK 2) is
for wishes ({生日|shēng rì}{快乐|kuài lè}). {开心|kāi xīn} is about the good time you're having.

{难过|nán guò} is "sad, upset": {难|nán} (hard) + {过|guò} (to pass: a time that is hard to get through).

{听|tīng}{了|le}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}，{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{难过|nán guò}。 — I was very sad to hear about it.

{别|bié}{难过|nán guò}{了|le}。 — Don't be sad.

{哭|kū} is "to cry", {笑|xiào} (HSK 2) "to laugh, to smile":

{孩子|hái zi}{哭|kū}{了|le}。 — The child is crying. (The child has started crying.)

{她|tā}{一边|yì biān}{哭|kū}{一边|yì biān}{说|shuō}。 — She talked as she cried. ({一边|yì biān}…{一边|yì biān}, lesson 14.)

## Strange and warm: {奇怪|qí guài}, {热情|rè qíng}

{奇怪|qí guài} is "strange, odd": {真|zhēn}{奇怪|qí guài}！ (how strange!). It often comes before a question:

{真|zhēn}{奇怪|qí guài}，{他|tā}{今天|jīn tiān}{怎么|zěn me}{没|méi}{来|lái}？ — Strange, why hasn't he come today?

{热情|rè qíng} is "warm, friendly, enthusiastic" about people: {热|rè} (hot) + {情|qíng} (feeling). It's a favourite
compliment for hosts:

{他们|tā men}{对|duì}{客人|kè rén}{非常|fēi cháng}{热情|rè qíng}。 — They're very warm towards their guests.

{邻居|lín jū}{热情|rè qíng}{地|de}{欢迎|huān yíng}{我们|wǒ men}。 — The neighbours welcomed us warmly. ({地|de}: adverbial, HSK 2.)

## Believing, agreeing, being willing

{相信|xiāng xìn} is "to believe, to trust": a person, words, or a whole clause.

{我|wǒ}{相信|xiāng xìn}{你|nǐ}。 — I believe you. / I trust you.

{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{相信|xiāng xìn}{他|tā}{说|shuō}{的|de}{话|huà}。 — I don't believe what he says. ({话|huà}: words, what someone says.)

{我|wǒ}{相信|xiāng xìn}{你|nǐ}{一定|yí dìng}{能|néng}{做|zuò}{好|hǎo}。 — I'm sure you'll do it well. ({一定|yí dìng}: lesson 27.)

{同意|tóng yì} is "to agree", alone, or with a plan or a clause after it:

{我|wǒ}{同意|tóng yì}。 — I agree.

{妈妈|mā ma}{不|bù}{同意|tóng yì}{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{去|qù}{旅游|lǚ yóu}。 — Mum won't agree to me travelling alone.

{你|nǐ}{同意|tóng yì}{吗|ma}？ — Do you agree?

{愿意|yuàn yì} is a modal verb, "to be willing to, to want to (gladly)", before another verb, like {想|xiǎng}
and {要|yào}:

{我|wǒ}{愿意|yuàn yì}{帮|bāng}{你|nǐ}。 — I'm happy to help you.

{你|nǐ}{愿意|yuàn yì}{跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{吗|ma}？ — Would you like to come with me?

{他|tā}{不|bú}{愿意|yuàn yì}{说|shuō}。 — He doesn't want to say. (He's unwilling.)

{愿意|yuàn yì} shows that the choice is yours and you're glad to make it; {想|xiǎng} (would like) is about wishes, {要|yào}
about plans. The negative {不|bú}{愿意|yuàn yì} is a polite but firm "doesn't want to".

## {感到|gǎn dào} and {受|shòu} / {受到|shòu dào}

{感到|gǎn dào} is "to feel", for feelings and impressions, a little more formal than {觉得|jué de}:

{我|wǒ}{感到|gǎn dào}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 — I feel very happy.

{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{感到|gǎn dào}{很|hěn}{奇怪|qí guài}。 — Everyone found it strange.

{觉得|jué de} (HSK 1) can also give an opinion ({我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}); {感到|gǎn dào} only gives a feeling.

{受|shòu} is "to receive, to suffer, to undergo", mostly in fixed words. {受到|shòu dào} adds the result complement {到|dào}
and is the word you'll use in sentences: "to receive, to meet with", for things that happen to
you, good or bad:

{这个|zhè ge}{节目|jié mù}{受到|shòu dào}{了|le}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{欢迎|huān yíng}。 — This act was very popular. (It met with everyone's welcome.)

{他|tā}{的|de}{音乐|yīn yuè}{受到|shòu dào}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{的|de}{喜爱|xǐ ài}。 — His music is loved by many young people.

{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}{受到|shòu dào}{了|le}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{影响|yǐng xiǎng}。 — Our lives were greatly affected. ({影响|yǐng xiǎng}: lesson 20.)

{受到|shòu dào} + {欢迎|huān yíng} / {喜爱|xǐ ài} / {影响|yǐng xiǎng} / {关心|guān xīn} is a very common written pattern. Compare {收到|shōu dào} (to receive something
sent) and {得到|dé dào} (to get, lesson 21).

## {让|ràng} + person + feeling

You know {让|ràng} + person + verb from HSK 2: {老师|lǎo shī}{让|ràng}{我们|wǒ men}{读|dú}{课文|kè wén} (the teacher had us read the text). With a
feeling instead of an action, {让|ràng} says what made someone feel that way:

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{开心|kāi xīn}。 — This made me very happy.

{他|tā}{的|de}{话|huà}{让|ràng}{妈妈|mā ma}{很|hěn}{生气|shēng qì}。 — What he said made Mum very angry.

{这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{让|ràng}{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{哭|kū}{了|le}。 — The film made everyone cry.

The cause comes first, then {让|ràng} + the person + the feeling. It's the natural way to say "X made me
(feel)…": ~~{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{做|zuò}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{开心|kāi xīn}~~ is a word-for-word mistake.

## {身边|shēn biān} and {面前|miàn qián}

{身边|shēn biān} is "by someone's side, around someone": {身|shēn} (body) + {边|biān} (side).

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}{都|dōu}{不|bú}{在|zài}{身边|shēn biān}。 — My friends aren't around (with me).

{他|tā}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{身边|shēn biān}。 — He was by my side the whole time.

{面前|miàn qián} is "in front of someone, in someone's presence": {面|miàn} (face) + {前|qián} (front).

{在|zài}{大家|dà jiā}{面前|miàn qián}{说话|shuō huà}，{我|wǒ}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{害怕|hài pà}。 — I'm a bit scared of speaking in front of everyone.

Don't mix it up with {前面|qián miàn} (in front, ahead: HSK 2), which is about places: {学校|xué xiào}{前面|qián miàn} (in front of the
school), {前面|qián miàn}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{超市|chāo shì} (there's a supermarket ahead). {面前|miàn qián} is about people: {在|zài}{老师|lǎo shī}{面前|miàn qián} (in front of
the teacher). In traditional characters both keep {面|miàn} ("face"); it's 麵 only for noodles.

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 害 | harm; afraid | hài | 宀 | 10 | {害怕|hài pà} |
| 怕 ✎ | fear | pà | 忄 | 8 | {怕|pà}, {害怕|hài pà} |

| 受 ✎ | receive; bear | shòu | {又|yòu} | 8 | {受|shòu}, {受到|shòu dào} |

### Sound components

- {怕|pà} = 忄 (heart) + 白 ({白|bái}, white). 白 is the sound part of a whole family: {怕|pà}, {拍|pāi} ({拍照|pāi zhào},
  lesson 14), and {伯|bó} (uncle). The sounds have moved apart, but b and p are close.
- 奇 = {大|dà} + {可|kě} ({可|kě}, "may, can": lesson 27). 奇 is itself a sound part: {骑|qí} (to ride, lesson 13) and {椅|yǐ} ({椅子|yǐ zi}, HSK 1)
  both have it. 奇 and {骑|qí} sound alike today; {椅|yǐ} has drifted.
- 愿 = {原|yuán} ({原|yuán}, original) + {心|xīn} (heart). {原|yuán} gives the sound, yuán for yuàn; the heart gives the
  meaning, a wish. Traditional 願 is {原|yuán} + 頁 (head) instead.

### The others

- 害: 宀 (roof) on top and {口|kǒu} at the bottom, with three horizontals and a vertical between them. 害 is
  "harm"; {害怕|hài pà} is to fear harm.
- 怪: 忄 (heart) + {又|yòu} and 土 on the right. Memory aid: a hand ({又|yòu}) digging in the earth (土) for
  something strange.
- {哭|kū}: two {口|kǒu} on top and 犬 (dog) below. The two {口|kǒu} can be read as two crying eyes; the dog part has
  been explained in different ways, so treat the picture as a memory aid. Watch the dot on the top
  right: it belongs to 犬.
- {受|shòu}: 爫 (a hand from above) on top, 冖 in the middle and {又|yòu} (a hand) below. The old form showed one
  hand passing something to another: to give and to receive. (Its partner {授|shòu}, "to teach, to
  hand over", adds 扌.)

### Stroke order

- **害**: 宀, then the three horizontals (the bottom one longest), then the vertical through them,
  and {口|kǒu} last.
- **{哭|kū}**: the left {口|kǒu}, the right {口|kǒu}, then 犬: horizontal, left-falling, right-falling, and the dot
  last.
- **{受|shòu}**: 爫 (left-falling, dot, dot, left-falling), then 冖, then {又|yòu}.
- **愿**: 厂 first, then 白 and {小|xiǎo} inside it, and {心|xīn} at the bottom last.
- **{怕|pà}, 怪**: 忄 first: the two dots (left, then right), then the vertical.


{李明|Lǐ Míng} (Li Ming) sees {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) sitting alone after class.

```dialogue
李明: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}，{你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{了|le}？{你|nǐ}{看起来|kàn qǐ lái}{很|hěn}{难过|nán guò}。
= Wang Fang, what's wrong? You look really upset.
王芳: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{好|hǎo}{朋友|péng you}{对|duì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{生气|shēng qì}。{昨天|zuó tiān}{是|shì}{她|tā}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}，{我|wǒ}{忘|wàng}{了|le}。

王芳: {打|dǎ}{了|le}，{她|tā}{不|bú}{愿意|yuàn yì}{接|jiē}。{我|wǒ}{怕|pà}{她|tā}{以后|yǐ hòu}{不|bù}{跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{说话|shuō huà}{了|le}。
= Yes, but she won't answer. I'm afraid she'll never talk to me again.
```

Write one or two sentences in characters about something that made you happy, sad, angry or
scared. Use {让|ràng} + person + feeling, or {感到|gǎn dào}.

<summary>Model answers</summary>

## Say it

```speak
{你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{了|le}？
= What's wrong?
{别|bié}{生气|shēng qì}！
= Don't be angry!
{别|bié}{怕|pà}，{我|wǒ}{相信|xiāng xìn}{你|nǐ}。
= Don't be afraid; I believe in you.
{你|nǐ}{放心|fàng xīn}{吧|ba}。
= Don't worry.
{我|wǒ}{愿意|yuàn yì}{帮|bāng}{你|nǐ}。
= I'm happy to help you.
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{开心|kāi xīn}。
= This made me very happy.
```

## Pronunciation

- {怕|pà} and {害怕|hài pà}: two falling tones. The *p* has a puff of air; {爸|bà} has none.
- {生气|shēng qì}: level, then falling. {奇怪|qí guài}: rising, then falling.
- {哭|kū} is level: lips rounded, a clean *u*. Don't confuse it with {酷|kù} (cool) or {苦|kǔ} (bitter).
- {热情|rè qíng}: *r* with the tongue curled back; *qing* rises.
- {愿意|yuàn yì}: two falling tones. *yuan* starts with ü: lips rounded as for "oo", tongue as for "ee".
- {相信|xiāng xìn}: level, then falling. {受|shòu}: retroflex *sh*, falling.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{生气|shēng qì}{他|tā}~~: the person takes {对|duì}: {我|wǒ}{对|duì}{他|tā}{很|hěn}{生气|shēng qì}.
- ~~{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{做|zuò}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{开心|kāi xīn}~~: "made me" with a feeling is {让|ràng}: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{开心|kāi xīn}.
- {前面|qián miàn} for people: ~~{在|zài}{老师|lǎo shī}{前面|qián miàn}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}~~ is about the place in front of the teacher's body; "in front of
  the teacher", as an audience, is {在|zài}{老师|lǎo shī}{面前|miàn qián}.
- {愿意|yuàn yì} after the verb: ~~{我|wǒ}{帮|bāng}{你|nǐ}{愿意|yuàn yì}~~. Modal verbs come first: {我|wǒ}{愿意|yuàn yì}{帮|bāng}{你|nǐ}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{愿意|yuàn yì}{你|nǐ}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}~~ for "I'd like you to help me": {愿意|yuàn yì} is about your own willingness. Ask the other
  person instead: {你|nǐ}{愿意|yuàn yì}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{吗|ma}？
- {收到|shōu dào} and {受到|shòu dào} mixed up: ~~{受到|shòu dào}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{邮件|yóu jiàn}~~ is wrong ({收到|shōu dào}); ~~{收到|shōu dào}{欢迎|huān yíng}~~ is wrong ({受到|shòu dào}{欢迎|huān yíng}).

## Key points

- {怕|pà} / {害怕|hài pà}: to be afraid ({怕|pà}{狗|gǒu}, {害怕|hài pà}{考试|kǎo shì}); {怕|pà}{冷|lěng} (can't stand cold), {我|wǒ}{怕|pà}{他|tā}{不|bù}{来|lái} (I worry that…), {别|bié}{怕|pà}.
- {担心|dān xīn} vs {放心|fàng xīn}: worry vs stop worrying ({你|nǐ}{放心|fàng xīn}{吧|ba}).
- {生气|shēng qì}: to be angry ({对|duì}…{生气|shēng qì}; {别|bié}{生气|shēng qì}). {开心|kāi xīn}: cheerful, having fun. {难过|nán guò}: sad. {哭|kū}: to cry.
- {奇怪|qí guài}: strange. {热情|rè qíng}: warm, friendly ({对|duì}{客人|kè rén}{很|hěn}{热情|rè qíng}).
- {相信|xiāng xìn}: to believe, trust. {同意|tóng yì}: to agree. {愿意|yuàn yì} + verb: to be willing.
- {感到|gǎn dào} + feeling. {受到|shòu dào} + {欢迎|huān yíng} / {喜爱|xǐ ài} / {影响|yǐng xiǎng}: to meet with.
- Cause + {让|ràng} + person + feeling: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{开心|kāi xīn}.
- {身边|shēn biān}: by someone's side. {面前|miàn qián}: in front of someone (vs {前面|qián miàn}, in front of a place).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: First, then, finally: 先…然后, 才 and 就
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Every story in this module has had a "first", a "then" and an "in the end". This lesson gives you
the words that hold a story together in time, and the two little adverbs that tell the listener
whether something happened early or late:

- the **[[sequence of actions]]**: {先|xiān}…{然后|rán hòu} / {再|zài}…, {最后|zuì hòu};
- **{才|cái} and {就|jiù}**: {他|tā}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{来|lái} (he didn't come until ten) vs {他|tā}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{来|lái}{了|le} (he came as early as seven);
- {刚|gāng}, {刚刚|gāng gāng} and {刚才|gāng cái} (just, just now, a moment ago);
- {以前|yǐ qián}, {以后|yǐ hòu}, {后来|hòu lái} and …{的|de}{时候|shí hou} (before, after, afterwards, when);
- {直到|zhí dào} (until), {最近|zuì jìn} (recently) and {周末|zhōu mò} (the weekend);
- the days and years around now: {前天|qián tiān}, {后天|hòu tiān}, {前年|qián nián}, {后年|hòu nián}.

The table of all of them is in the reference sheet for this lesson.

## First, then, finally: {先|xiān}…{然后|rán hòu}…, {先|xiān}…{再|zài}…, {最后|zuì hòu}

{先|xiān} (first) is an adverb: it goes before the verb, after the subject.

{我|wǒ}{先|xiān}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 — I'll eat first.

{然后|rán hòu} (then, after that) starts the next step, at the beginning of its clause:

{我们|wǒ men}{先|xiān}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}，{然后|rán hòu}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}。 — First we'll eat, then we'll go to a film.

{他|tā}{先|xiān}{给|gěi}{妈妈|mā ma}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{电话|diàn huà}，{然后|rán hòu}{出门|chū mén}{了|le}。 — He phoned his mum first and then went out.

{先|xiān}…{再|zài}… is the same order with {再|zài} (then, again: HSK 1), an adverb before the second verb. It's the
usual way to give instructions and plans:

{先|xiān}{洗|xǐ}{手|shǒu}，{再|zài}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 — Wash your hands first, then eat.

{你|nǐ}{先|xiān}{休息|xiū xi}{一下|yí xià}，{再|zài}{做|zuò}{作业|zuò yè}{吧|ba}。 — Have a rest first, and then do your homework.

The two can join: {先|xiān}…{然后|rán hòu}{再|zài}… (first…, and then…). {然后|rán hòu} works for the past and the future; {再|zài} in this
use is only for what hasn't happened yet: ~~{他|tā}{先|xiān}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}，{再|zài}{走|zǒu}{了|le}~~ is wrong, {他|tā}{先|xiān}{吃|chī}{了|le}{饭|fàn}，{然后|rán hòu}{走|zǒu}{了|le} is right.

{最后|zuì hòu} is "finally, last of all", the last step in the list. It is also an adjective, "last": {最后|zuì hòu}{一|yì}{天|tiān}
(the last day), {最后|zuì hòu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén} (the last person).

{我们|wǒ men}{先|xiān}{吃|chī}{了|le}{饭|fàn}，{然后|rán hòu}{去|qù}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}，{最后|zuì hòu}{去|qù}{公园|gōng yuán}{走|zǒu}{了|le}{走|zǒu}。 — First we ate, then we went to sing, and finally we went
for a walk in the park.

{终于|zhōng yú} (lesson 21) is "at last", after a long wait; {最后|zuì hòu} is "last" in an order of steps:
{等|děng}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}，{他|tā}{终于|zhōng yú}{来|lái}{了|le} (he came at last) vs {他|tā}{最后|zuì hòu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{来|lái} (he was the last to come).

## {才|cái} and {就|jiù}: late or early

Chinese marks how the speaker feels about a time. {就|jiù} says "already, as early as, sooner than you'd
think"; {才|cái} says "not until, only then, later than you'd think". Both go straight before the verb.

| | Early: {就|jiù}…{了|le} | Late: {才|cái} |
|---|---|---|
| Arrival | {他|tā}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{来|lái}{了|le}。 He came at seven already. | {他|tā}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{来|lái}。 He didn't come until ten. |
| Getting up | {她|tā}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{起床|qǐ chuáng}{了|le}。 She was up by six. | {她|tā}{十一|shí yī}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。 She didn't get up till eleven. |
| Finishing | {我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{就|jiù}{写|xiě}{完|wán}{了|le}。 I finished it in just an hour. | {我|wǒ}{写|xiě}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{才|cái}{写|xiě}{完|wán}。 It took me three hours to finish. |

Look at {了|le}: with early {就|jiù} the sentence ends in {了|le}, as usual for something that has happened; with
late {才|cái} there is **no {了|le}**. ~~{他|tā}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{来|lái}{了|le}~~ is a typical mistake.

The time comes before {就|jiù} / {才|cái}, and the stress falls on the time. Same event, different feeling:

{电影|diàn yǐng}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{开始|kāi shǐ}，{他|tā}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}。 — The film started at eight; he was there by half past seven.

{电影|diàn yǐng}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{开始|kāi shǐ}，{他|tā}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}{才|cái}{到|dào}。 — The film started at eight; he didn't get there till half past
eight.

{才|cái} has two other uses you'll hear all the time:

- {才|cái} + a number: "only, just" (fewer, smaller, younger than expected): {他|tā}{才|cái}{十|shí}{岁|suì} (he's only ten),
  {我|wǒ}{才|cái}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{页|yè} (I've only read one page).
- {直到|zhí dào}…{才|cái}…: "not until": {他|tā}{直到|zhí dào}{晚上|wǎn shang}{十二|shí èr}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{睡觉|shuì jiào} (he didn't go to bed until midnight). {直到|zhí dào} (until)
  sets the time, {才|cái} says it was late.

{就|jiù} joins {刚|gāng} for "as soon as": {我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{到|dào}{家|jiā}，{就|jiù}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le} (I'd only just got home when it started raining).

## {刚|gāng}, {刚刚|gāng gāng} and {刚才|gāng cái}

{刚|gāng} and {刚刚|gāng gāng} are adverbs: "only just, just". They go before the verb and say something happened a very
short time ago, or has only just started. {刚刚|gāng gāng} is a little stronger.

{我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{到|dào}。 — I've just arrived.

{他|tā}{刚|gāng}{走|zǒu}。 — He's just left.

{我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{来|lái}{三|sān}{天|tiān}。 — I've only been here three days.

{刚才|gāng cái} is a time noun: "a moment ago, just now". Like {昨天|zuó tiān} or {今天|jīn tiān}, it can go before or after the
subject, it can take {不|bù} / {没|méi} after it, and the verb can take {了|le}:

{刚才|gāng cái}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}{了|le}？ / {你|nǐ}{刚才|gāng cái}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}{了|le}？ — Where did you go just now?

{刚才|gāng cái}{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听|tīng}{清楚|qīng chu}。 — I didn't hear clearly just now.

| | {刚|gāng} / {刚刚|gāng gāng} (adverb) | {刚才|gāng cái} (time noun) |
|---|---|---|
| Position | only before the verb | before or after the subject |
| Negative | ✗ (not ~~{刚|gāng}{没|méi}~~) | {刚才|gāng cái}{没|méi}… |
| With a length of time | {我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{来|lái}{三|sān}{天|tiān} | ✗ |
| {了|le} at the end | usually none: {他|tā}{刚|gāng}{走|zǒu} | common: {刚才|gāng cái}{他|tā}{来|lái}{了|le} |

So "He was here just now" is {他|tā}{刚才|gāng cái}{在|zài}{这儿|zhèr}, and "I've only been learning Chinese for a month" is
{我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{学|xué}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}.

## Before, after, afterwards: {以前|yǐ qián}, {以后|yǐ hòu}, {后来|hòu lái}, …{的|de}{时候|shí hou}

{以前|yǐ qián} (before) and {以后|yǐ hòu} (after) go **after** the event they refer to, the opposite of English:

{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{以前|yǐ qián} — before eating

{下课|xià kè}{以后|yǐ hòu} — after class

{我|wǒ}{来|lái}{中国|Zhōng guó}{以前|yǐ qián}{没|méi}{学|xué}{过|guo}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。 — Before I came to China, I hadn't studied Chinese.

{下课|xià kè}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{打|dǎ}{网球|wǎng qiú}{吧|ba}。 — After class, let's go and play tennis.

Alone, at the start of a sentence, they mean "in the past" and "in the future, from now on":

{以前|yǐ qián}{我|wǒ}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 — I used to live in Shanghai.

{以后|yǐ hòu}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}{工作|gōng zuò}。 — In the future I'd like to work in China.

{后来|hòu lái} is "afterwards, later on", for a past story only. It starts a later stage of a story; it
never refers to the future and doesn't follow an event:

{他|tā}{去年|qù nián}{去|qù}{了|le}{北京|Běi jīng}，{后来|hòu lái}{去|qù}{了|le}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 — He went to Beijing last year, and later on to Shanghai.

| | {以后|yǐ hòu} | {后来|hòu lái} |
|---|---|---|
| After an event ({吃|chī}{饭|fàn}…) | {吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{以后|yǐ hòu} ✓ | ✗ |
| Past story | ✓ | ✓ |
| Future | {以后|yǐ hòu}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}… ✓ | ✗ |

…{的|de}{时候|shí hou} (when…, HSK 1) marks the moment: {我|wǒ}{到|dào}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{他们|tā men}{已经|yǐ jīng}{走|zǒu}{了|le} (when I arrived, they'd already gone).

## {最近|zuì jìn}, {周末|zhōu mò} and {直到|zhí dào}

{最近|zuì jìn} is "recently, lately, these days", for the time leading up to now (and a little ahead):

{你|nǐ}{最近|zuì jìn}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ — How have you been lately?

{我|wǒ}{最近|zuì jìn}{特别|tè bié}{忙|máng}。 — I've been really busy recently.

{周末|zhōu mò} is the weekend: the end ({末|mò}) of the week. {这个|zhè ge}{周末|zhōu mò} (this weekend), {周末|zhōu mò}{快乐|kuài lè}！ (have a good
weekend!). In traditional characters it's {+{周末|zhōu mò}+}.

{直到|zhí dào} is "until, right up to", before a time: {直到|zhí dào}{现在|xiàn zài} (until now), {我|wǒ}{直到|zhí dào}{昨天|zuó tiān}{才|cái}{知道|zhī dào} (I didn't know until
yesterday). It's {直|zhí} (straight: lesson 21) + {到|dào} (to arrive).

## The days and years around now

| Before | | Now | | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {前天|qián tiān} the day before yesterday | {昨天|zuó tiān} yesterday | {今天|jīn tiān} today | {明天|míng tiān} tomorrow | {后天|hòu tiān} the day after tomorrow |
| {前年|qián nián} the year before last | {去年|qù nián} last year | {今年|jīn nián} this year | {明年|míng nián} next year | {后年|hòu nián} the year after next |

{前|qián} (front, before) and {后|hòu} (back, after) make the outer pairs: two days or two years away.

{我们|wǒ men}{前天|qián tiān}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}{面|miàn}。 — We met the day before yesterday.

{后天|hòu tiān}{是|shì}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}。 — The day after tomorrow is Saturday.

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 刚 (traditional 剛) ✎ | just; hard | gāng | 刂 | 6 | {刚|gāng}, {刚刚|gāng gāng}, {刚才|gāng cái} |
| 才 ✎ | only then; talent | cái | 扌 | 3 | {才|cái}, {刚才|gāng cái} |
| 末 | end; tip | mò | 木 | 5 | {周末|zhōu mò} |

- {刚|gāng} = {冈|gāng} ({冈|gāng}, a ridge) + 刂 (knife). {冈|gāng} gives the sound exactly, gāng, and 刂 the first
  meaning, "hard, strong" (a hard blade). Traditional 剛 has the full form of the left part, 岡.
- {才|cái} has only three strokes. Make Me a Hanzi files it under 扌, as many dictionaries do, but it isn't
  a hand: it was once a picture of a young plant pushing through the ground. That
  is where its other meaning, "talent", comes from. In traditional characters it stays {才|cái}.
- 末 is 木 (tree) with a long line across the top: the tip of the tree, the end. Its look-alike is
  {未|wèi} ("not yet", in words you'll meet later), where the top line is the **shorter** one. 末:
  long line on top; {未|wèi}: short line on top.

### Stroke order

- **{刚|gāng}**: the left vertical, the bent stroke with its hook, then the two strokes inside (left-falling,
  dot), then 刂 (short vertical, long vertical with a hook).
- **{才|cái}**: horizontal, the vertical with a hook to the left, and the left-falling stroke across it
  last.
- **末**: the long top horizontal, the shorter one, the vertical, then left-falling and right-falling,
  as in 木.

```trace
刚才末
```

Write it: {刚|gāng} and {才|cái} are characters to know by hand. Write each three times from memory. For {才|cái},
the left-falling stroke crosses the vertical; in 寸 (as in {对|duì}) there's a dot instead.

### Handwriting review, module 5

By the end of HSK 3 you should be able to write 250 characters by hand. These 20 from HSK 1 and 2
are in this module's words. Cover the right-hand column, write each from memory, then check it on
the pad.

| Character | In this module |
|---|---|
| 比 | {比赛|bǐ sài} |
| 分 | {得分|dé fēn} |
| 会 | {运动会|yùn dòng huì}, {晚会|wǎn huì} |
| 天 | {半天|bàn tiān}, {聊天儿|liáo tiānr}, {前天|qián tiān} |
| 文 | {文化|wén huà} |
| 生 | {生活|shēng huó}, {生气|shēng qì}, {出生|chū shēng} |
| 年 | {新年|xīn nián}, {前年|qián nián}, {后年|hòu nián} |
| 习 | {习惯|xí guàn} |
| 时 | {平时|píng shí} |
| 好 | {好久|hǎo jiǔ} |
| 不 | {不久|bù jiǔ} |
| 同 | {同意|tóng yì} |
| 边 | {身边|shēn biān} |
| 后 | {然后|rán hòu}, {以后|yǐ hòu}, {最后|zuì hòu} |
| 以 | {以前|yǐ qián}, {以后|yǐ hòu} |
| 过 | {过节|guò jié}, {难过|nán guò} |
| 家 | {画家|huà jiā} |
| 对 | {对|duì}…{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù} |
| 打 | {打|dǎ}{网球|wǎng qiú} |
| 爱 | {喜爱|xǐ ài} |

```trace
比分会天文生年
```

```trace
习时好不同边后
```

```trace
以过家对打爱
```
=}

## Dialogue: why so late?

{大卫|Dà wèi} (David) has arranged to meet {李明|Lǐ Míng} (Li Ming) at the cinema at seven.

```dialogue
# Why so late?
李明: {大卫|Dà wèi}，{你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{才|cái}{来|lái}？{电影|diàn yǐng}{已经|yǐ jīng}{开始|kāi shǐ}{了|le}！
= David, why are you only coming now? The film's already started!
大卫: {对不起|duì bu qǐ}！{我|wǒ}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{出门|chū mén}{了|le}，{但是|dàn shì}{地铁|dì tiě}{上|shàng}{人|rén}{太|tài}{多|duō}，{我|wǒ}{等|děng}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}{才|cái}{上去|shàng qù}。
= Sorry! I left home at six, but the metro was so crowded I waited ages before I could get on.
李明: {我|wǒ}{刚才|gāng cái}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}，{你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{没|méi}{接|jiē}？
= I phoned you just now: why didn't you answer?
大卫: {我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{看|kàn}{到|dào}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{没|méi}{电|diàn}{了|le}。
= I've only just seen it. My phone's battery is dead.
李明: {好|hǎo}{了|le}，{没事|méi shì}。{我们|wǒ men}{先|xiān}{进去|jìn qù}{吧|ba}，{看|kàn}{完|wán}{电影|diàn yǐng}{再|zài}{去|qù}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。
= OK, never mind. Let's go in first, and after the film we'll go and eat.
大卫: {好|hǎo}。{这个|zhè ge}{周末|zhōu mò}{你|nǐ}{有空|yǒu kòng}{吗|ma}？{后天|hòu tiān}{我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}！
= OK. Are you free this weekend? The day after tomorrow, dinner's on me!
李明: {后天|hòu tiān}{不行|bù xíng}，{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{去|qù}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。{下|xià}{个|gè}{周末|zhōu mò}{吧|ba}。
= Not the day after tomorrow, I'm going to Shanghai. Let's say next weekend.
大卫: {好|hǎo}，{那|nà}{就|jiù}{下|xià}{个|gè}{周末|zhōu mò}{吧|ba}。{最近|zuì jìn}{你|nǐ}{太|tài}{忙|máng}{了|le}！
= OK, next weekend then. You've been far too busy lately!
```

- {有空|yǒu kòng} is "to be free, to have time" ({空|kòng}: free time).
- {我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ} is "it's on me": {请|qǐng} + person + {吃|chī}{饭|fàn} is "to treat someone to a meal" ({请客|qǐng kè}, lesson 07).
- {不行|bù xíng} (not possible, no good) is lesson 28's word.

## Reading: a busy Saturday

> {前天|qián tiān}{是|shì}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}，{也|yě}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}{安娜|Ān nà}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}。{我们|wǒ men}{早就|zǎo jiù}{说好|shuō hǎo}{了|le}，{那|nà}{天|tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{在|zài}{她|tā}{家|jiā}{给|gěi}{她|tā}{过|guò}{生日|shēng rì}。
>
> {那|nà}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}，{我|wǒ}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{起床|qǐ chuáng}{了|le}。{我|wǒ}{先|xiān}{去|qù}{商场|shāng chǎng}{给|gěi}{安娜|Ān nà}{买|mǎi}{礼物|lǐ wù}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{走|zǒu}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}，{也|yě}{没|méi}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{合适|hé shì}{的|de}。{后来|hòu lái}，{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{书店|shū diàn}{里|lǐ}{看见|kàn jiàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{本|běn}{中国画|Zhōng guó huà}{的|de}{书|shū}。{安娜|Ān nà}{对|duì}{中国画|Zhōng guó huà}{很|hěn}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{买|mǎi}{了|le}。{书店|shū diàn}{的|de}{阿姨|ā yí}{还|hái}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{书|shū}{包|bāo}{好|hǎo}{了|le}。{然后|rán hòu}，{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{蛋糕店|dàn gāo diàn}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{大|dà}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}。{我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{出门|chū mén}，{就|jiù}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}。{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{带|dài}{伞|sǎn}，{在|zài}{店|diàn}{里|lǐ}{等|děng}{了|le}{一|yí}{刻|kè}{钟|zhōng}，{雨|yǔ}{才|cái}{停|tíng}。
>
> {我|wǒ}{到|dào}{安娜|Ān nà}{家|jiā}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{已经|yǐ jīng}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}{了|le}，{朋友|péng you}{们|men}{都|dōu}{到|dào}{了|le}。{晚会|wǎn huì}{上|shàng}，{我们|wǒ men}{先|xiān}{吃|chī}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}，{然后|rán hòu}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}、{玩|wán}{游戏|yóu xì}，{最后|zuì hòu}{一起|yì qǐ}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{电影|diàn yǐng}。{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{玩|wán}{得|de}{非常|fēi cháng}{开心|kāi xīn}，{直到|zhí dào}{十一|shí yī}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。
>
> {安娜|Ān nà}{说|shuō}，{这|zhè}{是|shì}{她|tā}{过|guò}{得|de}{最|zuì}{开心|kāi xīn}{的|de}{一|yí}{个|gè}{生日|shēng rì}。{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}，{以后|yǐ hòu}{每年|měi nián}{安娜|Ān nà}{过|guò}{生日|shēng rì}，{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{要|yào}{跟|gēn}{她|tā}{一起|yì qǐ}{过|guò}。

{早就|zǎo jiù}{说好|shuō hǎo}{了|le} is "had agreed long before" ({说好|shuō hǎo}: to agree on, with the result complement {好|hǎo}). {停|tíng} is
"to stop".

1. When was the party, and whose was it?
2. Why did the writer buy a book?
3. Why did the writer wait in the cake shop?
4. What did they do at the party, in what order?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. The day before yesterday, Saturday evening ({前天|qián tiān}{是|shì}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}), for Anna's birthday.
2. After walking around for ages without finding anything suitable, the writer saw a book of
   Chinese painting, and Anna is interested in Chinese painting ({安娜|Ān nà}{对|duì}{中国画|Zhōng guó huà}{很|hěn}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}).
3. It started raining just as the writer came out, and they had no umbrella: they waited a
   quarter of an hour until it stopped ({等|děng}{了|le}{一|yí}{刻|kè}{钟|zhōng}，{雨|yǔ}{才|cái}{停|tíng}).
4. First the cake, then singing and games, and finally a film together ({先|xiān}{吃|chī}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}，{然后|rán hòu}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}、{玩|wán}{游戏|yóu xì}，
   {最后|zuì hòu}{一起|yì qǐ}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{电影|diàn yǐng}).

"The day before yesterday was Saturday, and it was also my friend Anna's birthday. We'd agreed
long before that we'd celebrate her birthday at her home that evening.

That morning I was up by seven. First I went to the shopping centre to buy Anna a present, but I
walked around for ages without finding anything suitable. Later, in a little bookshop, I saw a
book of Chinese painting. Anna is very interested in Chinese painting, so I bought it. The lady in the shop even wrapped it up for me. Then I went
to a cake shop and bought a big cake. I'd only just come out when it started to rain. I hadn't
brought an umbrella, and I waited in the shop for a quarter of an hour before the rain stopped.

When I got to Anna's, it was already half past six, and all our friends were there. At the party
we first had the cake, then sang and played games, and finally watched a film together. Everyone
had a wonderful time, and nobody went home until eleven.

Anna said it was the happiest birthday she'd ever had. I think that from now on, every year on
Anna's birthday, I'll celebrate it with her."
</details>

## Write it: your day in order

Write one or two sentences in characters about what you did yesterday or will do this weekend, in
order. Use {先|xiān}…{然后|rán hòu}… (or {先|xiān}…{再|zài}… for plans) and {最后|zuì hòu}, and {才|cái} or {就|jiù} if a time was early or late.

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {昨天|zuó tiān}{我|wǒ}{先|xiān}{去|qù}{银行|yín háng}，{然后|rán hòu}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}，{最后|zuì hòu}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{做饭|zuò fàn}。 — Yesterday I went to the bank first, then to the
  supermarket, and finally home to cook.
- {这个|zhè ge}{周末|zhōu mò}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{先|xiān}{休息|xiū xi}{一|yì}{天|tiān}，{再|zài}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}。{我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{十二|shí èr}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。 — This weekend I'd like to rest for a day
  first and then go hiking. Last night I didn't go to bed until midnight.

Check: {先|xiān} after the subject; {然后|rán hòu} at the start of its clause; no {了|le} after {才|cái}.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{我们|wǒ men}{先|xiān}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}，{然后|rán hòu}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}。
= First we'll eat, then we'll go to a film.
{你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{才|cái}{来|lái}？
= Why are you only coming now?
{我|wǒ}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}。
= I got here at six already.
{你|nǐ}{刚才|gāng cái}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}{了|le}？
= Where did you go just now?
{我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{到|dào}。
= I've just arrived.
{你|nǐ}{最近|zuì jìn}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
= How have you been lately?
{周末|zhōu mò}{快乐|kuài lè}！
= Have a good weekend!
```

## Pronunciation

- {才|cái} rises; {菜|cài} (dish) falls. {他|tā}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{来|lái} tā shí diǎn cái lái: two rising syllables
  together.
- {刚|gāng}, {刚刚|gāng gāng}, {刚才|gāng cái}: a high, level *gang*. In {刚刚|gāng gāng} both syllables are
  full.
- {然后|rán hòu}: *ran* with the tongue curled back for *r*; then a falling *hou*.
- {最后|zuì hòu} and {最近|zuì jìn}: two falling tones each.
- {前天|qián tiān} and {前年|qián nián}: *qian* rises.
- {周末|zhōu mò}: level, then falling.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{他|tā}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{来|lái}{了|le}~~: late {才|cái} takes no {了|le}: {他|tā}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{来|lái}.
- ~~{他|tā}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{来|lái}~~ about the past: early {就|jiù} needs {了|le}: {他|tā}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{来|lái}{了|le}.
- ~~{刚才|gāng cái}{我|wǒ}{来|lái}{三|sān}{天|tiān}~~: a length of time goes with the adverb {刚|gāng}: {我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{来|lái}{三|sān}{天|tiān}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{没|méi}{听见|tīng jiàn}~~: {刚|gāng} can't be negated; use {刚才|gāng cái}: {我|wǒ}{刚才|gāng cái}{没|méi}{听见|tīng jiàn}.
- ~~{后来|hòu lái}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}~~ for the future: {后来|hòu lái} is only for past stories. {以后|yǐ hòu}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}.
- ~~{以前|yǐ qián}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}~~ for "before eating": {以前|yǐ qián} follows the event: {吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{以前|yǐ qián}.
- ~~{他|tā}{先|xiān}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}，{再|zài}{走|zǒu}{了|le}~~: {再|zài} is for what hasn't happened; in the past use {然后|rán hòu}: {他|tā}{先|xiān}{吃|chī}{了|le}{饭|fàn}，{然后|rán hòu}{走|zǒu}{了|le}.

## Key points

- {先|xiān} + verb, {然后|rán hòu} + clause, {最后|zuì hòu} + verb: first, then, finally. {先|xiān}…{再|zài}… for plans and instructions.
- {才|cái} and {就|jiù}: time + {就|jiù} + verb + {了|le} (early: {七|qī}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{来|lái}{了|le}); time + {才|cái} + verb, no {了|le} (late: {十|shí}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{来|lái}).
  {才|cái} + number: only ({才|cái}{十|shí}{岁|suì}). {直到|zhí dào}…{才|cái}…: not until. {刚|gāng}…{就|jiù}…: as soon as.
- {刚|gāng} / {刚刚|gāng gāng} + verb: only just ({我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{到|dào}, {刚|gāng}{来|lái}{三|sān}{天|tiān}). {刚才|gāng cái}: a moment ago, a time noun ({刚才|gāng cái}{没|méi}{听见|tīng jiàn}).
- X {以前|yǐ qián} / X {以后|yǐ hòu}: before / after X. {以前|yǐ qián} / {以后|yǐ hòu} alone: in the past / in the future. {后来|hòu lái}: afterwards
  (past only).
- {最近|zuì jìn}: recently. {周末|zhōu mò}: weekend. {直到|zhí dào}: until.
- {前天|qián tiān}, {昨天|zuó tiān}, {今天|jīn tiān}, {明天|míng tiān}, {后天|hòu tiān}; {前年|qián nián}, {去年|qù nián}, {今年|jīn nián}, {明年|míng nián}, {后年|hòu nián}.
