vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{三|sān}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: There are three of us.

vocab.note: Tens are built with it: {二十|èr shí} (20 = two tens), {十二|shí èr} (12 = ten and two).
vocab.example: {三|sān}{十|shí}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: Thirty people.

vocab.note: After a country it gives the people: {中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}, a Chinese person, Chinese people.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm Chinese.

vocab.note: Also used for age: {你|nǐ}{多|duō}{大|dà}？ How old are you? (Chinese HSK 1). Its opposite is {小|xiǎo}.
vocab.example: {中国|Zhōng guó}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。
vocab.exampleEn: China is big.

vocab.note: Fourth tone, falling. Don't confuse it with {十|shí} (ten, rising): {四十四|sì shí sì} is 44.
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{四|sì}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: There are four of us.

vocab.example: {五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: Five people.

vocab.note: Spelled liù, a short form of liòu: you hear a light o before the u. The tone mark goes on the u.
vocab.example: {六|liù}{十|shí}{六|liù}。
vocab.exampleEn: Sixty-six.

vocab.note: q is said like the ch of "cheese", with a puff of air.
vocab.example: {七|qī}{月|yuè}。
vocab.exampleEn: July (the seventh month).

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{八|bā}{岁|suì}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm eight (years old).

vocab.example: {九十九|jiǔ shí jiǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: Ninety-nine people.

vocab.note: To one person: a friend, a classmate, anyone your age. The polite form for older people and strangers is {您|nín} (Chinese HSK 1).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Are you Wang Fang?

vocab.note: One word for "I" and "me": {我|wǒ} doesn't change.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm Wang Fang.

vocab.note: Said ní hǎo (two third tones: the first rises). Answer with {你好|nǐ hǎo} too.
vocab.example: {你好|nǐ hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Hello, I'm Wang Fang.

vocab.note: Alone it also means "OK, all right": {好|hǎo}！
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm fine. / I'm well.

vocab.note: bù, but bú before a fourth tone: {不|bú}{是|shì}, {不客气|bú kè qi}. This app writes the change; most dictionaries write bù everywhere.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm not Wang Fang.

vocab.note: Links two nouns: A {是|shì} B. It never changes for I, you or they. Its negative is {不|bú}{是|shì}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm Chinese.

vocab.note: Before a surname it's a friendly way to address a younger person: {小|xiǎo}{王|Wáng}, "young Wang".
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{狗|gǒu}{很|hěn}{小|xiǎo}。
vocab.exampleEn: My dog is small.

vocab.note: Literally "middle country". A capital Z in pinyin, as for every name.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm Chinese. / I'm from China.

vocab.note: The second xie is light and short (neutral tone). Reply: {不客气|bú kè qi}.
vocab.example: {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}！
vocab.exampleEn: Thank you!

vocab.note: The reply to {谢谢|xiè xie}. Literally "don't be so polite". 不 is bú here, before the fourth tone kè.
vocab.example: — {谢谢|xiè xie}！— {不客气|bú kè qi}。
vocab.exampleEn: — Thanks! — You're welcome.

vocab.note: An apology for something you did. The 不 in the middle is light (neutral tone). Reply: {没关系|méi guān xi}.
vocab.example: {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Sorry, I'm not Wang Fang.

vocab.note: The reply to {对不起|duì bu qǐ}. Literally "there's no connection".
vocab.example: — {对不起|duì bu qǐ}！— {没关系|méi guān xi}。
vocab.exampleEn: — Sorry! — That's all right.

vocab.note: Literally "again see". Two fourth tones: both fall.
vocab.example: {再见|zài jiàn}，{王芳|Wáng Fāng}！
vocab.exampleEn: Goodbye, Wang Fang!

vocab.note: Sounds the same as {她|tā} (she); only the writing differs: 亻 "person" here, 女 "woman" in 她.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's a teacher.

vocab.note: Sounds the same as {他|tā} (he). The radical 女 "woman" shows it means a woman.
vocab.example: {她|tā}{叫|jiào}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Her name is Wang Fang.

vocab.note: For teachers, older people, customers and strangers; {你|nǐ} for friends and people your age.
vocab.example: {您|nín}{是|shì}{王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Are you Teacher Wang?

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{李明|Lǐ Míng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My name is Li Ming.

vocab.note: Stays where the answer goes: {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}？ — {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{安娜|Ān nà}。 Second syllable neutral.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}？
vocab.exampleEn: What's he called?

vocab.note: Second syllable neutral: míng zi.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}{名字|míng zi}？
vocab.exampleEn: What's your name?

vocab.note: At the end of a statement, makes a yes-or-no question. Not used with question words such as {什么|shén me}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Are you a student?

vocab.note: Before an adjective in a plain statement, usually unstressed: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} is just "I'm fine".
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{谢谢|xiè xie}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm fine, thanks.

vocab.note: Also a title after a family name: {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}, Teacher Wang.
vocab.example: {她|tā}{不|bú}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: She isn't a teacher.

vocab.note: Second syllable neutral in mainland speech: xué sheng.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}，{不|bú}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's a student, not a teacher.

vocab.note: Only for people, never after a number: {三|sān}{个|gè}{学生|xué sheng}, not 三个学生们.
vocab.example: {老师们|lǎo shī men}{好|hǎo}！
vocab.exampleEn: Hello, teachers!

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。
vocab.exampleEn: We're all students.

vocab.example: {你们|nǐ men}{是|shì}{哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where are you all from?

vocab.note: Sounds the same as {她们|tā men} (they, all women). Used for any mixed group.
vocab.example: {他们|tā men}{都|dōu}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{英语|Yīng yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: They can all speak English.

vocab.note: Only when everyone in the group is a woman; otherwise {他们|tā men}.
vocab.example: {她们|tā men}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: They're teachers.

vocab.note: In country names: {中国|Zhōng guó}, {美国|Měi guó}. {哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}: a person of which country?
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where are you from?

vocab.note: Third tone. Don't confuse with {那|nà} (that), fourth tone.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{是|shì}{哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where is he from? (Which country is he from?)

vocab.note: The usual word in classes and textbooks. {中文|Zhōng wén} means the same, especially written Chinese.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: I can speak Chinese.

vocab.note: Used for the language in general and for written Chinese: a menu or a website in Chinese.
vocab.example: {她|tā}{也|yě}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{中文|Zhōng wén}。
vocab.exampleEn: She speaks Chinese too.

vocab.example: {他|tā}{说|shuō}{英语|Yīng yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: He speaks English.

vocab.note: A skill you have learned: {会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}. Also "will (probably)" later in the course.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Can you speak Chinese?

vocab.note: After a noun or pronoun: {你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？ "And you?" Neutral tone.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{英国人|Yīng guó rén}，{你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？
vocab.exampleEn: I'm British. And you?

vocab.note: Before the verb, never at the end: {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}. With {不|bù}: "not ... either".
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm a student too.

vocab.note: After the plural subject, before the verb. With {也|yě}: {也|yě}{都|dōu}, never 都也.
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{美国人|Měi guó rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: We're both American.

vocab.note: Negative {没有|méi yǒu}, never 不有. "There is" comes in lesson 17.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{哥哥|gē ge}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have an older brother.

vocab.note: The negative of {有|yǒu}. Later also "didn't" (lesson 25).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{姐姐|jiě jie}。
vocab.exampleEn: I don't have an older sister.

vocab.note: Owner + {的|de} + thing: {老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}. Usually dropped with family and home: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is the teacher's name.

vocab.note: Also said zhèi in speech, especially before a measure word.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is my mum.

vocab.note: Fourth tone. {哪|nǎ} (which) has the third tone. Also said nèi in speech.
vocab.example: {那|nà}{是|shì}{我们|wǒ men}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: That's our teacher.

vocab.note: Joins nouns and pronouns only, never sentences or verbs.
vocab.example: {爸爸|bà ba}{和|hé}{妈妈|mā ma}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: Dad and Mum are both teachers.

vocab.note: No {的|de} after a pronoun: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}, my home or my family. Later also a measure word for shops and companies.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: How many people are there in your family?

vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{家人|jiā rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: These are my family.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: My dad is a teacher.

vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is my mum.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{哥哥|gē ge}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Do you have an older brother?

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{姐姐|jiě jie}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: My older sister speaks Chinese.

vocab.note: For a small number you expect, with a measure word: {几|jǐ}{个|gè}. For any number: {多少|duō shao}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{姐姐|jiě jie}？
vocab.exampleEn: How many older sisters do you have?

vocab.note: Between a number and a noun: {一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}. Often light in speech. {一|yī} becomes yí before it.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: There are five people in my family.

vocab.note: Said once for each gap inside a number: {一千零五|yì qiān líng wǔ} (1,005).
vocab.example: {一百零五|yì bǎi líng wǔ}
vocab.exampleEn: one hundred and five

vocab.note: Always with a number in front: {一百|yì bǎi}, never 百 alone for 100.
vocab.example: {三百四十五|sān bǎi sì shí wǔ}
vocab.exampleEn: three hundred and forty-five

vocab.example: {两千零二十六|liǎng qiān líng èr shí liù}
vocab.exampleEn: two thousand and twenty-six

vocab.note: Before a measure word: {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}. In counting and inside numbers it's {二|èr}: {十二|shí èr}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{妹妹|mèi mei}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have two younger sisters.

vocab.note: Age needs no {是|shì}: {我|wǒ}{二十|èr shí}{岁|suì}. Ask children {几岁|jǐ suì}, adults {多大|duō dà}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{女儿|nǚ ér}{六|liù}{岁|suì}。
vocab.exampleEn: My daughter is six.

vocab.note: Usually with {很|hěn}: {很多|hěn duō}{人|rén}. Before an adjective it asks "how": {多大|duō dà}, how old.
vocab.example: {中国|Zhōng guó}{有|yǒu}{很多|hěn duō}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: China has a lot of people.

vocab.note: For any number; the measure word is optional. {几|jǐ} is for small numbers and needs one.
vocab.example: {中国|Zhōng guó}{有|yǒu}{多少|duō shao}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: How many people does China have?

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{儿子|ér zi}{九|jiǔ}{岁|suì}。
vocab.exampleEn: My son is nine.

vocab.note: Both syllables keep their tones: nǚ ér.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{女儿|nǚ ér}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is my daughter.

vocab.example: {您|nín}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}？
vocab.exampleEn: How many children do you have?

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{弟弟|dì di}{十五|shí wǔ}{岁|suì}。
vocab.exampleEn: My younger brother is fifteen.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{妹妹|mèi mei}{多大|duō dà}？
vocab.exampleEn: How old is your younger sister?

meanings: mouth (also: measure word for family members)
vocab.note: As a measure word for people, only for the size of a family: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{五|wǔ}{口|kǒu}{人|rén}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{口|kǒu}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: How many people are there in your family?

vocab.note: Also before a verb, for where it happens: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}. Sounds like {再|zài} (again).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: My mum is at home.

vocab.note: Verb and noun: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{工作|gōng zuò} (I work at a university); {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{工作|gōng zuò}{吗|ma}？ (Do you have a job?)
vocab.example: {他|tā}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: He works for a company.

vocab.example: {她|tā}{是|shì}{医生|yī shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: She's a doctor.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: My dad works for a company.

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: We speak Chinese at school.

vocab.example: {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: Teacher Wang works at a university.

vocab.note: {生|shēng} keeps its first tone here, unlike {学生|xué sheng}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{是|shì}{大学生|dà xué shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My older brother is a university student.

vocab.note: Before a noun: {男|nán}{老师|lǎo shī}, a male teacher. Not used alone as "a man".
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{老师|lǎo shī}{是|shì}{男|nán}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: Our Chinese teacher is a man.

vocab.note: Before a noun: {女|nǚ}{医生|yī shēng}, a female doctor. Not used alone as "a woman".
vocab.example: {她|tā}{是|shì}{女|nǚ}{医生|yī shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: She's a (female) doctor.

vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{星期一|xīng qī yī}。
vocab.exampleEn: Today is Monday.

vocab.example: {明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'll be at home tomorrow.

vocab.example: {昨天|zuó tiān}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}。
vocab.exampleEn: Yesterday was Sunday.

vocab.note: Counts without {个|gè}: {一天|yì tiān}, {两天|liǎng tiān}. Also "sky", as in {天气|tiān qì} (weather, lesson 20). Can be a measure word too.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{在|zài}{中国|Zhōng guó}{工作|gōng zuò}{三天|sān tiān}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's working in China for three days.

vocab.note: Takes {个|gè} when counted: {两个星期|liǎng gè xīng qī}. Add {一|yī} to {六|liù} for Monday to Saturday: {星期一|xīng qī yī}, {星期六|xīng qī liù}.
vocab.example: {一个星期|yí gè xīng qī}{有|yǒu}{七天|qī tiān}。
vocab.exampleEn: A week has seven days.

vocab.note: The written and more formal word, seen on calendars and timetables; in everyday speech {星期天|xīng qī tiān}.
vocab.example: {星期日|xīng qī rì}{学校|xué xiào}{没有|méi yǒu}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's nobody at the school on Sunday.

vocab.note: The everyday spoken word; {星期日|xīng qī rì} is the written one. There is no {星期七|xīng qī qī}.
vocab.example: {星期天|xīng qī tiān}{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: I don't work on Sundays.

vocab.note: Month names are number + {月|yuè}: {一月|yī yuè} (January), {十二月|shí èr yuè} (December). "One month" is {一个月|yí gè yuè}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{十月|shí yuè}{不|bù}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm not working in October.

vocab.note: Number + {号|hào} in speech: {十六号|shí liù hào} (the 16th); writing uses {日|rì}. Also "number", as in {手机号|shǒu jī hào} (mobile number, lesson 10). Can be a measure word too.
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{几号|jǐ hào}？
vocab.exampleEn: What's the date today?

vocab.note: Written and formal: 11{月|yuè}16{日|rì}. In speech, {号|hào}. As a noun, {日|rì} is also "sun".
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{是|shì}11{月|yuè}16{日|rì}。
vocab.exampleEn: Today is 16 November.

vocab.note: Counts without {个|gè}: {两年|liǎng nián}. Years are read digit by digit: 2026{年|nián}, èr líng èr liù nián.
vocab.example: {一年|yì nián}{有|yǒu}{十二个月|shí èr gè yuè}。
vocab.exampleEn: A year has twelve months.

vocab.note: Two o'clock is {两点|liǎng diǎn}. An amount of hours is {小时|xiǎo shí}. Also "a little" in {一点儿|yì diǎnr} (lesson 12).
vocab.example: {现在|xiàn zài}{几点|jǐ diǎn}？
vocab.exampleEn: What time is it?

vocab.note: Clock minutes: {八点十分|bā diǎn shí fēn} (8:10). An amount of minutes is {分钟|fēn zhōng}. Also a fen, a hundredth of a yuan.
vocab.example: {现在|xiàn zài}{九点二十分|jiǔ diǎn èr shí fēn}。

vocab.note: An amount of time, with no {个|gè}: {十分钟|shí fēn zhōng} (ten minutes). On the clock, {分|fēn}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{十分钟|shí fēn zhōng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have ten minutes.

vocab.note: After the hour, half past: {八点半|bā diǎn bàn}. Half an hour: {半个小时|bàn gè xiǎo shí}.
vocab.example: {现在|xiàn zài}{七点半|qī diǎn bàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's half past seven.

vocab.note: Usually with {个|gè}: {两个小时|liǎng gè xiǎo shí} (two hours). Two o'clock is {两点|liǎng diǎn}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{一天|yì tiān}{工作|gōng zuò}{八个小时|bā gè xiǎo shí}。
vocab.exampleEn: I work eight hours a day.

vocab.example: {现在|xiàn zài}{两点|liǎng diǎn}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's two o'clock now.

vocab.note: Time you have or spend: {有时间|yǒu shí jiān} (to have time). To ask the clock time, use {几点|jǐ diǎn}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Do you have time?

vocab.note: The whole morning up to noon. Goes before the clock time: {上午|shàng wǔ}{十点|shí diǎn} (10 a.m.).
vocab.example: {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}{上午|shàng wǔ}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}。
vocab.exampleEn: Teacher Wang is at school in the morning.

vocab.note: Before the clock time: {下午|xià wǔ}{三点|sān diǎn} (3 p.m.).
vocab.example: {下午|xià wǔ}{三点|sān diǎn}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm at home at three in the afternoon.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{中午|zhōng wǔ}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm at the office at noon.

vocab.note: The early part of the morning, getting up and breakfast; {上午|shàng wǔ} is the whole morning until noon.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{六点|liù diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I get up at six in the morning.

vocab.note: From about six until bedtime: {晚上|wǎn shang}{十一点|shí yī diǎn} is 11 p.m.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm at home in the evening.

vocab.note: A separable verb: {起|qǐ} (rise) + {床|chuáng} (bed).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{几点|jǐ diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}？
vocab.exampleEn: What time do you get up?

vocab.note: A separable verb: {睡|shuì} (sleep) + {觉|jiào} (a sleep), so no object follows it. "Sleep eight hours" uses {睡|shuì} alone (lesson 21).
vocab.example: {他|tā}{晚上|wǎn shang}{十一点|shí yī diǎn}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。
vocab.exampleEn: He goes to bed at eleven at night.

vocab.note: A separable verb: {上|shàng} (go on) + {班|bān} (a shift). The opposite is {下班|xià bān}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{八点|bā diǎn}{上班|shàng bān}。
vocab.exampleEn: I start work at eight.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{几点|jǐ diǎn}{下班|xià bān}？
vocab.exampleEn: What time do you finish work?

vocab.note: With {吃|chī} (to eat, lesson 11): {吃早饭|chī zǎo fàn}, to have breakfast.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{七点|qī diǎn}{吃|chī}{早饭|zǎo fàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have breakfast at seven.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{吃|chī}{午饭|wǔ fàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have lunch at the office.

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{七点|qī diǎn}{吃|chī}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: We have dinner at seven.

vocab.note: Also a morning greeting: {早|zǎo}！ or {你早|nǐ zǎo}！ (Morning!). Opposite: {晚|wǎn}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{早|zǎo}！
vocab.exampleEn: You're early!

vocab.example: {晚上|wǎn shang}{十二点|shí èr diǎn}{很|hěn}{晚|wǎn}。
vocab.exampleEn: Twelve at night is late.

vocab.note: Away from the speaker. No word for "to" before the place: {去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where are you going?

vocab.note: Towards the speaker: if you aren't there yourself, use {去|qù}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{来|lái}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Are you coming to my place?

vocab.note: Back to where you belong: {回家|huí jiā} (go home), {回国|huí guó} (go back to your country).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: I go home in the evening.

vocab.note: A wish, gentle and polite. Also "to think" and "to miss" someone. Negative: {不想|bù xiǎng}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to go to China.

vocab.note: More decided than {想|xiǎng}; also takes a noun ("I'd like…"). "Don't want to" is {不想|bù xiǎng}: {不要|bú yào} + verb means "don't!" (lesson 21).
vocab.example: {明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{上班|shàng bān}。
vocab.exampleEn: Tomorrow I have to work.

vocab.note: {做什么|zuò shén me}: (to) do what. Not {坐|zuò} (to sit, lesson 18), which sounds the same.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{星期六|xīng qī liù}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}？
vocab.exampleEn: What are you doing on Saturday?

vocab.note: {有事|yǒu shì}: to be busy, have something on. A thing you can hold is {东西|dōng xi}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{明天|míng tiān}{有|yǒu}{事|shì}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Are you busy tomorrow?

vocab.note: Neutral second syllable. With full tones, {东西|dōng xī} means "east and west". {买东西|mǎi dōng xi}: to go shopping.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{买|mǎi}{什么|shén me}{东西|dōng xi}？
vocab.exampleEn: What are you buying?

vocab.note: Third tone; {卖|mài} (to sell, lesson 13) is the same syllable with the fourth tone.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{什么|shén me}？
vocab.exampleEn: What would you like to buy?

vocab.note: Also "to go and see, visit" a person: {看|kàn}{妈妈|mā ma}. "To see, catch sight of" is {看见|kàn jiàn} (lesson 24).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{妈妈|mā ma}。
vocab.exampleEn: On Sunday I'm going to see my mum.

vocab.note: One syllable with erhua. {哪里|nǎ lǐ} (lesson 16) means the same and is used everywhere. Not {那儿|nàr} (there).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where are you?

vocab.note: Said wéi, rising, when you answer the phone; a sharp falling wèi is "Hey!".
vocab.example: {喂|wéi}，{你好|nǐ hǎo}！
vocab.exampleEn: Hello? (on the phone)

vocab.note: {打|dǎ} (strike) + {电话|diàn huà}. "To phone someone" needs {给|gěi} (lesson 23).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm on the phone.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{没有|méi yǒu}{电话|diàn huà}。
vocab.exampleEn: We don't have a phone at home.

vocab.note: Literally "hand machine". {手机号|shǒu jī hào}: mobile number.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{找|zhǎo}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm looking for my phone.

vocab.note: Before a verb: the action is going on right now. {在|zài} alone and a final {呢|ne} do the same job.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{正在|zhèng zài}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's sleeping right now.

vocab.note: On the phone or at a door, {我|wǒ}{找|zhǎo} + person means "I'd like to speak to…".
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{找|zhǎo}{谁|shéi}？
vocab.exampleEn: Who are you looking for?

vocab.note: Often said zhīdao, with a light second syllable. Knowing a person is {认识|rèn shi} (lesson 23).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}。
vocab.exampleEn: I don't know.

vocab.note: Also said shuí. {谁|shéi}{的|de}: whose.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{是|shì}{谁|shéi}？
vocab.exampleEn: Who is he?

vocab.note: {说|shuō} (speak) + {话|huà} (words): takes no object. For a language, use {说|shuō}: {说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}.
vocab.example: {谁|shéi}{在|zài}{说话|shuō huà}？
vocab.exampleEn: Who's talking?

vocab.note: Listening on purpose. "To hear" is {听见|tīng jiàn} (lesson 24).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{听|tīng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm listening.

vocab.note: For food; drinks take {喝|hē}. {吃|chī}{饭|fàn} is "to have a meal", whatever is eaten.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{吃|chī}{包子|bāo zi}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have steamed buns in the morning.

vocab.note: Every drink takes {喝|hē}: {喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}, {喝|hē}{茶|chá}. Not the English "he": the e is said far back in the mouth.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Would you like some tea? / Do you drink tea?

vocab.note: Cooked rice, and so a meal in general: {吃|chī}{饭|fàn} (to eat), {早饭|zǎo fàn}, {午饭|wǔ fàn}, {晚饭|wǎn fàn}. The rice itself is {米饭|mǐ fàn}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Do you eat at home?

vocab.note: {米|mǐ} is the grain, {米饭|mǐ fàn} the cooked rice on your plate.
vocab.example: {中午|zhōng wǔ}{我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}{和|hé}{菜|cài}。
vocab.exampleEn: At noon I have rice and a dish.

vocab.note: Also {面条|miàn tiáo} without the northern -r. Traditional {麵|miàn} (noodles, flour), not {面|miàn} (face, side).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{面条儿|miàn tiáor}。
vocab.exampleEn: My mum likes noodles.

vocab.note: The character {饺|jiǎo} is HSK 3's: recognise the word now.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{做|zuò}{饺子|jiǎo zi}。
vocab.exampleEn: I can make dumplings.

vocab.example: {他|tā}{早上|zǎo shang}{吃|chī}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{包子|bāo zi}。
vocab.exampleEn: He has two steamed buns in the morning.

vocab.note: Rising tone, chá; {菜|cài} (dish) falls.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。
vocab.exampleEn: My dad really likes tea.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}。
vocab.exampleEn: I don't want tea; I'd like water.

vocab.note: Also "vegetable". {中国|Zhōng guó}{菜|cài} is Chinese food; {买|mǎi}{菜|cài} is doing the food shopping.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{菜|cài}？
vocab.exampleEn: What dish is this?

vocab.note: + noun or + verb: {喜欢|xǐ huan}{茶|chá}, {喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}. Negative {不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan} (never {没|méi}{喜欢|xǐ huan}). Neutral second syllable.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{饺子|jiǎo zi}。
vocab.exampleEn: I like eating dumplings.

vocab.note: In names often a hotel: {北京饭店|Běi jīng Fàn diàn} (the Beijing Hotel). {店|diàn} is an HSK 2 character.
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{饭店|fàn diàn}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go and eat at a restaurant.

vocab.note: {请|qǐng} + verb: please (do). {我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ} is "it's my treat".
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。
vocab.exampleEn: Please have some tea.

vocab.note: Ends a suggestion: {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{吧|ba} (let's go). Compare {吗|ma}, which asks.
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's eat.

vocab.note: For food; a drink that tastes good is {好喝|hǎo hē}.
vocab.example: {饺子|jiǎo zi}{太|tài}{好吃|hǎo chī}{了|le}！
vocab.exampleEn: The dumplings are so good!

vocab.note: Traditional {麵|miàn} (flour), not {面|miàn} (face).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{吃|chī}{面包|miàn bāo}，{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。
vocab.exampleEn: In the morning I have bread and tea.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{会|huì}{做饭|zuò fàn}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Can you cook?

vocab.note: {杯|bēi} alone counts cupfuls: {一|yì}{杯|bēi}{茶|chá}, a cup of tea.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{杯子|bēi zi}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is my cup.

vocab.note: After a verb, softens it: {看|kàn}{一下|yí xià} (have a look), {等|děng}{一下|yí xià} (wait a moment). {一|yí} rises before the 4th tone.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{一下|yí xià}。
vocab.exampleEn: Let me have a look.

vocab.note: After the verb: {喝|hē}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{水|shuǐ}. Not {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} (lesson 21), which goes before adjectives.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: I can speak a little Chinese.

vocab.note: {太|tài}…{了|le}: {太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！ (great!), {太|tài}{多|duō}{了|le} (too much). {不|bú}{太|tài} = not very.
vocab.example: {太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！
vocab.exampleEn: Great!

vocab.note: After the surname: {王|Wáng}{先生|xiān sheng}, Mr Wang. Also "husband".
vocab.example: {王|Wáng}{先生|xiān sheng}，{您|nín}{好|hǎo}！
vocab.exampleEn: Hello, Mr Wang!

vocab.note: Polite and formal, after the surname: {李|Lǐ}{女士|nǚ shì}, Ms Li.
vocab.example: {李|Lǐ}{女士|nǚ shì}，{您|nín}{好|hǎo}！
vocab.exampleEn: Hello, Ms Li!

vocab.note: Second tone; {千|qiān} (thousand) is first.
vocab.example: {面包|miàn bāo}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？
vocab.exampleEn: How much is the bread?

vocab.note: The spoken word for {元|yuán}: {十|shí}{块|kuài}{钱|qián}. Also a piece: {一|yí}{块|kuài}{面包|miàn bāo}.
vocab.example: {一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}{四十|sì shí}{块|kuài}。
vocab.exampleEn: One book is forty kuai.

vocab.note: On price tags, menus and receipts (also ¥); people say {块|kuài}.
vocab.example: {包子|bāo zi}{两|liǎng}{元|yuán}。
vocab.exampleEn: Steamed buns, two yuan.

vocab.note: Fourth tone; {买|mǎi} (to buy) is third. {=The character 卖 has 十 on top of 买=}; in traditional script {+卖+} has 士 on top of {+买+}.
vocab.example: {你们|nǐ men}{卖|mài}{茶|chá}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Do you sell tea?

vocab.example: {太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}！
vocab.exampleEn: That's too expensive!

vocab.note: {便|pián} is pián here (biàn in {方便|fāng biàn}, convenient).
vocab.example: {面包|miàn bāo}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}。
vocab.exampleEn: The bread is cheap.

vocab.note: {店|diàn} is an HSK 2 character.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going to the shops to buy some things.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm buying two books.

vocab.example: {一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？
vocab.exampleEn: How much is one book?

vocab.example: {大学|dà xué}{的|de}{书店|shū diàn}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}。
vocab.exampleEn: The university bookshop is cheap.

meanings: measure word for clothes and matters
vocab.note: Clothes (especially tops and coats) and matters: {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}, {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to buy a piece of clothing.

vocab.note: Ends the names of kinds of shops: {书店|shū diàn}, {饭店|fàn diàn}, {商店|shāng diàn}. An HSK 2 character.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{的|de}{店|diàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is my mum's shop.

vocab.note: Often said zhèige in northern speech. Before a noun: {这个|zhè ge}{人|rén}, this person.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{要|yào}{这个|zhè ge}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'll have this one.

vocab.note: Often said nèige. Falling tone; {哪个|nǎ ge} (which one) dips.
vocab.example: {那个|nà ge}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？
vocab.exampleEn: How much is that one?

vocab.note: Often said něige. A question word: no {吗|ma}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{要|yào}{哪个|nǎ ge}？
vocab.exampleEn: Which one do you want?

vocab.note: {些|xiē} replaces the measure word: {这些|zhè xiē}{书|shū}.
vocab.example: {这些|zhè xiē}{苹果|píng guǒ}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}。
vocab.exampleEn: These apples are cheap.

vocab.example: {那些|nà xiē}{书|shū}{很|hěn}{贵|guì}。
vocab.exampleEn: Those books are expensive.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{哪些|nǎ xiē}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}？
vocab.exampleEn: Which fruits would you like to buy?

meanings: some (measure word for a number of things)
vocab.note: Makes plurals after {这|zhè}, {那|nà}, {哪|nǎ} and {一|yì}: {这些|zhè xiē}, {一些|yì xiē}.
vocab.example: {这些|zhè xiē}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}。
vocab.exampleEn: These are mine.

vocab.note: Compare {一点儿|yì diǎnr}, a little (amount).
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{买|mǎi}{一些|yì xiē}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's buy some eggs.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{苹果|píng guǒ}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm buying five apples.

vocab.note: Two third tones: said shuí guǒ.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Do you like fruit?

vocab.note: {第|dì}{一|yī} first, {第|dì}{二|èr} second; {一|yī} stays yī, and second is never {第|dì}{两|liǎng}.
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{第|dì}{一|yī}{天|tiān}。
vocab.exampleEn: Today is my first day.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{喝|hē}{牛奶|niú nǎi}。
vocab.exampleEn: I drink milk in the morning.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{一些|yì xiē}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to buy some eggs.

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go to the supermarket to do some shopping.

vocab.note: Counted with {件|jiàn}: {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。
vocab.exampleEn: This top is very pretty.

vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{你|nǐ}{穿|chuān}{什么|shén me}？
vocab.exampleEn: What are you wearing today?

vocab.note: Straight before a noun: {新|xīn}{衣服|yī fu}, {新|xīn}{书|shū}.
vocab.example: {她|tā}{穿|chuān}{新|xīn}{衣服|yī fu}。
vocab.exampleEn: She's wearing new clothes.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{穿|chuān}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}。
vocab.exampleEn: You look really pretty in this.

vocab.note: Also for films and books worth watching or reading.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}！
vocab.exampleEn: What do you think of this top? It looks great!

vocab.note: Stronger than {很|hěn}; before the adjective.
vocab.example: {饺子|jiǎo zi}{非常|fēi cháng}{好吃|hǎo chī}。
vocab.exampleEn: The dumplings are extremely good.

vocab.note: Exclaims your feeling: {真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}！ Not used in questions. Also an adjective, "real".
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{真|zhēn}{好|hǎo}！
vocab.exampleEn: You're so kind!

vocab.note: {不|bú}{对|duì}: wrong. Also a preposition, "to, towards" ({他|tā}{对|duì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}).
vocab.example: A：{你|nǐ}{是|shì}{大卫|Dà wèi}{吗|ma}？B：{对|duì}。
vocab.exampleEn: A: Are you David? B: That's right.

vocab.note: A share of something; {半|bàn} is for times and with measure words ({八|bā}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{一半|yí bàn}，{你|nǐ}{吃|chī}{一半|yí bàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'll eat half, you eat half.

vocab.note: Asks for an opinion; after a suggestion, "how about it?".
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}，{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go to the supermarket. How about it?

vocab.note: Said ná lǐ (two third tones). Means the same as {哪儿|nǎr}, which is northern speech.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{哪里|nǎ lǐ}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where do you live?

vocab.note: The northern form of {这里|zhè lǐ}; same meaning.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{书|shū}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{这儿|zhèr}。
vocab.exampleEn: Your book is with me. (I've got your book.)

vocab.note: Used everywhere and in writing; {这儿|zhèr} is the northern spoken form. {里|lǐ} is often light here.
vocab.example: {请问|qǐng wèn}，{这里|zhè lǐ}{是|shì}{大学|dà xué}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Excuse me, is this the university?

vocab.note: Fourth tone; {哪儿|nǎr} (third tone) asks "where?".
vocab.example: {超市|chāo shì}{在|zài}{那儿|nàr}。
vocab.exampleEn: The supermarket is over there.

vocab.note: Fourth tone on {那|nà}; {哪里|nǎ lǐ} (third tone) asks "where?". {那儿|nàr} is the northern form.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{那里|nà lǐ}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: My mum works there.

vocab.note: Goes after the noun: {杯子|bēi zi}{里|lǐ}, in the cup. Often said lightly (li).
vocab.example: {水|shuǐ}{在|zài}{杯子|bēi zi}{里|lǐ}。
vocab.exampleEn: The water is in the cup.

vocab.note: Also a noun of position: {书|shū}{上|shàng}, on the book. As a verb, "go up, go to": {上班|shàng bān}, {上课|shàng kè}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{书|shū}{上|shàng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My phone is on the book.

vocab.note: Also a noun of position ({衣服|yī fu}{下|xià}, under the clothes) and "next" before time words. As a verb, "come down": {下雨|xià yǔ}, {下课|xià kè}.
vocab.example: {手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{衣服|yī fu}{下|xià}。
vocab.exampleEn: The phone is under the clothes.

vocab.note: After a noun, for place or time: {饭|fàn}{前|qián}, before meals. In speech, usually {前边|qián bian}. Not {钱|qián} (money): same sound, different character.
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{前|qián}{来|lái}。
vocab.exampleEn: Please come before eight.

vocab.note: After a noun, for place or time: {饭|fàn}{后|hòu}, after meals. In speech, usually {后边|hòu bian}.
vocab.example: {饭|fàn}{后|hòu}{我|wǒ}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。
vocab.exampleEn: After meals I drink tea.

vocab.note: Alone after a noun it sounds compact ({学校|xué xiào}{外|wài}); in speech and on its own, use {外边|wài bian}.
vocab.example: {饭店|fàn diàn}{外|wài}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: There are lots of people outside the restaurant.

vocab.note: Opens a polite question to a stranger. To apologise, say {对不起|duì bu qǐ}.
vocab.example: {请问|qǐng wèn}，{超市|chāo shì}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？
vocab.exampleEn: Excuse me, where's the supermarket?

vocab.note: Also a suffix for position words: {外边|wài bian}, {上边|shàng bian}, {前边|qián bian} (light bian).
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{来|lái}{这边|zhè biān}。
vocab.exampleEn: This way, please.

vocab.note: Can stand alone, unlike one-syllable {外|wài}: {外边|wài bian}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}. {边|biān} is light.
vocab.example: {外边|wài bian}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: There are lots of people outside.

vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{来|lái}{这边|zhè biān}{坐|zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: Come and sit over here, please.

vocab.example: {那边|nà biān}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{超市|chāo shì}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's a supermarket over there.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{没有|méi yǒu}{电视|diàn shì}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's no TV in my room.

vocab.example: {桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's a book on the table.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{在|zài}{椅子|yǐ zi}{上|shàng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My clothes are on the chair.

vocab.note: Literally "electric brain".
vocab.example: {房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{电脑|diàn nǎo}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Is there a computer in the room?

vocab.note: {看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}: to watch TV. {开|kāi}{电视|diàn shì}: to turn the TV on.
vocab.example: {爸爸|bà ba}{晚上|wǎn shang}{看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}。
vocab.exampleEn: Dad watches TV in the evening.

vocab.note: Usually {住|zhù}{在|zài} + place, with the place after the verb.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I live in Beijing.

vocab.note: {坐|zuò} + vehicle + {去|qù} + place: go somewhere by. Same sound as {做|zuò} (to do) and the {作|zuò} of {工作|gōng zuò}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going to Beijing by train.

vocab.note: {开|kāi}{车|chē}, drive; {开|kāi}{电视|diàn shì}, switch on the TV; {开|kāi}{门|mén}, open the door.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{开|kāi}{出租车|chū zū chē}。
vocab.exampleEn: He drives a taxi.

vocab.note: Verb + object already: don't add another object.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{会|huì}{开车|kāi chē}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Can you drive?

vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{车|chē}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is my car.

vocab.note: {出租|chū zū} (rent out) + {车|chē}.
vocab.example: {妈妈|mā ma}{坐|zuò}{出租车|chū zū chē}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: Mum is taking a taxi home.

vocab.note: "Fire vehicle", from the age of steam.
vocab.example: {火车|huǒ chē}{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}？
vocab.exampleEn: What time does the train arrive?

vocab.note: "Flying machine". A passenger {坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}; a pilot {开|kāi}{飞机|fēi jī}.
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{去|qù}。
vocab.exampleEn: We're flying there.

vocab.note: Before a verb: {怎么|zěn me}{去|qù}？ (how do you get there?). Compare {怎么样|zěn me yàng}, "what is it like?".
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}？
vocab.exampleEn: How do you get to school?

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{学校|xué xiào}。
vocab.exampleEn: I get to school at eight.

vocab.note: Takes a subject or a skill, even a verb: {学|xué}{开车|kāi chē}, learn to drive.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{学|xué}{写|xiě}{汉字|hàn zì}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to learn to write Chinese characters.

vocab.note: A little more formal than {学|xué}, and fine on its own: {他|tā}{在|zài}{学习|xué xí}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{学习|xué xí}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm studying Chinese in Beijing.

vocab.note: Verb + object: say {上|shàng}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{课|kè} for "have Chinese class".
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{上课|shàng kè}。
vocab.exampleEn: Our class starts at eight.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}{下课|xià kè}？
vocab.exampleEn: What time do you finish class?

vocab.note: For pupils and students; teachers and office workers {上班|shàng bān}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{儿子|ér zi}{早上|zǎo shang}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{去|qù}{上学|shàng xué}。
vocab.exampleEn: My son goes to school at seven in the morning.

vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{下午|xià wǔ}{没有|méi yǒu}{课|kè}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's no class this afternoon.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{会|huì}{写|xiě}{汉字|hàn zì}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Can you write Chinese characters?

vocab.note: A word is {词|cí} (HSK 2); {学生|xué sheng} is one word written with two {字|zì}.
vocab.example: {这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{怎么|zěn me}{写|xiě}？
vocab.exampleEn: How do you write this character?

vocab.note: Third tone; {谢|xiè} in {谢谢|xiè xie} is fourth.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{写|xiě}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}。
vocab.exampleEn: I can write my name.

vocab.note: Teachers call the class {同学们|tóng xué men}.
vocab.example: {安娜|Ān nà}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}。
vocab.exampleEn: Anna is my classmate.

vocab.note: Ability, or the situation allows it. A learned skill is {会|huì}; permission is usually {可以|kě yǐ}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{不|bù}{能|néng}{来|lái}。
vocab.exampleEn: I can't come tomorrow.

vocab.note: Said ké yǐ (two third tones). Also an adjective, "not bad, OK".
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{可以|kě yǐ}{坐|zuò}{这儿|zhèr}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: May I sit here?

vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{天气|tiān qì}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
vocab.exampleEn: What's the weather like today?

vocab.example: {北京|Běi jīng}{冷|lěng}{了|le}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's got cold in Beijing.

vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{太|tài}{热|rè}{了|le}！
vocab.exampleEn: It's so hot today!

vocab.note: Verb + object, "come-down rain". Snow works the same way: {下雪|xià xuě}.
vocab.example: {外边|wài bian}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's started raining outside.

vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{雨|yǔ}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。
vocab.exampleEn: The rain is heavy today.

vocab.note: To snow: {下雪|xià xuě}.
vocab.example: {北京|Běi jīng}{下雪|xià xuě}{了|le}，{雪|xuě}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's snowing in Beijing, and the snow is beautiful.

meanings: change particle (something new: now, any more)
vocab.note: At the end of a sentence it marks a new situation ({下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}); after a verb, a completed action (lesson 25). Always light.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm not going after all.

vocab.note: Takes a whole clause: {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}. For "think" as an opinion it is usually {觉得|jué de} rather than {想|xiǎng}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}{这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
vocab.exampleEn: What do you think of this room?

vocab.note: A verb ({我|wǒ}{病|bìng}{了|le}: I'm ill, I've fallen ill) and a noun (illness). {看病|kàn bìng} is to see a doctor.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{病|bìng}{了|le}，{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bú}{去|qù}{上班|shàng bān}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm ill, so I'm not going to work today.

vocab.note: A verb-object word: {生|shēng} (to get) + {病|bìng} (illness).
vocab.example: {他|tā}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}，{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's ill and resting at home.

vocab.note: Separable (verb + object). Said by the patient (I go and see a doctor) and of the doctor (who sees patients).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{下午|xià wǔ}{去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}{看病|kàn bìng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going to the hospital to see a doctor this afternoon.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{医院|yī yuàn}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: My mum works at a hospital.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}，{休息|xiū xi}{一下|yí xià}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: You're busy. Take a little break.

meanings: rather (a bit too, before an adjective)
vocab.note: Before an adjective, usually for something unwelcome: {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{冷|lěng} (a bit cold). Compare {一点儿|yì diǎnr}, which goes after a verb or adjective.
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{冷|lěng}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's a bit cold today.

vocab.note: Also "to be free, to have nothing on": {我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{没事|méi shì} (I'm free today).
vocab.example: “{对不起|duì bu qǐ}！”“{没事|méi shì}。”
vocab.exampleEn: "Sorry!" "It's nothing."

meanings: to sleep (on its own, with a time)
vocab.note: {睡觉|shuì jiào} is "to sleep, to go to bed" as a whole; {睡|shuì} on its own takes times and other words: {睡|shuì}{八|bā}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}, {睡|shuì}{一下|yí xià}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{睡|shuì}{八|bā}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。
vocab.exampleEn: I sleep eight hours at night.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{白天|bái tiān}{工作|gōng zuò}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{学习|xué xí}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: I work during the day and study Chinese in the evening.

vocab.note: Mostly an adjective, used without {是|shì}: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}. As a verb: {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{忙|máng}{什么|shén me}？ (What are you busy with?)
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{明天|míng tiān}{忙|máng}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Are you busy tomorrow?

vocab.note: {不要|bú yào} + verb tells someone not to do something. {我|wǒ}{不要|bú yào} on its own is "I don't want it".
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{病|bìng}{了|le}，{不要|bú yào}{去|qù}{上班|shàng bān}。
vocab.exampleEn: You're ill. Don't go to work.

vocab.note: Stronger than {喜欢|xǐ huan}. With a verb: {爱|ài}{看|kàn}{书|shū} (loves reading).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{很|hěn}{爱|ài}{看|kàn}{书|shū}。
vocab.exampleEn: My dad loves reading.

vocab.note: {唱|chàng}{歌|gē}: to sing (songs).
vocab.example: {她|tā}{在|zài}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}{呢|ne}。
vocab.exampleEn: She's singing.

vocab.note: Same syllable as {哥哥|gē ge} (older brother): different character.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{听|tīng}{中国|Zhōng guó}{歌|gē}。
vocab.exampleEn: I like listening to Chinese songs.

vocab.example: {这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: This film is really good.

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{晚上|wǎn shang}{去|qù}{电影院|diàn yǐng yuàn}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go to the cinema this evening.

vocab.note: Both "to read (books)" and "to study, to be a student somewhere": {在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{读书|dú shū}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{读书|dú shū}。
vocab.exampleEn: My older brother is studying at university.

vocab.note: Reading aloud, or reading as study. Reading silently for fun is usually {看|kàn}: {看|kàn}{书|shū}.
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{读|dú}{一下|yí xià}{这些|zhè xiē}{字|zì}。
vocab.exampleEn: Please read these characters aloud.

vocab.note: Often {玩儿|wánr} in northern speech. {去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}{玩|wán} is "visit Beijing for fun".
vocab.example: {孩子|hái zi}{们|men}{在|zài}{外边|wài bian}{玩|wán}。
vocab.exampleEn: The children are playing outside.

vocab.example: {北京|Běi jīng}{很|hěn}{好玩儿|hǎo wánr}。
vocab.exampleEn: Beijing is a fun place.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}{很|hěn}{好听|hǎo tīng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Your name sounds lovely.

vocab.example: {他|tā}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{中国|Zhōng guó}{朋友|péng you}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's my Chinese friend.

vocab.example: {她|tā}{男朋友|nán péng you}{是|shì}{医生|yī shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Her boyfriend is a doctor.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{女朋友|nǚ péng you}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Do you have a girlfriend?

meanings: little one (friendly word for a child)
vocab.note: Adults call children {小朋友|xiǎo péng you}; it means "child", not "a small friend".
vocab.example: {小朋友|xiǎo péng you}，{你|nǐ}{几|jǐ}{岁|suì}{了|le}？
vocab.exampleEn: How old are you, little one?

vocab.example: {大家|dà jiā}{好|hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{安娜|Ān nà}。
vocab.exampleEn: Hello, everyone! My name is Anna.

vocab.note: A verb with two objects ({给|gěi}{他|tā}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}) and a preposition before a verb ({给|gěi}{妈妈|mā ma}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}: call Mum).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'll call you this evening.

vocab.note: Same sound as {在|zài} (at, in). {再|zài} is "again" for something that hasn't happened yet.
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{一下|yí xià}。
vocab.exampleEn: Could you say that again, please?

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān}{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}{见|jiàn}？
vocab.exampleEn: What time shall we meet tomorrow?

vocab.note: Can take two objects: the person, then the question.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{问|wèn}{老师|lǎo shī}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: Go and ask the teacher.

vocab.note: Knowing people (and characters you can recognise). Knowing a fact is {知道|zhī dào}.
vocab.example: {认识|rèn shi}{你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Nice to meet you.

vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm really happy today.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}。
vocab.exampleEn: We have a dog.

vocab.example: {这|zhè}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。
vocab.exampleEn: This cat is beautiful.

vocab.note: For animals and things. Sounds the same as {他|tā} and {她|tā}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}，{它|tā}{叫|jiào}{大白|Dà bái}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have a cat. It's called Dabai ("Big White").

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}，{它们|tā men}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{小|xiǎo}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have two dogs. They're both small.

meanings: measure word for animals and birds
vocab.note: Traditional {隻|zhī}. Simplified {={只|zhǐ}=}, read zhǐ, also means "only" (HSK 3), which stays {={只|zhǐ}=} in traditional.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}？
vocab.exampleEn: How many cats do you have at home?

vocab.note: Often in pairs: {有的|yǒu de}…，{有的|yǒu de}… (some…, others…).
vocab.example: {有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{猫|māo}，{有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{狗|gǒu}。
vocab.exampleEn: Some people like cats, and others like dogs.

vocab.example: {有些|yǒu xiē}{同学|tóng xué}{不|bú}{会|huì}{写|xiě}{这|zhè}{个|gè}{字|zì}。
vocab.exampleEn: Some classmates can't write this character.

vocab.note: {看|kàn} (look) + {见|jiàn} (the result: perceive). {看|kàn} is the action; {看见|kàn jiàn} is actually seeing.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{看见|kàn jiàn}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{猫|māo}{了|le}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Have you seen my cat?

vocab.note: {听|tīng} is "to listen"; {听见|tīng jiàn} is actually hearing.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{听见|tīng jiàn}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{在|zài}{说话|shuō huà}。
vocab.exampleEn: I can hear someone talking.

vocab.note: Also read {还|huán} (to give back) in HSK 3. {还有|hái yǒu}: and there's also…
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}，{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have a cat, and a dog too.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{今年|jīn nián}{二十|èr shí}{岁|suì}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm twenty this year.

vocab.example: {明年|míng nián}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}{学习|xué xí}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: Next year I'd like to go to China to study Chinese.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{去年|qù nián}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一个|yí gè}{新|xīn}{手机|shǒu jī}。
vocab.exampleEn: I bought a new phone last year.

vocab.note: {没|méi}{问题|wèn tí}: no problem.
vocab.example: {老师|lǎo shī}，{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一个|yí gè}{问题|wèn tí}。
vocab.exampleEn: Excuse me (teacher), I have a question.

vocab.note: An adjective ({人|rén}{很|hěn}{少|shǎo} (there are few people)) and a verb (to be missing). The opposite of {多|duō}. Read {少|shào} in a few words (young: HSK 3 and later).
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{超市|chāo shì}{里|lǐ}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}。
vocab.exampleEn: There are very few people in the supermarket today.

vocab.note: Covers both {初中|chū zhōng} (junior: about ages 12–15) and {高中|gāo zhōng} (senior: about 15–18).
vocab.example: {他|tā}{是|shì}{中学|zhōng xué}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's a secondary-school teacher.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妹妹|mèi mei}{是|shì}{中学生|zhōng xué shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My younger sister is at secondary school.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{女儿|nǚ ér}{上|shàng}{小学|xiǎo xué}{了|le}。
vocab.exampleEn: My daughter has started primary school.

vocab.example: {小学生|xiǎo xué shēng}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{上课|shàng kè}。
vocab.exampleEn: Primary-school pupils start lessons at eight.

meanings: the time when (as in "when I was little")
vocab.note: …{的|de}{时候|shí hou} means "when …". Clock time and amounts of time are {时间|shí jiān}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{小学生|xiǎo xué shēng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}。
vocab.exampleEn: When I was at primary school, I loved singing.

vocab.note: Takes the family name only: {我|wǒ}{姓|xìng}{王|Wáng}，{叫|jiào}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}. Also a noun, "family name". Polite question: {您|nín}{贵姓|guì xìng}？
vocab.example: {那|nà}{位|wèi}{老师|lǎo shī}{姓|xìng}{什么|shén me}？
vocab.exampleEn: What's that teacher's family name?

vocab.note: The word on forms and lists. In conversation, say {名字|míng zi}.
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{写|xiě}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{姓名|xìng míng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Please write your full name.

vocab.note: Also a measure word for places in a ranking ({第一|dì yī}{名|míng}, first place) and, in notices, for people ({十|shí}{名|míng}{学生|xué sheng}).
vocab.example: {她|tā}{是|shì}{第一|dì yī}{名|míng}。
vocab.exampleEn: She came first.

vocab.note: Respectful: {这|zhè}{位|wèi}{老师|lǎo shī}, {哪|nǎ}{位|wèi}, {几|jǐ}{位|wèi}？ Never about yourself; {个|gè} is the neutral one.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{位|wèi}{是|shì}{李|Lǐ}{医生|yī shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is Dr Li.

vocab.note: After a pronoun ({我|wǒ}{自己|zì jǐ}, myself) or alone. Before a verb, "by oneself"; with {的|de}, "one's own".
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{自己|zì jǐ}{做饭|zuò fàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: I cook for myself.

vocab.note: {我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{你们|nǐ men}{介绍|jiè shào}{一下|yí xià} (let me introduce you). Doubled: {介绍介绍|jiè shào jiè shào}.
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{介绍|jiè shào}{一下|yí xià}{你|nǐ}{自己|zì jǐ}。
vocab.exampleEn: Please introduce yourself.

vocab.note: Your mother's father is {外公|wài gōng} or {姥爷|lǎo ye}. Children also call any old man {爷爷|yé ye}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{今年|jīn nián}{八十|bā shí}{岁|suì}{了|le}。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandpa is eighty this year.

vocab.note: Your mother's mother is {外婆|wài pó} or {姥姥|lǎo lao}.
vocab.example: {奶奶|nǎi nai}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{我们|wǒ men}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: Grandma lives with us.

vocab.note: Usually in a topic-comment sentence: {他|tā}{个子|gè zi}{很|hěn}{高|gāo} (he's tall).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妹妹|mèi mei}{个子|gè zi}{不|bù}{高|gāo}。
vocab.exampleEn: My younger sister isn't tall.

vocab.note: Tall for people, high for things. How tall: {多|duō}{高|gāo}？ The opposite for people, {矮|ǎi}, is HSK 3.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{哥哥|gē ge}{真|zhēn}{高|gāo}！
vocab.exampleEn: Your older brother is really tall!

vocab.note: For length and time. Not for tall people ({高|gāo}). Read {长|zhǎng}, the same character means "to grow" (HSK 3).
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{太|tài}{长|cháng}{了|le}。
vocab.exampleEn: This top is too long.

vocab.note: Also a measure word for cattle: {一|yì}{头|tóu}{牛|niú}. {头疼|tóu téng}: headache.
vocab.example: {那|nà}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}{头|tóu}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。
vocab.exampleEn: That child has a big head.

vocab.note: Light second syllable. One eye: {一|yì}{只|zhī}{眼睛|yǎn jing}.
vocab.example: {她|tā}{眼睛|yǎn jing}{大大|dà dà}{的|de}。
vocab.exampleEn: She has big eyes.

vocab.note: In {手机|shǒu jī} (mobile phone) and {手表|shǒu biǎo} (wristwatch).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手|shǒu}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My hands are cold.

vocab.note: {身体|shēn tǐ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}: in good health. {您|nín}{身体|shēn tǐ}{好|hǎo}{吗|ma}？ is a kind greeting to an older person.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{身体|shēn tǐ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandpa is in good health.

vocab.note: After a verb, a state that lasts: {穿着|chuān zhe} (wearing), {开着|kāi zhe} (on, open). Negative {没|méi} + verb. Traditional (Taiwan) {著|zhe}.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{穿|chuān}{着|zhe}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's wearing red.

vocab.note: Ask: {什么|shén me}{颜色|yán sè}？
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{什么|shén me}{颜色|yán sè}？
vocab.exampleEn: What colour do you like?

vocab.note: Before a noun: {红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}, or short {红|hóng}{衣服|yī fu}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{要|yào}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'll have the red one.

vocab.example: {白色|bái sè}{的|de}{裤子|kù zi}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: The white trousers look nice.

vocab.example: {他|tā}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{是|shì}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}。
vocab.exampleEn: His phone is black.

vocab.note: Write the two dots: lǜ (type lv4). {路|lù} (road) is another word.
vocab.example: {她|tā}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{绿色|lǜ sè}。
vocab.exampleEn: She really likes green.

vocab.note: Counted with {条|tiáo}: {一|yì}{条|tiáo}{裤子|kù zi}. Worn with {穿|chuān}.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{穿|chuān}{着|zhe}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}{裤子|kù zi}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's wearing black trousers.

vocab.note: Counted with {块|kuài}: {一|yí}{块|kuài}{手表|shǒu biǎo}. Traditional {手錶|shǒu biǎo} ({錶|biǎo} for watches, {表|biǎo} for tables and forms).
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{块|kuài}{手表|shǒu biǎo}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{的|de}。
vocab.exampleEn: This watch is my grandpa's.

vocab.note: The neutral word. Also heard: {先生|xiān sheng}, {老公|lǎo gōng} (informal), {爱人|ài ren} (spouse).
vocab.example: {她|tā}{丈夫|zhàng fu}{是|shì}{医生|yī shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Her husband is a doctor.

vocab.note: The neutral word. Also heard: {太太|tài tai}, {老婆|lǎo po} (informal), {爱人|ài ren} (spouse).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妻子|qī zi}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: My wife works at a university.

vocab.note: Said xiǎo hár. Also {小孩|xiǎo hái} without the northern -r. {孩子|hái zi} is also someone's son or daughter.
vocab.example: {那|nà}{个|gè}{小孩儿|xiǎo háir}{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}！
vocab.exampleEn: That kid is really cute!

vocab.example: {他们|tā men}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{男孩儿|nán háir}。
vocab.exampleEn: They have a boy.

vocab.example: {那|nà}{个|gè}{女孩儿|nǚ háir}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{妹妹|mèi mei}。
vocab.exampleEn: That girl is my younger sister.

vocab.note: Before a measure word, with {都|dōu} before the verb: {每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{都|dōu}…, {每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}… ({天|tiān} and {年|nián} need no {个|gè}).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I get up at seven every day.

vocab.note: After the subject, before the verb (and before {在|zài} + place).
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{经常|jīng cháng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: We often eat at home.

vocab.note: Also {有时候|yǒu shí hou}. Before the verb or at the start: {有时|yǒu shí}…，{有时|yǒu shí}… (sometimes…, sometimes…).
vocab.example: {星期天|xīng qī tiān}{我|wǒ}{有时|yǒu shí}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}。
vocab.exampleEn: On Sundays I sometimes stay at home and rest.

vocab.note: {洗|xǐ}{衣服|yī fu} (do the washing), {洗|xǐ}{手|shǒu} (wash your hands). Doubled: {洗洗|xǐ xi}{手|shǒu}.
vocab.example: {吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{前|qián}{要|yào}{洗|xǐ}{手|shǒu}。
vocab.exampleEn: You should wash your hands before eating.

vocab.note: Often paired with {所以|suǒ yǐ}: {因为|yīn wèi}…，{所以|suǒ yǐ}…. Answers {为什么|wèi shén me} (why).
vocab.example: {因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。
vocab.exampleEn: I had a headache, so I didn't go to class.

vocab.note: Starts its clause, before the subject. Said suó yǐ (two third tones).
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's cold today, so I'm staying at home.

vocab.note: {不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}: unwell. {你|nǐ}{哪儿|nǎr}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}？ (What's wrong?)
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm feeling a bit unwell.

vocab.note: Both "tired" and "tiring": {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}, {这|zhè}{个|gè}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{累|lèi}{了|le}{吧|ba}？
vocab.exampleEn: You must be tired.

vocab.note: Body part + {疼|téng}: {我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng} (I have a headache). Also "to dote on": {奶奶|nǎi nai}{很|hěn}{疼|téng}{我|wǒ}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{哪儿|nǎr}{疼|téng}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where does it hurt?

vocab.note: Taken with {吃|chī}: {吃|chī}{药|yào}. Same sound as {要|yào} (want; should).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{要|yào}{吃|chī}{药|yào}。
vocab.exampleEn: You should take some medicine.

vocab.example: {学校|xué xiào}{外边|wài bian}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{药店|yào diàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's a pharmacy outside the school.

vocab.note: One word for both. {笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}: said with a smile.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{笑|xiào}{什么|shén me}？
vocab.exampleEn: What are you laughing at?

vocab.note: Third tone; {坐|zuò} (to sit) and {做|zuò} (to do) fall. Mostly in words and directions: {左边|zuǒ bian}, {左手|zuǒ shǒu}, {往|wǎng}{左|zuǒ}{走|zǒu}.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{的|de}{左手|zuǒ shǒu}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{疼|téng}。
vocab.exampleEn: His left hand hurts a bit.

vocab.note: Fourth tone; {有|yǒu} (to have) dips. {右|yòu} has {口|kǒu} under the top, {有|yǒu} has {月|yuè}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{右手|yòu shǒu}{怎么|zěn me}{了|le}？
vocab.exampleEn: What's wrong with your right hand?

vocab.note: {边|biān} is light. "To the left of X" is X ({的|de}) {左边|zuǒ bian}: {学校|xué xiào}{左边|zuǒ bian}. {左面|zuǒ miàn} means the same.
vocab.example: {超市|chāo shì}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{左边|zuǒ bian}。
vocab.exampleEn: The supermarket is to the left of the school.

vocab.note: {边|biān} is light. "To the right of X" is X ({的|de}) {右边|yòu bian}. {右面|yòu miàn} means the same.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{右边|yòu bian}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}。
vocab.exampleEn: On my right is my classmate.

vocab.note: Unlike {左边|zuǒ bian}, its {边|biān} keeps the first tone. No -{面|miàn} form.
vocab.example: {药店|yào diàn}{在|zài}{医院|yī yuàn}{旁边|páng biān}。
vocab.exampleEn: The pharmacy is next to the hospital.

vocab.note: The same as {前边|qián bian}; {面|miàn} is often light in speech. "In front of X" is X ({的|de}) {前面|qián miàn}.
vocab.example: {前面|qián miàn}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{书店|shū diàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's a bookshop ahead.

vocab.note: The same as {后边|hòu bian}. {={后|hòu}=} becomes {後|hòu} in traditional script; {面|miàn} stays {面|miàn}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{后面|hòu miàn}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{大学|dà xué}。
vocab.exampleEn: Behind my home is a university.

vocab.note: Mostly a suffix ({前面|qián miàn}, {后面|hòu miàn}). Also a measure word for flat things: {一|yí}{面|miàn}{镜子|jìng zi} ({镜子|jìng zi}: a mirror). This {面|miàn} stays {面|miàn} in traditional script; {面|miàn} "noodles, flour" is {麵|miàn}.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{面|miàn}{镜子|jìng zi}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{的|de}。
vocab.exampleEn: This mirror is my mum's.

vocab.note: A {离|lí} B {远|yuǎn} / {近|jìn}: how far A is from B. For a starting point ("from… to…") use {从|cóng}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{离|lí}{学校|xué xiào}{很|hěn}{近|jìn}。
vocab.exampleEn: My home is close to school.

vocab.note: Usually with {离|lí}: {离|lí}{这儿|zhèr}{远|yuǎn}{吗|ma}？ Third tone; {元|yuán} (yuan, money) rises.
vocab.example: {医院|yī yuàn}{离|lí}{这儿|zhèr}{远|yuǎn}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Is the hospital far from here?

vocab.note: Same sound as {进|jìn} (to enter, lesson 09).
vocab.example: {超市|chāo shì}{很|hěn}{近|jìn}，{走路|zǒu lù}{五|wǔ}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My home is close to the school.

vocab.note: Used as a preposition: {往|wǎng} + direction + verb ({往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}, {往|wǎng}{左|zuǒ}{走|zǒu}). Third tone; {忘|wàng} (to forget) falls.
vocab.example: {往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}，{书店|shū diàn}{在|zài}{右边|yòu bian}。
vocab.exampleEn: Go straight ahead; the bookshop is on the right.

vocab.note: A starting point in place or time: {从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{来|lái}, {从|cóng}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}. Also an adverb in {从小|cóng xiǎo} (since childhood, lesson 25). Distance "from" is {离|lí}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{来|lái}。
vocab.exampleEn: I've come from Beijing.

vocab.note: The movement itself; {去|qù} needs a destination. {我|wǒ}{走|zǒu}{了|le} = I'm off. {我们|wǒ men}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba} = let's go.
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}！
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go!

vocab.note: Verb + object ({路|lù}, road). {走路|zǒu lù}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}: walk to school. How long: {走路|zǒu lù}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{走路|zǒu lù}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}。
vocab.exampleEn: I walk to school every day.

vocab.note: Also the number of a bus route: {三十二|sān shí èr}{路|lù} (the No. 32).
vocab.example: {这儿|zhèr}{的|de}{路|lù}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{新|xīn}。
vocab.exampleEn: The roads here are all new.

vocab.note: {上|shàng} is light. {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{路上|lù shang} (I'm on my way) is a common message.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{路上|lù shang}，{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{到|dào}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm on my way; I'll be there in ten minutes.

vocab.note: "Ground iron": {地|dì} (ground) + {铁|tiě} (iron). {坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}: go by metro. A metro station is {地铁站|dì tiě zhàn}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{上班|shàng bān}。
vocab.exampleEn: I go to work by metro every day.

vocab.note: Short for "public transport vehicle". {坐|zuò}{公交车|gōng jiāo chē}; the No. 8 bus is {八|bā}{路|lù}{公交车|gōng jiāo chē}.
vocab.example: {坐|zuò}{公交车|gōng jiāo chē}{去|qù}{机场|jī chǎng}{要|yào}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。
vocab.exampleEn: It takes an hour to the airport by bus.

vocab.note: Any station or stop for vehicles. {火车站|huǒ chē zhàn} (railway station) and {地铁站|dì tiě zhàn} (metro station) name the kind.
vocab.example: {车站|chē zhàn}{离|lí}{这儿|zhèr}{不|bù}{远|yuǎn}。
vocab.exampleEn: The station isn't far from here.

vocab.note: After a noun: {地铁站|dì tiě zhàn}, {火车站|huǒ chē zhàn}. Also counts stops: {坐|zuò}{三|sān}{站|zhàn} (ride three stops). HSK 3 adds {站|zhàn} "to stand".
vocab.example: {下|xià}{一|yí}{站|zhàn}{是|shì}{机场|jī chǎng}。
vocab.exampleEn: The next stop is the airport.

vocab.note: Everyday speech for {坐|zuò}{出租车|chū zū chē}. {打车|dǎ chē}{去|qù}{机场|jī chǎng}: take a taxi to the airport.
vocab.example: {太|tài}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{打车|dǎ chē}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's too late; let's take a taxi home.

vocab.note: {机|jī} as in {飞机|fēi jī} (plane) + {场|chǎng} (an open area).
vocab.example: {从|cóng}{这儿|zhèr}{到|dào}{机场|jī chǎng}{要|yào}{四十|sì shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's forty minutes from here to the airport.

vocab.note: {飞机|fēi jī} (plane) + {票|piào} (ticket).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{机票|jī piào}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？
vocab.exampleEn: How much was your plane ticket?

vocab.note: {买|mǎi}{票|piào}: buy a ticket. Kinds of ticket: {机票|jī piào}, {门票|mén piào} (admission, lesson 10), {车票|chē piào} (for a bus or train).
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{买|mǎi}{票|piào}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go and buy the tickets.

vocab.note: {飞机|fēi jī} is a "flying machine". {从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{飞|fēi}{上海|Shàng hǎi}: fly from Beijing to Shanghai.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{飞|fēi}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。
vocab.exampleEn: Tomorrow I'm flying from Beijing to Shanghai.

vocab.note: {进|jìn} + place: {进|jìn}{商店|shāng diàn}. Same sound as {近|jìn} (near, lesson 07).
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{进|jìn}{商店|shāng diàn}{看|kàn}{看|kàn}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go into the shop and have a look.

vocab.note: {出|chū} + place: {出门|chū mén} (leave the house), {出国|chū guó} (go abroad, lesson 10).
vocab.example: {出|chū}{了|le}{学校|xué xiào}，{往|wǎng}{右|yòu}{走|zǒu}。
vocab.exampleEn: When you come out of the school, go right.

vocab.note: Towards the speaker: the speaker is inside. {来|lái} is often light (jìn lai). A place goes before {来|lái}: {进|jìn}{房间|fáng jiān}{来|lái}.
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{进来|jìn lái}！
vocab.exampleEn: Please come in!

vocab.note: Away from the speaker: the speaker is outside. {去|qù} is often light (jìn qu).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{进去|jìn qù}{吧|ba}，{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{进去|jìn qù}。
vocab.exampleEn: You go in; I'm not going in.

vocab.note: Towards the speaker: the speaker is outside. {来|lái} is often light (chū lai).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{出来|chū lái}{一下|yí xià}，{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}。
vocab.exampleEn: Come out for a moment; I'm at the door.

vocab.note: Away from the speaker: the speaker is inside. {他|tā}{出去|chū qù}{了|le}: he's gone out.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{出去|chū qù}{了|le}，{不|bú}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: My mum has gone out; she isn't home.

vocab.note: Back to where the speaker is. {回|huí}{家|jiā}{来|lái} puts the place before {来|lái}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}{回来|huí lái}？
vocab.exampleEn: What time will you be back?

vocab.note: Back to somewhere the speaker isn't. {回|huí}{家|jiā}{去|qù} puts the place before {去|qù}.
vocab.example: {太|tài}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{回去|huí qù}{了|le}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's late; I'm heading back.

vocab.note: {开|kāi}{门|mén} (open the door; also: a shop opens), {门口|mén kǒu} (the doorway). Almost the sound of {们|men} (the plural suffix), which adds the person radical on the left.
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{开|kāi}{门|mén}！
vocab.exampleEn: Please open the door!

vocab.note: "Door mouth". {学校|xué xiào}{门口|mén kǒu}: the school gate. {在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}: at the door.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{门口|mén kǒu}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm at the school gate.

vocab.note: {去|qù} + place + {旅游|lǚ yóu}: {去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}{旅游|lǚ yóu}. {={游|yóu}=} here is {遊|yóu} in traditional script; {={游|yóu}=} "to swim" (lesson 19) stays {={游|yóu}=}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}{旅游|lǚ yóu}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to go to Beijing on holiday.

vocab.note: Verb + {过|guo}: at some time in the past ({我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{北京|Běi jīng}). Negative {没|méi} + verb + {过|guo}: {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}. Light; {过|guò} "to pass, spend" is lesson 13's.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{北京|Běi jīng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I've been to Beijing.

vocab.note: After the verb: {去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì} (been twice). Before a noun: {这|zhè}{次|cì} (this time), {下|xià}{次|cì} (next time), {第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì} (the first time). {词|cí} (word, lesson 17) rises.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。
vocab.exampleEn: I've been to Shanghai twice.

vocab.note: {外国|wài guó}{人|rén}: a foreigner. {外国|wài guó} + noun: {外国|wài guó}{朋友|péng you}, {外国|wài guó}{菜|cài}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{外国|wài guó}{朋友|péng you}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have lots of friends from other countries.

vocab.note: Separable: {过|guo} goes between, {出|chū}{过|guo}{国|guó} (have been abroad).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{出|chū}{过|guo}{国|guó}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Have you ever been abroad?

vocab.note: Not a bar, though {酒|jiǔ} is alcohol. {饭店|fàn diàn} (HSK 1) is a restaurant and also appears in some hotel names.
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{离|lí}{机场|jī chǎng}{很|hěn}{近|jìn}。
vocab.exampleEn: Our hotel is very close to the airport.

vocab.note: "Gate ticket": for a park, a museum, a sight. {机票|jī piào} is a plane ticket.
vocab.example: {门票|mén piào}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？
vocab.exampleEn: How much is admission?

vocab.note: Leaving home for the day or an outing: {今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{出门|chū mén} (I didn't go out today). {出去|chū qù} is "go out" from wherever you are.
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{出门|chū mén}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's cold today; I don't want to go out.

vocab.note: Number + {楼|lóu} is a floor, with no {第|dì}: {五|wǔ}{楼|lóu} (the fifth floor), {二|èr}{楼|lóu}, {几|jǐ}{楼|lóu}？ Street level is {一|yī}{楼|lóu}. {楼上|lóu shàng} upstairs, {楼下|lóu xià} downstairs.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{五|wǔ}{楼|lóu}。
vocab.exampleEn: We live on the fifth floor.

vocab.note: Counts rooms: {三|sān}{间|jiān}{房间|fáng jiān}, {这|zhè}{间|jiān}. {个|gè} also works. Same character as in {时间|shí jiān}; {件|jiàn} (clothes) has a different tone.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{间|jiān}{房间|fáng jiān}。
vocab.exampleEn: Our flat has two rooms.

vocab.note: "Wash-hands room": the polite everyday word, at home and in public. Said *xí shǒu jiān* (two third tones in a row).
vocab.example: {请问|qǐng wèn}，{洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？
vocab.exampleEn: Excuse me, where's the toilet?

vocab.note: "In bed" is {床|chuáng}{上|shàng} (on the bed). Also in {起床|qǐ chuáng} (to get up).
vocab.example: {孩子|hái zi}{在|zài}{床|chuáng}{上|shàng}{看|kàn}{书|shū}。
vocab.exampleEn: The child is reading in bed.

vocab.note: Stands alone ({在|zài}{上面|shàng miàn}) or after a noun ({桌子|zhuō zi}{上面|shàng miàn} = {桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}). {上边|shàng bian} means the same.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上面|shàng miàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: Your phone is on the table.

vocab.note: Stands alone or after a noun: {床|chuáng}{下面|xià miàn}. {下边|xià bian} means the same.
vocab.example: {床|chuáng}{下面|xià miàn}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's a cat under the bed.

vocab.note: Can stand alone, unlike {里|lǐ}: {里面|lǐ miàn}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{吗|ma}？ After a noun, {房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ} and {房间|fáng jiān}{里面|lǐ miàn} both work.
vocab.example: {里面|lǐ miàn}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Is anyone in there?

vocab.note: Stands alone or after a noun: {门|mén}{外面|wài miàn}. The same as {外边|wài bian} (HSK 1).
vocab.example: {外面|wài miàn}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{里面|lǐ miàn}{很|hěn}{热|rè}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's cold outside and warm inside.

vocab.note: Towards the speaker. After a verb it's a direction complement, usually light: {拿|ná}{上来|shàng lái} (bring up).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{六|liù}{楼|lóu}，{你|nǐ}{上来|shàng lái}{吧|ba}！
vocab.exampleEn: We're on the sixth floor, come up!

meanings: to go up (away from the speaker)
vocab.note: Away from the speaker: {我|wǒ}{上去|shàng qù}{看看|kàn kan}. After a verb: {拿|ná}{上去|shàng qù} (take up).
vocab.example: {地铁|dì tiě}{上|shàng}{人|rén}{太|tài}{多|duō}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{上去|shàng qù}。
vocab.exampleEn: There were too many people on the metro; I didn't get on.

vocab.note: Said by someone below: {你|nǐ}{下来|xià lái}{吧|ba}. After a verb: {拿|ná}{下来|xià lái} (bring down).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{楼下|lóu xià}，{你|nǐ}{下来|xià lái}{一下|yí xià}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm downstairs; could you come down for a moment?

meanings: to go down (away from the speaker)
vocab.note: Going down to someone below is {下去|xià qù} in Chinese, where English says "I'm coming down".
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{楼下|lóu xià}{吗|ma}？{我|wǒ}{下去|xià qù}。
vocab.exampleEn: Are you downstairs? I'm coming down.

vocab.note: Across a space towards the speaker. After a verb: {走|zǒu}{过来|guò lái} (walk over), {拿|ná}{过来|guò lái} (bring over).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{过来|guò lái}{一下|yí xià}。
vocab.exampleEn: Come over here a moment.

vocab.note: Across a space, away from the speaker. HSK 3 adds {过去|guò qù} "the past" (a noun).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{过去|guò qù}{看看|kàn kan}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'll go over and have a look.

meanings: to rise (get up from bed, a chair or the floor)
vocab.note: {起床|qǐ chuáng} is only out of bed; {起来|qǐ lái} is up from anywhere. After a verb: {拿|ná}{起来|qǐ lái} (pick up).
vocab.example: {早上|zǎo shang}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起来|qǐ lái}。
vocab.exampleEn: I get up at seven in the morning.

vocab.note: Rising tone; {那|nà} (that) falls and {哪|nǎ} (which) dips. Usually with a direction: {拿|ná}{来|lái}, {拿|ná}{出来|chū lái}, {拿|ná}{回去|huí qù}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{拿|ná}{一|yì}{杯|bēi}{水|shuǐ}{来|lái}。
vocab.exampleEn: Bring a glass of water.

meanings: to open up (a book, box or door; to switch on)
vocab.note: For anything closed, and for books and boxes, where {开|kāi} alone isn't used: {打开|dǎ kāi}{书|shū}. Also switches on: {打开|dǎ kāi}{电视|diàn shì}.
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{打开|dǎ kāi}{书|shū}。
vocab.exampleEn: Please open your books.

vocab.note: Two objects: {告诉|gào su} + person + thing ({告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}). {说|shuō} can't take the person: not {说|shuō}{我|wǒ}. Second syllable light.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}，{你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{要|yào}{什么|shén me}？
vocab.exampleEn: Tell me, what would you like?

vocab.note: {生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}！ Happy birthday! {过|guò}{生日|shēng rì}: to have or celebrate a birthday.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}{是|shì}{几|jǐ}{月|yuè}{几|jǐ}{号|hào}？
vocab.exampleEn: When is your birthday?

vocab.note: For wishes and a happy life: {生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}. For your mood today, {高兴|gāo xìng} is more usual.
vocab.example: {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}！
vocab.exampleEn: Happy birthday to you!

meanings: to give as a present (also: to see off)
vocab.note: Two objects: {送|sòng}{她|tā}{花|huā}; also {送给|sòng gěi} + person. Second meaning: {我|wǒ}{送|sòng}{你|nǐ}{回家|huí jiā} (I'll see you home). Handing over a present: {送|sòng}{你|nǐ}！
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{送|sòng}{妈妈|mā ma}{一|yí}{块|kuài}{手表|shǒu biǎo}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm giving Mum a watch.

vocab.note: No measure word when not counting: {送|sòng}{她|tā}{花|huā}. The same character is the verb "to spend" (lesson 23).
vocab.example: {这些|zhè xiē}{花|huā}{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}！
vocab.exampleEn: These flowers are lovely!

vocab.note: + noun: prepare ({准备|zhǔn bèi}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}); + verb: plan to ({准备|zhǔn bèi}{明年|míng nián}{去|qù}). {准备|zhǔn bèi}{好|hǎo}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ Are you ready?
vocab.example: {妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: Mum is getting dinner ready.

meanings: ah (particle of warmth, exclaiming or softening)
vocab.note: At the end of a sentence, always light: {好|hǎo}{啊|a}！ (Sure!), {是|shì}{啊|a} (that's right), {真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}{啊|a}！ After some sounds it's written {呀|ya} or {哇|wa}.
vocab.example: {好|hǎo}{啊|a}，{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{吧|ba}！
vocab.exampleEn: Great, let's go and eat!

meanings: to celebrate the New Year (Spring Festival)
vocab.note: The lunar New Year, the Spring Festival. Greeting: {过年|guò nián}{好|hǎo}！
vocab.example: {你们|nǐ men}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}{过年|guò nián}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where are you spending the New Year?

meanings: to pass; to spend (a day, a festival)
vocab.note: Fourth tone, the main verb: {过|guò}{生日|shēng rì}, {怎么|zěn me}{过|guò}？ Not the experience particle {过|guo} (lesson 10), which is light and follows another verb.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{生日|shēng rì}{怎么|zěn me}{过|guò}？
vocab.exampleEn: How are you spending your birthday?

meanings: than (A 比 B + adjective; to compare)
vocab.note: A {比|bǐ} B + adjective: {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{高|gāo}. No {很|hěn} inside. The difference goes after: {大|dà}{三|sān}{岁|suì}, {贵|guì}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}. Also used as a preposition.
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{冷|lěng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Today is colder than yesterday.

vocab.note: {跟|gēn} + person + verb: with ({跟|gēn}{朋友|péng you}{去|qù}; {跟|gēn}…{一起|yì qǐ}). {跟|gēn}{他|tā}{说|shuō}: tell him. {跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{来|lái}: follow me. Also a preposition and a conjunction.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{妈妈|mā ma}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going to the supermarket with Mum.

vocab.note: Before an adjective or a verb of liking: {最|zuì}{贵|guì} (the most expensive), {最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan} (favourite). No {很|hěn} with it.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{什么|shén me}{颜色|yán sè}？
vocab.exampleEn: What's your favourite colour?

vocab.note: Before a verb: quickly ({快|kuài}{来|lái}！). {快|kuài}{点儿|diǎnr}！ Hurry up! Same sound and tone as {块|kuài} (a kuai, a yuan): context tells them apart. Also an adverb.
vocab.example: {地铁|dì tiě}{比|bǐ}{公交车|gōng jiāo chē}{快|kuài}。
vocab.exampleEn: The metro is faster than the bus.

vocab.note: {慢慢|màn màn}{说|shuō}: take your time, speak slowly. {慢|màn}{走|zǒu}！ Take care! (to a guest leaving).
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{慢|màn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{说|shuō}。
vocab.exampleEn: Please speak a bit more slowly.

vocab.note: Real praise: {很|hěn}{不错|bú cuò} is "really good". Said *bú*, rising before the fourth tone.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{很|hěn}{不错|bú cuò}！
vocab.exampleEn: Your Chinese is really good!

vocab.note: The opposite of {对|duì}: {你|nǐ}{错|cuò}{了|le} (you're wrong).
vocab.example: {对|duì}{不|bu}{对|duì}？——{不|bú}{对|duì}，{错|cuò}{了|le}。
vocab.exampleEn: Is that right? — No, it's wrong.

vocab.note: The opposite of {好|hǎo}. With {了|le}: broken, gone bad ({手机|shǒu jī}{坏|huài}{了|le}).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{坏|huài}{了|le}。
vocab.exampleEn: My phone has broken.

vocab.note: After the subject, before the verb: {你|nǐ}{为什么|wèi shén me}{不|bú}{去|qù}？ Answer with {因为|yīn wèi}. Literally "for what".
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{为什么|wèi shén me}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}？
vocab.exampleEn: Why are you learning Chinese?

vocab.note: Starts the second half, before its subject. With {虽然|suī rán}: {虽然|suī rán}…，{但是|dàn shì}… Short form {但|dàn}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}，{但是|dàn shì}{没有|méi yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to go, but I haven't got time.

vocab.note: The short form of {但是|dàn shì}, common in writing and between short phrases: {很|hěn}{小|xiǎo}，{但|dàn}{很|hěn}{舒服|shū fu}. Also a conjunction.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{贵|guì}，{但|dàn}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。
vocab.exampleEn: This piece of clothing is expensive, but it's beautiful.

vocab.note: Usually with {但是|dàn shì} in the second half, unlike English. Before or after the subject: {虽然|suī rán}{他|tā}… / {他|tā}{虽然|suī rán}…
vocab.example: {虽然|suī rán}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Although I'm tired, I'm happy.

vocab.note: …{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{意思|yì si}？ What does … mean? {我|wǒ}{的|de}{意思|yì si}{是|shì}… What I mean is…
vocab.example: {这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{意思|yì si}？
vocab.exampleEn: What does this character mean?
